EVENT_NARRATIVE: A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rain over the southern part of the Springs Fire burn scar. This heavy rain generated some flash flooding and mud flows across the Pacific Coast Highway between Las Posas Road and Deer Path Road. Both sides of the Pacific Coast Highway were closed due to the mudslide.
Roadway flooding and debris caused multiple lane closures on highway 101 near the Red Barn.
A strong thunderstorm generated flash flooding across southeastern sections of the Antelope Valley. Just southwest of El Mirage Road, water between 1 and 2 feet deep flooded several intersections.
Highway 178 was closed south of Badwater Basin due to flooding.
Flash flooding occurred in Zion National Park, particularly along Pine Creek. In addition, many waterfalls were reported across the park.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed from mile marker 12 to 22 due to flooding, and Stockton Hill Road was closed from mile marker 40 to Pierce Ferry Road.
Highway 95 was flooded between mile markers 67 and 71. Water, sand, and gravel were across the road.

According to local media reports, 65 homes in the Cannon Air Force Base area were impacted by the flooding, including roof damage, weather stripping, carpet, flooring, and sheetrock. Local officials evacuated 33 families from those homes and put them in hotel lodging. The flooding in Clovis forced the closure of U.S. Highway 60/84. Approximately 40 feet of state highway 108 between mile markers 6 and 10 was washed out. Clovis police had to use an armored vehicle to rescue 7 victims stranded by or caught in fast moving waters or flooded streets.
CHP reported Country Club Drive closed due to water flowing over road at dip.
CHP reported Quarry Road closed due to flooding in the low water crossing. The road had to be closed twice.
There were reports of San Diego fire and police responding to multiple (6 incidents) swift water rescues in the Midway and Mission Hills neighborhoods.

San Diego Fire and San Diego city lifeguard swift rescue reported at least 3 vehicles under water and responded to high water rescues. The Midway area at the Marine Corps Recruit Depot was closed with a vehicle under 4 feet of water. A vehicle floated and damaged other vehicles. Trash cans were also reported floating. Homes on Torrance and Reynard were flooded with some resident evacuations and garage and minor home damage reported.

A thunderstorm moved over the Fresno area producing a few tenths of an inch a short period of time. This heavy rainfall was compounded with poor drainage which lead to areas of curb to curb flooding, one road closure at an underpass where water was multiple feet deep, and flood waters entering buildings.
A resident reported flooding on El Cajon Boulevard in the North Park neighborhood of San Diego. Based on photos, the water appears to be around 6 to 8 inches deep.

A spotter in Day California reported a mudslide up against her house.  This slide was associated with a burn scarred area and affected two houses.  A sheriff deputy reported that clogged culverts caused mud and water to overflow the road.

Trained spotter measured 4.9 inches of rain over the course of 3 hours. This resulted in fast flowing water in their yard, with the highest watermark on the side of their house being 8 inches. No water was reported to have entered the home. The end time of the flooding and areal coverage were estimated.
Spotter noted that Yeso Creek had overflowed its banks and was also running rapidly. No further information or damage was reported.

Spotter reported several arroyos were overflowing their banks and washing out numerous roads. State Road 294 was closed due to flooding near junction with U.S. Highway 60 for several hours after causative event. Most of the flooding subsided by 3 am which allowed some roads to become passable. No damage was reported with this flooding.

Heavy rain caused all of the creeks to overflow their banks and washout a few roads. The spotter measured 3.5 inches of rain caused this flooding.  Power was out for a while before returning around 945 am.  No other damage was reported.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed state road 108 at mile marker 14 due to flooding from the heavy rains.  While flooding may have subsided, the DOT reported that the road will remain closed through memorial day weekend. A CoCoRaHS observer near Pleasant Hill reported 3.25 inches of rain in less than 24 hours.
The New Mexico Department of Transportation closed state road 272 at mile marker 9 due to flooding.
Flash flooding washed out sections of Echo Canyon Dam Road.
Flash flooding was reported along the East Fork of the Virgin River, particularly closer to Orderville and US 89.
Flash flooding was reported along Wahweap Creek and some surrounding drainages.
Rocks and mud washed over Highway 266 11 miles W of Lida.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with a peak flow of 2050 cfs recorded at the Paria River gauge near Kanab.

Heavy rain caused widespread flash flooding in the cities of Gunnison and Centerfield, with an approximate total of 30 homes and businesses sustaining some damage from the flood waters. About another 100 homes experienced yard flooding. Most damaged homes had minor damage to basements or lower levels. In addition, portions of the Gunnison Market grocery store were flooded, and some of the inventory was damaged.
Up to 2 feet of water on portions of Echols Avenue as well as along Cameo Street. The Dennis Chaves Park Lake was overflowing onto 14th Street which lead to several cars stalling out.
Flash flooding was reported along the Buckskin and House Rock Valley drainages, as well as a few other smaller drainages in the area.
Both Coalinga fire department and a NWS employee reported street flooding between 1830 and 1850 PDT. Storms continued to redevelop over the area so flood threat continued.

A large flash flood occurred along Wahweap Creek, particularly near the town of Big Water. The flood waters closed and damaged roads near Big Water, and stranded people at the Big Water Visitor Center for 3 hours.
Flash flooding overnight was reported across a wide area of drainages flowing into Lake Powell.
A large flash flood was reported in Sheets Gulch in Capitol Reef National Park.
The county sheriff's office reported 10 to 20 campers stranded in the White Wash Sand Dune Recreation area due to impassible roadways from fast flowing water and significant mud deposited onto roads.
The road to the Delicate Arch viewpoint in Arches National Park was closed as it was inundated from fast moving water from the Salt Wash due to heavy rainfall.
Flash flooding was reported along the Scenic Drive of Capitol Reef National Park. Rangers closed the road when water from Grand Wash began flowing over the roadway.

Significant flash flooding was reported in several locations along Lake Powell, including at Wahweap Creek, at Iceberg Canyon, and at Crystal Springs Canyon. Many visitors were stranded for several hours while they waited for the flood waters to subside. The most dramatic flooding occurred in Crystal Springs Canyon, where visitors to the lake watched as three of their boats were tossed around and damaged by the flood waters. One of these boats, a 23-foot 1997 Maxum, was hit and submerged by two boulders, and was considered a total loss after the event.

Park rangers at Goblin Valley State Park reported flash flooding along the Temple Wash, with Temple Mountain Road severely washed out at the Temple Wash crossing. Flood waters from Temple Wash and Chute Canyon also crossed Little Wild Horse Road.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the river gauge recording a peak flow of 2520 cfs.
Chunks of pavement removed from Big Mesa Road during heavy rainfall. High water was flowing over several portions of the roadway.

Per a spotter report, 1.13 inches of rain fell in about an hour in the Six Mile Canyon area near the Lyon and Storey County line. Lyon County Emergency Management  received reports of significant yard and landscaping damage as well as water in garages. Also, heavy equipment was required to remove mud from streets in the Mark Twain community as well as in Six Mile Canyon (Storey County).
Water and mud covered Echo Dam Road.

The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported 9 homes with damage due to flooding near the low water crossings in the Ruhenstroth subdivision area. A fire chief noted that the completely dry Pine Nut Creek was rapidly filled with a 4 to 5 foot wall of water.
The Douglas County Emergency Manager reported flash flooding impacts near low water crossings along Sawmill and Arroyo Roads.
Water, mud, and debris flowed over Highway 190. A traffic collision in the flooded area injured two people (indirect).
Rocks and debris were over Highway 190 near Father Crowley Point.

Strong thunderstorms produced flash flooding and mud/debris flows in southeast San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 33 and Highway 166.

Approximately 1.5 inches of rainfall fell over the cities of Taft and Maricopa in 30 minutes or so. This resulted in some flooding of an apartment complex in the city of Taft as well as a vehicles being stranded on flooded roadways. Also, SR 166 was closed around 7 PM due to flooding.
Flash flooding was reported during the overnight and morning hours along Wahweap Creek.
UDOT meteorologists reported Highway 128 from the Highway 191 intersection to mile marker 20 was closed due to numerous areas of fast moving water up to a foot deep running across the roadway.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the river gauge rising to 1160 cfs.
Several areas of debris filled water up to a foot deep flowed over Highway 211 between Highway 191 and the entrance to Canyonlands National Park.
Debris filled water up to a foot deep flowed over Potash Road and along portions of Highway 279.
Water and mud were over Highway 264 in three places between mile markers 3 and 9.
County road 155 washed away and culverts destroyed.

Strong thunderstorms produced flash flooding in the mountains of Ventura County. The Ventura County Sheriff reported flash flooding at the intersection of Lockwood Valley Road and Boy Scout Camp road.

Over two inches of rain fell over Tehachapi during the afternoon of the 12th. This resulted in a mud/debris flow near highway 58 and highway 202 in the center of Tehachapi, which closed the roadway for a couple of hours.

Strong thunderstorms produced flash flooding and mud/debris flows across the Antelope Valley. California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Largo Vista Road. Two vehicles were trapped by 2 to 4 feet of mud.
Water, rocks, and debris flowed over Linn Road and Belfield Boulevard.  A nearby spotter reported half an inch of rain in less than half an hour.
Another large flash flood was reported along the Paria River, this one extending into the upper drainages of the river, as well as a few other nearby drainages.

Heavy rainfall resulted in a flash flood within Arch Canyon with fast moving water at least four feet deep.  An SUV that was parked along the Arch Canyon Trail road was carried down the canyon about 2.2 miles.  The people who owned the SUV were camped on higher ground and had to hike out of the canyon for assistance after the flood waters subsided.
Intersection of 17th and 18th streets with 3rd and Kilgor flooding. No damage reported.

Heavy rainfall occurred across the mountains in Kern County which lead to a mud/debris flow across S. Kelso Valley road and Zimmerman St. in rural Kern County. This debris flow removed a 20 foot section of the roadway, though cost of the damage was not reported.
Highway 267 closed between milemarkers 10 and 11 due to flash flooding.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed US Highway 64 as heavy rain caused debris, boulders and a mud slide to cover several miles of the road. Philmont Scout Ranch also reported major flash flooding on the Ponil Creek basin that ran through a boy scout camp site in the nearby mountains. The flooding washed away 4 boys, killing 1.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding south of Jemez Springs, closing state road 485 and forest service road 376. The county emergency manager reported significant damage to state road 485. Low water crossings along state road 4 between mile markers 10 and 16 were also flooded, but the road was never closed. New Mexico Department of Transportation representatives also noted that the Rio Guadalupe was out of its banks and possibly into homes.  Further information not confirmed at this time.

CHP reported a second-hand report of flash flood wash out with a depth of 1.5 feet of soil across the pavement at Highland Valley Road and Highway 67 near Ramona, as well as a mud slide across roadway at Highland Valley Road and Archie Moore Road in Poway.
Rocks and mud washed over Death Valley Road in several locations near the intersection of Highway 168.

Slow-moving thunderstorms with torrential rainfall in the higher terrain overwhelmed city drainage systems, causing flash flooding in East Sparks. Some areas were under several feet of water, with standing water and debris making travel difficult along Sparks and Vista Blvds. According to Sparks Police at least a dozen cars were stuck in the flooding. Water damage to Whitehead and Moss Elementary Schools was estimated at between 400K and 450K.
California Highway Patrol reported water threatening highway 14 near Red Rock Canyon.

Lyon County Emergency Management reported that highway 342 through Silver City was flooded with water, gravel and debris. Traffic was diverted to an alternate truck route. The time of the flooding is estimated based on radar.
Highway 318 was closed at mile marker 2 due to flash flooding and debris on the road.
Heavy rain caused a mudslide along NM 38, causing it to close for 2 hours.  The rain also caused a rockslide to close all but one lane of County Road 578.
Ten feet of water was rushing through a normally dry gulley on the spotters property. No damage was reported as a result of this wall of water.
Several feet of water flowed over BLM Road 1045.  Over an inch of rain fell at the Bar Ten Ranch.
Highway 375 was covered with water and debris.
Mud and rocks washed onto Highway 322.
Facebook videos from a National Weather Service employee and KOLO News showed fast flowing water in Pine Nut Creek and over low water crossings on Cali Pequeno and Out-R-Way Roads.

Heavy rains caused a barn and two pastures to be flooded. One lane of a two-lane gravel road was also washed out with many other roads seeing 3 feet deep ravines created by the heavy rain. Numerous roads around the Zuni Mountains were washed out and residents were trapped in their homes for several days until county officials could repair the roads. Phone services were also lost.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm washed out three roads in spots between Chilchinbeto and Dennehotso.

Heavy rain caused State Road 491 north of Gallup to close due to flooding and debris. County Emergency Manager reported flash flooding caused 4 inches of mud and 8 inches of water to enter a juvenile center on the east side of town. He also noted that a few bridges were temporarily closed due to flood waters, along with numerous county roads suffering damage. Exact location and extent of damage was unknown. Allen Joe Begay of White Cone, Arizona was swept away in flood waters while in the Rio Puerco.
USGS river gauge measured a 5 foot rise in Carrizo Creek near Carrizo between 500 PM and 600 PM MST. The maximum flow reached 2470 CFS in a creek that usually runs less than 100 CFS.
Six inches of water flowed over the I-40 frontage road near mile marker 66. The Cedar Hills gage nearby measured 2.20 inches of rain.
The Nevada DOT reported a flash flood and rock slide along state route 360. The time of the flash flood is approximate and based on radar.

Thunderstorms developed across the central deserts during the early afternoon hours on July 5th, and they affected the community of Casa Grande. Peak rainfall rates were well in excess of one inch per hour and were sufficient to cause both areal flooding and flash flooding. According to local law enforcement, at 1530MST flash flooding at the intersection of McCartney Road and Weaver road resulted in a water rescue. The rescue was approximately 5 miles northeast of Casa Grande. At the time of the water rescue, the flood waters were receding. No injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Water and mud flowed over Highway 395 4 miles S of Haiwee and also near the Coso Junction Rest Area.
Vehicles were stuck on Highway 190 near the Mesquite Sand Dunes with water half way up the tires.
Park rangers at Zion National Park reported significant rises on the North Fork of the Virgin River, particularly through the Narrows. Hikers were temporarily stranded until the waters receded.
Water flooded the entire parking lot of the Amargosa Opera House and also entered the building.
Goffs Road was flooded between I-40 and Goffs, including two vehicles stuck on the off ramp from I-40.
Boriana Mine Road was washed out at McKenzie Wash.
Morning Star Mine Road was washed out.
A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported 6 inches of water at the intersection of Buena Vista Road and Buenos Aires Road.
Highway 247 was flooded near the I-15 interchange, and the intersection of Birch Road and Jasper Road in Lenwood was flooded.
A spotter in the Six Mile Canyon/Samuel Clemens area reported 1.15 of rainfall in less than 30 minutes. Water was flowing into homes with property damage.
Three inches of water and rocks flowed over Pole Line Road.
Antares Road was closed due to flooding.

The Douglas County Sheriff's Office reported that various places along Foothill Blvd.  experienced flash flooding, which made roads impassable. A spotter in the flash flood area noted 1.65 of rainfall in 45 minutes.
CHP reported one foot of water flowing over Highway 395.
Zion National Park rangers reported flash flooding along Clear Creek.
Rocks and mud washed onto Highways 58 and 395 at Kramer Junction.

The Lyon County Sheriff's office reported a car stuck in water flowing over V and T Way from a dry wash. The car had to be pulled out by heavy machinery. Pictures of the incident indicate that the water was approximately 18 inches deep at the time of the rescue.
Roads in Valley of Fire State Park were closed due to flooding.  The co-op observer reported 0.95 inch of rain in 15 minutes.
Water and rocks flowed over several roads, and at least seven swift water rescues occurred. Up to 1.13 inches of rain fell in one hour.
Water, debris, and boulders were over Highway 95 just north of I-40.
Titus Canyon Road was closed due to flooding and debris.
Scotty's Castle Road was closed due to flood waters washing four feet of debris over the road.
Temple Bar Road was washed out and impassable.
A foot of water flowed over U.S. 170 between mile markers 15 and 18. NMDOT had to clean mud, rocks, and debris off the roadway.

Flash flood wave moved down Yeso Rito arroyo in less than 30 minutes, resulting in significant damage at Ghost Ranch. At least three older structures and a ropes course were completely destroyed. One newer studio structure was seriously damaged. Trees were snapped in half and mud filled several other structures. Damage has been estimated between 500,000 and 1 million dollars. No injuries were reported.
Flash flooding was reported along Johnson Wash.

Very heavy rainfall caused water to overflow washes and overwhelm drainage infrastructure in the Johnson Lane area. Water damage to 141 properties, including major damage to 4 homes and minor damage to 7 homes, was reported by Douglas County Emergency Management officials. Damages are estimated and may include some costs from flooding on July 9 (total damage 2.2M between the two days).

Significant flooding with estimated 6 inches of flowing water at the corner of Cerrillos and Richards. Gravel washed across the road at the corner of West Alameda and Siler. Landscaping material washed out.
Humboldt County Sheriff reported water and debris over route 789. Damages are estimated.
Photographic evidence shows a vehicle stuck in flood waters on Prospect St. The occupant abandoned the vehicle and was rescued by fire department officials.
Fire marshal reported a tremendous sudden burst of torrential rainfall. A fast flowing mudslide surged over highway 38 between mile markers 8 and 9. A video of the event was posted to FB.
Highway 52 near Winston was closed due to flooding at the low water crossings.
Large flows were reported along the East Fork of the Virgin River, with the gauge near Springdale measuring flow rates as high as 1140 cfs.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flooding in Ryndon. Some houses were flooded and some roads were impassable. Damages are estimated.

A large line of thunderstorms moved through the Wasatch Front overnight on July 8, into the early morning hours of July 9, with the northern Wasatch Front getting hit the hardest by heavy rainfall. Flash flooding along roadways was reported in several locations, including along Interstate 15 and on Parrish Lane in Centerville, where water was up to four feet deep. One house in Woods Cross received significant flood damage, with all the possessions in the basement declared a total loss.

Multiple videos from Reno news media (on Facebook) showed fast-flowing water over Stephanie Way and over low-water crossings at East Valley Road and Nye Dr. (near Johnson Lane). Douglas County sheriff's deputies noted several road closures in the area. Around 21 properties experienced damage from the flash flooding. Damages are approximate and based on the dividing of Douglas County Emergency Management's damage estimates for both July 8 and 9.

Debris washed over Highway 190 in Stovepipe Wells, mud and debris were over Highway 190 near the Panamint Springs Resort, severe flooding closed Panamint Valley Road, and mud and rocks were over Panamint Springs Road up to Panamint Pass.
Water from Poverty Creek rapidly rising and crossing Highway 52 with a depth of 2 to 3 feet.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 264 between mile markers 12 and 15.

Reports from the Nevada Department of Transportation indicated water and debris over highway 447 south of Empire. The flooding caused significant erosion of road shoulders which required closure of the road for safety and repairs.
Water crossing highway 52 to a depth of 2.5 feet. Also pea sized hail.
Stirrup Road was closed east of Deming due to water flowing over the road.
Highway 92 had wash outs from mile marker 0 to mile marker 11.
Damage to roads and guard rails along canyons west of Interstate 25, particularly within Nogal Canyon.
A significant wash out with debris near Orchard Campground west of Bonito Lake. A couple places along highway 107 were impassable due to flowing water and debris. Marthas Canyon was the hardest hit.
Heavy rain in Nogales, Sonora caused strong flows in Nogales Wash. The Doe Street Bridge in Nogales was closed for a time as the Nogales Wash over topped its banks.
A truck was found crushed by a large boulder at the base of a 30-ft deep arroyo in Superman Canyon. The body of the man operating the vehicle was discovered 3 miles downstream at White Cliff.

Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused significant flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park. The Scenic Drive was closed due to water and debris impacting the road in multiple locations, particularly at the Grand Wash and near the Slick Rock Divide. Major flooding occurred in Capitol Gorge, and caused significant damage to the dirt road to Capitol Gorge, such that the road to this popular hiking area was closed for more than two months after the flood. Very heavy flows were also reported along Sulphur Creek and Pleasant Creek, as well as all associated washes, with water a foot deep in Sulphur Creek.
A pilot reported seeing flash flooding form the air just upstream from Upper Antelope Canyon. The pilot also reported seeing lots of water running in side canyons.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm flooded and closed the Williamson Avenue underpass.

A foot of water covered the intersection of Highway 180 and Highway 191 just east of St Johns. Highway 180 was closed about 8 miles south of St Johns (mile marker 375) with two feet of water over the road.

Thunderstorms developed across portions of La Paz county during the early afternoon hours, affecting the community of Bouse as well as Highway 72 between Bouse and Vicksburg. The storms produced intense rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of 2 inches. The heavy rain produced flash flooding across portions of Highway 72; at 1612MST local Fire Department and Rescue units reported that one foot of water covered Highway 72 between mileposts 26 and 30. As a result, the road was impassable and the Department of Transportation closed the highway. Fortunately, no accidents or injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Apache Road was closed due to flooding of the McKenzie Wash.
A swift water rescue occurred on Highway 95 five miles south of the CA/NV state line. The highway was closed from I-40 to the state line.
The CHP reported a hard closure of roadways near the intersection of Jackson St. and 66th Ave. due to roadway flooding.
Rocks and mud washed onto Davis Dam Road.
At least six inches of water flowed through the intersection of Casino Drive and Highway 163, and the intersection of Thomas Edison and Bruce Woodbury was closed due to flooding.
River Road was underwater with several cars stuck. Two underpasses in Needles also flooded.

During the late morning hours on August 18th, scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Riverside county and they affected the area around the community of Desert Center. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour. The heavy rain produced flash flooding around Desert Center during the early afternoon hours. According to a trained weather spotter, at 1135PST, water was reported to be flowing down both highway 177 and Kaiser Roads about 5 miles northeast of Desert Center. At least 3 inches of water was flowing down the roads. No accidents or injuries were reported due to the swiftly flowing water.
Three feet of water flowed over Highway 62.
Highways 93 and 168 were impassable due to flooding.
The CHP reported a vehicle almost submerged in water on one of the on-ramps at the intersection of Highway 163 and Interstate 8 near mission valley.
Rocks and debris washed onto Highway 93 at mile marker 86 near Caliente Summit.
Highway 62 was flooded near mile marker 119.
Heavy rain caused significant flooding in Hildale, with flood waters damaging both a few roads and a few homes across the area.
Flooding was reported near state road 14 near Jawbone Canyon road.
Debris and water was reported as moving across the intersection of Garlock road and Redrock Randsburg road.
Hackberry Road was closed due to flooding.
Antares Road was closed due to four feet of water.
Three main roads in Colorado City were closed due to flooding.
Water and debris covered Highway 95.
Flash flooding washed debris over at least two intersections in Kingman.
Flash flooding closed Alamo Road and Carmen Lane.

Park rangers reported flash flooding in Zion National Park, particularly in the Pine Creek drainage. The Virgin River had significant rises from Zion National Park down to St. George, with the river gauge at St. George rising from near 30 cfs up to 2310 cfs. Flooding was also reported in several other locations across the county, including Washington City, Bloomington, and St. George, with at least a dozen different roads in these areas receiving some level of flooding throughout the event.

Thunderstorms developed across the northwest portions of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the afternoon hours on July 18th; due to an infusion of tropical moisture from hurricane Dolores the stronger storms produced very intense rainfall with peak rain rates above 2 inches per hour. The heavy rain led to both urban and flash flooding in the area around Circle City. At about 1700MST, the public reported that 3 to 6 inches of rain was flowing over the roads from heavy rain, about 6 miles southwest of Circle City. Cars were unable to pass due to the swiftly flowing water. Initially, at 1701MST, an Urban and Small Stream Flood Advisory was issued for the area and this was upgraded to a Flash Flood Warning at 1756MST.
Debris flow from over one inch of rain in less than a hour over the Grand Fire burn scar area produced mud blocking the road between Frazier Park and Lake of the Woods.

Scattered strong thunderstorms developed across northwest Maricopa county during the afternoon hours on July 18th. Due to a significant infusion of tropical moisture from hurricane Dolores, the storms produced torrential rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 3 inches per hour; one of the communities that was especially hard hit by the heavy rain was Wickenburg. Heavy rain in the Wickenburg area began around 1630MST and continued through the evening hours; many flood control district rain gages in the area reported storm total rainfall amounts ranging from 3 inches to nearly 4.5 inches. The excessive rainfall led to episodes of flash flooding; according to the Department of Highways, at 1805MST U.S. Highway 60 was closed at milepost 111 due to the fact that the road was flooded and impassable. Earlier, at 1742MST a trained spotter 1 mile southeast of Wickenburg reported 2 inches of rain measured in 30 minutes which flooded area roadways. Additionally, another spotter 2 miles southwest of Wickenburg reported Cemetary Wash running with very heavy rapids and water was reported to be 2 inches deep across the front yard of some homes. At 1746MST heavy rain caused the Casandro Wash to rise to 6.7 feet which is above flood stage. Fortunately, no injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Flash flooding closed two roads in southern Yavapai County just north of Wickenburg.

Five roads were closed in Chino Valley because of flash flooding. A vehicle was stranded at Road 5 North and Reed Road. The fire department was able to rescue the occupants and a tow truck pulled the vehicle out.
Fifteen residents were rescued from homes in Verde Lakes Estates. Seven homes had significant flood damage. The flooding came form a tributary of West Clear Creek.
CHP reported Chihuahua Valley Rd. closed due to flooding.
CHP reported vehicles stranded in water at the intersection of Interstate 5 and Genesee on-ramp.
The CHP reported multiple vehicles stalled in flooded waters on the off-ramp from Fletcher Parkway to Interstate 8. Multiple vehicles were also submerged in flood waters along Alvarado Road.

CHP reported significant urban flooding in the Moreno Valley area due to a heavy line of thunderstorms. The most significant flooding was reported at the intersection of Interstate 215 and Van Buren Blvd, where 8 cars were stuck in high waters. In Reche Canyon residents were unable to leave their homes due to flooded roadways. Portions of State Highway 60 were also impassable.

Training thunderstorms produce heavy rainfall over Ramona with 0.58 in falling between 1401 and 1419 PST.  The CHP reported significant flooding and road closures along 11th St. in Ramona, that the road was completely washed out at the intersection of State Route 78 and Ramona View Dr., and water washing fences and debris over Vista Ramona Rd. A trained spotter reported water 3 ft deep at Ramona Rd. and Lawrence St. with some residents unable to evacuate their homes.

CHP reported significant flooding along State Route 91. Vehicles were reported to be stuck in flood waters at the intersections of State Route 91 and Van Buren Blvd., and State Route 91 and Adams St. Mud covered all lanes at the the Central Ave. intersection.

Thunderstorms developed across portions of Joshua Tree National Park during the afternoon hours on July 19th. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, the storms generated torrential rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour. The intense rainfall led to flash flooding across the western portion of the park. At about 1500PST, local law enforcement reported flash flooding of Park Boulevard, Route 12, near and just southeast of the western entrance to Joshua Tree National Park. In addition, the flooding washed debris onto portions of Park Boulevard. No injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.

CHP reported the roadway getting washed away at Lone Pine Canyon Rd. near East Canyon Dr. around 0345 PST. A spotter also reported significant flow through the normally dry Sheep Creek Wash, with lots of tree trunks going by.
Swift water rescues occurred at Sunfair Road and one mile east of White Feather Road. Boulders were on Highway 62 from Mile Square Road to Mt. Lassen Lane.

Aided by lingering tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, intense thunderstorms with torrential rain developed near Desert Center during the afternoon hours on July 19th. Based on radar estimates, over 6 inches of rain fell over several hours along and just to the south of Interstate 10, just to the west of Desert Center. According to a trained weather spotter about 4 miles west of Desert Center, the eastbound lanes of Interstate 10 collapsed where they crossed a heavily flowing wash, and one vehicle drove into the hole in the collapsed bridge. The driver became trapped by crushed asphalt and needed to be rescued. The injured driver was extracted from his truck and taken to a local hospital. According to local law enforcement, Interstate 10 was closed in both directions; water was flowing over the highway and the on and off ramps were flooded. Traffic was backed up for miles and needed to be re-routed. Within a short distance of the collapsed bridge, water flowing through a wash and under the freeway severely eroded and compromised the integrity of a second bridge; the second bridge did not collapse however. Interstate 10 will be closed in both directions for quite some time, probably at least one week, as bridges on both sides of the freeway will need to be re-built. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for the area from 1621PST through 1915PST.
CHP reported a vehicle stuck in flood waters on the interchange between State Routes 71 and 91.
Spotter reported 1 to 2 feet of water across US-395 near Shadow Mountain Road.
Strong thunderstorms developed near the burn scar of the Powerhouse Fire. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms generated significant mud and debris flows across Lake Hughes Road.
Kern County EOC reported severe flooding around Golden Hill, Tehachapi on route 202 and CHP reported closure of highway 58 due to flooding.

Scattered thunderstorms continued to develop across portions of eastern Imperial county during the evening hours on July 19th. Due to an infusion of tropical moisture from former hurricane Dolores, some of the storms produced torrential rainfall which led to localized flash flooding. Peak rain rates were well in excess of 3 inches per hour. At 1843PST, the California Highway Patrol reported that a portion of highway 78 to the southwest of Cibola was washed out due to flash flooding and as a result the highway was closed.
Strong thunderstorms developed across the Antelope Valley. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms resulted in over two feet of water across Pearblossom Highway in the community of Palmdale.
Nipton Road was washed out.
Two swift water rescues were conducted along the Lytle Creek Wash.

Strong thunderstorms developed across the Antelope Valley. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms resulted in significant flooding at the intersection of Highway 138 and 165th Street East. The flooding stranded several cars at the intersection.

California Highway Patrol reported flooding and buckling of the roadway along Mil Potrero Highway and Cerro Noroeste Road at 20:44 PDT. They also reported vechiles getting stuck along Lockwood Valley Road and Frazier Mountain Road at 21:18 PDT. However, the main event continued to be the mudslide occurring near the town of Frazier Park.
A boat launch ramp was washed out.
California Highway Patrol reported mud flowing onto the intersection of Rancho Road and Sebastian Road at 04:17 PDT.
California Highway Patrol initially reported one foot of water on Wheeler Ridge Road just north of David road at 20:12 PDT. At 05:00 a follow up report was received of flooding at the intersection.
California Highway Patrol reported mud flowing onto the intersection of Rancho Road and Sebastian Road at 04:17 PDT.
Mud and debris washed onto Stockton Hill Road from mile marker 16 to 26.

Yreka Dispatch reported at 20/1955 PST that homes were flooded in Grenada and that the Shepherd Of God Assisted Living Center was being evacuated due to water entering the building.  CHP reported standing water and debris near the I-5 southbound on-ramp at 20/1919 PST along with lots of debris on the southbound side of Old Highway 99.  At 20/1925 PST, they reported that the on-ramp was blocked by flooding.  At 20/1932 PST debris was reported across both lanes of county road A12. A spotter 4W of Grenada reported 1.50 inches of rain in less than 90 minutes ending at 20/1924 PST.  The same spotter reported 0.75 inch hail at 20/1810 PST.

Several foot bridges were washed away within Frijoles Canyon as the creek overflowed it's banks. Water did not make it into the parking lot at the visitor center. Rain gage reports averaged between 1 and 2 inches within the canyon.
Highway 168 was closed at Westgard Pass due to flooding and lots of debris in the road.

The Siskiyou County Sheriff's Department reported Flash Flooding in the Mud Creek Basin northeast of McCloud at 21/2020 PST.  They also reported Flash Flooding in the city of McCloud due to runoff from heavy rainfall.

Numerous pictures showed the aftermath of a flash flood in the canyon/alluvial fan west of the small community of Marietta. Minor damage was noted to area roads (unpaved) and a wire mesh fence. The time of the flood was estimated from radar.
Very heavy rain caused Fish Creek to overflow its bank and flow across state road 379. The water was at least 6 inches  deep. Damages are estimated.
Fire Official reported that the Sacramento River was over its banks at the Timberon Lodge. Heavy rain was still occurring and streets were flooding in Timberon.
Heavy rain caused water and debris to flow over State Route 306 between Interstate 80 and the river near Beowawe in 4 different places. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain caused water to flow over a road about 8 miles south of Charleston making it impassable. Damages are estimated.
Water was crossing Riata Road west of U.S. 54. Rain had fallen several hours earlier up near La Luz and flowed down toward Alamogordo.
Heavy rain caused the San Luis Wash to flow across Route 232 near the village of San Luis to a depth of 1 to 2 feet.

A swift water rescue of two adults occurred after their vehicle was swept away in Rodeo Wash. The vehicle eventually stopped when it became pinned under the Rodeo Wash Bridge near Interstate 19. Both occupants escaped the vehicle and were able to crawl partially up the side of the wash where they were rescued. They were not injured.
Highway 18 flooded, with portions of roadway washing away. Several vehicles were stuck in mud.
Water one foot deep flowed over Reche Road at Sunny Vista.
Roads were flooded with water and debris.

A woman and her dog became trapped in their truck when she attempted to drive through a flooded wash crossing Cascabel Road. The woman did not realize that water had washed the road away. When she attempted to cross the wash, the vehicle dropped 3 feet into the water before it was pushed downstream about 200 yards. Cascabel fire personnel and civilians were able to rescue both the woman and her dog. The woman was transported to a nearby hospital and treated for severe hypothermia.
Strong thunderstorms producing flash flooding in the community of Lake Los Angeles. At the intersection of 170th Street East and Avenue P8, over eight inches of water flooded the intersection.

Heavy rains caused several streets to flood with between 2 to 4 feet of water in downtown Grants.  The street flooding included First and Second streets from Washington to Roosevelt as well as Fifth and Santa Fe streets. It caused one vehicle to stall due to the water height.  No business or homes were reported flooded as well as no reported injuries.
Flood waters two to three feet deep flowed over Interstate 15, stopping traffic in both directions. The side of the roadway washed away.

Heavy rain of 2 inches in an hour caused flash flooding in San Manuel, which caused severe road damage. Public works estimated hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage to Avenues A, B, G, and Webb Drive.
A car was stalled in floodwaters along Highway 127 15 miles NNW of Baker.
Highway 62 flooded in several locations between Rice Ave. and Joshua Tree.

CHP reported boulders and a large amount of sand in roadway along Highway 74 from heavy rain. A nearby spotter reported 6 inches of water flowing across the road at the Highway 74 and Marshall Avenue cross-section in Valle Vista.

Strong thunderstorms formed over north central Los Angeles county, north of the community of Acton. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms generated numerous mud/debris flows across Highway 14 between Red Rover Mine Road and Escondido Canyon Road.
A spotter reported 4 to 6 inches of water flowing across Old Highway 80 in Guatay.
Strong thunderstorms developed in the mountains of Ventura county. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms generated flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 33 and Corral Canyon Road.

Strong thunderstorms developed near Pyramid Lake in Los Angeles county. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms generated flash flooding along Interstate 5 near Vista del Lago Road. Several vehicles were stranded in the flood waters.

A spotter reported torrential rains, marble sized hail, 2 of standing water in back yard, and 4-6 of water flowing in the road. Another spotter reported 1.00-1.25 of rain in 30 minutes and street flooding in Calimesa.
One foot of water flowed over Highway 95 at mile marker 50, partially washing out the road. Three feet of water also flowed over W. Monumental Pass Rd.
Strong thunderstorms developed near the community of Llano. Heavy rain from these thunderstorms produced flash flooding along the intersection of Highway 138 and 165th Street East.
Multiple homes were flooded in the 74000 block of Diamond Bar Road.

One person was stuck in vehicle that was stuck in flood waters near the railroad tracks at San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Road. The car was stuck in mud associated with the flash flooding.
Six inches of water flowed over Jamaica Blvd. S and Lake Havasu Ave.
CHP reported water and debris across the roadway at the intersection of Highway 138 and Evergreen Road. A spotter also reported 1/4 to 3/8 inch hail ongoing with heavy rainfall.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Riverside county during the evening hours on July 30th, and the stronger storms produced very heavy rainfall which affected the area around Desert Center. Peak rainfall rates approached 2 inches per hour, and this led to some flooding and flash flooding of washes and roads around Desert Center. Significant amounts of rain fell on Interstate 10 east of Desert Center, and local law enforcement reported flooding over the roads near State Route 177 and Oasis Road at mile marker 2.40. This was approximately 2 miles northeast of the town of Desert Center. No accidents or injuries were reported due to the flash flooding. Law enforcement reported the flash flooding at about 2000PST.
Flash flooding damaged Kelbaker Road in Kelso.
The Secret Pass Wash flooded Oatman Road and nearby secondary roads. One road partially washed out.

Strong thunderstorms developed near the community of Llano. Heavy rain from these thunderstorms generated flash flooding and mud flows. California Highway Patrol reported 6 to 8 inches of mud across sections of Highway 138.

Two feet of mud flowed through the pavilion area of Camp Stimpson, forcing 150 campers to leave. Trees and debris washed onto Highway 156 in Lee Canyon, closing the road. An automated gage nearby measured 2.15 inches of rain, including 1.99 inches in one hour.

Local media reported that 100 feet of railroad track for the Rail Runner between Albuquerque and Sante Fe was washed out.  The tracks were located on north side of the bridge at the Arroyo Maria Chavez.  Rail Runner service was suspended for the rest of the weekend.

Photos showed water rushing over Red Rock Road near Madrid and making it impassable.  The report indicated that the depth of the water over the road peaked at 3 feet.  It took about an hour for the water to subside enough before safely crossing.

Public weather station reported 3.35 inches of rainfall in 1 hour near Las Campanas. Video showed flash flood waters flowing quickly over East Sunrise Road northwest of Santa Fe, making it impassable. The water depth was reported to be between 1 and 1.5 feet.

Road closures occurred due to flash flooding in the northwest Tucson metro, including Overton Rd at the Canada del Oro Wash, Thornydale Rd at Freer Drive and Oasis Drive, and Linda Vista between Thornydale Rd and Camino de Oeste.
Water, mud, and rocks covered Highway 168 in The Narrows section.
Highway 264 was washed out in several places. The Dyer co-op observer measured 3.07 inches of rain between 4 PM and 9 PM, which set a 24-hour rainfall record for the station.

State police had to pull 3 vehicles out of mud on Highway 91 created by the heavy rains. Reilly Road between Highway 91 and Blue Hole was later closed as it was covered by flash flood water. These waters also went into the nearby senior center.
The Gila County Sheriffs Office reported that a flash flood washed out a Forest Service road near SR 288. A rescue operation was preformed after a SUV became stuck.
The Nazlini Wash flooded low water crossings.
Spotter reported between 1 to 2 feet of flash flood waters over the Puerta de Luna Road southeast of Santa Rosa.

Heavy rain moved across Lea County and produced flash flooding in Hobbs.  Local law enforcement reported that Highway 18 was flooded and smaller streets throughout Hobbs were flooded.  At least two cars were reported to be stranded.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produce heavy rain and a flash flood in de Chelly Wash. There was one fatality when a truck overturned in the flooded wash around 700 PM MDT.
Six inches of rapidly flowing water over U.S. Highway 550 at mile maker 117. Nearby arroyo was raging with flash flood waters out of its banks.
U.S. Highway 60 closed due to high water at mile marker 124.
A large flash flood was reported in the Wahweap drainage, north of Big Water.

Heavy rain over northern Davis County caused widespread street and parking lot flooding, particularly in Farmington and Layton. In addition, several homes in Fruit Heights experienced basement flooding.
Highway 62 was covered in mud.
Small rocks washed over the intersection of Kiowa and Palo Verde.
Water flowed down several streets in Kingman.
The Eureka County Sheriff reported flash flooding on county route 101 and Highway 50 north and west of Eureka. Damages are estimated.
Multiple reports were received of flooding on Route 89 near the Crescent Dunes solar energy plant. Damages are estimated.
Highway 264 was flooded between mile markers 13 and 17.
Water flowing across Linda Vista Blvd west of Hartman Lane caused at least 1 vehicle to become disabled.
Portions of Highway 165 were washed out between mile markers 11 and 13.
Reports and pictures from social media showed flash flooding in and around Austin. Time  estimated based off radar. Damages are estimated.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Highway 93 due to flooding.
Diamond Creek Road was flooded with fast moving water. A nearby stream gage rose to 5.3 feet.
Small rocks washed onto the road near Echo Canyon State Park.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain on top of ground saturated from storms earlier in the day. Runoff caused 3 vehicles to become stranded due to high water near Sunrise and Pontatoc Roads.

Heavy rain south of Winslow caused flash flooding. A car got stuck in the flood waters seven miles south of Winslow on SR 99. Flash flooding also restricted SR 99 to just one lane about 1 mile south of Winslow.
Nearly two inches of heavy rain fell in a short time period and caused significant flooding of streets and small washes in northwest sections of Sierra Vista.

Very heavy rain fell over the Marble Canyon area from near Navajo Bridge to near Jacob Lake. Up to five feet of was was flowing over Highway 89 in places. Significant mud, debris, and truck sized boulders washed onto the roads.  Highway 89 was closed for 24 miles while road crews could clean debris off the road. Some of the boulders had to be blasted before they could be moved because they were so large. The flash flood even changed Soap Creek Rapid on the Colorado River in Marble Canyon (upstream from the Grand Canyon) making it more difficult for river runners to navigate the rapid.
Antares Road was closed due to flooding.
A maintenance worker at the Lake Powell Tribal Park reported significant flooding in Antelope Canyon. Time estimated using radar data.

Rainfall amounts of 2 to over 3 inches were reported around Alamogordo with multiple road closures put into place. Water was across several roads 6 to 8 inches deep. Winds of up to 50 mph also occurred with the storm.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed U.S. highway 54 at mile markers 124 and 170 due to heavy rain and difficult driving conditions.  This closure lasted 45 minutes and prevented traffic to drive between Corona and Carrizozo.

Persistent showers and thunderstorms caused to up to 2 inches of rain in the Redington Pass area, including the Tanque Verde and Agua Caliente Washes. Redington Pass Road became flooded and impassible.
Flash flooding washed out the majority of the dirt roads in the Dilkon, Tees Toh, Indian Wells, to White Cone area.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flash flooding along Highway 160 between MP 361 and MP 379. The flooding stopped traffic.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Indian Route 59 at MP 22 and MP 33.
Water flooded the road near the junction of Highway 160 and State Route 98.

Nevada Department of Wildlife Spring Creek rearing station reported a loss of 1500 head of fish at the hatchery from flash flooding runoff of Snake Creek due to heavy rain. Recorded rain measurement of 1.35 inches in 2 hours from a nearby observer. Nearby roads were also flooded.
Several inches of water, mud, and debris flowed through yards and a horse farm.
Deep rushing water left debris along Highway 95 from mile marker 125 to 127.
DW Ranch Road was closed north of I-40 due to water and boulders flooding the roadway.
Several streets were covered with water, mud, and debris. At least one car stalled in the water. Water leaked through the roof of the Golden Nugget Casino onto the table games area.

Heavy rains caused a mud slide along a mile stretch of roadway that leads to the top of the Capulin National Monument.  The debris included mud and boulders that were up to 55 pounds in weight.  The road remained closed into the afternoon on the 14th as staff attempted to clear the debris.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 322 between mile markers 4 and 9.

A thunderstorm dropped very heavy rainfall near Woodland Hills and, combined with saturated soil from large amounts of rain the previous day, produced a large mudslide across the area. The mud damaged the basement of one home and also invaded five other properties, with extensive mud clean-up necessary on private driveways and along Skylake Drive. A total of 14 homes were evacuated as a precaution immediately following the mudslide.
The river gauge on the Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City jumped from near zero to 6,900 CFS in under 30 minutes. NWS personnel confirmed that the water was encouraging homes in the community of Moenkopi.
The intersection of Gubler and Heyer was flooded with water, rocks, and debris.
Highway 62 was flooded in three places with vehicles stuck.

Thunderstorms over Nogales produced 1 to 2 inches of rain, which resulted in heavy flows in Nogales wash. The Doe Street Bridge was closed for a time after flood waters breached the wash banks and over-topped the roadway.

Park rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding at multiple locations in the park. Flooding first occurred along Sulphur Creek, and then a second thunderstorm initiated flash flooding along Grand Wash, with flood waters reaching Highway 24.
SR-80 was closed at Apache Powder Road due to flash flooding. A few pieces of asphalt broke off into the flow as water over-topped the roadway.
Street flooding of 1-2 feet deep occurred near Park Ave and Pennsylvania St. Some minor flooding of businesses occurred near 12th Ave. and Lincoln St.
Snyder Rd. between Kolb and Sabino Canyon Road was closed for a time due to the flash flooding of Ventana Canyon Wash.
Water was flowing over State Route 188 near Jakes Corner.

Thunderstorms developed across portions of Joshua Tree National Park during the early afternoon hours on August 26th, and some of the stronger ones produced intense rainfall that quickly led to flash flooding across the northern portions of the park. According to local law enforcement, at 1400PST a flash flood occurred about one mile south of the north entrance to the park. The flash flood caused a debris flow across the road which led to the closure of the road. Shortly thereafter park rangers indicated that workers were quickly working to clear the debris. A Flash Flood Warning was in effect before the flash flooding occurred. Fortunately, there were no injuries reported due to the debris flow.

Thunderstorms developed across portions of Joshua Tree National Park during the early afternoon hours on August 26th, and some of the stronger ones produced very intense rainfall which quickly led to flash flooding across the northern portion of the park. According to local law enforcement, flash flooding was reported at 1325PST in the north central portion of the park, around the popular Queen Valley Mountain bike area near the Sheep Pass group camp along highway 12. This area is east of Ryan Mountain. A Flash Flood Warning had been issued shortly before the flash flooding was reported. Fortunately no injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Water was rushing across Echo Dam Road.
Baseline Road was closed between Utah Trail and Wilshire Avenue, and another road 4 miles N of Twentynine Palms was also closed. A swift water rescue took place at Highway 62 and Godwin Road.
Highway 317 was flooded near the train bridge just south of Highway 93.
Park rangers reported flash flooding in the Pine Creek slot canyon, with extreme used to described the flooding.

The Blanco Arroyo overflowed its banks and, combined with heavy rain across the area, led to significant flash flooding. Firefighters rescued a few individuals from the roofs of their homes, otherwise no major injuries or fatalities were reported.  Several homes were reportedly shifted off their foundation and a propane tank at one of those homes was swept away in the flood waters.  Multiple classrooms were damaged at three area schools, causing all schools to be closed on the 27th and one school, Lydia Rippey Elementary, to be closed on the 28th.  The Aztec Municipal Golf Course at Hidden Valley was closed until further notice due to damages incurred from the flooding.  A large rock slide closed Navajo Road 36 at mile marker 28, with other smaller road closures reported around Aztec.  Measured rainfall in the area ranges from an inch to a little over an inch and a half.

Very heavy rain caused a massive flash flood along Wahweap Creek. The flood wave was caught on video and it carried full size dead trees left over from previous smaller floods, along with boulders the size of cars.

Heavy rainfall in a catch basin north of Arches National Park on the afternoon of August 30th resulted in a flash flood which reached a section of Arches National Park later that evening and trapped many campers in the Delicate Arch Road area.  Flash flood waters were still flowing 3.5 feet deep and 50 feet wide as of noon the next day, August 31st and persisted through much of the afternoon.
Water was flowing over Indian Route 2 north of Winslow and State Route 99 at Mile Post 54 west of Winslow.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused water to flow over roads in the Christopher Creek Community for over two hours.

Strong thunderstorms moved across the central portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the evening hours on August 31st and in addition to strong gusty winds, some of the storms produced intense rainfall with peak rain rates well in excess of 1 inch per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of urban flooding and flash flooding; one location that was hit hardest by flash flooding was downtown Phoenix. According to a local broadcast media report, at 2020MST intense rainfall flooded the deck park tunnel in downtown Phoenix, causing numerous drivers to become stranded in the tunnel. Shortly thereafter another driver became stranded due to flooding at the intersection of 48th Street and Van Buren Avenue. In addition to the flash flooding there was urban street flooding in the area. At 2004MST the public reported that water was 4 inches deep on Interstate 10 at 7th Street. A bit later, at  2031MST a public report indicated curb-to-curb street flooding at the intersection of 22nd Street and Osborn Road 4 miles north of Sky Harbor International Airport. Flash Flood Warnings were issued for the area beginning at 1945MST and continuing through 2315MST. Fortunately there were no reports of injuries due to the flooding.

Significant flash flooding was reported in Capitol Reef National Park, with multiple flood waves reported along Sulphur Creek. Flash flooding also occurred in both Spring Canyon and Chimney Rock Canyon. The Spring Canyon flooding was generally between 6 inches and two feet deep, though it reached as high as 5 feet deep through the narrow section. Water flowing through Chimney Rock Canyon was reported to be one foot deep.
The Chinle Police Department reported that Indian Route 27 was impassable due to flash flooding south of Chinle.
Heavy rain caused extreme flows in Davidson Wash, which was flowing 300 ft across.  The wash flowed across Empire View Road, stranding residents on either side of it.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms produce flash flooding over the Old Jerome Highway closing the road.
CHP reported mud and rocks on Highway 78 near Yaqui Pass, closing Highway 78. CHP also reported flash flooding Highway S2 from mile marker 36 to mile marker 44, blocking the southbound lanes.
CHP reported a rock/mudslide blocking the roadway at Highway S-22 near San Felipe Road.

A flash flood at Mill Creek crossing...40 feet wide and 8 to 12 inches deep. The head of the flash flood was 3 to 4 feet deep. From Victor Valley news group: flood waters overtook a couple hiking. An off-duty sheriff's deputy heard the couple calling for help and was able to save the young woman, but the man was swept away. The body of the victim, a Rancho Cucamonga man in his 20s, was found shortly after 1800 PST.
Rock and debris washed all over Highway 62.

Multiple swift water rescues along Bear Valley Road. Water flowed fast down the road with some areas of water around 5 feet deep. A spotter reported water 4-6 deep at the intersection of Bear Valley Road and Apple Valley Road.

Scattered thunderstorms affected community of Yuma as well as surrounding communities such as Somerton during the late afternoon and evening hours on September 8th. Due to elevated moisture values, partially a result of tropical moisture from Hurricane Linda starting to move into southern Arizona, the stronger storms produced very heavy rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of 2 inches per hour. A trained spotter 3 miles northeast of Somerton measured 4.6 inches of rain within 2 hours ending at 1900MST. The heavy rain led to flash flooding in the Yuma area and resulted in the issuance of a Flash Flood Warning at 1802MST. At 2000MST, local broadcast media reported that people were leaving flooded houses south of highway 95 between Joshua Street and Bingham Avenue. The flash flooding took place about 1 mile southeast of the town of Somerton. Fortunately there were no injuries reported due to the flooding.
Valley of the Falls Drive is washed out and the road was closed.
Heavy rains caused state road 462 to be closed by the New Mexico DOT between mile markers 0 and 2.
An NWS employee reported a flash flood on Highway 79 in Aguanga leaving 1 foot of mud on the roads. Crews were still cleaning up mud the following day.
A male and a female were in a flood control channel and had to be rescued by the Orange County Fire Department when they were caught off guard by the quickly rising water.
Strong thunderstorms developed over the mountains of Los Angeles county. Heavy rain from these thunderstorms generated mud and debris flows across sections of Lake Hughes Road.
Strong thunderstorms developed near the community of Llano. Heavy rain resulted in several flooded roads.
The junction of Highways 58 and 395 flooded.
The intersection of Hinkley Road and Highway 58 was flooded.

A thunderstorm producing heavy rain moved over Hildale, Utah in the early afternoon, producing flash flooding along Short Creek and other neighboring drainages. This water flooded Highway 59, and portions of the road were closed and gated off, as this is a somewhat common occurrence for the community. However, a second strong thunderstorm trained through the area, producing very significant flooding out of Maxwell and Jans Canyons.||This second flood swept across a group of 16 people who had been waiting for the initial flood waters to recede. When the second flood began, the group retreated to the two vans they had been traveling in, and the large flood swept the vans away and down the channel. Three of these people were rescued and survived, but the remaining 13 people were killed by the flood. Three of these 13 victims were women, while the remaining 10 were children under the age of 12.||Property damage was also extensive across the area, including damage to water lines, area roadways, power lines, bridges, and other infrastructure. In addition, multiple private homes had flood and mud damage, while several others had minor water damage. Multiple vehicles were also destroyed in the flood.

Extremely heavy rain in the mountains above Hildale, UT resulted in major flash flooding on Short Creek in and downstream of Colorado City, AZ, as well as in other washes on the Arizona Strip. Several streets in Colorado Cit were flooded and impassable, and bridges were damaged. One man died on the back roads of the Arizona Strip when flood waters swept away his car.

Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall brought flash flooding to Zion National Park, including along North Creek, but the most notable flood occurred in Keyhole Canyon. A group of seven people entered Keyhole Canyon in the early afternoon, planning to travel through the small but popular canyoneering route. Flooding in Keyhole Canyon occurred quickly; no one in the group was able to escape the canyon or get to higher ground, and the flood killed all seven individuals. The seven victims were between 51 and 59 years old.
A spotter reported the right lane of the Pacific Coast Highway flooded at the intersection with Main Street...road was nearly impassable.
Additional heavy rainfall over Hildale caused minor flash flooding across the area while search and rescue operations were still ongoing from the previous day's major flood.

An Orange County Emergency Manager reported a debris flow 2 feet deep over Silverado Canyon Road at Maple Springs Truck Trail. Further downstream, there was another debris flow at Silverado Canyon Road and Oak Lane, but the road was still passable.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River, with the gauge at Lees Ferry rising from near 100 cfs up to 2064 cfs.

Several businesses in the Midway District were flooded...with water up to knee deep. Several vehicles were flooded in an underground parking garage in Ocean Beach, including a brand new Lamborghini luxury car flooded halfway deep.
Heavy rain caused a debris flow from the Patch Springs burn scar, with debris covering State Route 199 at Johnson Pass.
Park rangers at Zion National Park reported flash flooding through the area, with the worst flooding near the Emerald Pools. Waterfalls and minor rockfalls were also reported across the park.

A woman in her vehicle was swept into flash flood waters when attempting to cross a wash on High Knoll Rd east of Sierra Vista. Rescuers found the car had been swept downstream, but were unable to locate the driver.
Heavy rain caused Florida Canyon to overflow its banks near the Santa Rita Mountains.

One to four inches of rain fell near and especially southwest of Safford causing canals and washes to overtop their banks and flow over roadways. Water was a foot deep on parts of Highway 191 south of Safford. A vehicle on Lebanon Rd. had to be towed out of mud and rushing water.

Elevated amounts of tropical moisture spread northward and into the west central Arizona deserts during the day on September 21st; the moisture was shed off of tropical depression 16-E located over the northern Gulf of California. The elevated moisture, instability and upper wind values allowed thunderstorms to develop across western La Paz county. The stronger storms produced locally heavy rain with peak rain rates greater than 1 inch per hour. The heavy rain led to localized flash flooding which affected motorists on Highway 95 running north of Quartzsite. According to the Department of Highways, at 1650MST Highway 95 about 2 miles north of Quartzsite was closed due to high water as a result of the flash flooding. Fortunately no injuries were reported. Although no Flash Flood Warnings were in effect, there was a Flood Advisory issued at 1600MST which ran through 1900MST.

Media reports indicated a man was swept away and died in fast moving water that filled the north diversion channel arroyo.  Eye witness reports noted the man was outside the arroyo before somehow ending up in it and being swept away.  Search and rescue attempts by the fire department found the body two hours later in the Rio Grande.  The only other information available at this time is that it was a male between the ages of 20 and 30 years old. The intense rainfall rates also washed lots of landscaping material, including rocks, mud, and fabric material, into streets across the metro area. A water mark near Carlisle and Comanche suggested the water was as high as 2 feet in the intersection. Road crews spent several hours cleaning up streets across the city.

Emergency manager reported widespread street flooding in Roswell.  Later reports and information showed road closures in the northeast portion of the city near the Anderson Museum of Contemporary Art, notably North Virginia Road and North Garden Road.  There were unconfirmed reports of swift water rescues in the area as well.  Rainfall reports from trained spotters and the CoCoRaHS network around the area showed up to 3.68 inches of rain fell, with many reports in excess of 2.5 inches.

Plentiful tropical moisture was in place across the greater Phoenix area on September 22nd; the moisture spread into Arizona ahead of tropical depression 16-E located to the southeast of Arizona. As a low pressure system moved east across the central deserts, scattered thunderstorms developed and they affected the community of Scottsdale. Due to the high moisture content in the atmosphere, the storms produced intense rainfall with rates well in excess of 1 inch per hour. The heavy rain led to both urban street flooding as well as isolated occurrences of flash flooding in the Scottsdale area. According to an article in the Arizona Republic, heavy rains during the evening hours quickly flooded washes in central Scottsdale, just west of Highway 101 near Cactus Road. One flooded wash turned into a river, flooding homes in the area near 84th Street and Cactus Road. Water flooded into the home of Sonny Friedman, filling the floor with several inches of water and causing significant damage. The damaged home had an area of nearly 5000 square feet.

The atmosphere across the greater Phoenix area was very moist and unstable on September 22nd, courtesy of tropical moisture that spread into the area ahead of tropical depression 16-E. An area of low pressure moved across central Arizona during the evening hours and as a result scattered thunderstorms developed which affected the eastern portions of the Phoenix area, including the community of Mesa. Due to the high levels of moisture in the atmosphere, some of the stronger storms produced intense rainfall with peak rain rates approaching 2 inches per hour. The intense rain led to episodes of both urban flooding and flash flooding. According to a trained weather spotter, the exit ramps on the Superstition Highway at Crimson Road became flooded by 1920MST. The flooding was caused by 1.4 inches of rain which fell in the hour ending at 1920MST. About 12 to 18 inches of rain covered the roadway in this area, approximately 4 miles southeast of Superstition Springs Mall. A Flash Flood Warning was issued at 1923MST and it remained in effect through 2115MST. No injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Flash flooding was reported in Lehi, with some flooded residential roadways. In addition, approximately six homes sustained flood damage, primarily to basements.

Heavy rain brought road, parking lot, and basement flooding to the Sugarhouse and Foothill areas of Salt Lake City. The flooding damaged multiple streets including Roxberry Road, Sherwood Drive, and 1300 South near 2500 East. There was also a significant amount of water on Foothill Drive, particularly near 2200 South. Approximately six homes also experienced basement flooding across the area.

Heavy rain brought road, parking lot, and basement flooding to the Sugarhouse and Foothill areas of Salt Lake City. The flooding damaged multiple streets including Roxberry Road, Sherwood Drive, and 1300 South near 2500 East. There was also a significant amount of water on Foothill Drive, particularly near 2200 South. Approximately six homes also experienced basement flooding across the area.
Rocks and mud covered Highway 168 just east of Death Valley Road.
Roads were closed in Pahrump between Leslie St. and Highway 372 due to water and rocks.
Water and debris flooded NV Hwy. 374.
Several rooms at the Furnace Creek Inn were flooded. Many roads were closed, including Daylight Pass Road, Badwater Road, Highway 190, and Scotty's Castle Road.

Three bridges were damaged from flood waters northeast of Grants. A dozen jersey barriers were washed 100 yards downstream at low water crossings along Lobo Canyon. The most significant damage occurred to the George Hannish Bridge. Bridges along county roads 19A and 19D were also impacted.
Flood damaged roads along low water crossings near Encinal and Bibo. Jersey barriers erected to protect from flood waters were washed away.
Large boulders washed onto Whitney Portal Road.

Flash flooding was reported in several locations, including Deer Creek and Calf Creek. The Dirty Devil gauge at Poison Springs rose from 23 cfs to 1176 cfs, and part of Hole-in-the-Rock Road was washed out.
Boxcar Cove Road, Crawdad Cove Road, and Callville Bay Road were damaged and closed due to flash flooding.
A foot of flowing water closed Valley of Fire Road.
Flash flooding was reported in Capitol Reef National Park, with one foot of water over the Capitol Gorge Road.
Seventeen buildings on Fort Irwin were flooded, several sinkholes developed, there was widespread road damage, and there was also damage to underground water and fiber optic systems.
Up to 3.5 feet of water flowed over Hidden Valley Road at the California Wash.
National Trails Highway was washed out and there was a lot of mud over the road.
Multiple vehicles were stuck on Highway 95 between mile markers 47 and 49, with the road closed in both directions.
Five Mile Road was impassable. Scrapers were needed to remove the debris.

Several roads were flooded up to a foot deep, some with mud and large rocks. One swift water rescue was performed. 1274 customers lost power, and NHP responded to 76 vehicle crashes. Rain totals were as high as 2.80 inches.
A vehicle stalled in water near Highway 95 and Goffs Road.
Dirt and rocks were piled up like a ramp on the Goffs Road off ramp from Interstate 40.
Mud and rocks washed onto roads in Calico Basin.
Highway 95 was flooded and impassable north of Goffs Road. One vehicle was washed into the desert.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the early afternoon hours on October 6th. Some of the stronger storms produced locally heavy rainfall with rain rates in excess of one inch per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of flooding and flash flooding to the west of Estrella Mountain Regional Park and to the south of the Gila River. According to a report from the public, flash flooding caused the Waterman Wash to overflow the road at 215th Drive and Narramore Road at approximately 1345MST. The flooding occurred about 3 miles southwest of the town of Liberty. No injuries were reported due to the flooding. Although a Flash Flood Warning was not in effect at the time, there was an Urban and Small Stream Flood Advisory issued for the area starting at 1230MST and running through 1530MST.
Firefighters responded to a woman who was stuck in a pickup truck which was submerged in water near Bear Canyon Rd and Bear Paw Pl. She was uninjured.
A cyclist who tried to cross Alamo Wash which was flowing over a low water crossing on El Calle Betelgeux was rescued by first responders. He was not injured.
Shinarump Drive was closed from Aztec to Estrella due to flooding.
Fourteenth street closed near Dennis Chaves Lake.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding.  Trained weather spotters reported flash flooding of Last Chance Arroyo and up to a foot of water running over Highway 137.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
One mile stretch of U.S. Highway 60/84 closed due to flooding.
Water up to car doors on South Avenue K.

Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding in Jal.  The Jal Police Department reported that three roads were blocked off due to two to three feet of water over them.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Numerous roads were closed in Death Valley National Park, and some were damaged.
A vehicle was stuck in a flooded wash on Winter Road.
Public reported flash flooding on state road 33 near Maricopa. This lead to the roadway closing.
The intersection of Sunfair Road and Aberdeen Drive was flooded.

Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding and mud and debris flows near Lake Hughes and Elizabeth Lake. On Elizabeth Lake Road, a car was stuck in mud. Along Lake Hughes Road, four people were rescued by the Los Angeles county Swift Water Rescue Team.
Highway 62 was flooded between Larrea and Lupine.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris flowing across Interstate 5 around the Tejon Pass on the Grapevine. This report was also followed by numerous reports on social media and TV media.
Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the Antelope Valley. At the intersection of Highway 138 and 170th Street, a car was trapped in flood waters.
Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the mountains of Los Angeles county. Due to flash flooding as well as mud flows, both Elizabeth Lake Road and Bouquet Canyon Road were closed.

Numerous social media and later TV media reported mudslide along Highway 58. The area had experienced some heavy rainfall through out the afternoon. Then a heavy convective shower developed near a burnt area from years prior. This allowed a large debris flow to develop and move into the Tehachapi area. This area is a known alluvial basin that can develop quick flowing flash floods, but the amount of mud and debris with this event was on the order of four to six feet deep. This trapped multiple vehicles and closed the roadway for multiple days. One individual was reported later to have been swept away during the event, with no recovery made to date.
Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the Antelope Valley. At the intersection of 90th Street West and West Avenue I, a car was stuck in flood waters.

Public reported flooding at the State Road 99 and State Road 198 interchange. This area was closed due to the flooding that occurred. This area was under construction during time of this event with bare soils on the side of the roadway. Crews were able to get the road open quickly once storm drains were opened.
Several roads in Death Valley National Park, including Natural Bridge Road, Devil's Golf Course, and Mustard Canyon Drive were closed due to flooding.
Strong thunderstorms generated flash flooding across the Cuyama Valley. Along Highway 166 near New Cuyama, flash flood and mud flows stranded 100 cars and one school bus.
Highway 127 was flooded at Inyo County mile marker 8. One vehicle was overturned.
Several roads which cross Short Creek were flooded.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Hildale, with multiple roads damaged by the flood waters. Debris was flowing along the shoulder of State Route 59 between Milepost 0.5 and Milepost 1.0, and minor flooding occurred along Carling Avenue and Utah Avenue. In addition, several homes reported basement flooding.
Badwater Road was closed due to flooding.
Water six to 12 inches deep flowed over Highway 160 at Basin, Highway 372, and Calvada in Pahrump. Mud, rocks, and debris were reported on many roads in town as well.

Heavy rain upstream in the White Mountains caused flash flooding, both on highway 6 with mud and debris over the road (causing a closure), and in the town of Chalfant with 20 homes damaged from flood waters. Four or 5 of those homes (on Sacramento St) suffered major damage per a Cal OES report. The timing of the flash flood is estimated from between the time highway 6 was reported to have debris over it until about one hour after flooding reached the town of Chalfant (times on CHP incident page).
Highway 95 was closed between Nye County mile markers 26 and 27 due to flooding.
Water, mud, and debris flowed over Echo Dam Road.
Highway 95 was closed in and near Beatty due to flooding.
Highway 160 was closed one mile south of Highway 95 due to flooding. Two roads in the community of Crystal were also impassable.
Over six inches of rapidly flowing water was reported at the entrance to Spring Mountain Ranch State Park.
Bell Vista Road was severely damaged by flooding.
Highway 93 was closed due to severe flooding.
Flooding caused extensive damage to roads in the Ash Meadows National Wildlife Refuge.
Highway 93 was flooded in numerous locations near Lincoln County mile marker 63, with pavement starting to wash out.
Water and debris flowed across Highway 58.
Rocks and debris blocked Scenic Loop Road.
Highway 93 was flooded in several spots between Lincoln County mile markers 38 and 50.
