Highway 318 was flooded in Hiko.
Rocks and debris covered Black Canyon Road near Hole-in-the-Wall campground.
Kelbaker Road was closed due to rocks and debris.
Fort Irwin Road was covered with nearly a foot of mud and debris.

Flash flooding was reported in several locations across Zion National Park. This flooding included the Emerald Pools area, but most of the flooding occurred on the east side of the park, including Spry Canyon, Pine Creek Canyon, and a few other small canyons nearby.
Several backcountry roads in the Desert National Wildlife Refuge were flooded and damaged.
Highway 190 was flooded.
Valley of Fire Highway and I-15 Exit 75 were closed due to flooding.
State Line Road was closed from Death Valley Junction to the NV state line.
Hidden Valley Road was closed due to 4.5 feet of water flowing over the road.
Interstate 15 was closed at mile marker 60 to remove debris from flooding.
Nevada Telephone Cove Road was closed due to flooding, and damage occurred in the Christmas Tree Pass backcountry area.
Temple Bar Access Road was closed due to flooding.

Major flash flooding hit the Grapevine Canyon area of Death Valley National Park. The Mesquite Springs Campground and Grapevine Ranger Station were evacuated; eight vehicles full of visitors and three park rangers were stranded overnight near Ubehebe Crater. Trenches up to six feet deep were cut into Scotty's Castle Road in Grapevine Canyon. 24 power poles were downed, the water treatment facility was heavily damaged, and water lines and the historic water tank were destroyed. The stables building and long house were heavily damaged. Two feet of mud and debris filled the visitor's center. Several inches of mud, rock, and debris also entered the cookhouse. Scotty's Castle measured 2.72 inches of rain in roughly five hours.
Three feet of water from Overton Wash flowed over Highway 169.
Goffs Road was closed due to two feet of water flowing over the road.
A car was stuck in a low water crossing on Highway 95.
A driveway was damaged by flooding.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed from Highway 93 to Meadview, and Stockton Hill Road was closed from Cactus Wren Road to Pierce Ferry Road.
Several roads in Golden Valley were closed due to flooding.
Needles Highway was closed near River Road due to water flowing rapidly over the road.

Heavy rainfall in a basin north of Arches National Park on the evening of October 18th resulted in a flash flood which reached a section of Arches National Park on the morning of the 19th in the Delicate Arch Road area.
Flash flooding was reported along Wahweap Creek, Buckskin Gulch, and the lower portions of the Paria River.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across the northern portions of the greater Phoenix area during the early morning hours on October 20th, and they affected communities along Interstate 17 such as Anthem and New River. Due to elevated amounts of moisture in the atmosphere, some of the storms produced very heavy rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of 1.5 inches per hour. According to local broadcast media, at 0745MST flash flooding occurred along Skunk Creek, about 2 miles southeast of Anthem. The flooding resulted in a water rescue near 19th Avenue and Desert Hills Drive; the vehicle became trapped in Skunk Creek which was swollen with excessive runoff. The driver was rescued and no injuries were incurred. A Flash Flood Warning was not in effect at the time however a Flood Advisory was issued for the area beginning at 0538MST and it ran through 0930MST.
Signal Road was closed from Highway 93 to Alamo Road due to flooding.
High water was flowing in Martinez Wash from near Congress to near Wickenburg.
Water was up to two feet deep on Castle Butte Road east of Mile Post 8 off Navajo Route 60.

Scattered thunderstorms moved across the far northern portions of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the late morning and early afternoon hours on October 20th, and they affected areas surrounding the community of Anthem. Due to elevated amounts of moisture in the atmosphere, the stronger storms produced very heavy rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of 1.5 inches per hour. The heavy rain produced episodes of small stream flooding as well as flash flooding. According to a trained weather spotter 3 miles west of Anthem, at 1215MST water up to one foot deep was flowing across New River Road. A Flash Flood Warning was in effect for the area at the time of the flooding, starting at 1123MST and running through 1330MST. No injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
County Road 153 south of Oatman was closed due to flooding.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Interstate 40 due to flooding.
New Mexico State road 2 closed due to flooding.  A motorist was stranded in 3 to 4 feet of water.  The road remained closed into the next day.

Heavy rain near Marana High School fell on already saturated ground and caused a quick rise in small washes crossing Twin Peaks Road just west of Sandario Road. Three vehicles became stuck in a foot of water and mud that was crossing the road.
New Mexico State road 246 closed between mile markers 59 and 60 due to flooding over the roadway.
Arroyo overflowed from heavy rain. There was a water rescue from a flooded vehicle in Dona Ana.
Heavy rainfall caused flooded roads and four high water rescues in the City of Hobbs that were reported by law enforcement.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
California Highway Patrol reported debris and mud flowing on the northbound lanes of Interstate 5, which shutdown traffic for several hours.
California highway department reported a mudslide on highway 178 in the Kern Canyon at 1004 PST, which closed the roadway for several hours.
Heavy rainfall over the Solimar burn scar resulted in a significant mud and debris flow. The southbound lanes of Highway 101 were closed due to water and debris across the roadway.

Heavy rainfall over the Colby burn scar resulted in a significant mud and debris flow. On Rainbow Drive, 2-3 inches of water and debris was reported in a house. Additionally, Sierra Madre Road at Hicrest Road was closed due to water and debris.
CHP reported a mud and rock slide at La Cresta Road and Coyote Ridge Road in Granite Hills, just east of El Cajon.
Highway 95 was closed from I-40 to the NV state line due to flooding near mile marker 79.
Old St. Thomas Road was closed due to flood damage.
Heavy rainfall over the Solimar burn scar resulted in a significant mud and debris flow. On Highway 101, multiple lanes were closed due to mud and debris flows.
Heavy rainfall over the Calgrove burn scar generated a significant mud and debris flow. Mud and debris closed a mobile home park near the burn scar.
CHP reported flooding on I-5 near the Avenida Pico exit.
A spotter reported 6 of mud on Santiago Canyon Road at Lakeview in the city of Orange.
Heavy rainfall over the community of Piru resulted in a mud and debris flow. The intersection of Main Street and Piru Canyon Road was blocked by mud and debris.

An NWS San Diego employee reported flash flooding near Los Coches and Business 8 with between 6 inches and 2.5 feet of water flowing over the road, as well as flash flooding near El Cajon Blvd. and Main Street with 6-12 of water flowing over the road. A local spotter reported 1.5 feet of water on Johnson Ave. next to Parkway Plaza in El Cajon.

CHP reported the northbound off-ramp from Interstate 5 to Grand Avenue was closed due to severe flooding, as well as the Genesee Avenue off-ramp from Interstate 5 was flooded with several cars stuck. TV media reported a sinkhole at the end of Avenida de la Playa in la Jolla as a result of the heavy rain. A little further south the public reported 6-12 of water flowing down Newport Avenue, over the sidewalks with minor flooding of local businesses in Ocean Beach. The public reported Ward Road in Mission Valley was flooded with several cars submerged. Nine high water rescues were performed in the greater San Diego area on January 6th.
Heavy rainfall over the Los Angeles county mountains generated significant mud and debris flows. Highway 39 was closed at East Fork Road due to a significant mud and debris flow.
Debris washed onto the intersection of Yucca Mesa Road and Barron Drive, closing the road.
Portions of Teddy Roosevelt Road and Shinarump Drive were closed due to flooding.
Willow Beach Road was closed due to significant debris on the road.
Heavy rainfall near the Cabin Fire burn scar resulted in flash flooding and mud and debris flows. CHP reported that a section of State Route 39 was washed out by water and debris.
Large rock slide blocking the south bound lanes of State Highway 18.
Strong thunderstorms brought heavy rain to the Solimar burn area in Ventura county. Ventura County Fire Department reported mud and debris flowing across Highway 101.
Water flowed across Highway 58.
Water, rocks, and debris partially blocked Fort Irwin Road.

Water 1-1.5 feet deep flowed into a house near W. Lake Mead Blvd. and N. Tonopah Dr. A patio awning in North Las Vegas collapsed under the weight of heavy rain. Water 6-12 inches deep flowed over several streets around the valley.
Mud and large rocks washed over Northshore Road near mile marker 27.
Water flowed over Old Woman Springs Road at San Juan Road. One vehicle was pushed off the road by the flood, resulting in one minor injury.
Water and mud flowed over Valley of Fire Highway.
Highway 62 was flooded southwest of Vidal Junction, with several vehicles backed up.
Water about 1.5 feet deep flowed over roads in White Hills after 0.49 inch of rain fell in 20 minutes. Washes were also out of their banks.
Flooding washed out Fort Irwin Road near mile marker 4.

The USACE and Bureau of Indian Affairs reported severe damage to Camino San Ignacio Road due high water and a debris flow. Areas upstream of the incident received moderate to heavy rainfall for approximately 3 hours. The damage to the roadway cut access to 15 homes. An application for a Presidential Declaration was filled for this event.
One foot of water flowed over Bank Street at Gordon Drive.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud and debris flows around the intersection of Highway2 33 and 166. Several vehicles were trapped in mud.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud and debris flows across sections of Highway 46, northeast of Shandon.
Multiple cars were partially submerged at the intersection of Grove Ave. and E Francis St., resulting in the temporarily shut down of the intersection.
CHP reported vehicles unable to move due to high water at the on ramp from  Vineyard Ave. to State Route 60.
Highway 169 was impassable due to about a foot of water over the road.
Valley of Fire Highway was impassable due to fast flowing water over a 100 yard long section of the road.
Mud and debris washed onto North Shore Road near mile marker 46. St. Thomas Road was also closed due to flooding.
State Road 252 north and east of House closed due to severe flooding over the roadway. House reported 3.18 inches of rainfall in around 2 hours.

County roads 88 and 98 washed out, exposing pipes, water and utility lines. One vehicle was partially underwater at a nearby low water crossing. Mud, water, and debris were noted over State Road 76 and U.S. Highway 285.
Pojoaque Valley Arroyo flowing rapidly out of it's banks into nearby yards. Swift water rescues took place in the area. No significant property damage sustained.

A thunderstorm produced between 0.50 and 1.25 inches of rain over the Juniper Fire scar. Debris flows closed Highway 288 at MP 277 at Pocket Creek. Reynolds Creek washed out the highway at MP 286. There was a minor washout on Cherry Creek Road.

Multiple swift water rescues within the midtown area. A family of 4 became stranded near Lee St. and 9th Ave when their vehicle stalled in flood waters up to their windshield. Other rescues were needed when vehicles traveling through roads covered in water became inoperable. Rainfall amounts of 0.50 inches in 15 minutes occurred, with storm total amounts of up to 2 inches across parts of the metro.

Radar estimated that 0.5 to 1.2 inches of rain fell over the Cedar Fire scar. A 12 to 18 inch crest moved down Cedar Creek and through the town of Cedar Creek. This is the first of many post fire floods that happened during the summer of 2016.
A debris flow covered Highway 168 with mud.

Radar estimated 1.50 to 2.50 inches of rain over the central part of the Cedar Fire scar starting around 530 PM MST. A 4 to 5 foot flood crest reached the Highway 73 bridge at the town of Cedar Creek at 720 PM MST.
Flooding of the Truxton Wash closed Hackberry Road.
Flooding of the Truxton Wash closed Antares Road.
Flash flood debris reached the Arizona Department of Transportation yard near  Workman Creek. The flow included large boulders, deep mud, and debris from recent fire activity.
A debris flow covered Highway 159 near Bonnie Springs.
Several intersections were inundated with fast flowing water and debris, and eight swift water rescues occurred. Two people were killed (one direct and one indirect), and one person was injured.
Highway 93 was closed due to flooding.
Twelve to 18 inches of water flowed over Highway 161.
Flash flooding occurred along the East Fork of the Virgin River, where the river gauge indicated a rise from 43 cfs to 1880 cfs in 15 minutes.
Water and mud covered the intersection of Highway 95 and Goffs Road. 95 was eventually closed all the way to Interstate 40.
A debris flow covered Diamond Bar Road.
Flash flooding closed Needles Highway and River Road, and also washed out several nearby roads.
Fast flowing water and debris closed Antares Road.
Flash flooding closed numerous roads in the area, and one car was swept into the Sacramento Wash, resulting in a swift water rescue.
Fast flowing water covered parts of Chaparral Drive.
Highway 190 was flooded from Daylight Pass Cutoff to Cow Creek.
Highway 160 was closed due to flooding.
Highway 178 was closed from the Nevada state line to Shoshone, and Highway 127 was closed from Shoshone to Death Valley Junction.
Several roads were washed out and basketball size boulders dislodged in and around Oatman.
Traffic was stopped on Highway 95 at mile marker 70 due to flooding.

Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in parts of Benson. Benson Middle School was most severely impacted by flood waters. Water was at least ankle deep in an entire wing of the school, damaging rugs and floorboards in ten classrooms. The city of Benson Public Works Building also sustained minor flood damage.

Over 60-water related calls and road closures occurred, mainly within metro Tucson, due to up to 2.5 inches of rainfall. A swift water rescue occurred at Elm St near Tucson Blvd. The Stone Street Underpass was closed for several hours with up to 8 feet of standing water and a stalled vehicle. Vehicles also stalled in water in the Orange Grove Road underpass. Many surface streets were running with a foot or more of water. A daily record of 0.83 inches of rain fell at Tucson International Airport.

Eight to 12 inches of water flowed over Rimrock Road near and east of H Street. A swift water rescue occurred at Center St. and Upton Dr. Water, mud, and debris overflowed the Guadalupe Channel, causing significant damage to two homes on Creosote Ct.

Eight to 12 inches of water flowed over Rimrock Road near and east of H Street. A swift water rescue occurred at Center St. and Upton Dr. Water, mud, and debris overflowed the Guadalupe Channel, causing significant damage to two homes on Creosote Ct. Flooding and debris covered all lanes of Highway 247 at mile marker 77.
Up to 3 inches of rain fell between Helendale and Victorville, causing significant flooding. Highway 66 was closed near Bryman.
Highway 317 was closed south of Caliente.

A line of thunderstorms with intense rainfall moved east across southwest Maricopa County during the evening hours on July 1st; earlier in the evening at 1930MST a trained spotter 11 miles north of Gila Bend measured 1.44 inches within a 30 minute period. As the thunderstorms and heavy rain translated eastward they produced flash flooding along Highway 238 to the east of Gila Bend and near the town of Mobile. A spokesman for the Arizona Department of Highways indicated that flash flooding resulted in the closure of Highway 38 at 2130MST. The closure was about 1 mile to the east of the town of Mobile. No accidents or injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.
Highway 190 was flooded with water and mud at mile markers 97-100.
Mud and debris closed Crystal Road.
Casino Drive was covered in mud.
Rocks and debris washed onto AZ Highway 95.
Hackberry Road was closed from Truxton Wash to I-40 due to flooding.
Signal Road was closed from Highway 93 to Alamo Road.
Tonto Creek rose 6 feet in one hour. The creek was dry and then rose to 5840 CFS.

Torrential rainfall created flash flooding within Bell and Kennedy canyons west of the Beaverhead Ranger Station. Roads in the area were damaged due to high flows in ditches and arroyos. Low lying areas filled up with significant amounts of standing water. The ranger station reported 1.31 inches of rainfall however much higher amounts were likely within the canyons west of the area.

Isolated strong thunderstorms developed across the central portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the late afternoon and early evening hours on July 18th. The storms produced very heavy rain and radar estimated that over one inch fell quickly around south Phoenix, leading to flash flooding. According to local broadcast media, at 1825MST,  heavy rain near 24th Street and Baseline Road led to significant street flooding as well as minor property damage to a local gas station. Another family in south Phoenix reported that water flowing down south Mountain knocked down the back wall to their property and rushed into and around their home leading to significant water damage at the home.
Park rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding along Sulphur Creek.

Several reports were received indicating that some roads were impassible due to flooding. Flood water also entered house in Sedona. The gauge on Oak Creek at Tlaquepaque showed a two and half foot rise.

Video footage showed torrent of water flowing down arroyo through Chilili up to base of the highway 337 bridge. Water was flowing out of bank into the yard of a nearby residence but no damage was sustained. Sandbags worked great to block the water from the home.
A spotter measured 2.50 inches of rain. Several roads in the area were flooded.

Two Forest Service employees were caught between two flooded Forest Service roads on the North Fire burn scar. Each road dipped into an arroyo where the water was bank-full.  They waited out the flood before leaving the area.

The 50s Diner and Bar flooded with 3 foot deep water throughout the building.  The Arizona DPS reported that cars were stuck in flooding on I-70 with mud and hail piled on the road surface. The river gauge on Agua Fria River rose 6.5 feet (0 to 2,900 CFS in less than 15 minutes at 730 PM).
Flood waters swept a vehicle into the Sikul Himatk Wash on the Tohono O'Odham Nation. The motorist escaped to dry land.
The Tohono O'Odham Nation dispatch reported an ongoing swift water rescue approximately 4 miles north of SR 86 on Indian Route 35. A motorist was trapped in their vehicle.

Lomas and Carlisle intersection closed due to high water. Many yards experienced damage to landscaping from flooding over curb levels. Particularly hard hit was area around Lafayette and Mountain within Summit Park neighborhood.
Intersection of Silver and Yale flooded. Cars reported flooded out in water across several areas of Nob Hill.
Two feet of water covered Hobbs Circle. Water in the storm drain blew off a manhole cover and spouted like a geyser.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Highway 80 northwest of Bisbee.

Heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches in a short time flooded several roads in southwest Cochise County including Moson Road near Hereford, Charleston Rd between Sierra Vista and Tombstone and Davis Rd between Tombstone and McNeal.
Heavy rainfall measured at nearly 3.5 inches caused flash flooding near Interstate 10 and Kolb Rd. Three vehicles became stranded in flood waters but no injuries occurred.
Ten to 12 inches of water flowed over the Central Street crossing of Short Creek.
Eight homes were flooded in Dolan Springs.
Water and debris were in the intersection of Goffs Road and National Trails Highway.
The USGS stream gauge at Cherry Creek measured a 6 foot rise with a peak stage of 8.07 feet (4,800 CFS). Base flow is less than 10 CFS.
Flowing water covered portions of Beale Street and Andy Devine Avenue, as well as the nearby sidewalks.
Three to four feet of standing water covered Interstate 40.
A vehicle was stranded due to flash flooding on Highway 62.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding and 3 swift water rescues on the periphery of the Tucson metro area. The first rescue occurred around 830 am LST on Silverbell Rd between Ina Rd and El Camino del Cerro. Around the same time, flood waters 1 to 2 feet deep rushed across Sahuarita Rd near Calle Rinconado. A swift water rescue by the Corona de Tucson FD occurred around 10 am on South Houghton Rd near East Andrada Rd. A third rescue of a woman and her child occurred around 1120 am on South Desert Sunrise Trail near W Snyder Hill Rd. Both Andrada and Pantano High Schools were evacuated and closed early as a precaution due to road closures and a possible sinkhole. Classes resumed the next day.
Two feet of water moved through a restaurant, the Yarnell Post Office was inundated with water, and portions of Highway 89 was close due to debris and mud.
Flash flooding covered Kelso Cima Road.

Two homes on Camino del Rancho were flooded, displacing 9 people. The Red Cross provided temporary housing the the families. Numerous roads were closed around town. Over 1 inch of rain fell, and culverts were damaged along SR-80. Effects were exacerbated from heavy rain which also fell the previous day.
A 9.1 foot rise was reported on Martinez Creek. Residents downstream reported washed out roads.  Some area were not accessible because of the flooding.
Multiple roads within the Mojave National Preserve were covered with mud and debris.
An 8 foot rise in water was reported at the bridge in Cedar Creek.

Strong thunderstorms developed across the northeastern portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the afternoon hours on August 2nd and they affected communities such as Carefree, Cave Creek and Paradise Valley. The storms produced intense rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of one inch per hour; this resulted in flash flooding near Cave Creek. According to a report from local broadcast media, at 1729MST flash flooding 6 miles southwest of Cave Creek necessitated a swift water rescue for a vehicle stuck in water. The rescue was trapped in the vicinity of East Carefree Highway and North 3rd Street.
High water, mud, rocks, and debris flowing across highway 165 from nearby dirt roads.
Large trees toppled into Santa Cruz River assisted destruction of a small bridge downstream from Santa Cruz Lake.

Numerous thunderstorms developed across the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the afternoon hours and they persisted into the evening; the stronger storms produced intense rain with peak rain rates in excess of 4 inches per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of flash flooding which impacted the central portion of the Phoenix area including the Interstate 17 corridor north of Grand Avenue. According to a report from the public, at 1753MST flash flooding along Interstate 17 at the Indian School underpass resulted in a water rescue. No injuries were reported. Additionally, a mesonet weather station 3 miles northeast of central Phoenix, near the Phoenix County Club, measured 2.1 inches of rain within 30 minutes ending at 1739MST. The mesonet station was part of the Maricopa County Flood Control gauge network.
Las Huertas Creek flooded out of it's banks and up to back door of one home. No damage. Sand bags were requested.
Vehicle with two occupants washed into the Santa Cruz River and tumbled downstream. Both individuals were rescued with non life threatening injuries.
A 2-3 foot surge in water prompted a swift water rescue involving 5 people and one pet.
Highway 288 was impassable at mile post 277 due to downed logs that washed onto the road.
Flood waters undermined the road and damaged a guard rail on Highway 158.

Video showed a torrent of water raging through the arroyo flowing up to the base of the highway 337 bridge at Chilili. Chopper footage also showed cattle and a rancher fleeing the flood wave upstream.
Flash flooding was reported along Lick Wash and Willis Creek.

Thunderstorms with locally heavy rain developed to the north of the greater Phoenix area during the early afternoon hours and some of the more intense rainfall occurred along the Interstate 17 corridor to the south of New River. Rain rates in excess of one inch per hour were observed, resulting in episodes of flooding and flash flooding. According to a report from the public, at 1450MST flash flooding resulted in the road becoming rapidly submerged near the intersection of 17th Avenue and Joy Ranch Road. This was located about 7 miles to the southeast of the town of New River. A Flash Flood Warning was not issued, however an Urban and Small Stream Flood Advisory was issued for the area beginning at 1426MST and it remained in effect until 1730MST.

Heavy rainfall in and around the city of Kanab led to widespread flash flooding across the area. Significant damage occurred at Kanab Elementary, a city park, youth baseball fields, a city swimming pool, a local hospital, and approximately 20 homes.

Park rangers in Zion National Park reported flash flooding in multiple locations, including near the Temple of Sinawava and in the Narrows. Several hikers were temporarily stranded in the Narrows until flood waters receded. The North Fork of the Virgin River rose from 53 cfs to 787 cfs due to the heavy rains.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to Route 66 due to flooding.

Nearly two inches of rain in parts of Nogales, Sonora caused Nogales Wash to overtop the Doe St. bridge in Nogales, Arizona.  As a result, businesses were flooded along Hohokam Drive with surface runoff 8 inches deep. Morley Avenue was also flooded.
Flash flooding occurred along North Creek, with multiple waterfalls reported by Zion National Park rangers.

Park rangers in Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding along Sulphur Creek and the Fremont River. The Fremont River jumped its banks and flowed over State Route 24 within Capitol Reef National Park.

Heavy rainfall on the La Sal Mountains drained into the previously dry Placer Creek which resulted in flash flooding that produced road damage. A section of East Castle Valley Drive within the community of Castle Valley was cut two feet deep and became impassable until repairs were made.  The flash flood waters were generally 1 to 2 feet deep.  Radar estimated rainfall over the La Sal Mountains ranged from 1.0 to 1.5 inches in less than two hours.  Incidentally, about an hour before the flash flood struck the town of Castle Valley, the town received 0.20 of an inch of rain within 20 minutes.
A road washed out near Oak Knoll.
Heavy rain caused flooding across Park Link Drive over one foot deep in some spots. This caused some of the edges of the road to be washed out.
DW Ranch Road was closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain caused Blanco Wash to flood Tucker Road west of Picture Rocks. Several inches of water also covered the road near Avra Valley Rd and Anway Rd.
Approximately 10 vehicles were stuck in flood waters at David Drive and River Drive. Sections of Needles Highway near Capri Road also washed away.

Heavy rain in Utah caused the Paria River to flash flood as it flowed south into Arizona and into the Colorado River. The Paria River was estimated to rise more than 2 feet at the Utah Arizona border in around 15 minutes.
Highway 93 was flooded just south of Railroad Pass Casino. Two cars were stuck in water up to the hoods.
A debris flow was reported across Highway 191 at mile marker 289 to 390. The road was temporarily close.  Radar estimated an inch of rain in less than 60 minutes.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters on Nipton Road at Interstate 15.
The Flamingo Road on ramps to Highway 95 were closed due to flooding.
The Hassayampa River rose about 8 feet and was flowing rapidly. It is normally dry.

A spotter reported 6 inches of water about 50 feet wide flowing down Buena Vista Road with dirt and rock on the roads, including Highway 18 and Custer Road. Total rain of 1.5 inches reported. Another spotter reported 1 inch of rain in ten minutes nearby.
Fast moving water flowed over Highway 62 in low water crossings from Steeg Road to Wonder Valley.
The Big Bug Creek rose an estimated 4 feet.
Flash flooding was reported along Buckskin Wash, the Paria River, and Wahweap Creek.
High water forced rocks, mud, and debris over Catwalk Road near Glenwood. Mineral Creek road was washed out east of Alma.
National Trails Highway and Goffs Road were closed due to flooding with large amounts of debris.
Roadways turned to a flooded, muddy mess south of Hospah.
Two feet of standing water covered Essex Road. The road was eventually closed from National Trails Highway to Interstate 40.
Low water crossings flooded in Glenwood Hills neighborhood. Many residents also reported landscaping washed into streets at several homes in the area near Menaul and Juan Tabo.
Flooding closed Highway 62 from Highway 177 to Highway 95, and Highway 95 from Blythe to Needles.

The observed rise in the Paria River gauge at Highway 89 (in Utah) was around 745 PM MST on August 4th. The crest reached the Lees Ferry gauge at around 415 AM on August 5th. Flash Flood levels in excess of 5 feet were estimated to have been in the Arizona section of the Paria River from 11 PM on August 4th through 7 AM on August 5th before entering the Colorado River.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain developed across the northeastern portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the morning hours on August 5th; some of the stronger storms produced peak rain rates in excess of 2 inches per hour. Very heavy rain and flash flooding occurred 7 miles southeast of Deer Valley and to the northeast of Phoenix Mountain Park. At 0930MST local broadcast media reported flash flooding which resulted in  one car being stuck in flood waters near Cave Creek and Hatcher Roads. One person needed to be rescued from the stranded automobile. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for the area at 0930MST and the warning remained in effect through 1115MST.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across the northeast portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the morning hours on August 5th, and the stronger storms produced locally heavy rains with peak rain rates well in excess of 2 inches per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of flash flooding over portions of north Scottsdale which resulted in a number of road closures. According to a trained weather spotter in north Scottsdale, 1 inch of rain fell in 20 minutes ending at 0931MST and this resulted road closures at Hayden Loop and Frank Lloyd Wright roadway due to flooding. In addition, the center lane of Frank Lloyd Wright road at the Scottsdale airport was flooded. Finally, the right line of Northsight Boulevard at Frank Lloyd Wright road became flooded due to the intense and heavy rains.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rains developed across the far northeast portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the morning hours on August 5th. Some of the heaviest rains occurred in communities such as north Scottsdale and Paradise Valley. As of 1000MST, multiple mesonet weather stations measured storm totals of 1.5 inches or more in the area; one station near Desert Highlands Golf Club measured at total of 1.54 inches. The heavy rains led to episodes of flash flooding which resulted in road closures and vehicles trapped in flood waters.  At 1000MST local broadcast media reported a U-Haul truck stuck in flood waters 6 miles north of north Scottsdale, near the intersection of North Scottsdale Road and East Happy Valley Road. At the same time another broadcast media reported roads closed due to flash flooding 7 miles south of Carefree, near the intersection of East Jomax and North Pima roads. No injuries were reported due to the flash flooding. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for the area beginning at 0920MST and it remained in effect through 1115MST.
Oil truck washed into Large Canyon at 5 mile bridge near CR7007. Body found outside of vehicle downstream.
Flash flooding was reported along Highway 191 at mile post 389.
Flash flooding was reported over Highway 191 near mile post 389.
Flood waters 2 to 3 feet deep on Aztec Road between 8th and 10th streets.
Mud slide covering portion of U.S. Highway 84 near Medanales.
The Arizona Department of Transportation reported water on Highway 160 between Mile Post 432 and 445. Debris were also reported on the road near Mexican Water.
Highway 56 flooded between 4th and 6th streets. One to two feet of water over the roadway in low spots. Road impassable.
Fairgrounds flooded.

Serious flash flooding developed on Salt Creek Wash and created major damage to a community near Mesa Farm Road. Three to four homes were severely damaged and one home was destroyed. Several vehicles, motorcycles, recreational vehicles washed into creek and destroyed. Water rescues occurred from roof tops and amazingly no one was killed.
Water flooding over highway 53 at mile markers 14 and 17.
Heavy rain of about 2.5 inches in 1 hour caused flash flooding south of Sierra Vista. Miller Creek overflowed Moson Rd while Ramsey Rd and Arabian Rd were also flooded.

Three to four inches or more of rainfall in one to two hours caused Sonoita Creek to overflow its banks into parts of Patagonia. Eight mobile homes were evacuated as a precaution with water 18 inches deep surrounding them. An additional 14 homes were also evacuated. Only minimal damage occurred to the skirting of these homes since they were elevated off the surface.
Heavy rain caused Peck Canyon to overflow its banks and flood adjacent streets in Rio Rico.

Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2.5 inches in 90 minutes caused widespread flash flooding in Tucson and resulted in a total of 45 stranded motorist calls and 8 swift water rescues. One rescue involved a Pima County Supervisor, who was swept away in her vehicle near Ft. Lowell and Oracle Rd. Flood waters caused major road damage near Lee St. and Santa Rosa Avenue. The Stone St. underpass was flooded to a depth of 8 feet. Flash flooding also caused delays and closures along Sandario Rd in Picture Rocks. Near Silverbell Rd and Speedway Rd, multiple lower level townhouses incurred flood damage. A few residences in Green Valley suffered minor flooding.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain developed across the eastern portion of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area, including the community of Mesa, during the late afternoon hours on August 9th and peak rain rates with the stronger storms approached 2 inches per hour. The heavy rain led to episodes of flash flooding from East Mesa eastward into Apache Junction. At 1135MST, a National Weather Service employee reported that flash flooding had inundated several portions of Brown Road as well as portions of Loop 202 and these roads were under water. The flooded roads were located roughly 3 miles northeast of East Mesa. A Flash Flood Warning for the area was issued shortly thereafter, at 1153MST. No serious accidents or injuries were reported due to the flash flooding.

Thunderstorms with locally heavy rain developed across portions of south central Arizona, including the greater Phoenix metropolitan area, during the late morning hours on August 9th. Peak rain rates with the stronger storms approached 2 inches per hour which led to episodes of street flooding and flash flooding across the central deserts. By the early afternoon, flash flooding had spread to areas southwest of the greater Phoenix area; at 1318MST the Arizona Department of Transportation indicated that flash flooding caused Highway 238 to become closed about 5 miles to the southwest of the town of Mobile. A Flash Flood Warning was not in effect for the area at the time of the flooding.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain developed across Apache Junction during the late morning hours on August 9th and peak rain rates with the stronger storms approached 2 inches per hour. Locally heavy rain in the area led to flash flooding in Apache Junction; according to local law enforcement, at 1156MST Second Avenue between Idaho Road and Winchester Road was closed due to flash flooding. No significant accidents were reported as a result of the flooding however. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for Apache Junction beginning at 1153MST and it remained in effect through 1400MST.
The last three to four miles of Diamond Creek Road were flooded and covered with debris. The Diamond Creek USGS station recorded 2.56 inches of rain in three hours.

Heavy rain caused washes to overtop secondary roads between Kearny and Florence. A |32-yr old man attempted to drive his truck across a wash near Whitlow Ranch and Hawkview Roads and became stuck when water rushed into his vehicle.

Flash flooding was reported in Zion National Park, particularly along SR-9, where a significant rock fall on the switchback near Pine Creek Bridge blocked both sides of the road. This rock fall included a large house-sized boulder, and the road was closed between Canyon Junction and the East Entrance of Zion National Park for several hours.
Flash flooding was reported in Lick, Willis, and other canyons south of Bryce Canyon National Park.
Buck and Doe Road was flooded.

The river gauge on Oak Creek in Sedona (Tlaquepaque) showed a 3 foot rise starting around 215 PM MST and peaked around 230 PM MST. The thunderstorm was moving from north to south through Oak Creek Canyon and then out over the Sedona area. Smaller washes then started flowing and caused the closure of several roads (Back 'O Beyond,  Sunset Drive, and Doodlebug Drive).
Flash flooding occurred along the North Fork of the Virgin, which peaked at 1480 cfs.

Thunderstorms with intense rainfall developed across the west central deserts, including La Paz county, during the afternoon hours on August 10th. Peak rain rates exceeded 2 inches per hour at times and the intense rain led to episodes of flash flooding. As an example of the heavy rain that occurred, a trained weather spotter 1 mile east of Bouse measured 2.05 inches within a 45 minute period ending about 2000MST. At 1931MST, the Arizona Department of Highways reported that Highway 72 was impassable to the southeast of Bouse due to flash flooding. A Flash Flood Warning was issued for the area at 1815MST and it remained in effect through 2218MST.
Numerous roads impassable in and around Silver City. Ridge Road also closed along San Vicente arroyo west of Grant County Airport.

Thunderstorms with locally heavy rain moved across the central and southeast portions of the greater Phoenix metropolitan area during the evening hours on August 10th and some of the storms generated intense rain with peak rain rates approaching 2 inches per hour. Heavy rain led to episodes of flooding and flash flooding over the central deserts. At 2030MST, the Arizona Department of Highways reported that Highway 238 was closed at milepost 40 due to flash flooding. This was approximately 4 miles to the northwest of Ak-Chin Village. A Flash Flood Warning was not in effect for the area at the time of the flooding. No accidents or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flash flooding which deposited large logs and rocks across area roads.
Heavy rain over the Cedar Fire scar caused flash flooding and debris flow over Highway 60. The water pushed large boulders over Highway 60.
Heavy rain over the Cedar Fire scar caused flash flooding in Cedar Creek. The water over topped the K-rails that were put in place after the fire to prevent flood damage.

Heavy rain caused ponding of water along Highway 79 north of Park Link Drive, and caused Durham Wash and other small washes to flow across the highway, making it impassable for 2 hours. Farther south, heavy rain also occurred near I-10 along the Pinal/Pima county line. Flash flooding occurred at Pinal Air Park, where flood waters entered several buildings. Runoff flooded small washes near Red Rock and washed out Sasco Road at the Santa Cruz River.
A flood wave hit State Highway 288 that washed debris over the roadway.
Heavy rain caused mud and debris (8 to 12 inches deep) to flow over a few roads in Yarnell. A fence around a home was destroyed by the mud and debris.
Eight inches of water flowed over Highway 95 at mile marker 35.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters on Highway 95 at mile marker 51. Nearly three feet of road eventually washed away.
Stockton Hill Road was closed from mile marker 19 to Pierce Ferry Road.
Flash flooding was reported in Gisela with washes running high.  A few road crossings were temporarily impassible because of the water and deposited debris on the roads.
Martinez Wash rose 5.7 feet in less than an hour.
Highway 95 was impassable from Vidal Junction to mile marker 24 due to flooding and debris.
Walnut Creek overflowing banks on Spence Road, Jackson Road, and Highway 2 southwest of Lake Arthur. Roadways impassable.
Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding about 20 miles north of Carlsbad.  There was six inches of water running across County Road 34.  No damage was reported.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding in Carlsbad.  There was significant ongoing street flooding.  Lea Street in Carlsbad was flooded curb to curb six to twelve inches deep at some intersections.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding near and on the south side of Carlsbad.  There was major flooding of US Highway 62/180 from the Carlsbad Airport north to Walmart in South Carlsbad at the junction of Center Street.  The highway was flooded curb to curb six inches to a foot deep.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding.  A cooperative observer reported one to two feet of water from Last Chance Creek running over the road about twelve miles west of the Cavern City Air Terminal.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Flash flooding reported along Alvarez Road with mud and debris across road.

Road damage occurred from flash flooding in Leasburg Dam State Park.  Water made it into park buildings with over a foot of standing water in the Maintenance yard.  Daily rainfall from afternoon and overnight rains totaled 4.04 inches.
Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding southwest of Carlsbad.  County Road 408 intersecting with County Road 672 was flooded.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding in Carlsbad.  County Road 672 in Carlsbad had four to five feet of flowing water across low water crossings.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
At least three vehicles stalled in flood waters along county road 56A.
Vehicle overturned on highway 74 near mile marker 2 due to flood waters. Women was rescued from vehicle by fire department.
Water over U.S. Highway 84 in Hernandez near highway 74.
Over one foot of water surrounding homes near La Villita.
Numerous roadways flooded and impassable around Hernandez.

Two elderly residents rescued from a mobile home that was washed off it's foundation and displaced over 50 feet downstream. Up to 30 homes inundated with water and at least 10 families displaced from flood waters. U.S. Highway 285, highway 74, and county road 57 all closed to remove mud and debris. County Road 57 washed over with mudslides from nearby mesa.
Numerous roads flooded and impassable around Alcalde.
Two feet of water flowed over several streets on the northeast side of Golden Valley.
Water from Animas Creek was flowing over Capaz Road making it impassable.
Highway 95 was flooded near Interstate 40. Rocks were in the road, and some cars were being pushed off the road by the water.
DW Ranch Road was closed due to flooding.

Several swift water rescues occurred on the north side of the Las Vegas Valley. Multiple vehicles were stuck in flooding at Las Vegas Blvd and Cheyenne, and Craig Road was flooded over the sidewalks between Interstate 15 and Losee Road. Highway 215 was closed from Range Road to Lamb Blvd. The Nellis AFB main gate was closed for over 12 hours due to debris.
Warm Springs Road and Ranch Road were closed due to flooding and debris.
Mud and debris were on Interstate 15 at Exit 64.
Roads and washes flooded in the New Kingman-Butler area. Water was over eight inches deep on Irving Road between Gordon and Kino.
Four to five inches of mud covered Kelso Cima Road, requiring a grader to clear.
Valley of Fire Road was closed due to flooding and debris.
Rancher reported a six to seven foot wall of water down Dark Canyon Draw at County Road 408.
Flash flooding occurred along the Paria River drainage, including Buckskin Wash, for several hours. House Rock Road was closed and multiple people were temporarily stranded due to the flooding.
Dark Canyon Road/County Road 408 was closed due to flooding caused by heavy rainfall in the area.
Widespread flash flooding occurred in Capitol Reef National Park, including flash flooding along Pleasant Creek, Grand Wash Road, and the Scenic Drive.
Flash flooding occurred across portions of Capitol Reef National Park, including in Grand Wash. In addition, the Fremont River overflowed onto State Route 12 near Fruita.
Flash flooding was reported along the Upper Escalante drainage.
Highway 95 was closed from mile marker 36 to 39, and Cottonwood Cove Road was damaged and closed by flooding.
A vehicle was stuck in water and debris on Highway 127 at mile marker 15.
Highway 95 and Five Mile Road were closed for major flash flooding and potential collapse of the road.
Water, rocks, and debris were over Casino Drive near the Old Town Saloon.
Highway 95 was closed near Highway 163 to clear flood debris from the road.
Water, rocks, and debris were on Miracle Mile.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters on Highway 62 near mile marker 126.
A semi truck was stuck in flood waters on Highway 95, requiring a swift water rescue. The highway was closed from I-40 to NV Highway 163 until 1025 PST.
Six or more inches of water flowed down several streets in Lake Havasu City.
Two to three feet of water covered roads that crossed Black Canyon Creek.
All three roads leading into and out of Topock were flooded and impassable.
Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding.  Highway 8 between Hobbs and Eunice has been closed due to high water.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding in Hobbs.  Joe Harvey Boulevard on the north side of Hobbs was flooded with six to twelve inches of water over the road.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding in Hobbs.  There was knee deep water over the road at the intersection of Copper and Grimes in Hobbs.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding in Jal.  The intersection of Montana and Third Street in Jal had been closed due to high water.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Three to four feet of water flowing over highway 337 near Tajique. Many arroyos flowing out of banks, culverts at maximum capacity, and large areas of standing water from near Tajique north toward Chilili.
Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding near Maljamar.  Highway 82 was closed between mile markers 115 and 153 in Lea County.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding southwest of Carlsbad.  Last Chance Arroyo was flooded resulting in Highway 137 to be impassible.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain fell across Eddy County and produced flash flooding southwest of Carlsbad.  Dark Canyon Arroyo was flooded with 20 to 25 foot deep water.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Several streets were barricaded in Artesia due to high water from heavy rainfall in the area.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Granite Creek rose 3.5 feet near Prescott with a peak flow of 1468 CFS. An upstream gauge rose 4 feet with a peak flow of 1209 CFS.
Significant street and stream flooding was reported throughout downtown Silver City.
Thunderstorms produced brief heavy rain that caused 6 to 12 inches of water to flow over Dragoon Road and Old Ranch Road.
Flash flooding was reported in the Lower Paria drainage.
Father and daughter killed after entering a flooded arroyo.
Flash flooding was reported along the House Rock Valley Road and surrounding areas. This flooding closed the House Rock Valley Road and stranded multiple people for a period of time.
Flash flooding was reported in Price and other surrounding areas, including near the Book Cliffs.
High water flooding over low water crossings. Roads impassable.
Torrential rainfall and flooding of arroyos and streams within eastern Mora County led to a massive rise of nine feet in 15 minutes downstream on the Canadian River at Sanchez.

A swift water rescue occurred on South Burro Drive south of Ramsey Road in Hereford. Two people and their dog were rescued when their vehicle was washed down a low water crossing. No injuries occurred. Additionally, a portion of Leonardo de Vinci Drive in Sierra Vista was closed due to flash flooding.
Cuchillo Creek overflowed and flooded Highway 52 in Winston.  Water was up to 2 feet deep across the highway.

Ranchers reported water in creek rose 15 feet and was the highest they have observed in over 50 years. Precipitation gauges on the property measured 1.93 inches, 3.95 inches, and 4.15 inches from training thunderstorms. Several areas along the creek were out of bank and flooding nearby pasture. Several low water crossings were washed out.

Heavy rain caused widespread flash flooding across Washington County, including the town of Hildale. The gauge of the Virgin River at Virgin reported an increase from the normal flow of under 100 cfs to nearly 3300 cfs by late morning on September 22. The North Fork of the Virgin River, in Zion National Park, also rose from less than 50 cfs to over 2100 cfs.
Flash flooding was reported along the Paria River, with the gauge at Lees Ferry reporting a rise from 4 cfs to over 4200 cfs.

Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall brought widespread flooding to Carbon County. Significant flooding occurred in Wellington near 100 East, and severe damage was reported to approximately 10 homes. In Carbonville, the Pilling Trailer Park received extensive flooding, forcing the evacuation of 80 different mobile homes. Flooding also occurred in Sunnyside, with widespread street flooding causing manhole covers to pop up across the city. The Price River also experienced significant flooding, with flow along the river jumping from the normal flow of less than 10 cfs to greater than 8,000 cfs. In total across the county, flooding damaged over 140 private homes, several businesses, and many local roads. County officials reported uninsured damages of $1,602,000 to infrastructure, $971,000 in damage to businesses, and $1,071,000 to private property.
Flash flooding was reported along the Escalante River, with readings at the river gauge increasing from under 50 cfs to over 1500 cfs in a short period of time.
Several roads in Colorado City were closed due to flooding and debris.
Widespread flash flooding was reported in Capitol Reef National Park, including along Sulphur Creek. The flooding also caused park rangers to close the Scenic Drive.
Heavy rain caused the Paria River at Lees Ferry to rise 4 feet.
Rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding in the Capitol Gorge.

More than two inches of rain accompanied by large hail that piled up to six inches deep in some locations caused flash flooding in Safford.  Runoff filled Freeman Wash which caused minor damage to several homes and a school, and washed out part of 12th Avenue. The flood waters temporarily displaced twenty five residents. The school was closed for two weeks until repairs were completed. Flood waters also blocked roadways in rural areas, stranding 8,000 county fair visitors until waters receded.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received around a 5 mile radius of Williamsburg. Flooding was reported on King Canyon Road and water was above bridge level on Highway 187 along with debris on the road. Palomas Creek was flooded about 6 miles northwest of the I-25 bridge.
Flash flooding was reported across Highway 142 in Monticello.

A public report including photos through social media indicated flooding was occurring on Fred Haight Drive in Smith River after 10-12 inches of rain fell across the county over the previous three days.

Numerous roads were closed along and near Highway 180 in Silver City due to flash flooding.  Other cities affected by the flooding included  Santa Clara around Twin Sisters Peak Road and numerous roads around Bayard and Hurley.  Rainfall amounts around this area averaged 1 to 2 inches in a couple of hours with a maximum of 4.50 inches in Bayard.
Highway 187 at mile marker 35 south of Williamsburg was closed due to flash flooding.
All the low water crossings south of Hillsboro were flowing across Highway 27.

Two to three inches of rain caused Union Canal to overflow into the streets of Pima. In addition, flood damage occurred to cotton that was already harvested and being stored as modules in area fields.
Water and debris were flowing across Highways 52 and 59.  Hermosa Road was also closed.
NM 169 closed at the Rio Salado Bridge. Flood waters undermined roadway and bridge.
A swift water rescue occurred near the intersection of Egar Rd and Diabase Rd in Golden Valley.
Flash flooding on Green Valley Road near Graton.
Flash flood. Water one foot deep at intersection of SR 37 and SR 121.
Roadway was washed away at Lichau/Cold Springs Road near Copeland Creek.
Roadway flooded on ramp at intersection of SR 131 and 101N.

Heavy rain over the Fish burn area generated flash flooding as well as mud and debris flows in the city of Duarte. At the intersection of Brookridge Road and Melcanyon Road, over 6 inches of mud and debris was reported.

Heavy rains developed across portions of La Paz county including around the town of Parker and in the Parker Strip, during the morning hours on December 24th. Peak rain rates were in excess of 1 inch per hour. The rains resulted in flooding of roads and low lying drainage areas around Parker and along Highway 95 running south of Parker. The heavier rains led to flash flooding north of Parker; according to a trained weather spotter 5 miles northeast of Parker, the heavy rains caused large amounts of debris, including trees and small boulders, to wash onto area roads including highway 95 along the Parker Strip. Washes were reported running and other roads in the area were flooded at low water crossings. Flash Flood Warnings were not issued for the area but a Flood Advisory was issued at 0911MST.
Multiple vehicles were reported stuck in a flooded roadway on Malaga Road near Lamont by law enforcement.
The I-15 northbound on ramp from Lenwood Road was flooded with water, mud, and rocks.
A car was stuck in rushing water on Minneola Road.
Colgan Creek near Sebastopol went above flood stage.
Three feet of water in roadway near Paradise Rd/Lakeview Dr intersection.
Media reported flash flooding of Uvas Creek overflowing near Christmas Hill Park in Gilroy, CA. Damage are estimates.
Kern County Department of Highways reported flooding in Bodfish on Caliente Bodfish Road at Rim Road for southbound traffic.
Kern County Department of Highways reported flooding east of Bakersfield on Breckenridge Road about 3 miles from Commanche Drive.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding on Highway 198 and Craig Ranch Road northeast of Three Rivers.
California Highway Patrol reports mud slide and boulders blocking Mineral King Road near Three Rivers.
California Highway Patrol reports that Highway 198 at Long Road is closed due to a mudslide just southwest of Kaweah Lake.
California Highway Patrol reported that Highway 168 westbound was closed due to boulder and rock slide west of Humphreys Station.
Willow Brook at Penngrove Park stream gage rose above major flood stage.
Stream gage on Sonoma Creek at Kenwood exceeded flood stage between 7 and 8 am PST.
Mark West Creek stream gauge at Mirabel Heights exceeded flood stage starting at 8:15 am on January 8.
Local law enforcement officials reported widespread flooding due to runoff from heavy rain.
Levee breach on the Carmel river near Paso Hondo in Carmel Valley village. Inundation from the levee breach impacted 20 to 30 homes. Swift water rescue underway.
Utility company reported that the mobile home park near Willow Creek and downstream from Crane Valley Dam was to be evacuated due to flood threat from planned Crane Valley Dam releases.
Los Gatos Creek flooding.

Stream gauges indicated that flash flooding was occurring on the Willow Brook and other portions of the Petaluma River. Also, Flooding was occurring on the lower Sonoma Creek watershed at the Agua Caliente stream gauge.
Flooding east of 5th street. Fife Creek overflowing.
Heavy rain caused the Napa River at Lodi Lane in Saint Helena CA to exceed flood stage between 3:00-10:30 pm PST on January 10, 2017.
Corte Madera Creek stream gauge at Ross exceeded flood stage between 6:43 pm and 8:00 pm PST on January 10.

Heavy rain over the Soberanes Burn Scar resulted in flooding on the Big Sur River. The Big Sur River stream gauge near Big Sur rose above flood stage at 7:00 pm PST on January 10 and continued above flood stage until 6:30 am PST on January 11.

Heavy rain in the Santa Cruz Mountains caused the San Lorenzo River to flood. The San Lorenzo River stream gauge at Big Trees exceeded flood stage between 8:45 pm on January 10 and 1:30 am on January 11.
Heavy rain caused the Alameda Creek to flood.  The stream gauge on Alameda Creek near Niles to rise above flood stage between 8:45 pm PST on January 10 and 5:30 am PST on January 11.
Strong thunderstorms brought heavy rain to the Fish burn scar. The heavy rain produced mud and debris flows which impacted Encanto Parkway in the city of Azusa.
California Highway Patrol reported about a foot of water across all lanes on Highway 180 near Reed Avenue near Minkler.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding on the Sonoma Creek.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 7:30 pm PST on January 18 and remained above flood stage until 10:30 pm PST.

Heavy rain on January 18 caused the Laguna de Santa Rosa to flood. The stream gauge on the Laguna de Santa Rosa at Stony Point Road rose above flood stage at 7:45 pm PST on January 18 and remained above flood stage until 1:45 am PST on January 19.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding on both the Willow Brook at Penngrove and Sonoma Creek at Agua Caliente.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 4:45 am on January 20 and remained above flood stage until 8 am that day.

Heavy rain in the Santa Cruz Mountains resulted in flooding on the San Lorenzo River.  The San Lorenzo stream gauge at Big Trees rose above flood stage at 7:25 am PST on January 20 and remained above flood stage until 8:30 am PST.

Heavy rain generated flash flooding across southern Santa Barbara county, impacting El Capitan Canyon Resort near the Sherpa burn scar. In the private campground, 70 people were evacuated while the combination of 8 cabins and vehicles were flooded.
The Pacheco Creek near Dunneville flooded.  A stream gauge on the Pacheco Creek near Dunneville rose above flood stage at 10:30 AM PST and remained above flood stage until 4:15 PM PST.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding as well as mud and debris flows near the Sand burn scar. Soledad Canyon Road was closed due to mud and debris flows and one vehicle was stuck in the mud.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding as well as mud and debris flows near the Fish burn scar. Mud and debris flows closed down areas around the intersection of Melcanyon and Brookridge Roads in the city of Duarte.
A swift water rescue to save 2 people and a dog was conducted at the intersection of University Ave. and Aragon Dr. in the neighborhood of Rolando.
Widespread flooding occurred near Gilman Springs Rd. and Soboba Rd. in San Jacinto with multiple water rescues conducted.

Rapid water rises after 1500PST flooded parts of Carroll Canyon Rd with 1-2 ft of rushing water. The flow carried dumpsters and debris. Three people were trapped in their vehicle that stalled as the water rose rapidly, resulting in multiple swift water rescues around 1530PST.

Multiple low water crossings were closed due to rapid rises in the San Diego River, including Camino Del Rio and Ward Rd. Several cars were submerged by the rapidly rising waters. The Fashion Valley Transit Center was closed due to flooding. The river peaked at 0215PST on the 21st with a crest of 11.81 ft.
The CHP reported a vehicle in jeopardy of being washed off a bridge near Sandia Creek Dr. and Rock Mountain Rd.
Six feet of water inundated an apartment building in City Heights on 48th street. One family nearly drowned due to the flood.

Locally heavy rains developed across the northern portion of the greater Phoenix area, along Interstate 17 and near the communities of New River and Anthem, during the evening hours on January 20th. Spotters indicated that up to 2 inches fell within a 6 hours period. The heavy rain led to flash flooding and flooding along Interstate 17 during the very early morning hours on January 21st. According to a trained spotter, as of 0130MST a water rescue was underway from a flooded wash about 1 mile east of Interstate 17 along Table Mesa Road. This was about 4 miles northeast of the town of New River. A Flash Flood Warning was not issued rather a Small Stream Flood Flood Advisory. No injuries were reported to those affected by the water rescue.

Heavy rain on January 22, 2017, resulted in flooding on the Sonoma Creek.  The Sonoma Creek stream gauge at Agua Caliente rose above flood stage at 4:15 AM PST on January 22 and remained above flood stage until 8:30 AM PST.
Roadway flooding Palo Colorado Rd at Hwy 1.

Heavy rain on January 24 caused the Pacheco Creek in San Benito County to flood.  The Pacheco Creek stream gauge near Dunneville rose above flood stage at 11:45 am PST on January 22 and remained above flood stage until 4 pm PST on January 22.

Rapid water rises along Temecula Creek caused flooding in south Temecula. Firefighters rescued a woman stranded on a small island in Temecula Creek. The woman was transported to the hospital with minor injuries.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of the Pacific Coast Highway and Interstate 710.

Excessive rain induced flash flooding in the Cajon Wash. A swift water rescue was conducted to pull 2 people from the wash near Swarthout Canyon Road. Further south along the wash, San Bernardino County Public Works closed Glen Helen Pkwy. from Glen Helen Rd. to Cajon Blvd. for an extended period.

Widespread heavy rain brought flash flooding to a large portion of Orange County. A water rescue occurred on Hamilton Ave. at the Santa Ana River in Huntington Beach. Numerous streets from Sunset Beach to Santa Ana to Newport Beach were also flooded with 1-3 ft of water. Numerous reports of vehicles stranded in flood waters were received, including half a dozen along Highway 55.

A swift water rescue team pulled a man from a submerged car in a small creek near Old Highway 395 and 5th St. in Rainbow. A young boy, also in the car, was swept down stream before rescuers arrived. The boys body was recovered on the 26th.
Pala Temecula Rd. was closed due to flooding and rocks in the roadway.
Heavy mountain rain drained into the deserts leading to flooding along several area roadways. A closure occurred along Highway 18 west of Victorville due to flooding across all lanes.
Swift water rescue conducted near North Golf Course in Sun City.
Cal Fire reported of a swift water rescue along the Pyrite Channel near Van Buren Blvd.
Roadway closure due to flooding on Cole Grade Rd.
Roadway closure at the intersection of Highway 138 and 173 with a swift water rescue and 2 vehicles stranded in flood waters.

Cal Fire and Riverside County Firefighters conducted 2 water rescues along the Temescal Wash in Alberhill near the intersection of Hostettler Rd. and Temescal Canyon Rd. Four vehicles were stranded in 2-3 ft of water.
Highway 83 between Pine Ave. and Highway 71 closed due to flooding along Chino Creek.

California Highway Patrol reported road flooding near Lodge Road and Wiemiller Road with a vehicle stuck in flood waters west of Tollhouse in Fresno County. Road was temporarily closed to let water subside.
Napa River at Lodi Lane Stream gauge went above flood stage.
San Lorenzo River at Big Trees gauge above flood stage.
Arroyo Corte Madera Del Presidio Mill Valley stream gauge went above flood stage during this time period.
Coyote Creek near Gilroy gauge above flood stage.
Alameda Creek near Niles gauge above flood stage.
Pacheco Creek near Dunneville gauge above flood stage.
San Francisquito Creek at Standford gauge above flood stage.
Corralitos Creek at Freedom gauge above flood stage.
California Highway Patrol reported road impassable due to roadway flooding from heavy rainfall and creek overflow on Colorado Road just south of Briceburg.
Big Sur River near Big Sur gauge above flood stage.

Rising waters behind Twenty One Mile Dam caused the dam to fail sending a 2 to 3 foot wall of water downstream. The flood waters washed out a section of State Route 233 and railroad tracks. The waters flooded buildings at the Gamble Ranch and washed out some county roads. Damages are estimated.
Sonoma Creek at Agua Caliente gauge above flood stage.
Milliken Creek at Atlas Peak Rd gauge above flood stage.
Lakeville HWY at Emies Tin Bar...west bound lanes completely flooded and east bound lanes partially flooded.
Mariposa Dam reached capacity and was being over-topped. Army Corps of Engineers was releasing water down the emergency spillway.
County emergency manager reported flooding in eastern Le Grand due to Mariposa Dam over topping its emergency spillway.
Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms generated mud and debris flow around the Sand Fire burn scar. Mud and debris flows were reported across Sand Canyon Road and Iron Canyon Road.
Heavy rain generated flash flooding at Santa Barbara airport. The airport was evacuated due to the flooding.
Heavy rain generated flash flooding as well as mud and debris flows in Ventura county. Highway 101 was closed in both directions near the Solimar burn area due to mud and debris flows.
California Highway Patrol reported water across all lanes of Highway 138 near Summit Valley Rd.
Heavy rain generated flash flooding in Ventura county near the community of Thousand Oak. In Wildwood Creek, there men were rescued from the water when the creek flooded.

Heavy rain generated flash flooding as well as mud and debris flows in Los Angeles county around the Sand Fire burn scar. Significant mud and debris flows were reported. Twenty homes were evacuated and a two inch gas pipe snapped.
Heavy rain generated flash flooding in Ventura county near the community of Camarillo. The heavy rain caused Conejo Creek to overflow its banks, flooding acres of agricultural land.
Three vehicles swept from Rodeo Dr. near Pebble Beach Park. Swift water rescues were conducted to rescue 3 people. One fatality was reported.
Flood waters from the Wintersburg Channel exceeded the channels banks, producing flooding in a mobile home park.
Kern County Roads reported mud and flash flooding along Redrock Randsburg Road and Garlock Road between State Route 14 and US Highway 395. Roadway was closed at 1920 PST.

Flood waters and related erosion caused a collapse of lane number 5 along Interstate 15. A fire truck and big rig were caught up and destroyed in the collapse. No injuries were reported but damages to the Interstate reached into the millions.
Flood waters in the Cajon Pass submerged a vehicle along Keenbrook Rd. Three swift water rescues were conduced with no injuries reported.
The Red Rock Scenic Loop and the access roads to Bonnie Springs Ranch and Spring Mountain State Park were all closed due to flooding.
Mesonet reported 1.37 in/hr from 5:30AM to 6:30AM PST.
Big Sur River at Big Sur gauge above flood stage.
Stream gauge on Alameda Creek at Niles was above flood stage between 9:30 am on February 20 and 1:00 pm on February 21.
Roadway flooding SR 152 at Casa De Fruta.
Pacheco Creek near Dunneville gauge above flood stage.

A levee breach 5-10 feet wide occurred along the San Joaquin River, 6 miles south of Lathrop. An evacuation was ordered by San Joaquin OES for south of Woodward Ave., west of Union Rd., and north of Mortensen. |Most of the areas affected are rural-agricultural areas.|As of approximately 21:00, the levee breach was plugged with rock and soil. Rip rap was applied on the waterside for wave wash protection. There were 10 structures were located near the inundation area.
State route 84 completely closed in both directions due to Alameda Creek flooding between Mission in Fremont to Main St in Sunol, 4 to 5 rock slides with flooding.
Upper Penitencia Creek at Dorel gauge above flood stage.
Stream gauge on the San Lorenzo River at Big Trees indicated the San Lorenzo River was flooding between 5:15 pm on February 20 and 12:45 am on February 21.
Stream gauge on the Belmont Creek in Belmont indicated the stream flooded between 5:29 and 7:30 pm.
Stream gauge on the Arroyo de la Laguna at Verona exceeded flood stage between 6:30 pm and 10 pm on February 20.
Stream gauge on the Pescadero River near Pescadero exceeded flood stage between 7 pm on February 20 and 12:30 am on February 21.
A 59-year-old man from Cottonwood drowned around 6:30am while attempting to cross Beaver Creek at Reay Road in Rimrock.

Heavy rain on the steep western walls of Oak Creek Canyon caused a flash flood with mud, debris, and rocks.  This flow covered Highway 89A at mile post 379. The guard rain and mile post sign were washed away.  A snowplow was called to clear the road.

A wet Pacific storm system moving through Arizona led to urban and small stream flooding in the greater Phoenix area on February 28th and caused many area washes and rivers to flow. As a result, flash flooding was observed on the west side of Phoenix near the community of Tonopah and along Interstate 10. According to local broadcast media, at 2100MST a swift water rescue of a man trapped in a vehicle occurred near Tonopah. A nearby Hassayampa river gauge with roughly zero flow jumped to 800 cubic feet per second in a matter of minutes with a flow depth of 2.5 feet reported. The fast water trapped the man and thus the need for the water rescue.
Submerged vehicle reported in low water crossing just northwest of Tularosa on Railroad Avenue in a low water crossing.
Flash Flooding was reported with a picture on Twitter at the intersection of McKinley Ave and Fine Ave in Fresno.

Radar estimated 4 to 8 inches of rainfall over a large area of the Alamogordo Creek drainage. The creek nearly reached the base of the U.S. Highway 84 bridge near Sumner Lake. Several low water crossings northeast of this area along the creek washed out.
Rangers at Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding in Grand Wash.

Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall persisted for almost 2 hours in the hills east of Yerington (near the Lyon/Mineral County line). A deputy sheriff reported a large wall of water coming down from the hills (in a typically dry wash). A National Weather Service employee investigated the scene a week later and noticed high water marks as much as 2.5 feet above Prospect St, with water damage to landscaping for multiple properties. Appreciable sediment was noted on Bybee Ln, Almond Rd, and Prospect St, with damage to Bybee Ln. (unpaved road). Damage roughly estimated based on little or no known home damage (mainly landscaping, unpaved roads).

Heavy rain fell across Lea County and produced flash flooding near Hobbs. Millen Drive east of Highway 18 was closed due to flooding. There were reports of multiple cars floating on the sides of the road and water rescues. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Spotter reported water 4 feet deep crossing Highway 52 at the low water crossing in Winston.
U.S. Highway 54 was closed for several hours after torrential rainfall and large hail flooded the roadway.
Rocks and boulders washed onto Needles Highway.
Photos posted on Facebook of moving water in the Pine Mountain Club.
Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain on the Burro Fire burn scar caused flash flooding near Rose Canyon and Scout Ranch.

Heavy rain over Kanab produced widespread flash flooding across the town. Multiple businesses suffered flood damage and approximately 20 homes had some mud or water in their basements. Many roads were flooded, and one drainage canal suffered damage.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters 11 miles W of Panamint Springs.
Highway 190 was closed due to flooding of the Centennial Wash.
Flash flooding closed Emigrant Canyon Road and West Side Road in Death Valley. The Amargosa River also flowed over the south end of West Side Road.
Cedar Creek was flowing at a gauge height of 8 feet at the bridge on Highway 73 at 1600.
The flow in Bonita Creek increased as a result of heavy rain on the Highline Fire scar. The water remained within banks and did not impact the homes in the area.

The Utah Department of Transportation reported a flash flood and debris flow in Paragonah after heavy rain fell over the Brianhead burn scar. The flood waters came down Red Creek Canyon and reached all the way down to Main Street/State Route 271 in Paragonah.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in portions of Capitol Reef National Park, including Cohab Canyon, Sulphur Creek, and Grand Wash.
Heavy rain over the Goodwin Fire scar caused a debris flow across Forest Road 67.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain over the Goodwin Fire scar. This caused dangerously high flows in Grapevine Creek. Central Avenue in Mayer was closed at Big Bug Creek because of flooding, mud, and debris over the roadway. About two feet of debris flow was observed in the creek which had been previously dry.

Heavy rainfall on the Brianhead burn scar caused flash flooding near Panguitch Lake. The flooding was most significant along the Clear Creek drainage, with water overwhelming the culverts and side roads.
Heavy rain over the Brooklyn Fire scar caused flash flooding in Black Canyon Creek. The water was flowing black from ash in the normally dry riverbed.
Hackberry Road was closed from I-40 to Highway 93 due to flooding.
Sybil Road at Dragoon Wash was impassable due to flash flooding.

Very heavy rain over the Highland Fire scar and surrounding areas produced flash flooding in Ellison Creek which flows into the East Verde River. This is a very popular swimming area during the summer. Ten people were killed by the flooding (ages 2 to 57). Four people were rescued by helicopter after they were trapped in trees.
Yavapai Flood Control reported that Fain Lake was overflowing causing flooding in Lynx Creek.

Strong thunderstorms developed in the Wickenburg area during the late afternoon hours and some of them generated locally heavy rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of one inch per hour. The extreme rainfall near Wickenburg resulted in an episode of flash flooding; at 1830MST the Wickenburg Fire Department and Rescue reported that flash flooding had closed the Sols Wash at Vulture Mine Road. A Flash Flood Warning had already been issued for the area, beginning at 1813MST and continuing past 2100MST. Fortunately there were no accidents or injuries caused by motorists driving into the flooded wash.

Isolated strong thunderstorms developed over portions of southwest Maricopa County as well as northwest Pinal County during the evening hours on July 15th and some of them produced locally heavy rainfall with peak rain rates in excess of one inch per hour. The rain led to some flash flooding along Highway 238 between the towns of Maricopa and Gila Bend. Highway 238 is very vulnerable to even modest amounts of rain near the highway as numerous washes cross the road and are easily flooded. According to the Arizona Department of Highways, at 2120MST Highway 238 was flooded at several wash crossings between milepost 40 and milepost 24. This resulted in the road being closed. Rainfall had mostly ended by late evening, however the road remained closed into the morning hours the next day when road crews were able to clean off the mud and debris over the road.
Flash flooding was reported on Scott Wash over State Route 377 between mile marker 7 and 8.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across much of the greater Phoenix area during the evening hours on July 16th, and some of the stronger storms produced locally heavy rain which fell across central portions of Phoenix including the downtown area. Rain rates between one and two inches per hour occurred and this led to flash flooding in downtown Phoenix. Heavy rain had already fallen by 2200MST and at 2229MST a Flash Flood Warning was issued for much central Phoenix. At 2246MST a trained spotter 2 miles north of central Phoenix measured 0.71 inches within 21 minutes. According to the Department of Highways, at 2237MST flash flooding occurred 1 mile northeast of Phoenix in the central downtown area; the 7th Street exit off of Interstate 10 was flooded by the torrential rains. The Flash Flood Warning remained in effect until the early morning hours on the next day.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across much of the greater Phoenix area during the evening hours on July 16th and some of the stronger storms produced locally heavy rainfall with peak rain rates between one and two inches per hour. Heavy rain fell across the western portion of the Phoenix area and resulted in minor flash flooding near Luke Air Force Base during the late evening hours. The heavy rains led to the issuance of a Flash Flood Warning as early as 2230MST and this warning persisted into the early morning hours the next day. At midnight, trained weather spotters 1 mile northeast of Luke Air Force Base reported flash flooding; Olive and Litchfield Roads near Luke AFB were inundated with water resulting in curb to curb flooding. Additionally, the Litchfield/Northern underpass was flooded.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain developed over portions of southern Gila County during the late evening hours on July 16th and some of them affected the communities of Globe and Miami. According to a report from the public, at about midnight, flash flooding developed just southeast of Claypool and between the towns of Globe and Miami. A low water crossing was closed near the Cobre Valley Community Hospital due to significant flow. The depth of the flow in Russell Gulch at the low water crossing was one foot, and the width was 100 feet.
