The North Fork of the Virgin River jumped to 180 CFS, a rise of 1.5 feet, after heavy rainfall over the headwaters overnight.
Kodachrome Basin State Park officials reported brief flash flooding of washes within the Park, including at the campground at the north end of the park.

One to two inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in the Benson and St. David areas. Several washes to overtopped in the St. David area and North Miller Rd was closed due to flooding. Ocotillo Road was closed due to flooding north of Benson.

Heavy rain over the Museum Fire scar caused flash flooding down Spruce Avenue Wash into north central Flagstaff. Debris flows, ash, logs, and flood waters up to three feet deep moved down the wash, over bridges, through streets, and the neighborhoods.
A flash flood down Dry Beaver Creek crossed Kimberlys Way making the road impassable.
Three hour rainfall of 2.5 fell at the headwaters of Rincon Creek, causing rapid rises in stream flow and flash flooding of Old Spanish Trail.
A flash flood was reported over Highway 87 between Pine and Payson. Water was over the road with almost one lane covered. A road in East Verde Estates neighborhood flooded.

Heavy rain across eastern Quay County resulted in flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 469. Local law enforcement reported that the roadway became impassable and the road was closed. There are no known impacts.
Flash flooding in Cold Creek washed out the shoulders of some roads.
The river gauge on Granite Creek near Watson Lake rose 5 feet in a flash flood due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm.
Flash flooding washed out the main access road to Old Irontown from State Route 56. Emergency managers stated the road was closed until repaired.

A 10-12 inch rise was reported on Hess Creek in Heber-Overgaard. The creek came out of its banks putting debris on the roadway and threatening one home. This prompted using sand bags to protect the home.
Water and debris flowed across State Route 21.
One foot of water flowed over the intersection of Boulder Highway and Sunset.
Main Street was flooded with water and debris.
One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in the Clifton-Morenci area. One school was damaged by floodwaters.
Hidden Valley Road was closed at the Muddy River crossing due to flooding.
Water flowed over Interstate 15 near Moapa, causing traffic to be diverted.
The Overton Wash flooded Highway 169 about two feet deep.
Cataract Creek at Redlands Crossing rose two feet in less than an hour due to heavy rainfall upstream.
A considerable area of more than 2 of rain fell in less than 1 hour east of Haekel Rd. in southeast Graham County. A section of the roadway was washed out by floodwaters near the Artesia Rd turnoff.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour in the Sunsites area caused flash flooding and the closure of Birch Rd. near Highway 191.
Half an inch of rain in 15 minutes caused flooding of Dogwood Street between Minneola Road and Spyrock Avenue.
Spencer Drive in Meadview was flooded and covered with mud.
Law enforcement reported flooding along State Route 87 and Indian Route 60 in Dilkon.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour south of San Simon caused flash flooding of roadways and resulted in the closing of Coyote Song Rd.
At least three roads were closed, at least one home was inundated, and major flooding occurred inside the park, impacting several campground cabins.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour north of Willcox caused flash flooding of roadways and the closure of Hardy Rd.
Water, rocks, and mud flooded the intersection of Old Fort Irwin Road and Old Highway 58.
Flash flooding caused mud and rock slides along Highway 168 near Aspendell, blocking the road and causing several vehicles to be stuck.
Urban flash flooding was reported in Cedar City.  A video received via social media showing water flowing down streets near the Ashdown Subdivision.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in both the main canyon and in tributaries feeding the canyon from the east.
Lillyhill Drive was flooded six to eight inches deep near Bailey Avenue.
Flash flooding occurred in a tributary of Shoal Creek. An abandoned pickup truck was observed submerged in the water.
An estimated two feet of water flowing through Banning Creek over the low water crossing on East School House Gulch Road in the community of Groom Creek.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sulphur Creek, with water running 6-12 inches high. Also flash flooding occurred in the Fremont River and Grand Wash.

Multiple sources reported flooding around Eldorado as an intense thunderstorm produced rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour. A CoCoRaHS observer in Eldorado reported 2.03 inches of rain with 1.1 inches of that falling in just 45 minutes. The heavy rainfall flooded arroyos around Eldorado. A couple residents also reported that their yards had been flooded while another resident reported that the flood waters entered their garage. Damages are estimated for the flooded garage.

A thunderstorm producing rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 14 in the Cedar Crest area southward into Pinon Ridge. A trained spotter in Cedar Crest also reported that arroyos in the area were full and storm drains were becoming overwhelmed. Extent of damages is unknown.

A thunderstorm with heavy rain rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour resulted in flash flooding across eastern portions of Albuquerque. Several reports of flooded roadways and yards in the Albuquerque foothills was received. The rainfall also quickly filled up in city's arroyos, and three people within the arroyos were swept away. Emergency crews performed water rescues for the three individuals for several hours on July 20th, but rescue efforts were not successful. Unfortunately, emergency personnel recovered the bodies of two adult men on July 21st in the diversion channel washout area, and the body of a third adult man was recovered on July 22nd. A spokesperson for Albuquerque Fire remarked that this was the deadliest flooding event in Albuquerque in recent memory.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise of 397 CFS, or about 1.5 feet.
Two feet of water flooded Temple Bar Road.
The Snowflake-Taylor Police Department reported flash flooding in Snowflake with 6 inches of water over the roadways and houses threatened in the West 1st Street area.
Two to three feet of water flooded DW Ranch Road from 1225 to 1330, and again from 1425 to 1600.
Water was flowing and estimated two feet deep over Stagecoach Road where it crosses Groom Creek.

An estimated 1.5 to 4 inches of heavy rainfall over the course of 3 hours resulted in flash flooding across the historic Picuris Pueblo. As water over topped an arroyo, flood waters rapidly entered the tribal administration building which sustained damages to the flooring. A gym, senior center, and transportation building were also hit hard by the flood waters which also all sustained various amounts of floor damage. Several grave markers in the tribal cemetery were dislodged by the flood waters. Damages to a hydrologic weir that feeds the fish hatchery pond, which houses about 5,000 fish, were also reported. No injuries or fatalities were reported, and damages are estimated.
The wash along Paradise Road flooded.
Social media post indicated road flooding in Fort Defiance.
The river gauge on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt measured a 6 foot rise.
Lewis Street in Williams was flooded.
The Bright Angel Trail in the Grand Canyon was washed out by a flash flood.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gage on Powder House wash near Powder House Wash Road reached alarm stage and flood waters continued into and down Constellation Road and flooded the intersection with Jack Burden Road. A nearby rain gage measured 2.09 inches of rain in 56 minutes. The Public Works Department had to remove sand and debris from the road the following day. No damages or injuries were reported.
Havasu Creek at Supai rose 18 inches in about an hour. It took six hours for the creek to return to normal.
Water flowed over Stockton Hill Road.

Hassayampa River Preserve closed several trails due to water/debris with a sudden rise in the Hassayampa River. Palm Lake in the reserve reportedly rose by 3 feet due to flood waters and video from the day after the heavy rain showed evidence of 1-3 feet of flow in the typically dry river bed. A USGS streamflow gage a few miles downstream measured a rapid 1 foot rise in 30 minutes. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water and debris flowed over Aztec Road and Bacobi Road near Shinarump Drive.
Water flowed over Gordon Drive.
A Capitol Reef National Park official shared a video of flash flooding in Sulphur Creek.

Heavy rain and extreme flash flooding impacted Chaco Canyon National Historical Park. Damage to roadways, including the north and south entrances to the park, was reported along with damages to the Gallo campground. One individual attempted to drive through the flooded road which prompted a successful water rescue. Due to the flooding and damages, the park was forced to close for several days. Damages are estimated.

Warm Springs was closed between Arroyo Grande and Valle Verde, water covered the intersection of Sunset and Stephanie, and the onramp from Sunset onto Interstate 515 southbound was flooded a foot deep with two cars stalled.
A weather spotter reported water running down streets in Tropic.

Beaver County dispatch and emergency management personnel reported street flooding in Milford with water 3 feet deep. In addition, debris from flooding was reported on State Route 21 near Milford. The Milford automated weather station recorded 1.10 inches of rain in one hour.

The Catron County emergency manager reported that heavy rain in Old Horse Springs resulted in flash flooding across the area. A local resident measured 3.5 inches of rain in just 45 minutes. This resulted in multiple barns and homes in the area flooded as well as the local fire department. The emergency manager also reported that several county roads had been washed away. Damages are estimated.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a 3 foot rise, with peak flows of 1800 CFS.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding along the Escalante River and Calf Creek.
Flash flooding was reported in main side canyons that flow into Marble Canyon and the Colorado River just west of Navajo Bridge. The two named side canyons were Soap Creek and Jackass.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sheets Gulch.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flooding on State Route 260 on the south side of Show Low. A car got stuck in the high water.  Flooding was also reported east of Show Low near Highway 60 and Little Mormon Lake Road meet and on to the Second Knoll Shooting Range (Forest Road 206).

One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour over east central Tucson caused flash flooding along and near Alamo Wash.  A child was rescued from flood waters near 22nd and Kolb.  Farther north, Alamo Wash overtopped Speedway Blvd and Sahuara Ave.
Runoff from a heavy rain event over the Coal Hollow Fire Burn Scar flowed over railroad tracks and onto the south shoulder of U.S. Highway 6.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Salton City with flood waters collecting in Truckhaven and Coral washes. California Highway Patrol reported flood waters were crossing Nile Drive near Atlantic Boulevard, resulting in the closure of the road. No damages or injuries reported.
Heavy rain over the Ether Hollow Fire Burn Scar produced a debris flow that moved across Quiet Meadows Lane on the outskirt of Mapleton.
Flash flooding reported near a truck stop at Sunland Gin Road and Interstate-10. Water was a few feet deep in spots. Timing estimated from radar rainfall estimates. No damages or injuries reported.
Social media video showed water flowing over Sunland Gin Road near Tonto Road. Time estimated from radar rainfall estimates. No damages or injuries reported.

Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2.5 fell in less than 1 hour in the Douglas area causing flash flooding of streets and caused the closure of Washington Ave where several homes were flooded and a block wall was knocked down by flood waters. West of town, Kings Highway just north of State Route 80 was closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain of 2 to 2.5 fell in less than 2 hours between the Pinaleno Mountains and Highway 70 west of Safford. This caused flash flooding of roads in the Pima area and significant rises in Cottonwood Wash. A large SUV which was attempting to cross the wash and carrying two adults and four children was swept away in the floodwaters. A four-year old girl drown during the rescue attempt. Her body was found four days later downstream in the Gila River near Eden.

Very heavy rain fell in the Scottsdale area beginning around 2100MST on the 22nd. A rain gage at Indian School Road and Indian Bend Wash measured a little over 2 inches in 50 minutes. A significant amount of runoff collected in Indian Bend Wash that flooded multiple low water road crossings as well as flooded recreational parks built in the wash. Osborn Road across the wash was impassable with roughly 2 feet of moving water over the road. One vehicle became stuck trying to cross the flood waters and had to be rescued by the fire department. A flood control streamflow gage on Indian School Road, a block north, exceeded alarm stage at 2146MST on the 22nd and did not fully recede below alarm stage until 0239MST on the 23rd. Helicopter footage after sunrise on the 23rd still showed minor levels of flooding in the wash. No injuries were reported.

The Thunderbird Road underpass at Interstate-17 became impassable with 2 to 3 feet of standing water after over 1 inch of rain fell in roughly one hour. One vehicle stalled in the flood water and had to be towed out. The road was eventually closed. No injuries reported.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported the Greenway Road underpass at Interstate-17 was flooded and the on/exit ramps were also under water. A couple vehicles became stranded in the flood water. This forced the closure of the underpass. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 fell in less than 1 hour along the entire length of the San Pedro River from San Manuel to Dudleyville and 3 fell near Dudleyville caused the river to rise rapidly, with a greater than 7 foot rise measured in one hour near Mammoth. Extensive flash flooding and severe damage to nearby roadways occurred in the San Manuel, Mammoth and Dudleyville areas.

A large area of 1 to 2 of rain fell in less than 90 minutes in southeast Pima County and caused extensive flash flooding from southeast Tucson and Vail southwest to Sahuarita and Green Valley. In the Vail area, three to four feet of water washed out East Andrada Rd at the Santa Rita Wash and a car was swept downstream 300 yards, but the occupants escaped unharmed.  Many roads in Saguaro National Park East were also flooded or closed.  In southeast Tucson, a person was rescued from a sandbar in the Pantano Wash near Harrison Rd. and farther south, Sahuarita and Wilmot Rds. were closed. In Sahuarita a woman was rescued from her vehicle at Beta Street and the Interstate 19 Frontage Rd.  In Green Valley, several roads were closed and homes were flooded in the Casa de Abrego neighborhood east of I-19.

Arizona Department of Transportation closed Highway-188 between mile posts 246 and 253 due to flooding with an overtopped drainage cut and debris on the road. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2020 Bush burn scar. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Flood waters in the Paria River reached the river gauge near the Colorado River at 0500 and rose 3.3 feet in 15 minutes. The flood waters likely traveled down this slot canyon from Utah through the early morning hours.
Highway US 60 was closed between Mile Post 384 and Vernon due to flash flooding.

A large area of 1 to 3 of rain fell in less than 1 hour over much of the Tucson Metro Area, including parts of the Bighorn burn scar. Around ten swift water rescues were performed during the overnight hours for motorists trapped in vehicles including near Escalante and Sarnoff. Plus, two people were rescued from the Rillito River near La Canada Dr. Also, many trails were damaged at Sabino Canyon Recreation Area and six homes were flooded in near Finger Rock Wash in the Catalina Foothills due to runoff from the Bighorn burn scar. No injuries were reported.

A local bridge along Mackey Camp Road reportedly washed out following a rapid rise in flood waters in Bloody Tanks Wash. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2021 Telegraph burn scar. Timing based on upstream rain gage and radar. No injuries reported.

A broad area of 1 to 2 of rain fell in less than 1 hour from the Tucson Mountains west to Picture Rocks. Numerous streets were flooded, closed and/or damaged as a result. At least one vehicle was stranded in flood waters, on Manville Rd.
A stream gauge on Cherry Creek reported a 3.61 foot rise.

Water in Black Canyon Creek had receded across Maren Avenue to 6 to 8 inches by the time the Sherriff officer saw it in the morning. High water marks indicated that it was much higher at the flood crest.
Several reports of over-flowing drainages, rocks, and debris on the roads making them impassable.

Hatcher Road was closed due to flooding between 11th Street and 11th Place. Nearby rain gages measured from 0.25 to 1.10 inches. Time estimated from radar and rain gages. No damages or injuries reported.

Heavy rain fell in Fountain Hills with a few rain gages measuring a little over 1 inch in an hour. Rapid runoff led to significant flow in Ashbrook Wash. Social media videos showed at least 6-12 inches of swift moving water over Fountain Hills Boulevard near Ashbrook Drive as well as over Del Cambre Avenue near Grande Boulevard. The roads were impassable to all traffic. No damages or injuries were reported.

A little over 1 inch of rain fell in roughly 1 hour east of Cave Creek between 1000MST and 1100MST. Light to moderate rain was falling beforehand and continue to fall through the early afternoon. Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported at 1335MST that Needlerock Road north of Rio Verde Drive was closed due to flooding. No injuries or damage was reported.

Two people had to be rescued from their mobile home near Central Avenue and Mingus Road after flood waters rapidly overcame the area. Water was reportedly flowing through their windows and there was concern that the home would flow away. They were rescued via helicopter because responders were unable to reach the home on the ground with multiple impassable flooded roads. Rain gages in the area measured over 1.5 inches of rain in less than an hour The two people were uninjured, but their two dogs did not survive.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gage on Cline Creek near Jenny Lin Road and 12th Street exceeded alarm stage at 1250MST and bank full at 1254MST. Flow crested at 6.9 feet at 1255MST and fell back below alarm stage at 1307MST. No injuries or damages were reported.

Very heavy rain fell in the afternoon with over 2 inches measured in the Anthem and New River area with radar estimates up to 4 inches over the New River Mesa between 1200MST and 1400MST. A social media video taken around 1400MST showed a few feet of rapid moving water running within Skunk Creek with an unoccupied SUV flowing downstream near Fig Springs Road. Timing of when flooding began estimated from radar and streamflow gages. No injuries were reported.

Significant flood water moving downstream within Skunk Creek led to the closure of the low water crossing along Honda Bow Road between 7th Avenue and 9th Avenue. Time estimated from streamflow gages and radar. No damages or injuries reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gage along Skunk Creek at Desert Hills Drive exceeded alarm stage around 1315MST and bank full around 1325MST. Streamflow crested around 5.81 feet at 1329MST and was back below action stage by 1800MST. At 1805MST Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported 19th Avenue was closed between Desert Hills Drive and Irvine Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video from Maricopa County Sheriff's Office showed two individuals being rescued via helicopter from the roof of a delivery truck that became stranded in a flooded wash near 7th street and Cloud Road. The two individuals were uninjured. The chopper footage also showed at least one home with roughly 1 to 2 fee of water surrounding it. No additional info provided on any impacted homes. Another video near 12th Street and Carefree Highway showed several inches of water flowing down 12th Street. An individual had to be rescued from their car after it became stranded in the flood water. The individual was uninjured, but the vehicle was lost.

Skunk Creek experienced a significant rise after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area and upstream. At 1400MST the the streamflow gage on Skunk Creek at Carefree Highway exceeded alarm stage. The gage then exceeded bank full at 1410MST and exceeded flood stage at 1418MST. Flow crested at 6.87 feet at 1426MST and would remain above alarm stage until 1715MST. A video posted at 1307MST on social media showed significant flow and debris over Dove Valley Road between I-17 and North Valley Parkway. Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported 27th Avenue was closed between Cloud Road and Dolores Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Street flooding was reported in and around Prescott Valley. One road in Prescott Valley was washed out due to the flooding.

A streamflow gage on New River near Table Mesa Road exceeded alarm stage at 1404MST, bank full at 1419MST, and flood stage at 1422MST. The flood wave crested at 7.88 feet at 1426MST and remained above alarm stage until 1620MST. Three individuals were rescued by Maricopa County Sheriff's Office via helicopter after their SUV stalled in the flood waters near Table Mesa Road. A low water crossing roughly 7 miles downstream along Old Stage Road, north of New River Road, experienced significant flow and the road had to be closed. No injuries were reported.

Strong thunderstorms that moved southwest through Socorro County brought heavy rain with reports of one to two inches. This resulted in widespread flooding across central Socorro County. The La Joya area was especially impacted with additional damage to the La Joya Acequia. A large section of the concrete ditch system north of La Joya was severely damaged, and several ditches and drains were filled with silt. All of the arroyos in the La Joya area flooded which washed away several of the arroyo banks and caused additional damage. The Rio Puerco River created to 17.75 feet Friday evening which was its highest level since 2013. Homes in the Contreras area were surrounded by flood water. Damages are estimated.

A strong thunderstorm near Ghost Ranch produced several inches of water along U.S. Highway 84, and mud, rock, and debris were reported along the highway between mile marker 231 and mile marker 234. Several large boulders were also noted to have fallen from cliffsides onto the shoulder of the highway. Damages are estimated for along the highway.
U.S. Forest Service reported a 4 foot rise in Camp Creek with flow originating from the Sears burn scar. Time estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Street flooding was reported in Cottonwood with water flowing over the road.
Heavy rain over the Rafael Fire caused a 4 foot rise on the Verde River at Clarkdale (an increase of at least 1,300 CFS).
Heavy rain caused Dry Creek to rise 2.5 feet in a flash flood.
Heavy rain led to multiple cars becoming stuck in mud around Radium Springs.

Heavy rain resulted in significant flash flooding near Apache Creek. The fast moving flood waters rushed through at least one home and overtopped an earthen dam. A metal tank was swept downstream, and a truck in the Apache Creek was submerged in the water. Damages are estimated.
A trained spotter in Fence Lake reported that County Road 35D had been washed out due to heavy rain in the area. Damages are estimated.
Law Enforcement reported that Highway 191 was close due to flooding in St Johns at Water Street. There was 12 to 18 inches of water covering the road.
Video received showed 2 to 3 feet deep water flowing down a street in Hildale, eroding a portion of the road.
Short Creek flooded and closed several bridges and low water crossings in Colorado City. One vehicle was rescued.

A video from social media showed swift moving water flowing down a creek in Ice House Canyon with known low water crossings along the creek. Timing was estimated from the video. No damage or injuries were reported.

Video received showed significant flows through a normally dry wash just south of Tropic, including a mature fully grown tree floating beneath an underpass along Bryce Highway. In addition, Bryce Canyon National Park officials reported the closure of the Queens Garden Trail, Navajo Loop, and the road to Bryce Point due to flooding.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in portions of the park, including the  Narrows, Kolob Canyons, and Telephone Canyon.
Water was flowing through a yard south-southeast of Concho.
The manager of Veyo Pool Resort reported a 7 foot rise on the Santa Clara River. Campsites were evacuated near the river.
The Agua Fria river gauge near Dewey-Humboldt measured a 6.5 foot rise around 1800 on July 24.  The river gauge near Cordes Junction reported a 6.7 foot rise around 240 AM on July 25..
McClaws Road was close in Holbrooke due to the flash flooding of the Little Colorado River.
A flash flood in The Little Colorado River covered the Highway 191 bridge in St Johns and made it impassable.
Flash flooding was reported along Navajo Route 4 west of Pi��on Rodeo.  The flood water was 6-12 inches deep.
Minor street flooding with some garages flooded in Wildwood Hills Mobile Home Park area of west Flagstaff.
Flash flooding covered the roads (including Highway 160) with water, mud, and rocks near Tonalea and Cow Springs.

Flood waters swept a vehicle away in a low water crossing on Camino Real near Rocky Knolls Road. The flood water was estimated to be 8 feet deep. The body of the driver was found several days later at the confluence with the Verde River.
Some roads in Cottonwood were impassable with flowing water.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 in less than 1 hour fell in Green Valley and caused flash flooding and the closure of several roads. Five homes were flooded in the Casa de Abrego neighborhood, some of which had just been flooded less than 48 hours earlier.
River Valley Road and Herold Ranch Road on the southeast side of Flagstaff were flooded and impassable.
Big Hollow Wash almost overtopped the bridge at Highway 61 west St Johns.
Kirkland Creek was flowing 4.5 feet deep (estimated) and was flowing over Highway 89. Water had begun to recede by 0630 AM.
The Agua Fria River came up 7.2 feet at the gauge on Tara Springs Road near Black Canyon City. The flood waters came from as far away as Dewey (20 straight miles).
Early morning rainfall of 1 to 1.5 on saturated ground quickly resulted in flash flooding and closure of several roads in north Marana.
Early morning rain of 1 to 1.5 on saturated ground caused flash flooding, closure and damage of Camino Adelante Rd between the Picacho Peak Interstate 10 interchange to Park Link Dr.
A trained weather spotter reported multiple running washes with 6-12 inches of running water over Warren Road in multiple locations.
Local Law Enforcement reported that Polacca Wash was overtopping State Route 264 just east of First Mesa.
A trained weather spotter reported 4-6 inches of running water over the road near Legacy Park Boulevard and Mauna Loa Lane. No damage or injuries were reported.

Local media reported that heavy rainfall led to a home being flooded near 7th Street and Carefree Highway. Water was reported to having rose 5 feet into the home causing significant flood damage. The homeowner, who also runs a personal fitness gym at the home, reported that the gym equipment was destroyed in the flooding. The location was approximated as the exact location of the home is unknown. No injuries were reported.
Major flash flooding was reported on a widely used dirt road between Whippoorwill and Low Mountain.

The Maricopa County Flood Control District's Sonoran Wash streamflow gage exceeded bank full after peaking at 5.72 feet. Downstream impacts about one mile from the streamflow gage include unbridged crossings along North Valley Parkway and Dixileta Drive. No damage or injuries were reported.
More than 1 of rain fell on saturated ground causing flash flooding of several roadways from Sahuarita to Corona De Tucson, including Sahuarita Rd. near Wilmot Rd.

A photo shows a vehicle became stranded in two to three feet of water near the intersection of Dell Webb Boulevard and Bell Road. Timing estimated from radar and other nearby reports. No injuries were reported and extent of water damage to the vehicle is unknown.

Multiple water rescues were reported in Sun City, including 98th Avenue and Granada Drive as well as 99th Avenue and Burns Drive. A flood control channel along the center of 99th Avenue was also reported to be overflowing onto the street. As a result, a Maricopa County Sheriff's Office deputy stopped southbound traffic at Desert Rock Drive due to the depth of the water. No injuries were reported.
A water rescue was reported at 107th Avenue and Mountain View Road. No injuries were reported.

One to two inches of rain on saturated ground cause numerous flooded and closed roads in the Vail area from just east of Rita Ranch to Old Spanish Trail and south to near Interstate 10. One vehicle was stuck in floodwaters near Old Spanish Trail and Drexel Rd.

The Arizona Department of Transportation reported that Highway 238 was closed between MP 14 and 38, which runs through both Maricopa and Pinal Counties, due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Several lanes on I-10 near 75th Avenue and 91st Avenue were flooded and became impassable. The I-10 westbound off-ramp at 59th Avenue was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed several feet of standing water in the parking lot of an apartment, flooding numerous cars at the apartment. No injuries were reported.

Emergency management reported multiple road closures in Buckeye due to flooding. Roads that were closed after experiencing flooding include Dean Road and Broadway Road, Lower Buckeye Road between Watson Road and Rainbow Road, Verrado Way and Broadway Road, and Verrado Way and Yuma Road. No damage or injuries were reported.
Social media video from local media showed three vehicles stuck in the flooded intersection at 107th Avenue and Union Hills Drive. No injuries were reported.
County Public Works reported Price Road east of SR 79 in the Florence area was closed due to flooding. No injuries were reported.
A social media post showed knee deep water covering the road near Skyline Drive and Felix Road. No damage or injuries were reported.

A trained weather spotter reported that Bloody Tanks Wash was running near bankfull and containing debris. Water levels were reported to still be on the rise. The high flow in the wash was the result of heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph fire burn scar, leading to enhanced runoff. No damage or injuries were reported.

Heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph fire burn scar led to enhanced runoff into Pinal Creek. Video from a trained weather spotter showed significant flow through Pinal Creek impacting the unbridged crossing at Beer Tree Crossing and Jesse Hayes Road in Globe. No damage or injuries were reported.

Video obtained by KOAT TV showed flash flooding in Angus with fast moving water rushing against a home and leaking underneath the doorway. No significant damages are known, and damages are estimated for minor home flood damage.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gage at Waterman Wash exceeded alarm stage, peaking at 4.66 feet and impacting downstream unbridged crossings along Tuthill Road and Narramore Road. Roads in this area along the wash were closed with social media videos showing swift moving water impacting these roads. No damage or injuries were reported.
The Iron County Emergency Manager reported flooding in Parowan. Floodwaters moved protective concrete barriers for the power plant and pushed them into the power plant  building.
Up to 1 of rain on saturated ground caused Franco Wash to rise rapidly and flood and damage several roads in the Summit area.

Video received showed deep and swift moving water flowing westward down Center Street and 700 E in Paragonah. Flows originated from Red Creek, which empties into Paragonah from the east. Radar estimated up to 2.15 inches of rain upstream over the Red Creek drainage.

The Sycamore Creek USGS gage (SYCA3) near Fort McDowell recorded a rapid rise with a 6 foot rise in 1.5 hours, cresting at 6.4 feet. This rapid rise is attributed to heavy rain that fell over the Bush fire burn scar, leading to enhanced runoff.
An official with Joshua Tree National Park reported that Lost Horse Mine Road, Keys View Road, and Geology Tour Road were closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain dislodged rocks that fell on Highway 89 between Flagstaff and Sedona (switchbacks near FR-237).
Heavy rain caused the Verde River to rise 2 feet (near the junction of the Verde River and Sycamore Creek).
A pickup truck tried to cross a flooded intersection on Queens Bay Road and got swept downstream.

Several videos shared by broadcast media and social media showed instances of multiple vehicles getting stuck and/or swept away with multiple people having to be rescued in flash flood waters in Lower Sycamore Creek between the Verde River and Forest Service Road 403. Videos showed an SUV overturning in the creek with two men and an eight-year-old boy still inside. They were able to escape the vehicle with bystanders helping to pull them to safety on land. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

Tonopah-Salome Highway between 315th Avenue and 339th Avenue was closed due to flooding. This part of the highway is unbridged and crosses through the Hassayampa River. Timing estimated from a Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gage along the Hassayampa River. No damage or injuries were reported.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to East Austin Peak Road, and Knight Creek Road was closed from Hackberry Road to milepost 4.6 due to flooding.
A trained weather spotter reported several inches of flowing water over the roadway near SR 177 and Kaiser Road. No damage or injuries were reported.
Antares Road was closed from Highway 66 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding.

Heavy rain in Jemez Springs resulted in the Jemez River to overflow its banks. People who were near the river were forced to move their cars away from their houses to prevent them from washing away. One observer noted that this was the highest they had seen the Jemez River in 25 years. No damages were known.

According to the California Department of Transportation, there were multiple reports of mud and debris covering SR 177 in multiple locations near Desert Lily Sanctuary as running washes flowed over the road, impeding travel. No damage or injuries were reported.
There were at least four swift water rescues, and numerous roads were closed.
Flooding left debris across Valley of Fire Highway.
Waist deep water flowed over the intersection of Bank Street and Calle Castano.

A vehicle was caught in the flood waters of Dinnebito Wash near Route 6720 and Saltwater Wash. There was one fatality and two others trapped in the water. This was located about 72 air miles downstream from the headwaters of this wash.

A vehicle was caught in the flood waters of Dinnebito Wash near Route 6720 and Saltwater Wash. There was one fatality and two others trapped in the water. This was located about 72 air miles downstream from the headwaters of this wash.

A video on social media showed a tractor trailer attempting to cross a flooded part of Highway 95 at MP 61. As the tractor trailer drove through the flowing flood waters, it quickly tipped over onto its side. According to the Arizona Department of Transportation, Highway 95 ended up closing due to the flooding. No injuries were reported.
Hackberry Road was closed from Main Street to Route 66 due to flooding.
The Arizona Department of Transportation reported water, mud, rocks, and debris flowing onto Riverside Drive in Parker, impeding travel. No damage or injuries were reported.
Lakeshore Road and Boulder Beach Frontage Road were covered with two feet of debris, including basketball sized rocks, due to flash flooding.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported six feet of water flowed over a flood control barrier in Paragonah, resulting in flash flooding in the city. Several homes were flooded. Fifty people were stranded in Red Creek Canyon east of the city.
Oatman Highway was closed due to flooding.
The intersection of Oatman Highway and Route 66 was flooded.
Signal Road was closed from Highway 93 to Alamo Road due to flooding.

Radar estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rainfall at the mouth of Box Canyon which caused flash flooding at the entrance of Box Canyon Road and along Painted Canyon Road. There were a couple vehicles involved with the flooding which caused a road closure. Located south of I-10 and north of Highway 111.

According to local officials, Box Canyon Road near Shavers Well was closed due to sand and rock debris across the road due to flooding. Emergency Management also reported that flooding caused some shoulder damage along the road. Timing was estimated from the first call to California Highway Patrol regarding Box Canyon Road at 0408PDT. No injuries were reported.
One vehicle swept off the roadway on box canyon road with 10 to 12 other vehicles potentially stranded.
Caltrans reports boulders in the roadway near Vista Point on SR 74.

Damage and washed out section of concrete sidewalk as embankment gave way to flooding along Country Club Drive and Avenue 42. Water covered roadway on Jefferson Street. Photos shared by emergency management. Rain of 0.70 inch per hour observed.
Flooding on Varner road near Bermuda Dunes.
Water, mud, boulders, and debris flowed over Calico Basin Road.
Several roads were closed due to flooding, and approximately 20 swift water rescues occurred.
Highway 127 was flooded and impassable.
The intersection of Blue Diamond Road and Rainbow Boulevard was closed due to flooding.
Highway 127 was flooded.
A significant flash flood wave in Pine Creek was reported by Zion National Park staff.

Strong thunderstorms near Encinoso produced an estimated 1.5 to 2 inches of rainfall. This resulted in severe flooding along New Mexico State Road 246 which forced the closure of the roadway from mile marker 18 to mile marker 36. Damages are estimated for the washed out roadway.
Echo Dam Road and Rose Valley Road were flooded.
The intersection of Highway 190 and Cow Creek Road was impassable due to mud and water. Flooding also damaged a water main, cutting off water service to nearby homes.
State Line Road was flooded east of Death Valley Junction.

A strong thunderstorm produced an estimated 1 inch of heavy rainfall in a short period of time on the Ute Park burn scar. This resulted in rapid runoff with emergency personnel reporting a six foot wall of water that flowed through Ute Park with a three foot rise of water in Cimarron. This damaged many roads in the area and trapped numerous residents within their homes. No injuries or fatalities resulted from the flash flooding. Damages are estimated.
Water one to two feet deep flowed over the intersection of Highway 190 and Beatty Road.
Twenty Mule Team Road was closed due to flooding.
Water flowed across many roadways in Cedar City, including across Interstate 15 near milepost 59.
Titus Canyon Road was closed due to flooding.
The Escalante River gauge near Escalante indicated a rise from 3 CFS to 1060 CFS, a rise of 4 feet.
A video showed flash flooding at the confluence of Birch and North Creeks into the Escalante River.
Water and mud covered 2 lanes of Highway 70 at the intersection of Owen Road.
Main Street in Pioche was flooded with water, rocks, and debris.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported that significant damage was sustained on House Rock Road near Wire Pass due to flash flooding.

An estimated 2.5 to 3.5 inches of heavy rainfall in under an hour caused flash flooding in Placitas. Several roads and drainage ditches in the Placitas area were flooded with mud and debris also covering roadways. Damages are estimated.
A received video showed a flood wave with significant debris moving through Big Water, UT.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 23 CFS to 1450 CFS with the primary flood wave.  The time above 1000 CFS was from 2315 MDT to 0130 MDT.
Heavy rain over the Paria River drainage (in Arizona and Utah) caused the river gauge at Lees Ferry to rise 2.5 feet.

An estimated quarter of one inch of rain in under one hour on the Luna burn scar resulted in flash flooding in the area and areas downstream. This resulted in building damage along Luna Creek in Luna Canyon. The number of buildings damaged and to what extent is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding across Scenic Drive in multiple locations, including Grand Wash and across State Route 24, closing the road. A muddy debris flow was also reported in Sulphur Creek.
One to two inches of rain fell in less than 1 hour in Nogales and caused flash flooding of several roads and minor damage to a couple of homes near Western Ave.

A trained weather spotter reported that high flow in Pinal Creek made Beer Tree Crossing Road in the Globe area impassable. The high flow in Pinal Creek was the result of heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph fire burn scar, leading to enhanced runoff. No damage or injuries were reported.

Around 2.5 of rain in less than 1 hour was measured near the headwaters of Sabino Creek in the Bighorn burn scar and caused a two-foot rise in the stream that crosses trails in the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area. Six hikers had to be rescued after becoming trapped by the high flows.

Heavy rain in northeast Albuquerque resulted in the city's arroyos filling quickly with fast-moving water. Albuquerque Fire and Rescue reported that two people were caught in the arroyo's flood water. One person was able to escape, but rescue efforts were not successful on the second individual. A woman's body was recovered the next day in the diversion channel.

Heavy rain of 2.5 in less than 90 minutes occurred near the headwaters of Rincon Creek. Flash flooding occurred downstream in the Rincon Ranch Estates area. Camino Loma Alta became flooded and impassible.

A strong thunderstorm near the Colorado and New Mexico border produced flash flooding along the La Plata River. No structures were damaged, but water did cover the roadway along New Mexico State Road 170 and nearby roadways such as Road 1788 south of La Plata. Water marks suggested that the flood waters covering the roadway were about 100 yards wide and 2 to 3 feet deep.
Major portions of the Twin Arrows Casino were flooded. Flood debris went all over their roads.

Officials with Joshua Tree National Park reported several inches of swiftly moving water flowing over Indian Cove Road, making the road impassable. Timing was estimated using radar. No damage or injuries were reported.

Officials with Joshua Tree National Park reported that vehicles traveling along Pinto Basin Road Between Fried Liver Wash and Turkey Flats were forced to turn around due to several inches of swiftly moving water flowing over the roadway due to running washes. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain led to flash flooding in downtown Moab.
A thunderstorm with heavy rain produced heavy runoff into washes and roadways. One barn northeast of Shumway had water running through it (2 inches in 45 to 60 minutes). .
Flooding was reported on McLaws Road in Holbrook.
A COOP observer near Cuba reported heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding in the area with drainages overflowing along with inundation across fields. No damages are known.

After 2.5-3.5 inches of rain fell over the northern portion of the Telegraph burn scar, runoff rapidly collected in Bloody Tanks Wash and flowed downstream through the town of Miami causing catastrophic damage. A rain gage in Russell Gulch to the south measured 2.01 inches of rain between 1316MST and 1414MST with a brief period where rain rates were as high as 8-9 inches per hour with 0.87 inches measured in 10 minutes. At 1438MST Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) reported US-60 was closed in both directions at mile post 243 due to water moving over the road. Between 1440MST and 1500MST, a trained spottered reported the flood water was coming out of the banks of the wash at the intersection of Canyon Avenue and US-60 and video showed 6 to 8 feet of flood water in the wash coming up to the base of multiple bridges between Sullivan Street and US-60. Water and mud spilled out of the wash near Cordova Avenue, with flow down Sullivan Street, and entered homes and businesses. ADOT ended up having US-60 closed in both directions between Miami and the town of Superior until 1920MST. According to Gila County Emergency Management and Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs, approximately 600 homes and 10 businesses experienced some form of flood damage.  No injuries were reported and the full extent of damage costs are unknown.
Heavy rain of 2 to 3 in less than 1 hour at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument caused flash flooding of roadways making them impassible.

At 1600MST, Arizona Department of Transportation reported Highway 188 was closed in both directions at mile post 219 due to flooding of Pinal Creek. Flood water originated from the Telegraph burn scar with flow from Bloody Tanks Wash and Russell Gulch merging into Pinal Creek. Timing of initial flood wave estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Chapter House in the community of Cornfields reported flash flooding in five areas along Indian Route 15 between the communities of Greasewood and Burnside, including  near the community of Cornfields.  The road was covered with more than two feet of water, heavy debris, and thick mud.
State Highway 60 was close due to flooding about 14 air miles south of Cibecue.
Pump Station Road was closed from Highway 93 to Back Road due to flooding.

Several reports of flash flooding in and around Escalante, including Birch Creek. Storm spotters reported logs and trees floating in the Escalante River just north of Escalante. Time of event coincident with time of first report.
Four feet of water was flowing through Poquito Wash. Flooding was also reported in near buy near-by homes in north Prescott Valley.

The USGS stream gage along Pinal Creek at Inspiration Dam near Globe measured an approximate rise of 4.25 feet in a 15 minute period. The gage recorded a peak of 5.73 feet at 1820MST. No damage or injuries were reported.

One inch of rain in less than 90 minutes caused rapid rises in Josephine Canyon. Two teenagers swimming near a waterfall were swept downstream by a rapid rise in the water level. One teenager drowned and another escaped the floodwaters while sustaining minor injuries and was later rescued.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported 5 inches of debris, mud, and gravel overflowing the Scenic Drive by the Capitol Gorge area. High-flowing water was also reported in a usually dry wash at the end of the Scenic Drive. Scenic Drive was closed beyond Grand Wash.

A USGS gage along Cave Creek below Cottonwood Creek recorded a rapid rise and exceeded action stage. This gage measured an approximate rise of 5 feet in a 20 minute period and crested at 8.05 feet at 2030MST. No damage or injuries were reported.

A USGS stream gage along Tonto Creek above Gun Creek recorded a rapid rise, peaking above 6.9 feet, with high flow exceeding action stage. Flash flooding impacted unbridged crossings along Tonto Creek downstream of the gage. The public confirmed the closure of unbridged crossings due to the flooding. Timing was estimated from the gage reaching action stage. No damage or injuries were reported.
Local Law Enforcement reported that the flash flooding left large rocks, trees, bushes, and debris on area roads. Public works was called out to clean up the mess.
A Zion Nation Park ranger reported significant flash flooding occurred on Taylor Creek at the north end of the Kolob Canyon area of the park during the night.

Washington County dispatch officials reported water over the road on State Route 17 near Toquerville, briefly closing the road.  The bridge where water crossed the road is above full grown trees in the creek below, indicating a significant rise in water level.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 27 CFS to 493 CFS in 15 minutes, a rise of 1.5 feet.

Significant debris flow occurred 1:30 to 2:00 pm on July 30 on Highway 38 along northern portions of the El Dorado burn scar. CalTrans reports road closure both directions on Highway 38 from Glass Road to Seven Oaks due to rock and mudslides on roadway. Restriction from Forest Falls to Lake Williams Drive. Radar has large thunderstorms over Highway 38 and Upper Santa Ana watershed estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rain on radar in Frog Creek, Barton Creek and South Fork Santa Ana River.||Most significant flows occurred between PM 24.1 and 25.2, where boulders up to 1 m in diameter (potentially up to 2 m) moved. Net anchors initially held and restrained the initial surge of debris, but the volume eventually overtopped the nets and filled catchment basins. Debris overtopped a catchment basin at VAR EF0094 (west fork of the creek) and flowed onto the highway, resulting in a debris flow 150 feet wide and 5 feet deep.|||Vehicles reported stuck and road is impassable at 3 locations. Highway 38 was closed for 7 hours due to several areas of debris flows. Large rocks, logs, mud and boulders being removed. Some damage reported to road. 4300 cubic yards or 400 truckloads were removed from Highway 38.
The intersection of Highway 247 and Highway 62 was flooded.
Mud and rocks covered Highway 190.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding from Washington Park to Tonto Village. Water was cascading through yards and flooding roadways. The East Verde River rose 3 feet near Washington Park at 540 PM MST.

Prolonged and heavy rainfall from showers parked over the Ruby Mountains produced radar estimated rainfall accumulations of 2 to 3 inches. This caused flash flooding and an area of debris flow including mud, sand, and rock over the roadway. It was estimated some spots of debris be 2 to 4 feet deep on the roadway per photos and first-hand reports.
The intersection of Highway 62 and Sunfair Road was flooded.

A video on social media showed several inches of water across the roadway along Park Boulevard and Pinto Basin Road in Joshua Tree National Park, impeding travel. The owner of the video reported that there was heavy flooding and roads washed out in multiple locations from the north entrance of the park to the south entrance. The location was approximated from the report in combination with known areas with low water crossings and flood prone areas along Park Boulevard and Pinto Basin Road. No damage or injuries were reported.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour from south of Ajo to east of Why. This caused flash flooding of area washes and the closure of Highway 86 east of Why and Highway 85 between Ajo and Why.
Water and mud covered the road at Zabriskie Point, and flooding was estimated to extend as far north as Furnace Creek.
California Highway Patrol reported that Ogilby Road between I-8 and SR 78 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
California Highway Patrol reported that Araz Road at I-8 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

Cal Fire/Riverside County Fire Department reported that a vehicle was trapped in flowing water approximately 3 feet deep on Power Line Road near the I-10 Red Cloud Mine Road exit. Two occupants and a dog were rescued from the vehicle with no injuries reported.
Spotter reported 4-6 inches of water running where Fish Springs and Jacobsen Lane meet. Nearby Pine Nut Creek full due to runoff on the Numbers Fire burn scar.

One to two inches of rain fell in less than 1 hour northeast of the Tucson International Airport causing flash flooding of area roads. One swift water rescue was conducted for a vehicle stalled in a wash.
More than 1 of rain fell in less than 1 hour along South Wilmot Rd causing flash flooding and the closure of the roadway north of Sahuarita Rd.
Highway 93 was closed at Lincoln County mile marker 81 due to water and mud on the road.

A CoCoRaHS observer reported flash flooding along Luna Creek and Luna Canyon Road that resulted from heavy rain along the Luna burn scar north of Chacon. The observer also reported that some structures in the area had been damaged, but the extent or type of structures that sustained damage is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.
A family of 5 was hit by a flash flood in  Labyrinth Canyon that drains into Lake Powell. The wife and mother drowned.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported up to 2.5 feet of water on streets in Enoch, as well as water breaching into homes. The water was deepest near Homestead Boulevard. Several homes were flooded.
Law enforcement reported 6 to 12 inches of water flowing across SR-228. A vehicle driving along the road was washed off the road and pushed into the ditch.

A National Weather Service employee in Madrid measured 1.85 inches of rain from a thunderstorm producing heavy rain. This led to flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 14 in Madrid and south of Los Cerillos along with mud and other debris washed onto the roadway. Damages are a rough estimate.
Law enforcement reported 6 to 12 inches of water flowing across lower South Fork Road. A vehicle driving along the road was washed off the road and pushed into the ditch, no one was injured.
Law enforcement officials reported a debris flow moved through the Pinnacles and Promised Land Resort areas.
The Verde River gauge  12 miles north-northwest of Jerome showed a 2.5 foot rise.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sunglow Canyon.
A debris flow was reported into the Elk Ridge area.

Zion National Park dispatch personnel reported numerous slot canyons experienced flooding, including Pine Creek and Spry Canyon. The Zion automated weather station recorded 1.29 inches of rain in one hour. In addition, the East Fork Virgin stream gauge on the East Fort Virgin River near Springdale recorded a peak flow of 2790 CFS.
Water and debris flowed over Stockton Hill Road.
Nevada DOT reported flooding across US 95 east of Hawthorne at mile marker 40 and flooding across US 95 between Mina and 9 miles north of Mina. The road was closed near Mina due to flooding.
Antares Road was closed after flooding carved a foot deep rut into the road.
Hildale Fire Department dispatch personnel reported water flowing over three street crossings. The streets were closed due to the flows.
The Virgin stream gauge on the Virgin River at Virgin spiked from 108 CFS to 2180 CFS, a rise of over 3 feet.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a peak flow of 865 CFS.

Heavy rain was reported in the are with some estimates of 1-2 inches of rainfall. Law Enforcement reported several inches of water over US Highway 50 at mile marker 9. They also reported several inches of water across SR-488, 487, and US-6.
An observer reported 3 feet of rocks, mud, and water flooded into a ranch basement and nearly moved a second home off its foundation near the Crawford Mountains.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek and the Fremont River, along with muddy conditions on Scenic Drive. The initial flood wave through Sulphur Creek contained black boulders.
County dispatch reported Kingston Canyon was underwater with rock and debris over a portion of state Route 62.
A debris flow moved across a road in Timber Canyon.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in Enoch and Cedar City, with up to 300 homes damaged by flood waters.  Water rescues were performed, and cars were swept off the road.  Interstate 15 was closed during the event.  Numerous roads were eroded by floodwaters, and Fiddlers Canyon was reported underwater.

At least 15 different debris flows were caused by previous thunderstorms/heavy rain during the afternoon. Multiple reports came from the US Forest Service, Elko County Road Department, and Nevada Department of Transportation. USFS 660 will be closed until further notice. The height of debris flows is estimated to be between 4 and 8 feet within a 4-mile length of road.
Substantial flooding was reported within Vernon. County Roads 3131, 3137, and 3187 were impassable.
In Tooele, 37 homes were flooded. Additionally, multiple roads were closed due to flooding.
Big Cottonwood Canyon Road was closed due to flash flooding carrying debris and rocks across the roadway.
Flash flooding was reported on the Bountiful Bench, with water flowing through a home.
Water and debris were flowing over the roadways in Polacca/Second Mesa.
A photo on social media showed a dirt road that was partially washed out north of Greasewood Springs Chapter House. A video on social media also showed a significant rise on wash.
A creek in Payson rose 19 inches. Water was flowing across one lane of Highway 87.
A video showed a significant rise of water flowing through the wash.

A USGS stream gage along Cibecue Creek near Chrysotile, Arizona recorded a rapid rise of over 4 feet in less than 15 minutes. At 2205MST, the creek crested at 6.9 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.

A significant flood wave carrying debris moved down Bear Creek Canyon, sweeping away mining vehicles at the Gentry Mountain Mine. Several miners were caught in the flood waters, with one miner able to save himself by clinging to a tree a quarter mile down the drainage. Another miner was not able to escape the flood waters and was found deceased 6 miles downstream. Another Mine car was flipped 8 times in the flood waters, but the miners were able to kick out the windows and escape. Significant infrastructure damage occurred at the Mine.
UDOT reported two flash floods the Trail Mountain Fire burn scar flowed across state Route 31 between milepost 40 and milepost 44.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on several drainages in the Park.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding of washes across roadways in northeast Tucson. One vehicle became stranded in floodwaters near Tanque Verde Rd and Conestoga Ave.

Another 1 to 2 of heavy rain in less than an hour with a 3-hour total of 2 to 4 caused additional flash flooding of washes and roadways on Tucson's northeast side. Three people were rescued when their vehicle was swept down Bonanza Wash near Bonanza Ave. and E Forest Grove Loop.
Two to four inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes up to 3 feet deep across Arivaca Rd. prompting its closure.
Two to four inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes up to 3 feet deep across Arivaca Rd. prompting its closure.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour southwest of Rio Rico caused roads in the area to become flooded and impassable.
One to two inches of rain fell in less than two hours east and southwest of Gleeson causing flash flooding across parts of Gleeson and Davis Rds.
One inch of rain in 30 minutes caused a rapid rise in Dragoon Wash and flash flooding across Sabin Rd. near St. David, making it impassable.
Highway 62 near mile marker 42 was flooded with two feet of flowing water and large debris.
A trained spotter reported that Lynx Creek in Walker was running four to five feet deep in spots.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than one hour near Kohatk resulted in minor flooding of two homes in that village.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours over the Bighorn burn scar area in the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding of several washes and roadways.  Sutherland Wash rose over 5 feet at a gauge just east of Oro Valley and the Canada del Oro Wash also rose, especially downstream of its confluence with the Sutherland Wash. Downstream flash flooding resulted at Overton Rd where 5 people were rescued from two different vehicles which were swept downstream.

Loop 202 westbound exit ramp to Gilbert Road in Chandler was closed due to flooding. Nearby Chandler Airport measured 2.68 inches of rain from approximately 0700MST to 0900MST with 2.13 inches falling in 1 hour. The exit ramp did not re-open until around 1100MST. No injuries or damages were reported.

Over one inch of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Sabino Canyon Recreation area and the closure of roadways. Several hikers were stranded and needed to be rescued after floodwaters rose.

A streamflow gage on Vekol Wash at Ralston Road experienced a 2 foot rise in roughly 25 to 30 minutes, from 0.15 feet at 1154MST to 2.14 feet at 1220MST. A webcam from the gage showed Ralston Road was impassable to traffic. The flood waters originated several miles upstream from thunderstorms just south of Interstate-8 (I-8) near the Pinal and Maricopa county border. A streamflow gage on Vekol wash near I-8 also registered a 2 foot rise in roughly 1 hour, from 4.95 feet (base value) at 0720MST to 6.94 feet (crest) at 0816MST. Radar estimated rainfall in the area of Vekol wash and I-8 was around 1 inch. Flood waters took roughly 4 hours to travel from I-8 to Ralston Road. Although not reported, Val Vista Road, Peters and Nall Road, and Farrell Road may have also experienced impacts. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain of 2 to 3 inches in less than an hour caused flash flooding of several roads in the Sierra Vista area including Moson Rd. and Nevada Rd. A fence near a residence was downed by a wall of water. The water line to the home was also damaged.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed from mile marker 13 to Antares Road due to flooding.

A stream gauge on Granite Creek (northeast of downtown Prescott--GRCA3) reported a 6.7 foot rise with a peak flow of 3,558 CFS.  At least five roads were closed in Prescott due to flooding between 2:50 and 3:50 PM.  Several roads were also closed in Wilhoit due to flooding.  Two cars were stuck in flowing washes near Chino Valley/Paulden. Water was beginning to move the vehicles so Law Enforcement was called to the scene.
Antares Road was closed from Route 66 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Davis Rd. between Tombstone and McNeal.
The intersection of Morrow and Burbank was flooded.
Eight inches of water flowed over Bank Street just north of the high school.
Bogeles Ranch Road was closed from Upper Trout Creek Road due to flooding.
Huffritter Road was closed from Highway 93 to Back Road due to flooding.
Pump Station Road was closed from Highway 93 to Back Road due to flooding.
State Route 95 was closed at mile post 111 due to flooding. Time estimated by radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Highway 86 near Indian Route 26 northwest of Sells.

Video on social media, posted at 2057MST, showed an estimated 6 inches of swift-moving water through the intersection of Mockingbird Street and Plymouth Road in Quartzsite. Timing based on radar. No damages or injuries reported.
CHP reports flash flooding at Borrego Salton Seaway road at Fonts wash, where a car was stuck in the low water crossing.

Highway 78 was closed due to flooding, first reported at 2237MST by California Highway Patrol. Imperial County Public Works also received unconfirmed reports of damages to county roads in Palo Verde Valley. Onset of flooding impacts estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flash flooding reported by Desert Research Institute officials morning after heavy rains went through the area. Monsoon storms led to flash flooding of Coyote Canyon and adjacent citrus tree fields.
Oatman Highway was closed from Ramada Road to Cool Springs due to flooding.

Reports of water and mud covered Borrego Valley Airport after the storm's heavy rainfall. Pilots were not able to land on the runway. The airport also reported blowing dust with two miles of visibility and a wind gust to 40 mph.

An Imperial County Public Works official reported there were multiple washouts along Ogilby Road, after heavy rain impacted the area, that would take a few days to repair. Ogilby Road had to be closed to traffic as a result. There were two areas east of the road with radar estimated rainfall of around 2 inches and several washes flow toward and across Ogilby road. The specific locations of flooding impacts and extent of damages to the road were not shared. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

A large area of two inches of rain occurred in three hours in east Tucson, generally east of Craycroft Rd. to the Rincon Mts. with more than 4 inches of rain from Broadway and Wilmot to Tanque Verde and Pantano Rds.  Numerous roads were flooded or damaged including Pima Rd. and Robb Wash. Several swift water rescues of motorists occurred including one vehicle washed downstream near Camino Loma Alta and Old Spanish Trail. Alamo Wash left its banks and flooded several homes between Pima and Speedway.
One inch of rain in less than 1 hour in Catalina Foothills caused flash flooding of River Rd. near Pontatoc Rd.
Heavy rain of 2 to 3.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes and the closure of many roadways in Green Valley.

The Arizona Department of Transportation reported that US 60 was closed between Superior and Miami (mileposts 226-243) due to water over the roadway and erosion causing damage to a guardrail and right lane of the highway along Bloody Tanks Wash near milepost 242. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1 to 2 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in rural areas west of Green Valley. Mission Rd. north of Duval Mine Rd. was closed.

The USGS stream gage along Sycamore Creek near Fort McDowell recorded two rapid rises during the morning on the 11th. A 2.73 foot rise occurred in 15 minutes from 0900MST to 0915MST and a 3.60 foot rise occurred in 30 minutes from 1030MST to 1100MST. At 1100MST, the creek crested at 6.29 feet. No injuries or damage were reported.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour along Whitewater Draw caused flash flooding downstream where a vehicle abandoned in floodwaters was swept downstream at Kings Hwy. Brooks Rd. was also closed.

A photo on social media showed flash flooding occurring in Flying E Wash in Wickenburg with significant flow over Vulture Mine Road north of US 60, resulting in the closure of the road. No damage or injuries were reported.
There were several roads closed in the Prescott area due to flash flooding.

The Arizona Department of Transportation reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. The location was estimated based on the area with the heaviest rainfall and information provided on social media by ADOT. No damage or injuries were reported.
NMDOT reported water flowing across Highway 9 about 19 miles west of Columbus.

Increased flow in Waterman Wash led to flash flooding at a low water crossing on Narramore Road, resulting in a closure of the road. A nearby Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road recorded a peak flow of 2.51 feet. Timing was estimated using the nearby stream gage.

A broad area of 1.5 of rain, with pockets of 3 to 4, fell in less than 90 minutes and caused numerous road closures from Picture Rocks to Saguaro National Park West to southeast of Three Points. Kinney Rd. near Sonora Desert Museum was one of the major roads that was closed due to flooding.

Videos on social media showed a low water crossing along Bartlett Dam Road at Camp Creek being impassable as a result of approximately 6-8 inches of flowing water over the road. Additionally, Horseshoe Dam Road between Bartlett Dam Road and Horseshoe Lake was closed by Tonto National Forest due to flood damage. No injuries were reported.

Heavy rainfall over the Bush burn scar led to enhanced runoff into Sycamore Creek. A USGS stream gage along Sycamore Creek near Fort McDowell recorded a rapid 10 foot rise in the creek approximately between 0500MST and 0600MST. At 0600MST, the creek crested at 11.15 feet. No injuries or damage were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage recorded Cave Creek north of Carefree Highway climbing above alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings such as Canyon Creek Road. At 0632MST, the creek crested at 6.06 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.
The Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported that Needlerock Road was closed at Rio Verde Drive due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Skunk Creek climbed above alarm stage, impacting downstream roads such as Dixileta Drive. The gage peaked at 3.60 feet. Timing was estimated based on travel time information provided by the Maricopa County Flood Control District. No damage or injuries were reported.
Highway patrol reported to the Arizona Department of Transportation that flooding was occurring on SR 238, leading to the closure of the highway. No injuries or damage were reported.
Photos from broadcast media indicated water and mud over a roadway in Kanab.

Heavy rain with totals of two to three inches within an hour produced flash flooding along New Mexico State Highway 272. A trained spotter reported that the highway near Fort Sumner was impassable due to water over the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Richard Street was closed for five to ten minutes due to flooding of Short Creek.

Water topped an earthen dam and resulted in flooding across much of La Union. Several cars were washed off the road and some houses were inaccessible for awile. Several inches of standing water also resulted across the area due to the heavy rain. This was all the result of almost 2 inches of rain in about an hour.
The La Paz County Sheriff's Office reported that traffic was at a standstill along Highway 72 north of Bouse due to a wash running across the roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.
Water and debris were over Northshore Road near mile marker 8.

Heavy rain near Nogal forced the closure of U.S. Highway 380 from mile marker 74 to mile marker 76. Per a trained spotter, the bridge in the area was unsafe to cross as road surfaces had been damaged from repeated rounds of heavy rain over the summer.
One inch of rain in 30 minutes caused flash flooding of Highway 191 about 15 miles south of Safford.
A truck needed to be rescued from flooded roads in Talavera.

One to three inches of rain in 2 hours caused flash flooding of roadways south and east of the Willcox Playa. One person was rescued from their vehicle after being stalled in flood waters on North Cochise Stronghold Rd.

Another round of heavy rain hit La Union down to Santa Teresa a day after flooding had already occurred in the area. Over a foot and a half of water was reported on Alvarez Road in La Union while down in Santa Teresa, Hansen Circle was impassable due to overflowing water from a retention pond.
Over an inch of rain in an hour caused flash flooding of roadways in Benson and State Route 80 in St. David. In Benson, one house and the community center were flooded.
Hackberry Road was closed from Main Street to Route 66 due to flooding.

Photo on social media shows two unoccupied sedans floating in flood water near Helena Drive and 2nd Street. Flood water continued down the water channel and spilled into the apartment complex on Bell Road and Central Avenue. Broadcast media reported multiple ground floor apartments experienced flood damage with an estimated 4 feet of water moving through them. Extent of the damages and number of apartments affected was not reported. Time estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Public report of flooding along 23rd Avenue between Dunlap Avenue and Northern Avenue. Video shows the intersection of 23rd Avenue and Butler Drive flooded with at least 6 inches of water. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Greenway Road underpass at Interstate-17 flooded with a few feet of standing water and was closed as a result. Before being closed, a reported 5 vehicles stalled in the flood water, requiring a rescue. The underpass did not reopen until roughly noon on the 14th. No injuries were reported.

Video on social media showed significant flow in Ashbrook Wash over El Pueblo Boulevard just north of Grande Boulevard. In the video an uprooted mature palo verde tree was flowing across the road. The following morning it was found that a sedan had been swept off the road at some point during the night and crushed by debris, but the owner of the vehicle was able to escape. No injuries were reported.

Multiple streamflow gages along Indian Bend Wash exceeded action or alarm stage, particularly between Highway-51 and Scottsdale Road. Streamflow gages crested around 3 to 5 feet and most did not fall below action or alarm until midday on the 14th. The USGS gage at Sweetwater Avenue recorded a roughly 4 foot rise in 30 minutes and crested at 3.95 feet. Rainfall amounts between 1.5 to 2.5 inches were measured upstream just west of Highway-51. No damages or injuries were reported.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported State Route 88 was closed in both directions between mile posts 229 and 242 due to flooding. Timing estimated based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Interstate-17 was closed in both directions due to significant standing water on the freeway near Indian School Road. Multiple cars also became stalled in the standing water. Interstate-17 was not fully reopened until approximately 0115MST on the 14th. No injuries were reported.

Interstate-17 was closed in both directions at the Durango Street curve due to standing water on the freeway, making it impassable. Interstate-17 did not fully reopen until approximately 0100MST on the 14th. No damages or injuries were reported.

Thunderbird Road from Interstate-17 to 35th Avenue flooded with 1 to 3 feet of standing water. At least one car became stranded in the underpass below Interstate-17. The underpass was closed for several hours. No injuries were reported.
The City of Surprise closed Jomax Road between 147th Avenue and El Granada Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based on radar.
City of Surprise closed Cotton Lane between Peoria Avenue to Cactus Road due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Video on social media shows at least 6 inches of swift-moving water flowing down 96th Street near Duncan Street. No damages of injuries were reported.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported that US-60 was closed in both directions between Superior and Top-Of-The-World, specifically between mileposts 227 and 235, due to rocks on the roadway following heavy rainfall in the area. The highway was reopened around 0030MST on the 14th. No damages or injuries were reported.

Photos on social media showed considerable tree debris washed up against a walking bridge along with washed out trails and picnic area at the Boyce Thompson Arboretum due to high flow in Queen Creek and/or Silver King Wash. As a result of the damage left behind from the flooding, the picnic area along with a couple of gardens and trails were closed. Further downstream, a USGS stream gage along Queen Creek below Whitlow Dam recorded a rapid rise near midnight going from the 13th into the 14th. Discontinuities in the data suggest that the flow in Queen Creek exceeded the gage's 6 ft maximum operating limit at around 0230MST when the gage recorded a height of 5.37 ft. Timing was estimated using the USGS gage. No injuries were reported.
Report through mPing of impassable street flooding in the town of Maricopa. Additional details not reported.
Highway 72 was flooded and impassable near Bouse. Timing adjusted based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported via social media at 0202MST on the 14th that Highway-238 was closed in both directions between milepost 40 near Maricopa and State Route 85 near Gila Bend due to flooding. Heaviest rain, estimated around 2 to 3 inches, fell from the Maricopa mountains west toward Gila Bend. Highway-238 would remain closed through the 14th. Timing of impacts adjusted based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported at 0226MST that Agua Caliente Road, a dirt road, was closed between Old US 80 to Lahman Road due to flooding. Timing of impacts adjusted based on radar and location focused on area with greatest radar rainfall estimates. No damages or injuries were reported.

Following 2 to 4 inches of rain in 1 to 2 hours over the Sand Tank Wash watershed, catastrophic flooding occurred in the small town of Gila Bend with feet of water, mud, and debris moving through town. Storm surveys were completed by NWS Phoenix, Maricopa County Department of Emergency Management (MCDEM), American Red Cross, and Flood Control District of Maricopa County (FCDMC). FCDMC gages on Sand Tank Wash, Bender Wash, and in the Maricopa Mountains measured rainfall amounts around 3 to 4 inches in 1 to 2 hours for an annual exceedance probability of 0.1%. FCDMC found the most significant floodwaters were within Sand Tank Wash, with lesser flows in Bender and Scott Avenue Washes. The NWS Phoenix survey found evidence of out of bank flooding in Sand Tank Wash 1 to 3 miles south of Interstate-8 (I-8) with 2 to 6 feet of water and sizable debris. The streamflow gage on Sand Tank Wash at I-8 reached alarm stage at 0157MST, bank full at 0341MST, and flood stage at 0352MST. The gage crested at 7.69 feet with 5000 cfs of flow at 0408MST. The floodwaters and debris that moved through town caused flood damage to at least 140 homes and 25 businesses. Most structures impacted were between the Gila Bend Canal and Main Street and then along Pima Street. During the flooding, Maricopa County Sheriff's Office rescued at least 30 individuals from their roofs along with others pulled from stranded vehicles. Photos after the water receded showed the canal was eroded and breached where Sand Tank Wash flows over it. Photos also showed 2 to 5 foot water lines both on the outside and inside of many of the structures, piles of debris, damaged property and vehicles, and erosion. Of the homes MCDEM assessed, 21 were deemed uninhabitable after the flooding. Unfortunately there were 2 direct fatalities with this event.
