One made a heroic effort to save a stranded motorist before they themselves were swept away in their own vehicle. The other was swept away in one of the flooded washes. Additionally, many farm animals were killed. Besides the fatalities, no other injuries were reported. A state of emergency was declared for this event.

Highway 70 was closed due to water running across the road at mile marker 174 as well as across the White Sands Missile Range Headquarters Road. The center median eroded due to the running water. A spotter reported 4.67 inches of rain in the 24 hour period ending at 6pm on 8/14.

A streamflow gage on the Agua Fria River at Buckeye Road exceeded alarm stage at 0241MST with peak flow of 1932 cfs and a crest height of 0.79 feet. Impacts to the low water crossing at Lower Buckeye Road are common with this flow level, but no impacts were reported. No damages or injuries were reported.

A streamflow gage on Sauceda wash near Highway 85 exceeded alarm stage at 0349MST, with a peak flow of 1396 cfs and crest of 4.10 feet at 0509MST. The stage fell below alarm at 0552MST. With alarm stage flow, impacts to Watermelon Road just north of Interstate-8 can experience impacts, but none were reported. No damages or injuries were reported with this flow, but catastrophic impacts, including loss of life, were experienced in nearby Gila Bend from flooding of Sand Tank wash. See that event entry for details.

Widespread flooding was reported across La Union due to over 7 inches of rain over the previous 3 days from just north of Domenici Highway through La Union. The Dona Ana County Emergency Manager ordered evacuations of La Union due to the flooding and possible dam breach of an earthen dam to the west of town.
The Rio Penasco River came out of it's banks from just east of Mayhill into Chaves County with widespread flooding across the area.

Two inches of rain in 1 to 2 hours caused flash flooding in central Cochise County.  Highway 191 near Birch Rd was flooded. Gleeson Rd. was washed out near mile post 20 and a swift water rescue occurred at mile post 14.

More than 1 inch of rain in an hour caused flash flooding in northeast Tucson. Flash flooding was reported along Castle Rock Wash and one vehicle was stranded in flood waters near Bear Canyon and Tanque Verde Rds. Fort Lowell Rd. was closed due to flooding.
An inch of rain in 30 minutes caused flash flooding of Mescal Rd. Two occupants of a vehicle that drove into floodwaters were rescued 8 miles north of Mescal.

Heavy rain in Ojo Caliente resulted in flash flooding. Flood waters reportedly entered at least one mobile home, and debris and water covered many secondary roads east of U.S. Highway 285. The extent of damage to the mobile home is unknown, and damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain near Aztec resulted in the flooding of an arroyo which rendered San Juan County Road 3073 unpassable as fast-moving water flowed over the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Two to three inches in one hour caused flash flooding of washes and several road closures in Oracle.
Highway 61 south of San Lorenzo was impassable due to heavy rain and resulting flash flooding.
Numerous low water crossings were flooded and roads were closed due to flash flooding  in the Heber area.
Many roads were flooded in Concho. Water was up to the door steps of businesses.
Arizona Department of Transportation reported that Highway 180A was closed due to flooding at mile post 347.  Pictures on social media showed water at least a foot deep on roadways in this area.
More than 1 inch of rain in less than an hour in the mountains north of State Rte. 266 caused flash flooding down the mountains and mud and rocks to block a portion of that route.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding and road damage in,  as well as both north and east of Douglas. One person was rescued from their vehicle in floodwaters on Pedregosa Rd. near State Route 80. Leslie Canyon and Glen Rds. and Washington St. were closed due to flooding. Nine metal gates of the international border wall were damaged by Silver Creek flood waters just west of the San Bernardino National Wildlife Refuge.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours caused flash flooding from east of Sierra Vista to north of Bisbee to Elfrida. Floodwaters deposited several rocks on State Rte. 80 near N. Old Divide Rd. northwest of Bisbee and caused the closure of Moson and Escapule Rds and the junction of State Rtes. 80 and 90 east of Sierra Vista. Along Davis Rd. near mile post 13, six motorists were rescued from three vehicles amidst floodwaters. Courtland and Jefferson Rds, northwest of Elfrida were also closed due to flooding.

Heavy rainfall over the Salt Fire burn area led to enhanced runoff that resulted in flash flooding. The Arizona Department of Transportation reported closures along SR 188 north of Globe/Claypool due to flooding. Timing was estimated using a nearby USGS stream gage along Pinal Creek at Inspiration Dam, which rose over 3 feet beginning at 2145MST and crested at 4.47 feet near midnight. No damage or injuries were reported.
One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Picture Rocks. Manville Rd. was closed due to flooding at the Brawley Wash and Sandario Rd. was also closed.

Sossaman Road and Via Del Jardin was closed at Sonoqui Wash due to flooding. A nearby Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage near Hawes Road recorded flow in the wash climbing above alarm stage at around 2340MST. Flow in the wash continued to increase during the early morning hours on the 17th before cresting above bank full at 7.10 feet and 2237 CFS at 0010MST. Timing was estimated using the stream gage. No damage or injuries were reported.
The Arizona Department of Transportation reported that SR 87 was closed due to flooding near Arizona Boulevard. No damage or injuries were reported.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in south central Pinal County. Considerable damage occurred to Park Links Rd. between Cattle Tank Rd. and the I-10 Frontage Rd. McClellan Wash also flooded Milligan Rd. resulting in its closure.

Two to three inches of rain in 2 hours along and south of Highway 86 caused flash flooding south of Ryan Field Airport and around Tucson Mountain Park Estates. Sierrita Mt. Rd. was closed near Hilltop Rd. and both Sandario Rd. and Snyder Hill Rd. was closed at the Black Wash.

One to two inches of rain in two hours caused flash flooding in Marana and Avra Valley. Anway Rd. was closed south of El Camino de Tres Arroyos as well as Silverbell Rd. near the Cocio Wash. Avra Valley Rd. was closed at the Brawley Wash.
Heavy rain flooded the underpass of I-17 at Greenway Road with at least one driver becoming stuck. No injuries were reported.

Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage ACDC at 43rd Avenue exceeded alarm stage resulting in downstream impacts at Thunderbird Paseo Park. Timing was estimated from when the gage reach alarm stage and time to travel downstream. No damage or injuries were reported.
Video on social media showed water rapidly flowing across 12th Street near the Torre Blanca community making the street impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
The City of Goodyear reported that Citrus Road was closed between I-10 and Van Buren Street as well as Yuma Road and Durango Street due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain over the Museum Fire scar (2019) produce significant flooding down Spruce Wash and into north central Flagstaff and down into the Rio de Flag on the south and southeast Flagstaff. The flood water first entered developed area around 1245 PM with trees, logs, and other debris 60-70 feet wide over topping a road about 2.5 - 3 feet deep. The flood waters were over 9 feet deep in some channeled areas through the forest. Many roads were flooded and closed. The flood barriers were overtopped in some places.

Heavy rain over the Fort Valley Trail System (2-3 inches in an hour) caused flash flooding through some yards north of Highway 180, the Rio de Flag in the Cheshire Subdivision (crossed two roads--first time in at least 27 years)m and all the way through Flagstaff.
The river gauge on Dry Beaver Creek near The Village of Oak Creek rose 4.5 feet.  Downstream, Dry Beaver Creek rose 4.4 feet between 430 PM and 530 PM MST.

One inch of rain in 15 to 30 minutes created flash flooding of washes and roadways in a small portion of east Tucson. A vehicle was stranded in flowing water near 5th St. and Wilmot Rd. Flood waters also crossed roadways in Wilshire Heights near Broadway and Craycroft.
Bright Angel Creek rose 6 feet at Phantom Ranch.

More than one inch of rain in less than an hour caused a rapid rise in Alamo Wash where a storm had produced an inch of rain three hours earlier.  A motorist was rescued from a vehicle stuck in floodwaters on Chantilly Rd. at the Alamo Wash.
The Little Colorado River gauge near Cameron (LCCA3) showed a 2.9 foot rise between 815 PM and 1100 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge near Montezuma Castle showed a 2.7 foot rise between 830 PM and 1045 PM.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge rose 3.3 feet, with an increase in flow from 4 CFS to 1790 CFS.

Flash flooding was reported on Coal Creek. The Coal Creek near Cedar City gauge rose from 8 CFS to 1160 CFS overnight. Several homes within the Flying L Ranches subdivision outside of Cedar City were damaged by floodwaters.
The Paria River gauge at Lees Ferry showed a 4 foot rise between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM MST. The Paria River drainage originates in Utah and flows into the Colorado River near Lees Ferry.
Flash flooding carried debris across Old U.S. Highway 91 through Kanarraville.
The North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale spiked from 26 CFS to 1560 CFS in just 15 minutes, corresponding to a rise of 4 feet.
The East Verde River near Childs (EVDA3) had a 2.9 foot rise between 0800 and 0845 MST.

Dirt road up to Reevis Mountain School, which cuts through Campaign Creek, was washed out by significant flash flooding. A couple yurpees on the property of the school were damaged or destroyed. Their fire circle and labyrinth were also washed away. The school and road are inside the 2019 Woodbury burn area. Rainfall of 4.5 inches was measured in 3 to 4 hours. Timing based on radar. No injuries were reported.

Multiple photos and videos show significant flow within the typically dry Reno Creek with flow over Old Highway 188, leading to its closure. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2020 Bush Fire burn area. Reno Creek would experience another flash flood again in the early afternoon following another round of heavy rain upstream. This kept 188 closed for an extended period. No damages or injuries were reported.
The Tonto Creek stream gauge above Gun Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.1 foot rise between 0845 and 1000 AM MST.

Multiple photos and videos showed a few feet of rapidly flowing water within Campaign Creek, leading to the closure of Mesquite Street in Roosevelt Estates. One video even showed a 6 to 8 foot standing wave of water. Video after the water receded showed significant damage to the road. No injuries were reported.

Video shows considerable flow through Pinal Creek with at least 6 inches of swift-moving water over Beer Tree Crossing near Jess Hayes Road. Rainfall of 1.5 to 2 inches was measured in the area and upstream. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2021 Telegraph burn area. No damages or injuries were reported.

Photos and videos show large sections of Russell Road, in multiple spots, were eroded and washed into Russell Gulch during significant flash flooding. Some photos, after the water receded, suggest the floodwaters may have been 6 to 8 feet deep. The significant destruction of Russell Road occurred roughly 2 miles south of the catastrophic flooding that occurred in the Claypool area, between Miami and Globe. Timing based on webcam footage in the area. No injuries were reported.

After 2 to 4 inches of rain fell, beginning around 0830MST, over the 2021 Telegraph burn area, catastrophic flooding occurred in Claypool area between Miami and Globe. Runoff mostly collected in Russell Gulch and a few feet of floodwaters moved downhill through the Claypool community. Security cam footage from a pizza shop showed floodwaters reached US-60 near mile post 247 around 1056MST. US-60 became impassible a couple minutes later and was closed in both directions for a couple hours before being reopened around 1240MST. The same areas were impacted again in the mid-afternoon after another wave of flash flooding move through the area. The Gila County Emergency Manager estimated over 50 homes and structures were damaged by flooding. Included in the damage was the pizza shop with the security footage, which was fully surrounded by flooding. A hotel next to the pizza shop had all of its ground level rooms flooded, including a wall that collapsed due to the force of the water. Roads to the nearby hospital were cutoff by floodwaters. The hardest hit area was Little Acres Mobile Home Park, 1 mile south of US-60. Most if not all of the mobile homes had flood damage as an estimated 4 feet of water and mud moved through the park. Security footage shows one home was even swept from one side of the park to the other and was destroyed. Many of the owners were displaced from their homes for several days while the park was cleaned. A power substation next to the park also experienced significant flooding. Fortunately there were no injuries or fatalities reported from this event.

Multiple photos and videos show significant flow in Pinto and Spring (tributary to Pinto) along State Route 188 near mile post 234. One photo showed a storage structure (possibly abandoned) in Spring Creek with roughly 8 feet of water flowing through it. It is unknown if the structure had any damage. Many of the photos and videos were posted in the early afternoon, but flood impacts likely began in the morning after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the 2019 Woodbury burn area. No injuries were reported.
Arizona Department of Transportation reported State Route 77 was overtopped by floodwaters at mile post 163.2. Timing based on report time and radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Arizona Department of Transportation reported State Route 188 was closed in both directions near mile post 219 due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

A USGS streamflow gage along Pinal Creek near Inspiration Dam measured multiple a couple rapid rises between 1230MST and 1430MST with a peak stage cresting at 8 feet. The flood waves likely originated from heavy rain roughly 15 miles upstream over the 2021 Telegraph burn area southwest of Globe. There were a couple more smaller follow-on waves that were recorded as the flow was decreasing from its crest. No damages or injuries were reported.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Grand Wash, Capitol Gorge, and Pleasant Creek were all closed due to flash flooding.
The water was flowing 4.85 feet deep (normally dry) in Munds Canyon under Interstate 17 and about 25 feet wide. The estimated flow was 900 CFS.

Heavy rainfall led to a rapid increase in flow in Sycamore Creek. A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Sycamore Creek near NF-201 and Beeline Highway recorded the creek climbing above alarm stage, cresting at 4.54 feet at 1247MST. Downstream impacts included old SR 87 and low-lying homes. No damage or injuries were reported.

Photos and videos show considerable floodwaters, roughly a few feet deep, rapidly moving down Reno Creek and flowing across Old Highway 188, making it impassable. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2020 Bush Fire burn area. Reno Creek flooded earlier in the morning as well. No damages or injuries were reported.
A camera located along Kitty Joe Creek showed high, swiftly moving flow that was nearly topping the banks of the creek. No damage or injuries were reported.

FCDMC STREAM GAUGE||A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage located along Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard exceeded alarm stage, resulting in impacts to downstream low water crossings as well as to the Indian Bend Wash greenbelt. At 1501MST, flow in Indian Bend Wash crested at 3.02 feet and 2031 CFS. According to a nearby mPING report close to Paradise Valley Mall, a flooded street led to a vehicle becoming stranded. No injuries were reported.

The Cave Creek Ashdale Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage recorded flow exceeding alarm stage, impacting low water crossings along with properties in the area. At 1513MST, the creek crested at 6.7 feet and 2027 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

A couple videos showed significant flowing water through Skunk Creek with flow over Honda Bow Road. One of the videos showed someone being rescued on the hood of a truck by a good Samaritan from their SUV that stalled in the floodwaters. Rainfall amounts over 1 inch were observed over the foothill areas upstream of this location. Timing of impacts adjusted based on radar. No injuries were reported.

According to local media reports, the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office found two people had perished inside an ATV that was buried in mud and debris downstream in Camp Creek. MCSO was notified and began searching for the missing people around 1600MST on the 18th but did not recover the ATV until 0800MST on the 19th. Media reported that other recreationists were successfully rescued from the area, including a father and daughter who were trapped near Needle Rock Recreation Site and had to be rescued by helicopter. A Camp Creek rain gauge recorded 3.54 inches of rain between 1300MST and 1420MST. The Rackensack Canyon rain gauge measured 3.83 inches of rain between 1250MST and 1430MST. The Maricopa County Flood Control District also reported that Bartlett Dam Road was closed due to swiftly flowing water over the roadway from Camp Creek.

Old Stage Road and parts of New River Road were closed due to flooding associated with increased flow in New River. A Maricopa County Flood Control District upstream from the impacts climbed above alarm stage, cresting at 2.93 feet and 2801 CFS at 1442MST. No damage or injuries were reported.

Videos show significant floodwaters in Galloway Wash with flow across Spur Cross Road, making the road impassable to all traffic. Measured and radar estimated rainfall amounts were around 2 to 4 inches in 2 to 3 hours over areas upstream of this location. Timing adjusted based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Significant flow in a typically dry wash made Carefree Highway between Tom Darlington Drive and Stagecoach Pass impassable to all traffic. There was also a photo that showed a lot of mud and gravel in one of the southbound lanes of Tom Darlington Drive near Meander Way. Both of these were reported around 1550PM. Very heavy rain began over the area and just upstream closer to 1300MST, with measured and radar estimated rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches in 1 hour. Timing of impacts adjusted based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Seven Springs Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting the unbridged Seven Springs Road downstream. At 1418MST, the flow crested at 5.06 feet and 1574 CFS.

Broadcast media coverage showed significant flow in East Fork Cave Creek leading to the closure of 7th Avenue near Coral Gables Street. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County streamflow gage a few hundred feet upstream from 7th Avenue exceeded alarm stage at 1422MST, crested at 3.66 feet at 1509MST, and fell back below alarm stage at 1645MST. A man tested the floodwaters with his unicycle, but wisely turned around. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Cave Creek north of Carefree Highway exceeded bank full stage, impacting downstream low water crossings. At 1502MST, the creek crested at 7.65 feet and 5178 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

Videos from a local TV station showed deep, swiftly moving water flowing in a wash across an unbridged crossing along 7th Avenue near Coral Gables Drive in Moon Valley. Nearby, Greenway Road was closed at I-17 due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Arizona Department of Transportation closed State Route 88 between mile posts 230 and 242 due to flooding. Timing of impacts based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Flash flooding produced significant trail damage in Bryce Canyon National Park. Park officials reported the Wall Street section of Navajo Loop, the Bryce Connector Trail, and Peekaboo Loop were closed were closed due to the damage.

Arizona Department of Transportation closed State Route 188 in both directions due to a mudslide across the highway. Initially the closure was between mile posts 246 and 255, but was updated to between 252 and 255. The mudslide was around mile post 253 and was the same location as a debris flow in July 2020. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2020 Bush Fire burn area. Photos of the mud slide show roughly 1 to 3 feet of sediment, with burnt tree branches and twigs, across the highway and the guardrail in the southbound lane was destroyed. No injuries or additional damages were reported.

After 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the northern portions of the 2020 Bush Fire burn area, a USGS streamflow gage on Sycamore Creek (SYCA3) registered a rapid rise from 2.53 feet at 01530MST to 9.38 feet at 1545MST. Flow continued to rise and crested 11.77 feet at 1730MST, 1.73 feet below action stage. No damages or injuries were reported.

The unpaved portion of State Route 88/Apache Trail was closed between NF-79 (mile post 230) and NF-51 (mile post 242) due to significant flash flooding and the road being washed out in many places. Arizona Department of Transportation reported the closure on the 19th, but the flooding impacts occurred on the 18th. According to Apache Lake Marina & Resort, some customers and employees had to be evacuated out of the area. Videos on social media show some of the road damage and washouts. The nearest rain gage at Reavis Trailhead measured 1.61 inches between 1350MST and 1550MST and radar estimates were upwards of 2 inches. Runoff on the southern end of the closure may have been enhanced by the 2019 Woodbury Fire burn area. Timing based on the rain gage and radar. No injuries were reported.

A photo showed an outhouse public bathroom at the Eads Wash River Access Point Recreation site had the ground beneath it eroded away due to flash flooding. Floodwaters appeared to be traveling within Poison Spring Wash toward the Salt River. Tonto National Forest posted a couple days later that access to the Eads Wash rec site was closed due to erosion damage and unsafe conditions in the area as a result of the flash flooding. Exact timing of when impacts occurred is unknown, so based the timing off of radar. No injuries were reported.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out and impassible due to flash flooding south of Sandy Ranch at Dog Water Wash.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Cave Creek at Cactus Road recorded flow climbing above alarm stage, impacting nearby low-lying areas. At 1632MST, the gage crested at 11.14 feet and 1,567 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

Video shows significant flow in Six Shooter Canyon with floodwaters overtopping a small bridge at Six Shooter Canyon Road and Delores Lane. Homes may have been impacted with this flow level, considering a previous event, but there were no reports of damages and no reports of injuries either. It is uncertain if this event occurred in the morning or afternoon, but a downstream gage at Beer Tree Crossing registered a greater rise in the afternoon versus the morning. The gage crested at 3.91 feet at 1659MST. Although not reported, Beer Tree Crossing was likely impassable.

Gila County Emergency Manager reported Russell Gulch experienced flash flooding, in the Claypool area between Miami and Globe, after heavy rain fell over the Pinal Mountains within the 2021 Telegraph Fire burn area. Measured and radar estimated rainfall amounts were around 1 to 2 inches over the area and upstream, bringing the day's total to around 2.5 to 4.5 inches over the burn scar. Flash flooding impacted the same areas as the catastrophic flooding earlier in the morning, but was less intense according to the emergency manager. Still the bridge to the hospital near Hospital Road and Russell Road was impassable and nearby homes likely experienced impacts again. No injuries were reported and there were no reports of new damage costs.

Pictures on social media show at least 10 inches of water flowing in Dinnebito Wash near Hardrock. The water had been flowing for at least 2 hours. Road going into Hardrock were not passible due to the water flowing over the roadways.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Burr Trail, Strike Valley, and Halls Creek Road were all impassible due to flash flooding.
Roads into Bartlett Lake were reported to be flooded and impassable in multiple locations, with some people having to be rescued out of the lake area.
Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose from 7.17 to 10.22 feet in 45 minutes.
Granite Creek (GRWA3) below Watson Lake rose 2.2 feet to 3.97 feet in one hour and 44 minutes. Water crested at 7:20 PM MST.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported State Route 238 was closed for several hours between mile posts 35 and 40 due to flooding. Timing of impacts based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Emergency Management reported a 4 foot rise on Black Canyon Creek at 8:08 PM MST.  This creek is downsteam from parts of the Tiger Fire (2021).
The Verde River near Clarkdale rose over 17 feet in 58 minutes (VDCA3). The water crested at 19.49 feet at 942 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge (BCMA3) near Montezuma Castle National Monument rose from 1.0 to 3.03 feet in 65 minutes.  It crested at 11:13 PM MST.
A dike collapse due to heavy rainfall led to a large amount of debris across Old U.S. Highway 91, with the road being closed.
Zion National Park officials reported the Kolob Canyons section of the Park was closed due to significant mud and rock slides from overnight flash flooding.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding of the East Fork of the Virgin River. The flood wave started near the East Fork of the Virgin River near Glendale, which rose from 16 CFS to 544 CFS, corresponding to a 3 foot rise. The flood wave grew downstream from additional heavy rain, where the East Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale rose from 45 CFS to 2410 CFS, corresponding to a 6 foot rise.
The Escalante River near Escalante gauge indicated an increase in flow of 1440 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 5 feet.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Scenic Drive was closed at Grand Wash due to a large amount of mud across the road, deposited by flash flooding, making it impassible. Rangers also estimated Pleasant Creek and Sheets Gulch had 6-8 feet of flooding overnight, and Burro, Cottonwood, and 5 mile Washes had 2 to 4 feet of flooding overnight.

Zion National Park dispatch officials reported a rockslide due to excessive rainfall along the Scenic Drive north of the Visitor Center. A portion of the road was damaged due to the slide, and was closed as a result. In addition, the river gauge on the North Fork of the Virgin River near Springdale had a sharp rise and peaked at 1690 CFS, corresponding to a rise of over 3 feet.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported Notam-Bullfrog Road was washed out at Bullfrog Creek Crossing near Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, resulting in a 5-foot drop-off, making the road impassible.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose just over 10 feet in 4 hours (VAVA3).  The water crested at 14.23 at 9:30 AM MST.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Grand Wash, with 6 to 8 inches of rapidly flowing water.

Two to four inches of rain in 3 hours in the southern Chiricahua Mountains caused flash flooding of streams over and west of the mountains. Two motorists in one vehicle were stuck in floodwaters east of McNeal on Davis Rd. near milepost 30. An elderly man attempted to drive through waters to rescue them when his vehicle was swept downstream. He was rescued but not before suffering hypothermia from being in the cold water.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise on Nogales Wash in Arizona, causing it to overtop its banks. Two drowning victims were washed across the border from Mexico and retrieved in Arizona.
More than 1 of rain in less than 1 hour in Vail caused flash flooding of roadways including Old Vail Rd. and Dawn Rd.
Flag Mine Road was closed due to flooding.
Signal Road was closed from Highway 93 to Alamo Road due to flooding.
Thirty low water crossings on Highway 95 between Needles and Havasu Lake Road were covered in mud and debris.
Bogeles Ranch Road was closed from Upper Trout Creek Road to Bogeles Ranch due to flooding.
Nipton Road was flooded east of Ivanpah Road.
The Nipton Road off ramp from Interstate 15 was flooded, and vehicles were stuck.
Indian Trail Road was damaged by flooding between Adobe Road and Mesquite Springs Road.
The California Highway Patrol reported that Sea View Way in the North Shore area was closed due to flooding. Timing was estimated using radar. No damage or injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall across northeast portions of Imperial County where nearly 7 inches of rain was estimated to have fallen in a 5 hour period. The Cibola RAWS site recorded 1.58 inches of rain between 1348PDT and 1548PDT. As a result, extensive flooding occurred along SR 78 from Palo Verde and areas south, damaging the road and leading to an extended closure for repairs.

Very heavy rainfall occurred along SR 78 in northeast Imperial County with amounts estimated to be approaching 7 inches in some places. This resulted in considerable flooding along the highway. The California Highway Patrol reported that a vehicle was swept off SR 78 at Milpitas Wash before overturning in the wash. Both occupants perished in the flash flood.
Heavy rain caused Oso Creek to overfill its banks and overtop Dawson Road. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that Dawson Road was flooded for about 20 to 30 minutes. No damages are known.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose almost two feet with a crest of 4.39 feet at 6:00 PM MST (VAVA3).
The California Highway Patrol reported water and debris across SR 86 at Willow Wash, making the road impassable. No injuries were reported.
Pierce Ferry Road was damaged by flooding in multiple areas between Highway 93 and mile marker 3.
The California Highway Patrol reported that Cole Boulevard at Dogwood Road was closed due to flooding. No injuries were reported.
Antares Road was closed from Route 66 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding.
Two to two and a half feet of water flowed over DW Ranch Road from the Frees Wash.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Tiger Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings on Eagle Eye Road. Timing of impacts to Eagle Eye Road were estimated to be 65 minutes after the stream gage exceeded alarm stage. No damage or injuries were reported.
Zion National Park rangers reported flash flooding in slot canyons between Temple of the Sun and Twins.
Carrizo Creek near Carrizo (CRZA3) rose from 1 to 3.7 feet in less than an hour. The water dropped back below 2 feet about 3 hours later.

The East Verde River near Childs (Gauge EVDA3) rose from 10 to 12.4 feet in less than 30 minutes at 930 AM on September 1.  It dropped below 12 feet about 3 hours later. At 830 PM,  it rose to 13.8 feet.  The water dropped back to around 11.6 feet by 900 AM on September 2.
Heavy rain flooded a wash which created a waterfall over the rim and into Glen Canyon just below/south of Glen Canyon Dam.
Water was flowing over a 40 foot section of Highway 87 at Mile Post 343 near Coyote Wash.
Six inches of water flowed over Main Street in Pioche.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported 6 inches of water flowing across state Route 24 in several locations east of Fruita. UDOT also reported 6 inches of water flowing across state Route 24 between mileposts 81 and 84.

The stream gauge on Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City rose from 17.6 feet to 20.8 feet in less than half an hour at 430 PM on 1 September. The gauge went down to 18.4 feet then rose again to 23.7 feet in less than half an hour at 900 PM on 1 September.  The water rose a third time to 22 feet in less than half a hour at 3:00 AM on 2 September. The water receded below 18 feet by 800 AM on 2 September.

A significant flash flood occurred in the town of Hanksville, with nearly every structure in town impacted by flooding. Floodwaters were reportedly as deep as 6 feet in places. Rainfall totals were 1.2 inches in Hanksville, and were as high as 1.7 inches in the Henry Mountains. In Capitol Reef National Park, 1.66 inches fell.

Heavy rain over the Little Colorado River Basin and tributaries created a surge of water at the river gauge (LCCA3) on the Little Colorado River near Cameron.  The water rose from 1.8 feet to 5.43 feet on the gauge in less than 15 minutes at 1245 AM on 2 September.  The water was still above 4.7 feet at 945 AM.

Highway 191 was closed due to flooding over the highway at Mile Post 491.8 between Round Rock and Rock Point (by Whale Rock) at 1135 PM. A social media video post showed a dangerous swollen wash along Highway 191.
Blake Ranch Road was flooded with six inches of flowing water in four places.
The Escalante River gauge near Escalante rose from 375 CFS to a peak of 1840 CFS.

One to three inches of heavy rainfall in a short period of time caused flash flooding in Roswell. The north and northeast side of the city experienced the most severe flooding where multiple cars were stranded on flooded roadways. Numerous water rescues were conducted on Atkinson, Mescalero, and Berrendo roads in northern Roswell. Flood waters entered homes on Holly Loop, and the road was barricaded due to high water rises. Damages are estimated.

One to two inches of heavy rainfall caused flash flooding in Moriarty. Torrance County Dispatch reported torrential rainfall with a severe thunderstorm crossing Interstate 40 near Moriarty. Visibility was near zero which forced many travelers to pull off the road. Several Moriarty residents reported flood damage from the heavy rainfall. The water continued to flow southward through McIntosh and even caused Estancia Park Lake to overfill its banks. The extent of damages is unknown, therefore, damage amounts are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain flooded portions of New Mexico State Road 52 which rendered the roadway impassable. The New Mexico Department of Transportation was forced to close to roadway for several hours as a result. The extent of damages is unknown.
Fire official reported some sink holes and a couple of cars swept away in La Union. Radar estimated about 1 inch of rain in less than an hour.

Heavy rain in the Gila Cliff Dwellings flooded many creeks, canyons, and trails in the National Monument. Water overtook a bridge as debris clogged the canyon underneath which stranded visitors for a short time. Damages are estimated.
Twitter report showed flash flooding on Bill Evans Road south of Gila, NM.
Nearly 1.5 of rain in about 30 minutes caused flash flooding of streets in Safford.

Utah Department of Transportation officials reported flash flooding and a debris flow across U.S. Highway 6, with an associated road closure of westbound lanes at milepost 229.  Additionally, eastbound lanes were closed at milepost 220.
Capitol Reef National Park rangers and broadcast media reported flash flooding in Capitol Gorge. The road to the trailhead washed out in several places.

Local law enforcement reported road closures in several locations due to flash flooding. This included State Route 177, which was closed between Ragsdale Road and State Route 62. Closures reported at 1755PDT. Timing adjusted based on radar estimated rainfall. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video on social media showed part of Highway 238 appearing to be impassable between mile posts 33-35 due to flooding. The Arizona Department of Public Safety (DPS) also responded to a vehicle stalled due to flooding in this area. No injuries were reported.

Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose around 4.15 feet between 445 PM and 615 PM. The waster began to decrease after 700 PM.  A video posted on social media showed ongoing flooding in Granite Creek Park a mile north of Prescott Courthouse at 632 PM.
Campo Road flooded between Avocado Rd and Via Mercado. Three vehicles were stuck in the water.
Jacks Canyon Creek near Winslow rose 2.8 feet in 90 minutes from 2.2 feet to 5 feet at 945 AM.
Heavy rain caused Dry Beaver Creek to rise 3.6 feet in 30 minutes cresting at 1215 PM.
A 3.9 foot rise was recorded on the Agua Fria River (AFMA3) east of Cordes Junction.
Kaibab National Forest reported that flooding closed Forest Road 22 from Forest Road 422A to Big Springs.

Flash flooding occurred in Capitol Gorge. The Scenic Drive was closed for over 24 hours due to flooding. Several vehicles were stuck, and required towing to be removed. Water and mud also flowed over state Route 24 east of the Hickman Bridge trailhead.
Banegas Ranch Road was closed from Banegas Ranch to Highway 93 due to flooding.
Signal Road was closed from Alamo Road to Highway 93 due to flooding.
Pump Station Road and Huffritter Road were closed from Back Road to Highway 93 due to flooding.
Bogeles Ranch Road was closed from Upper Trout Creek Road to Bogeles Ranch due to flooding.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to Route 66 due to flooding.

Social media video showed swift-moving water within Weekes Wash and flowing across State Route 88 near 1st Water Road, making the road impassable. Timing approximated. No damages or injuries were reported.
A Zion National Park official reported that Pine Creek experienced a flash flood.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported State Route 188 was closed between mile post 251 and 255 due to a mudslide. Photos show 4 to 6 feet of mud across the highway near mile post 253 that had to be cleared with heavy machinery. Flow originated from a portion of the 2020 Bush fire burn scar. NWS Phoenix in collaboration with Arizona Geological Survey declared the mudslide a hyperconcentrated flow and therefore entered as a flash flood. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.

A flash flood wave of 1000 CFS was recorded by the Paria River near Kanab gauge, with multiple smaller flood waves following. A single large flood wave of 3000 CFS was observed father downstream at Lees Ferry.
The Utah Department of Transportation reported U.S. Highway 6 was closed between Soldier Summit and the U.S. Highway 191 junction due to flash flooding from the Bear Fire burn scar.

An atmospheric river aided in heavy rain development across the River Complex burn scar. One or possibly more debris flows occurred as a result. Removal, protective measures, and repair costs from this debris flow are estimated to be $3.2 million.
California Highway Patrol reported 3.5 feet of water over the road on the north end of Constantia Road making the roadway impassable.

California Highway Patrol reported ton of rocks and water come off the mountain side of old 40, (Donner Pass Rd between Truckee and Donner Summit.) the road is now closed as it is not safe to pass due to erosion and falling debris.
California Highway Patrol reported some of the ramps at the SR 99 and SR 180 exchange in Fresno were completely flooded forcing a temporary closure of both highways.
California Highway Patrol reported several vehicles spun out on southbound SR 41 south of the SR 99 intersection due to flash flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported flooded culverts on SR 168 between Tollhouse Rd. and Sample Rd. due to debris flow flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported a mudslide along SR 41 just to the south of Coarsegold resulting in a brief closure of SR 41.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide on SR 198 near Lake Kaweah. A large boulder was located on the eastbound lane of SR 198.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide with boulders in the roadway at the intersection of East Trimmer Springs Rd. and North Piedra Rd. north of Piedra.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide with boulders in the roadway of SR 49 southwest of Ponderosa Basin.
California Highway Patrol reported water runoff covering Tollhouse Rd. southwest of Shaver Lake.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide with large builders on the roadway near the intersection of SR 46 and SR 33 at Blackwell's Corner.
California Highway Patrol reported a rockslide covering the westbound lanes of SR 178 near mile marker 18 in Kern Canyon.

Large amount of water flow near Potato Canyon and Oak Glen Roads, possibly on Birch Creek Road. A vehicle was swept off roadway and rescue was performed. Heavy rainfall of 0.4 to 0.6 in 1 hour occurred across the El Dorado burn scar and San Bernardino Mountains. Highway 38 was closed for several hours through the evening while Caltrans removed mud and debris from the highway. Total rainfall in the area was about 0.75 to 1.00 inch. County Public Works removed 250 cubic yards of debris from Birch Creek. Survey of the flood and debris flow was done by California Geological Survey jointly with WCM Alex Tardy.

Vineland and Noble Streets in Beaumont area. 10+ foot long tree branches/trunks washing through as well and rocks larger than a foot round washing through the wash. Water flowing over 1 foot over crossing. Web cameras showing dark water flow and debris from Apple fire burn scar. Rainfall rates were as high as 0.60 per hour.
State Highway 38 closed at Bryant street in Yucaipa to Lake Williams east of Big Bear due to rock and debris flows. Heavy rain occurred past few hours in the afternoon.

Reported 6 debris flows in Bond Fire scar and 4 in Silverado Canyon. Santiago Creek Road blockage from high water flows and mud. Jackson Creek Road flooded with mud and debris. Rainfall rates of up to 1.2 inches reported at Irvine Lake and Santiago Canyon site.
Highway 159 was closed due to flooding.
Debris flow reported 1 mile NNE Crestline. The Department of Highways reported boulders in northbound lanes of SR138 / Old Mill Road.

Heavy rain near Los Lunas caused a section of New Mexico State Road 6 to wash out. One vehicle with a family of three was traveling on the roadway when the road was washed out. Their car was submerged, but fortunately, nearby contruction workers were able to pull the family out of the car. No injuries were reported. The flooding forced the closure of the roadway during the evening hours. Damages are estimated.

An estimated 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain caused an arroyo near Embudo to spill out of its bank, causing water to flow over County Road 69. Embudo Creek was also reported to be running high with clogged culverts at mile marker 3 on New Mexico State Road 75 near Dixon. Damages are estimated.
Grand Wash Road and Capitol Gorge Road were closed due to mud from flash flooding.

Received video via social media of flooding of the Price River in Helper. Video showed flows at or above bank full with large debris contained in the flow. Downstream river gage along the Price River at Woodside indicated a peak flow of 749 CFS at 1100 am MDT. Time of flooding estimated by radar.
Heavy rain in the San Fidel area caused major flooding of arroyos and washed out County Road 13. Damages are estimated.

A trained spotter reported major flash flooding around Cubero. Several roads were washed out or inundated with water. Many other roads were forced to closed. The local fire station was also flooded. Damages are estimated.
Water from Cuchillo Creek was crossing over the road, making it impassable.
Mud and debris were across Highway 28 at mile marker 22.  Hillsboro during the overnight hours received around 1.50 inches of rain.
Law enforcement reports roadway flooding, mostly in the #1 lane on the I-10 E near mile marker 18.

CHP law enforcement reported a wash flowing across CA 177, north-northeast of Desert Center. One of their patrol vehicles sustained damage trying to get through to an accident. No injuries were reported.
Report of running water across the Interstate 10 Frontage Road near Mesquite.  Radar estimates upstream of Mesquite indicated upwards of 3-3.5 inches of rain had fallen.

Capitol Reef National Park reported SR-24 was impassable near milepost 83 due to flood waters from grand wash. Scenic drive was also closed, and the parking lot at the Grand Wash trailhead flooded. The flooding stranded nearly 60 people, and trapped or washed away several vehicles. Numerous water rescues were conducted by Utah Department of Public Safety helicopter operations to bring people to safety.
Bull Creek flowed across the road near Main Street, bringing with it large debris.
Heavy rain of 1.5 to 3 inches in less than 3 hours caused flash flooding along Empire Ranch Rd.

Heavy rain in the Santa Fe area caused the arroyos to fill up, and unfortunately, one man was found dead in the arroyo near Cerrillos and Rodeo. According to the Santa Fe emergency manager, the flooding within the arroyo was thought to be a contributing factor to the individual's death. However, the man also sustained blunt force trauma to the head and was also intoxicated, and these factors also contributed to his death. His age is unknown.

Heavy rain fell over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) and caused flooding on Highway 89 southbound near road NF-9122H. Flooding also was seen in the Wupatki Trails neighborhood on Camio de los Vientos. Homes and roads were impacted by the flood waters.
Heavy rain flooded the Milton/Route 66 under the railroad overpass in downtown Flagstaff. Cars were caught in the flood water.
A flash flood occurred in Cottonwood and Burro Washes as well as Sheets Gulch. Notom-Bullfrog road was washed out.

Over three inches of rain in Roswell caused significant flooding on the northeast side of the city. At least twelve homes in the Holly Loop subdividion were flooded, and emergency crews had to divert water through cinder block walls away from the subdivision and onto East Country Club Road. Farther east, a small bridge collapsed at East Mescalero Road near La Jara Road due to flood waters in Borrendo Creek. Damages are estimated.

The Bouse Fire Department reported washes were running along SR-72 near Bouse, resulting in difficult access as well as the closure of several sections of the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flood water over Kortsen Road and SR-347. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed North Trekell Road just south of W Hopi Drive flooded with water flowing down the road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway 130 was closed due to widespread flash flooding west of Weed.
Flash flooding off the Flag Fire scar affected the Pine Lake community and the summer camp inside Hualapai Park. Water flowed into several structures.
Vock Wash flowed over Stockton Hill Road.
Flash flooding occurred in Spry and Pine Creek Canyons in Zion National Park.

Two inches of rain (radar estimate) from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding in Clarkdale. Water flowed over sections of Wildhorse Lane and Old Jerome Highway. Police reported mud and rocks on the roadways with both streets barricaded.
Flash flooding occurred on Burro, Cottonwood, and Five Mile Washes, along with Sheets Gulch and on Notom-Bullfrog Road where the pavement ends.
The Mora County emergency manager reported that the Canoncito Creek overtopped the culvert and flooded Canoncito Road. Damages are estimated.
The Mora County emergency manager reported debris flow near a house west of Highway 121 along Lea Road. Damages are estimated.
Images showed Beer Tree Crossing barricaded due to Pinal Creek running across the road. Other images also showed Walliman Road was impassable due to flooding across the roadway.
Heavy rain of 3-4 inches in 2 hours caused flash flooding across State Route 286 and 2-3 inches of rain caused flash flooding and the closure of Sasabe-Arivaca Road at mile post 2.

An estimated 2 to 3 inches of rain across the northern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn area caused significant flash flooding and debris flow across portions of western Mora County. Canoncito Creek overtopped the culvert and flooded Canoncito Road. Highway 94 was also impacted with widespread flooding and debris flow which forced the closure of the highway. Damages are estimated.

Rainfall totals of 2 to 3 inches across southern portions of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused significant flash flooding and debris flow. Widespread flooding was observed along Highway 105 with drainages well out of their banks. A barn along Highway 105 was also flooded. This forced the closure of the highway for several hours on July 1st. County Road A4B was also flooded with debris flow across the roadway. Damages are estimated.
A flood wave around 3 feet or higher passed through Pleasant Creek within Captitol Reef National Park. The flood wave was associated with heavy rainfall in close vicinity to the creek.
Heavy rain of 1-2' in less than 1 hour caused the flooding of Magee Rd. east of La Canada Dr. at Pegler Wash and the closure of Ina Rd. at Pima Wash east of Oracle Rd.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 1 hour caused urban washes to flow over roadways from midtown to southeast Tucson. One person was washed downstream in the Columbus Wash near Blacklidge Dr. but was able to get themselves to safety. A young woman was rescued from her car which was stuck in Arcadia Wash near Pima and Rosemont. Kolb Rd. was closed between Irvington and Valencia while Irvington Rd. was closed due to flooding at the Atterbury Wash.
Heavy rain near Lamy caused Old Lamy Trail Road to nearly wash out by the Legal Tender Saloon. Three to four feet of water was also reported along the railroad. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 2-3 hours caused Old Ajo Hwy. and West Snyder Hill Rd. north of Ryan Field to be closed due to flash flooding.

Local law enforcement reported that heavy rain and debris flow made Highway 94 as well as County Road C 001 impassable which forced the closure of the roads. New Mexico Department of Transportation personnel worked through the overnight hours to clear the roadways and reopen them. Along Maestas Canyon, a lifelong resident was caught by surprise when four feet of water, mud, and debris came rushing down the canyon. A large shipping container also caught within the flood crashed into his cabin. The resident fled in his vehicle, and fortunately suffered no injuries. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain of 3-5 in 2 hours in the Chiricahua Mountains caused high flows on Turkey Creek. Fort Bowie Rd. was washed out well downstream.
Heavy rain near Mexican Springs flooded U.S. Highway 491 along with multiple dirt roads, including Navajo Service Road 30. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain in the Nageezi area flooded U.S. Highway 550 along with County Road 7800. Damages are estimated.
Flash flooding was reported in X Canyon, Antelope Canyon, and Lower Antelope Canyon (all the same drainage). Standing water remained in Lower Antelope Canyon on July 6.

A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall, primarily over the high terrain just east of U.S. Highway 191/U.S. Highway 6 near milepost 292. Radar estimates showed roughly 1 to 2 inches of rain over the course of around an hour to an hour and a half. This resulted in a flow of water, mud and debris, including railroad ties from an adjacent railroad, to flow over the highway in the vicinity of milepost 292. It was later reported that this led to a family's SUV being washed off of the road, and the family required rescue. No injuries were reported.

The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that an estimated 1.5 inches over the McBride burn scar caused flooding of Lower Eagle Creek with water, mud, and debris over Eagle Creek Road which is also known as New Mexico State Highway 120. Many 6 to 18 inch diameter boulders flowed over the roadway along with large segments of burned timber. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain on Tecolote Creek on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused the creek to exceed its banks, flooding New Mexico State Road 283 and County Road A19A near Mineral Hill. Damages are estimated.

About 1.5 inches of heavy rain fell near Chacon on the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. This caused flash flooding on area roadways, including Highways 121 and 519. Highway 121 reportedly had 2 to 3.5 feet of water along it while County Road B009 was under 5 feet of water due to a backed up culvert. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain near Springer flooded U.S. Highway 56, making it impassable. A barn along the highway had 4 inches of standing water while a house and its backyard had 2 to 3 inches of standing water. Damages are estimated.

An estimated 1 to 1.5 inches of heavy rain on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar flooded New Mexico State Road 434, forcing the closure of the roadway. Near Guadalupita, a residential driveway turned into a raging river with deep water and debris. Canoncito Creek also flooded which was caused by debris caught in culverts. The creek overflowed into nearby pastures, onto Highway 518, and impacted homes within the area. The water was two feet deep in some locations. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused water and debris to overtop a bridge along Highway 266 at the Sapello River. Damages are estimated.

Manuelitas Creek rose four to five feet and overtopped two bridges along County Road A1 east of State Road 94 between Sapello and Manuelitas. One CoCoRaHS observer near Sapello measured 3.76 inches of rain and remarked that it was the highest flooding levels they had seen in their 58 years at that residence. Damages are estimated.
US-60 at Val Vista was closed due to standing water on the highway. One car stalled in the standing water. No injuries were reported.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flash flooding in Government Wash with 8 inches of water, mud, and debris flowing over Highway 89 once the culvert was overwhelmed.  Four garages on Heritage Drive and Pioneer Valley Road were flooded.
A public report of significant ponding of water and water over roads and curbs.

A thunderstorm moved along Birch Creek near state Route 12, east of the town of Escalante. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall 1-hour estimates were around 1 to 1.5 inches in the vicinity of Birch Creek, near the confluence with the Escalante River. A video from social media showed that this resulted in flash flooding on Birch Creek into the Escalante River.
The first wash on Old Highway 279/Camino Real flooded in Cottonwood.
Hackberry Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to I-40.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Rd.
Stockton Hill Road was closed from mile marker 36 to Pierce Ferry Road.
Bogels Ranch Rd was closed from Upper Trout Creek to Back Rd.
Huffriter Crossing was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.
Pump Station Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.
Water on roadway - on US-95 in both directions near Garfield Flat Road in Mineral County, NV. Single lane alternating traffic.

Flooding was reported along North Copeland Lane and nearby homes. Large rocks and debris covered the road and residential yards. Flash flooding was also reported in the Wupatki Trails neighborhood. The flooding was at least 100 feet wide with 2-3 foot debris in the flow.
US-6 is closed in both directions approximately 10 miles north of Chalfant valley due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and road closures in Verde Lakes.

A series of moderate, to at times strong, thunderstorms moved through Capitol Reef National Park over the span of 2 to 3 hours. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 3-hour rainfall estimates showed around 1 to 2 inches within the park. As a result, a flow of 6-8 inches of water moved through Capitol Gorge, as reported by Park officials.
Minneola Rd and Yermo Rd west of Minneola were flooded. A railroad crossing signal was undermined by rushing water.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Jasper Rd and Cedar Rd.
Christopher Creek Rose at least a foot. Local roads were flooded and closed.

A flash flood wave on Ellison Creek near the cascades was 2 feet deep and 10-15 feet wider than normal flow was reported at 730 PM. The flood wave (2-3 feet deep) reached the confluence with the East Verde River by 740 PM.

Heavy rain on the northern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused significant flash flooding near Holman. Video obtained by KRQE showed fast moving water near residences in Holman, and this flooding also washed out Highway 518. Canoncito Creek overflowed again as well, creating deep water below homes and destroying a number of pastures. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar caused flash flooding and debris flow within Gavilan Canyon. Photos shared by the Lincoln County emergency manager shows mud and debris across Gavilan Canyon Road which made the roadway impassable. Photos shared also depicted significant flooding and debris flow at the Gavilan Canyon Hideaway and Escape RV Park with mud and debris making roadways impassable. Damages are estimated.

Prescott Valley Police reported hazardous flooding at the intersection of East Lakeshore Drive and East Towago Drive and the intersection of Navajo Drive and Florentine Road.       Rain Gauges in the area recorded  from 1.50 and 1.86 inches of rain.

Training thunderstorms across the southern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar in San Miguel County produced an estimated 2 to 4 inches of rainfall within the Tecolote Creek and Gallinas Creek areas which caused significant and catastropic flash flooding. Flash flooding and debris flow washed out many roadways within the area, rendering them impassable. The camp director at the Camp Blue Haven said that their playground was underwater for about 40 minutes until water receded. At 2:40 PM MDT, the chief of the Cabo Lucero Volunteer Fire Department received a call about a vehicle floating within the flood waters. When officials responded to the floating vehicle, they also discovered two people dead nearby. While initially thought to have been in their vehicle, officials later determined that the two women, 62-year-old Linda June Cummings and 84-year-old Betty Greenhaw, were swept away from a destroyed home within the Tecolote Canyon subdivision. A third individual from the same home was reported missing, and the National Guard, New Mexico State Police, and San Miguel County Sheriff's Office assised in search and rescue for several days. Finally on Tuesday, July 26th, they found the body of 62-year-old Jimmy Chris Cummings. All three were from Hale Center, Texas, but had a 100-year-lease on a cabin in Tecolote Canyon on the Camp Blue Haven property which they were visiting at the time. Eight feet of water rushing down into the canyon took down two walls of the cabin and partially destroyed the other two walls. Damages for this event are estimated.

An estimated one to two inches of rain across the northern portion of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar in Mora County. This caused significant flash flooding across the burn scar with Highway 518 and the Holman area hit particularly hard. Highway 518 was washed out from near the Taos County line to Cleveland. Video obtained from multiple broadcast media sources showed fast moving water and debris flow impacting numerous residences in Holman, Chacon, and Cleveland. Canoncito Creek was had major overflow with water flowing onto pastures, around homes, across area roadways, and one spotter remarked that it created a lake in some places. Damages are estimated.

Videos show Pinal Creek overtopping a bridge along Six Shooter Canyon Road near Delores Lane making the road impassable. Flood waters from the overtopped bridge are seen in a video traveling down Six Shooter Canyon Road. A rain gage upstream recorded 1.1 of rain in 15 minutes. No injuries or damage was reported.

Heavy rainfall over the Telegraph burn scar led to heavy runoff into Pinal Creek. The rapid increase in flow in Pinal Creek made Beer Tree Crossing impassable, with images showing barricades in place to close the road. A nearby stream gage observed a 1.84 ft increase in flow in Pinal Creek. No damage or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain fell over the western part of the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022). This caused Schultz Creek (Dry Lakes gauge) to jump 2.84 feet. This flowed over Mt Elden Road, overwhelmed the drainage system along Highway 180, and flooded apartments and homes along Stevanna Way.

Heavy rain on the northern end of the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused flooding on the Canoncito Creek. This washed out roads, destroyed pastures, and inundated homes. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010), Tunnel Fire scar (April 2022), and Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flooding in the area below. The water transported mud, ash, and debris across roads and filled ditches.
Heavy rain caused Oak Creek to rise 1.5 feet at the gauge in Sedona (OAKA3).

A heavy thunderstorm over the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar early in the day on July 23rd dropped between 0.50 and 0.75 inches of rain. This prompted a Flash Flood Warning for the burn scar, however, no reports of flooding were received. The water from this thunderstorm was held back thanks to debris flow. Around midnight, the New Mexico State EOC relayed reports of major flooding and debris flow from a light shower that was only producing a couple hundredths of an inch. This light rain was enough to release the heavier rain that had fallen earlier that day which washed out roads and impacted the Holman area. Damages are estimated.
State Route 238 was closed between Gila Bend and Maricopa due to flooding.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and rock slides across Route 80 northwest of Bisbee.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 1 hour near Tucson Mountain Park, caused flash flooding of several roads in Tucson Estates. Sheridan Ave. was washed out south of Kinney.
Heavy rain caused flooding over State Route 77 and Feedmill Road.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Dragoon Rd. south of Interstate 10.
Landscaping and trash cans washed away in front of the Space Museum due to high water flows.  The radar estimated 1.5 to 2 inches of rainfall upstream of the museum over Horse Ridge.
The Little Colorado River rose over 8 feet from 300 to 500 PM MST (Woodruff guage WDRA3).
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused a rapid rise in Canada Del Oro Wash, causing the flooding and closure of Overton Rd.
Heavy rain of 3-4 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of Highway 85 near Puerto Blanco Dr. north of Lukeville.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in the Clifton-Morenci area resulted in flash flooding and mud flows along Chase Creek which flooded Coronado Blvd. before flowing into the San Francisco River.
Heavy rain fill a wash with water four feet deep in Cameron.
Hackberry Rd was closed from Hwy 66 to I-40.
Antares Rd was closed from Hwy 66 to Pierce Ferry Rd.
Heavy rain of around 3 in 2 hours caused flash flooding of Highway 86 southeast of the Gu-Achi Trading Post. Santa Rosa Wash rose several feet north of Highway 86 but remained within its banks.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon which closed the popular slot canyon for at least a day.
Heavy rain caused water to flow bank to bank, two feet deep, moving very quickly.

Public videos showed Waterman Wash flowing with several feet of water, making Riggs Rd impassable. A water rescue was also reported in this area. Further downstream, ADOT reported that Tuthill Rd between Fairview St and Pecos Rd as well as Narramore Rd between Airport Rd and Dean Rd were closed due to flooding. These roads are unbridged crossings through Waterman Wash.
Hualapai Mountain Rd was flooded with water and debris.
Flooding was reported in Alberson Wash/Rose Creek, Lynx Creek, and Agua Fria River all the way to Skull Valley.

Heavy rain in the Church Rock and Fort Wingate areas caused flash flooding along Interstate 40 and New Mexico State Highway 118 as reported by the New Mexico Department of Transportation. There are no known damages.
Mud and debris covered Lake Mead Pkwy near Lake Las Vegas Pkwy.
Water covered the intersections of Blue Diamond and Rainbow, and Blue Diamond and Pioneer.

The Lincoln County emergency manager reported flash flooding and debris flow from the McBride burn scar at Gavilan Canyon and Warrior Drive. This forced the closure of the roadway. Local law enforcement remarked that this flooding was worse than the event on July 20th. Damages are estimated.
Flooded roads near the intersection of Decatur and Silverado Ranch stranded 15 to 20 cars.

Forest thinning in the Magdalena Mountains resulted in a flash flooding event that made it easier for water to rush down an unnamed canyon. Floodwaters left behind a pile of debris 6 feet high and 20 feet wide that included steel fence posts and barbed wire, damaged trailed, and boulders that were 200 to 300 pounds. Damages are estimated.
Las Vegas Blvd flooded underneath I-15.
Greggs Hideout Rd was closed from Pierce Ferry Rd to mile marker 10.
A COOP observer near Encino measured 1.75 inches of rain from a heavy thunderstorm. This resulted in flash flooding near their property. Time is estimated based on radar. No damage was reported.
Huffriter Crossing was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.
Heavy rain near Alamo caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 169 and mile marker 29. Damages are estimated.
Pump Station Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall in the high terrain around the town of Hildale, as well as within the town itself. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor (MRMS) 1-hour estimates showed around 1 to 2 inches of rainfall with this storm. Light to moderate rain continued for a while thereafter, with 3-hour MRMS estimates exceeding 2 inches of rainfall in spots. This rainfall ran into Short Creek, and resulted in a flow through the town of Hildale, though the flow was not significant enough to overtop any road crossings within town.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall over the course of an hour or so in the high terrain northwest of the town of Leeds, UT. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour estimates show around 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rainfall with this storm. An initial report was received of water over the bridge at Red Cliffs Campground as water flowed out of Water Canyon and through Harrisburg Creek. A short time later, a video was found on Twitter showing water flowing through the campground and overtopping the access bridge.
Bogles Ranch Rd was closed from Upper Trout Creek to Bogles Ranch.
Banegas Crossing was closed from Hwy 93 to Banegas Ranch.
Signal Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Alamo Rd.
Street flooding on South Milton was reported (videos) on social media.
Water and debris flowed over Hwy 247 north of Crestview Dr.
Water and debris flowed over Hwy 95 south of Goffs Rd.
Flash flooding in Golden Valley closed several roads and resulted in one swift water rescue of a stranded driver.
A stream gauge reported a 1.6 foot rise on Moenkopi Wash.
Several streets flooded in the Riviera and Rotary Park neighborhoods.
Reports of flooding on the Hopi Nation included First Mesa, Highway 264, Polacca Wash, and other locations.
A storm chaser posted a video of flash flooding in the Cameron area on Twitter.
A video on social media showed water flowing across New River Rd, causing the driver taking the video to turn around. A nearby FCDMC at the New River Landfill recorded over 2 of rain in an hour.
Heavy rain over the Government Tank drainage and Pipeline/Tunnel fire scars caused flooding along the side of Highway 89 with only  one lane open.

An Army representative working at the ICP on the Calf Canyon Fire reported that Gallinas Creek overflowed its banks by two to three feet. No damage was reported. Note: Previously, this fire had been referred to as the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon Fire. Officials have remained this fire the Calf Canyon Fire, therefore, from here on out, it will be referred to as such.
Sycamore Camp Rd was closed from Burro Creek Crossing to mile post 9.
Burro Creek Crossing was closed from Hwy 93 to mile post 14.
Seventeen Mile Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Signal Rd.
Heavy rain resulted in water over Highway 217 near Greenridge Boulevard. No damages were noted.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in 1 hour caused flash flooding of roadways in southeast Tucson. Road closures included Wilmot Rd. north of Noyes, Escalante Rd. at Atterbury Wash and Harrison Rd. at the Pantano Wash.
Numerous roads in and south of Golden Valley were closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in less than 1 hour in the Broadway/Alvernon area led to rises in Arroyo Chico Wash. Crossings at Plumer Ave. and others were impassable. Additionally, a man on foot was swept away near 6th St. and 9th Ave.  He was rescued, but sustained minor injuries.

Heavy rain in the Flora Vista to Bloomfield area in San Juan County caused significant flash flooding in the area. A spotter reported that approximately two feet of water covered County Road 3150, rendering it impassable. Two vehicles were washed away and one home was flooded. Near Crouch Mesa, the San Juan emergency manager reported flash flooding over area roadways, and an RV was washed out. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain of 2 to 3 inches near Lamy and Glorieta caused flash flooding in the area. A CoCoRaHS observer reported that this heavy rain flooded the arroyo in their backyard, forming a lake. Video shared by local broadcast media also showed flash flooding through a property at La Posta Way. Damages are estimated.
Stockton Hill Rd was closed.

Heavy rain in the Tesuque and Chupadero areas resulted in flash flooding. North-northwest of Tesuque, an arroyo overflowed its banks and flooded a backyard near the intersection of Tesuque Village Road and Highway 592. Flash flooding and mud flow also trapped 15 cars in a Tesuque market. Near Chupadero, the emergency manager reported that water over Rio En Medio Road in six locations along roadway. Damages are estimated.
Oatman-Topock Hwy was closed just north of I-40.
A few people were evacuated from a home that flooded in eastern Chinle near Canyon de Chelly. The time was estimated from radar.
The stream gauge on Cibcue (CBQ) Creek near the confluence with the  Salt River showed a 3.5 foot rise to 2,500 cubic feet per second.

Flash flooding was observed on the northern portion of the Calf Canyon burn scar as heavy rain estimated at 0.75 inches to 1.5 inches fell. The Rito de Gascon rose about four feet and overtopped its banks. Nearby, raging flood waters were observed along a road near Monte Aplanado. The problematic Canoncito Creek also overtopped its banks again which flooded roads and pastures and destroyed fences. Damages are estimated.
Flash flooding was reported over Highway 98 five miles east of K'ai'bii'to.  Some roads washed out in the area.
Dispatched reported Highway 35 was washed out from flooding out of Shingle Canyon.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (2022) resulted in 1-2 feet of water flowing in Schultz Creek, over Mount Elden Road, and overwhelming the culvert at Highway 180, and flowing onto the bike path next to Highway 180.  The water flowing over the highway caused a temporary closure.
Pierce Ferry Rd was closed due to flooding of the Archibald Wash.
Flooding of Short Creek closed several streets in Colorado City.
White Hills Rd was closed.
Flash flooding closed numerous roads in Golden Valley and also left water and debris on Hwy 93.
Heavy rain near Navajo washed out Service Road 9452 as water flowed out of the arroyo due to debris caught in the drainage. Damages are estimated. Time is estimated based on radar.
A report of at least a foot of running water and debris over the road near the intersection of North Florida Ave and North Scenic Drive on the north side of Alamogordo.
Video shared by local broadcast media on Twitter showed flash flooding and mud flow along County Road 117S in Nambe. There are no known damages.
Cottonwood Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to mile marker 16.
Video shared by local broadcast media shows raging water in a rural part of Pojoaque. Time is estimated based on radar data. No damage reported.
Video of rapid-moving floodwaters through a wash through Waggin' Vineyard and report that waves reached nearly 10 feet at times. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based on radar.

Videos on social media showed high flow in a wash near the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation line between Globe and San Carlos, making low water crossings through the wash impassable. Further downstream, a 5 ft rise was recorded in Gilson Wash. No damage or injuries were reported.
Flash flooding unearthed two main water pipelines (8 and 10 inch) which had to be shut down. This left around 75 people with out flowing water in Indian Wells, Dilkon, and Seba areas.
A swift water rescue took place along Indian Route 4 by Burnt Corn Wash (about 5 miles east of Pi��on) where an elderly gentleman in his car was rescued.
Flooding was reported in rural Steamboat Canyon. Water washed out a residential road.
Flash flooding was reported on the north side of Tuba City washed away dirt roads and people had to be rescued from the water.

Between 1 and 3 inches of rain fell within 1-2 hours across Apache Junction and the adjacent higher terrain north and east of the city, towards the Goldfield and Superstitions mountains. Water from those mountains drained down towards the area washes, including Weekes Wash, which runs through the city. Numerous roads were flooded and damaged along with multiple water rescues taking place of residents in homes that either were surrounded with water or had water inside them. One of the more dramatic water rescues occurred when a woman had to be rescued from her vehicle that was swept away by the flood waters of Weekes Wash and traveled half a mile downstream before encountering a box culvert. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

A video posted on social media showed strong flow moving along the Bloody Tanks Wash, resulting a street crossing the wash near Mackey Camp to be completely impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
The Arizona Department of Transportation reported SR 88 was closed due to flooding between milepost 201 and 205. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video showed Bloody Tanks Wash in major elevated stage as it was flowing down the city of Miami. No damages or injuries were reported.

Water Users Recreation Site just downstream of Saguaro Lake was closed due to flash flooding and debris deposited into the Lower Salt River, making the water unsafe for public use. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 2 hours over the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding in San Manuel and nearby areas with several dirt roads washed out.
North Lake Rd along Bartlett Lake was closed due to flooding and debris making the road impassable to vehicular traffic. No injuries were reported.
A wash in the Sedona area was flowing 8 to 10 inches deep.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 2 hours fell across the Rincon Mountains causing rises in Tanque Verde Creek that caused road closures of Wentworth Rd. and Tanque Verde Loop Rd.
Castle Rock Rd was closed from Northern Ave to Swan Dr.
Stockton Hill Rd was closed.
Flash flooding closed numerous roads in and south of Golden Valley.

Heavy rain estimated at 1 to 1.5 inches caused major flooding on the northern portion of the Calf Canyon burn scar. The Gascon and Cleveland areas were hardest hit again as they have been for most of the month of July. In Gascon, fast moving water carried logs and boulders downstream, and Highway 105 near Camp Davis was flooded. A spotter remarked that four waterfalls were rushing down Gascon Peak. Near Cleveland, signficant flooding was reported along the Rio la Casa with boulders flowing downstream. At least two bridges were flooded, including one on Highway 518. Also near Cleveland, the Canoncito Creek overflowed its banks again, flooding pastures and several properties along the creek. Highway 518 was flooded along this creek as well. Damages are estimated.
A stream gauge showed a 7 foot rise on Beaver Creek in less than 15 minutes.
Tonto Natural Bridge State Park posted pictures of Pine Creek rising 4 feet between 5:47 PM and 5:52 PM.
Tees Toh Wash was flowing about 2 feet deep about one mile west of Seba Delki.
I-15 southbound was flooded near Littlefield.
White Valley Road (N8031) was completely washed out.
Multiple intersections were flooded, large rocks washed into a road near Mountains Edge, and water poured into at least two casinos through the ceilings and walls.

La Paz County Dispatch reported the following roadways were closed due to flooding from water overflowing from Tyson Wash:  Tyson Street, North Washington Avenue from Quail Trail to Kenoyer Streets, and Plymouth Road. at Mockingbird St. No damages or injuries were reported.

A total of 2.25 inches of rain fell at the Newcalero Tribal Fish Hatchery in about an hour and a half.  Flash flooding was subsequently reported between mile markers 247 and 252 on Highway 70 with 3 feet of water and debris crossing the road. In addition to the highway flooding, six inches of water flowed into the Mescalero Community Center.
Six feet of water was flowing through Burnt Corn Wash.
Heavy rain in the Manuelito area forced the closure of New Mexico State Highway 118 at mile marker 11 in both directions due to flooding. No damages are known.

Heavy rain near Mexican Springs flooded Service Road 30. The emergency manager reported that several areas of the roadway were damaged to the flooding. Damages are estimated. Time is estimated based on radar.
Heavy rain across the Calf Canyon burn scar caused the Manuelitas Creek to overflow its banks and flood low water crossings along County Road A1. No damages were reported.
Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused the Rito San Jose to overflow its banks and flood low water crossings along County Road A4 near Rociada. No damages were reported.
A video shared via Facebook showed flash flooding in the Gallup area. Area and timing is estimated via radar as video was made unavailable shortly after it was shared. No damages are known.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) and Schultz Fire (2010) scars caused extensive flash flooding northwest through northeast of Flagstaff. Highway 89 northeast of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around mile post 425 around 442 PM MST. The following roads in far northeast Flagstaff were flooded: Copeland Lane, Gunman Road, Vista de Oro, Pioneer Valley Road, and Neptune Drive. Highway 180 northwest of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around MP 218 at 419 PM. The Stevanna Way and Coconino Estates neighborhoods on the northwest side of Flagstaff flooded with apartments, homes, and streets impacted.
Rangers at Zion National Park reported flash flooding in Pine Creek and side canyons off of Bridge Mountain due to excessive rainfall in the region.
