A video of flash flooding three miles north of Fort Defiance was posted on social media.
Hwy 190 was impassable in spots between Beatty Junction and Furnace Creek Wash Rd.
The intersection of Wilson Rd and East St was flooded.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused flash flooding and debris flow with a rock slide on County Road 65 near the E.V. Campground. Three people were rescued from flooding in this area. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain in portions of the headwaters region of the Paria River resulted in a flow downstream. The Paria River Near Kanab, Utah gauge indicated a rise from 5 CFS to over 520 CFS in a span of 10 minutes, and peaked at 842 CFS, with a rise of over 2 feet.
Nipton Rd was washed out just east of I-15.
Yates Well Rd was flooded five feet deep near I-15.
Temple Bar Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to mile marker 8.

Heavy rain in Utah caused a flash flood in the Paria River that drains into Arizona and the Colorado River near Lees Ferry. The river gauge near on the Paria River near the Colorado River peaked at 6.8 feet at 600 AM.
The river gauge on Granite Creek showed a rise of 2.55 feet in 90 minutes (at 1130 AM).  Flooding was reported on Highway 69 near milepost 295.
Heavy rain over the Pipeline, Tunnel, and Schultz Fire scars caused flash flooding that closed Highway 89 in both directions from mile marker 426 to 434.
A video showed a wash flowing over a low water crossing along 48th Street, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.

Areas downstream of the Pack Creek Fire burn scar experienced flash flooding as a result of heavy rains over the fire. This included Sunny Acres Lane north of Spanish Valley, which had to close due to flooding.

Areas downstream of the Pack Creek Fire burn scar experienced flash flooding as a result of heavy rains over the fire. This included Old City Park Road south of Moab, which had to close due to flooding.
Around 1 of heavy rain in less an 1 hour caused Valley View Wash to flood N. Flecha Dr. as well as River Rd. between Swan and Pontatoc Rds. in the Catalina Foothils.
Flash flooding closed numerous roads in and south of Golden Valley.

Heavy rain in the Rio Rancho and Vista Hills areas caused flooding. At a home in Rio Rancho, standing water was reported two inches deep in someone's backyard. In Vista Hills, dirt roads were flooded and arroyos were reported to be running. Damages are estimated.
Stockton Hill Rd was closed.
A trained spotter near Edgewood reported that their home was inundated with water from flash flooding. Damages are estimated.
SR-247 closed at Rabbit Springs Road (northbound) due to flooding and debris flows.

Flash flooding 4 SW Forest Falls. A car was reported stuck in flood waters at Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road. Ten homes were shelter in place due to flash flooding of Potato Canyon from Birch Creek. Potato Canyon Road covered in mud and debris and eventually washed out at Birch Creek. Road closed from Saturday night into Sunday morning. Rainfall of 1.8 inch was measured at Yucaipa Ridge upstream, 1.2 of which occurred in one hour.

Spring Creek was reported to be running approximately 8-9 ft in depth, impacting low water crossings through the creek. Over 2 of rain was reported to have fallen in the span of about an hour in this area. No damage or injuries were reported.

Forest Service Road 396 was closed between Stagecoach Trail and the Eads Wash Day Use Site and River Access Point due to unsafe road conditions from flash flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
SR 238 westbound was closed at milepost 41 due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Hwy 190 was flooded.

A video showed firefighters performing a swift water rescue after an SUV stalled in floodwaters when attempting to drive across a low water crossing along 7th Avenue between Greenway Parkway and Coral Gables Drive. At 1925MST, a nearby FCDMC stream gage exceeded bank full stage after recording a peak height of 8.07 ft and a peak flow of 5,080 cfs, which broke the record for this gage. No injuries were reported.
A video showed approximately 1-2 ft of water flowing across the road near 12th Street and Hatcher Road. No damage or injuries were reported.

Up to 3 ft of water and mud entered some first floor apartments at Central Avenue and Bell Road after the drainage system was overcome. Some cars in the parking lot of the apartment were also damaged. No injuries were reported.

Eagle Eye Road was closed between Salome Highway and US 60 due to flooding in multiple locations along the road. A FCDMC stream gage along Tiger Wash, which flows across an unbridged crossing along the road, briefly climbed above alarm stage after peaking at a height of 5.98 ft and a flow of 541 cfs. No damage or injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed approximately 6-8 of water flowing south down 16th Street next to Buffalo Ridge Park. No damage or injuries were reported.
A video showed six cars stalled in floodwaters at the I-17 and Greenway Road underpass. No injuries were reported.

Photos showed flooding across Scottsdale Road near Deer Valley Road, making the road impassable. Police were on scene to prevent people from attempting to cross the flooded roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon.  The popular tourist slot canyon was closed for at least a day so that the water could be removed and sand could be replaced.
A video showed a car stalled in floodwaters over two feet deep near 7th Street and Hearn Road. No injuries were reported.
A video showed Galloway Wash flowing over School House Road, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
A FCDMC stream gage along Cave Creek climbed above alarm stage, peaking at 6.24 ft and 2,459 cfs at 1943MST.

Heavy rain of 3.5 to 4 inches caused flash flooding south of Clayton. A trained spotter reported that the heavy rain caused Carrizo Creek to overflow its banks. Standing water and debris was reported across area roadways and within fields. Damages are estimated.
All the low water crossings over Short Creek were flooded and closed.
Image showed stalled SUV in floodwaters at a low water crossing along Cloud Road between 7th Street and 10th Street. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall over the high terrain near the town of Hildale over the course of an hour, with Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour estimates of around 1 to 1.5 inches of rainfall. Light to moderate rain persisted for 2 to 3 hours thereafter. The rainfall resulted in a strong flow in Short Creek through Hildale and on into Colorado City. Dispatch from Colorado City reported all street crossings across the creek were closed due to flooding, and 3 feet of fast moving water was reported to be flowing across Hildale Street.
A video of flash flooding in Antelope Canyon was posted on social media.

Elevated flow in Skunk Creek led to the closure of a low water crossing along 19th Avenue between Desert Hills Drive and Irvine Road. A nearby FCDMC stream gage along Skunk Creek recorded a peak flow of 624 cfs and a peak height of 2.71 ft. No damage or injuries were reported.
Debris and rocks across Highway 38 at Hill Ranch Road, where there was also water flowing across the road. Vehicles stuck on roadway, requiring rescue.
I-15 was flooded at Bailey Rd.
Highway 38 closed between Valley of the Falls to Lake Williams. Multiple cars stuck, requiring rescue west of Jenks Lake.
Hwy 190 was closed.
A video showed flooding on Hwy 95 south of the solar farms.
Flooding washed large rocks onto Hwy 168.
A flash flood completely buried a vehicle in mud.
Several intersections along and near Hwy 160 were flooded over a foot deep.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused Gunsight Wash to rise rapidly and flood/close Highway 85 near mile post 55.
Kelbaker Rd was flooded and severely damaged.
Hwy 127 was flooded with lots of rocks and debris in the road, and one vehicle was stuck in the water.
Longstreet and Peterson Reservoir Rds were closed.
Water and mud flowed over I-15.
Flooding damaged a road and inundated a hay field.
Lone Pine Creek flooded Whitney Portal Rd.
White Hills Rd was closed.
A woman and two dogs were stuck in flood waters.
More than 50 vehicles were stuck on Hwy 127 due to waist-deep flood waters.
Hwy 95 was flooded just north of I-40.
The intersection of Horseshoe Meadows Rd and Lubken Canyon Rd was flooded.
A trained spotter near San Fidel reported flash flooding on San Jose Loop. No damages are known.
Cottonwood Rd was closed.
All roads into, out of, and through the Mojave National Preserve were closed due to widespread flood damage.

Cruff Wash streamflow gauge reached bank full with peak flow of 1000 cfs and a rapid 3.75 foot rise. A low water crossing along Agua Caliente Rd was likely impacted. No damages or injuries were reported.
Hwy 95 was flooded.
Water and debris flowed over Horseshoe Meadows Rd.
Heavy rain northwest of Magdalena caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 169 at mile marker 9.8, forcing the closure of the roadway. No damages are known.

Numerous roads in and around Golden Valley were closed, and multiple water rescues took place. One fatality occurred when a truck overturned in a normally dry wash. The decedent was discovered several days later.

Flash flooding across the High Desert. Two to three feet of water across the roadway at SR-18 and Johnson Road north of Phelan. SR-247 at Rabbit Springs closed due to flooding. Also, report from MPing of street/road flooding with road closures. Vehicles stranded by flood waters.
Oatman Hwy was closed.
Flash flooding stranded a train and closed numerous roads.
Heavy rain on the Rito de Gascon within the Calf Canyon burn scar caused it to overflow its banks and cause debris and ash flow within the area. No damages are known.
Oatman-Topock Hwy was closed.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of roadways from southeast to north central Tucson. Road closures included Escalante at Atterbury Wash, Harrison and Pantano Wash, Old Spanish Trail and Freeman Road, Bears Path Rd. south of Tanque Verde Road and Rudasill at Pima Wash.
Water flowed over roads.
Heavy rain of 1 in less than 1 hour caused streets to become flooded and impassable in eastern portions of Nogales. Morley Ave. was closed at Madison St.
Heavy rain near Santa Clara Pueblo caused the Santa Clara Creek to overflow its banks and cause flash flooding in the area. No damage was reported.
Mineral Park Rd was closed.

Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 fell in less than 1 hour over the Finger Rock Canyon watershed with 2.29 recorded in 30 minutes at the Mt. Kimball gauge near the headwaters, which was in the severe burn area of the 2020 Bighorn Fire burn scar. Finger Rock Wash rose over 14 feet at a downstream gauge at the mouth of the canyon. Residents of seven homes and 12 people from another which was used as an assisted living facility were evacuated due to as much as 3 feet of water inside the structures.  Most of the structures will be purchased by the county and torn down. Several of the roads in the area were washed out and the wash structure itself was damaged.
Car stalled in 4 feet of water at Highway 38 at Stanfield Cutoff. Parties trapped inside were rescued by Fire Department. Road was closed to clear debris.

Roadway flooding near 1509 Shay Rd in Big Bear City. North and south side of Shay Road was flooded. Storm survey by WCM showed several inches of water still flowing over Shay Road. Radar estimated 2 to 3 inches of rain in less than 3 hours. Water flowed around numerous homes, flowing into Baldwin Lake. Nearby Big Bear Yard reported 1.80 inches.
The intersection of Lilac and Acoma was flooded. The spotter measured 0.66 of rain in 25 minutes.
Two to three feet of water flooding across the roadway at SR18 and Johnson Road.
Highway 62 was flooded with water and debris between Sunfair Rd and Rotary Way.
Westbound Highway 164 was closed due to flooding.
Emery County dispatch reported state Route 29 was impassible from milepost 9 to Joes Valley Reservoir. Up to a foot of mud and debris was deposited across the road.
Highway 95 was closed in both directions due to flooding.
Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek. Water was several feet deep and came within 2 feet or so from the bottom of the bridge on state Route 24.
The river gauge in Granite Creek at Prescott measured a rise from 7.08 feet to 9.51 feet in about 30 minutes.

Heavy rain over the Calf Canyon burn scar during the afternoon drained towards the Las Vegas area through the evening hours. An inebriated motorcyclist attempted to cross a flooded low water crossing at Gallinas Creek and El Llano Road in Las Vegas, but had to be rescued when they failed. Any potential injuries to the motorcyclist are unknown. Timing of this event is a rough estimate given radar. Damages are estimated.
Big Horn Pass road was closed due to flooding and debris on the roads. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based from radar.
The Nipton Rd offramp from I-15 was flooded.
A member of the public reported that the intersection of Spring Drive SE and Black Hills Road SE near Cabezon was underwater from fast flowing flood waters. No damages were reported.
Heavy rain caused 4 to 6 inches of fast moving water to impact the intersection of Frost and Broken Arrow near Sedillo. No damages were reported.
Hwy 190 was completely impassable east of Panamint Valley Rd due to a large flow of water, debris, and rocks.
Highway 266 was closed from Highway 168 to Highway 95. Rocks, debris, and mud four to six feet deep blocked a 30 mile stretch of the highway.
A COOP observer near Villanueva reported that the heavy rain caused flooding with water over roadways within the village. No damage was reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 90 minutes caused flash flooding of roads and yards northwest of the intersection of Highway 90 and Route 82.

Heavy convective precipitation combined with glacial melt from the Whitney Glacier on Mount Shasta to create a debris flow down Whitney Creek, downstream from the Lava Fire scar.  This resulted in the closure of US97 between 1700 PDT and 2100 PDT.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain moved through an area near the McKinney wildfire in the evening.  Rainfall was estimated to be between 1 and 3 inches in an hour. This created a debris flow down Humbug Creek, on the eastern edge of the fire.  Four vehicles were reported swept off a culvert over Humbug Creek, and videos showed the swiftly rising water in the area.  One person had to be rescued from a partially submerged vehicle.  He sustained injuries, but survived.

A thunderstorm set up over the a portion of the 2021 River Complex Burn Scar and caused a debris flow as reported by Trinity County OES on Coffee Creek on 2 August. The debris flow caused Coffee Creek Road to be unpassable. A Flash Flood Warning was issued shortly after 03/0110Z.
Heavy rain in Chacon near the Calf Canyon burn scar caused flooding across Highway 121. No damages were known.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused flash flooding in and around Rociada. Heaviest rains drained into Capulin Canyon flowing to the Rito San Jose and San Jose Church. Video shared on Twitter showed flood waters approaching homes, but exact damages are unknown. Damages are estimated.
A report of 1.63 inches of heavy rain within one hour on the Calf Canyon burn scar flooded New Mexico State Road 105 near Gascon. No damages were known.
Heavy rain in the Tajique area caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 55, rendering it impassable as crews worked to clear water and debris off the roadway. No damages were known.
The Lincoln County emergency manager reported flash flooding on Gavilan Ridge within the McBride burn scar that forced road crews to clean up debris on area roadways. Damages are estimated.
Heavy monsoon rain caused a flash flood at a normally dry wash. The flood swept away a truck at N Stephen Rd and Blake Ranch Rd, causing one fatality.
Water, dirt, and rocks covered Highway 136 southeast of Keeler. A few cars were stranded, and the highway was closed from Lone Pine to Highway 190.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Route 80 northwest of Bisbee.

Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Davis Rd. east of Route 80 north of Bisbee. Flash flooding also occurred in Tombstone with the road washed out at the intersection of Ave. De La Loma & S. Laguna Ave.

ADOT webcams showed flooding at the I-17 and Greenway Road underpass, making the road impassable. Flooding was also reported at the I-17 and Thunderbird Road underpass. No damage or injuries were reported.

Multiple videos and pictures on social media showed Dreamy Draw Wash flowing across low water crossings near 12th Street and Kaler Drive as well as 14th Street and Desert Park Lane. No damage or injuries were reported.

A video on social media showed a large amount of mud and rock debris across a low water crossing along Onyx Avenue near 42nd Street, indicating high flow in Tatum Wash earlier in the morning had made the road impassable. Further downstream along 40th Street near Mission Lane, another video indicated flow in the wash climbed high enough to overtop a bridge, partially pushing a guardrail over and leaving mud and small debris on the bridge. No injuries were reported.
Video showed I-17 southbound at Indian School Road under about a foot of water with law enforcement having to push a stalled vehicle out. No injuries were reported.

The Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gage along East Fork Cave Creek exceeded alarm stage, peaking at a height of 2.15 feet and a flow of 473 cfs and impacting a downstream low water crossing along 7th Avenue. No damage or injuries were reported.
ADOT reported that SR 72 at milepost 30 near Bouse was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported. Timing was estimated from radar.
Highway 190 was flooded and closed 4.5 miles E of Highway 136.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar produced flash flooding in Rociada. Video shared by localy broadcast media showed fast moving debris flow overrunning property and structures. Damages are a rough estimate.
Highway 62 was closed near Rotary Way due to dirt, debris, and road damage.

A reporter for the Santa Fe New Mexican relayed reports of flash flooding on the Medio burn scar. A large work truck was found destroyed from the flood waters, and large boulders and trees were moved and found in the streambed. The date of this event was not clear, and thus date and timing is a rough estimate based on radar. Damages are estimated.
Every road in Death Valley National Park was closed, and several were damaged by flooding as well. One vehicle was stuck in mud near Stovepipe Wells, and the Cow Creek water system was broken.
A mud, dirt, and rock slide closed Highway 136 at Keeler.
Highway 168 was flooded near Deep Springs College.

Flash flooding on the Calf Canyon burn scar led to flash flooding and debris flow in the Holman area. A couple of homes near New Mexico State Road 518 one half mile south of State Road 121 were impacted by the flood waters, and water was reported over the roadway in some spots. Signifcant flooding was also reported on Canoncito and Encinal Creeks, endangering property and destroying pastures. County Road B-022 was flooded all the way across State Road 518 to the Mora River. Damages are estimated.

It was reported on August 5 by a Washoe County official that flash flooding occurring on August 4 closed the lower Whites Creek trail in Galena Creek Park from Timberline Road to Thomas Creek Road due to extensive trail damage from recent flooding. It was also reported that rainfall amounts between 2.5 and 3 inches occurred in the area on Thursday 8/4.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar led to flash flooding and debris flow in the Cleveland area. Flash flooding was reported along New Mexico State Road 518 with flood waters very close to nearby homes. Damages are estimated.

Duckwater road near Fish Creek was closed due to a dirt portion of the road being washed out by flooding. This occurred south of the Eureka county line in White Pine county. Monsoonal moisture aided in producing thunderstorms with the capability of producing brief heavy rain, or storms with high rainfall rates.
Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar drained into Montezuma, flooding New Mexico State Road 65 and forcing the closure of the roadway at mile marker 4. Damages are not known.
Heavy rain in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise in Nogales Wash, causing it to overtop its banks and flood the Doe St. Bridge.

The Schultz Creek gauge showed a 5 foot rise in about 30 minutes. The upstream rain gauge measured 0.71 inches in 30 minutes. The Flagstaff Emergency Manager reported 1.5-2 feet of water from Schultz Creek flowing over Mt Elden Road. This flow over toped portions of Highway 180 closing both lanes.||This event was larger than the previous flood event in this area. Several dozen homes were directly impacted by the flood waters and several streets are impassable due to mud and flood waters. Highway 180 (primary access to Flagstaff from the northwest was close form around 1230 PM through at least 300 PM MST.||Flooding had severe impacts for the ongoing construction projects, public infrastructure and private property in the area. Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused flash flooding on Highway 434 near El Turquillo. A vehicle containing the 30-year-old driver John Vasquez and a 64-year-old passenger Benjamin Torres attempted to cross the flooded roadway, but were unsuccessful as the vehicle was caught in the flood waters. Vasquez was able to escape through an open car window with only minor injuries, but Torres remained trapped in the vehicle. Once the flood waters receded, first responders discovered Torres deceased in the vehicle 100 yards downstream. Vasquez was arrested and charged with vehicular homicide while under the influence of alcohol and fleeing an accident with knowledge of death or great bodily harm. Damages are estimated for the loss of the vehicle.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar caused flash flooding in Government Wash. The water flowed east of Highway 89 and over topped Vista Del Oro and Heritage Drive, generally less than one foot deep and otherwise stayed within the ditches.
Water, sand, gravel, and rocks covered Navajo Route 60 in several locations near Castle Butte.
A webcam showed Russell Gulch experiencing a flash flood of at least a few feet high. No damages or injuries were reported.
The river gauge on the Verde River near Perkinsville measured 12.16 feet. Base flow is about 2 feet.
Walnut Creek Road was flooded.
Big Bug Creek in Spring Valley rose 1-2 feet.
The Aqua Fria-Mayer river gauge measured a two foot rise.

The Surprise Emergency Manager said there was significant flash flooding in the Asante Community, with evidence of water over the roads. The Emergency Manager also shared there was significant mud and runoff at a water treatment plant near 29 Palms RV Park. On social media there were several reports of at least minor street flooding around the area as well. Timing of impacts estimated from radar. No reports of damage or injuries from flooding.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 1 hour east of Saint David caused flash flooding in town. Homes were flooded near Cottonwood and Miller Lanes.
Nearly 1.5 of rain in 30 minutes on the Empire Mountains washed out Hilton Ranch Rd. which leads to the KEMX radar.
Six inches of water flowed through the intersection of Prescott Ave and Del Mar St.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused flooding along Highway 105 and Highway 276. This forced the closure of Highway 105 at mile marker 5 and the closure of Highway 276 at mile marker 0. Damages are estimated.
Pinto Basin Road in Joshua Tree National Park was closed due to washes running over road. The water was estimated to be running 1 foot in depth over the road. No damages or injuries were reported.
The intersection of Yucca Mesa Rd and Aberdeen Dr was flooded.
Box Canyon Road near I-10 was closed due to flooding. Vehicle with two occupants was stranded in the flood water. No damages or injuries were reported.

More than 200 people were stranded at the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway as heavy rain in the San Jacinto Mountains and State Park caused impassible mudflows along the exit road from the valley station. Operations of Palm Springs said mud began flowing down east of the station onto the road. The flow appeared to be mostly mud, and not debris. Rainfall of 1.99 inches was measured at the Mt San Jacinto Peak RAWS site.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Interstate 40 due to flooding.
South Boundary Road of Joshua Tree National Park was closed due to flooding. All visitors were evacuated from the southern portion the park. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flash flooding occurred through the mid to late evening hours. Multiple cars were stalled across Deming, underpasses were flooded and at least one house started taking in water.
Ogilby Rd was closed due to flood debris and a road washout. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
CHP Incident report of a large rock slide and portions of S2 extending into San Diego County washed out.
Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road near the intersection of Eagle Creek Canyon Road in Ruidoso. Damages are estimated.
Flooding was reported along SR-95 Northbound near Cyprus Mine Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along SR-95 northbound near the Yuma and La Paz County Line. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along SR-95 Northbound near Blevens Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1-2' in 1 hour in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise in Nogales Wash. The Doe St. bridge was overtopped and nearby roadways were flooded.
Flooding was reported in Dry Valley.

The river gauge at Granite Creek showed nearly a 4 foot rise in one hour. It rose from 7.19 feet at 230 PM to 10.96 feet at 320 PM. Ten feet is considered moderate flood stage and 11 feet major flood stage.  The gauge dropped below major flood stage at 445 PM and below flood stage at 545 PM.
Southbound Interstate 15 was flooded near Nipton Road, and closed to the Nevada state line. One person was injured (indirect) in a crash on the wet highway before it was closed.

Heavy rain near Golden caused flash flooding on Puertocito Road, forcing the closure of the roadway with debris and large boulders rendering it unpassable. Time of the report is estimated based on radar. Damages are estimated.
Highway 127 was flooded at Baker Blvd.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Camino Verde Rd. near Bilby.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Tangerine Rd. between Interstate 10 and Twin Peaks Rd.
Oatman Highway was closed from mile marker 40 to Silver Creek Road.
Highway 127 was closed between mile markers 15 and 21.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed due to flooding.
White Hills Road was closed due to flooding.
The Vock Wash flooded Stockton Hill Road.
Six inches of water with lots of rocks and debris flowed over Pierce Ferry Road.
Multiple roads were closed due to flooding.
Highway 95 was closed due to flooding.
Highway 165 was closed from Highway 95 to Nelson due to flooding in multiple locations.

The MIC at the Elko office reported that 1 to 2 miles east of the South Fork Reservoir, a wash on the east side of the lake filled and overflowed. It was also noted that the overflowing water picked up some debris or had some mixed in it. The water overflowed onto the road for a few inches of depth. Additionally, it was noted that the road that goes around the lake has a steep cliff, and mud and dirt came down the cliff onto the road. This occurred inside a Flood Advisory that was in effect for the area.
Heavy rain over the northern portion of the Pipeline fire cause flash flooding over Highway 89. Both directions were closed due to the flooding between milepost 428 and 430.
Two feet of water was flowing in Yaber Wash. The water was 40 to 50 feet wide with low water crossings flooded.
A video of a flood in Big Bug Creek was posted on social media. The creek is normally dry.
SR-238 was completely closed between Gila Bend and SR-347 due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Stream gauge at Delaney Wash reached above action stage at 1.90 feet at 1859 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 on the Bighorn burn scar caused rapid rises in Finger Rock Wash. Road closures resulted near Havasu Rd and Columbus Blvd and Pontatoc Rd. south of Skyline Dr.
Charleston Blvd was flooded one to one and a half feet deep near Jones.

NV Roads website reported adverse driving conditions due to a mudslide caused by heavy rain in the area. The slide occurred between mile markers 21 and 24 on NV-722, SW of the city of Austin, in Lander County. Both sides of the highway were affected. The roadway was not closed.
Highway 70 was closed between mile markers 242 and 247.  Heavy debris was across the road near mile marker 242.  Rainfall amounts in excess of 1 inch in an hour were recorded near the burn scar.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Road and Stockton Hill Road.
Flash flooding over Highway 160 was reported (Social Media and Law Enforcement) between on Highway 160 between Tonalea, Shonto, and Tsegi. Highway 98 was flooded near Shanto Wash.
A Summit County official reported a foot of water and some gravel spilled out onto Chalk Creek Road.
The Dilkon Chapter House received multiple reports of Tribal members calling for help because of washed out dirt roads.  Indian routes 6 and 7 were flooded between Indian Wells and White Cone.

The Cornfields Chapter House reported that water was overtopping Navajo Route 15 with Law Enforcement diverting traffic. Greaswood Springs Road to Klagetoh was flooded.  State Route 264 was flooded near County Road 317.
Water and mud covered Goffs Road in multiple locations.
Multiple roads were closed due to flooding.

The Havasu Creek Gauge at Supai Village showed water rising 4 feet in 30 minutes from 430 PM to 500 PM. The stream crested around 530 PM (1970 CFS) at 5 feet above normal levels .  The flow remained elevated through 700 PM.
Video shared by local broadcast media showed flooding and debris flow on the Cerro Pelado burn scar near Sierra de Los Pinos and the East Fork Jemez River. No damages are known.

Several side streets and low lying areas flooded along Mill and Pack Creeks as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar. Water ran out of its banks in many spots. The Mill Creek stream gauge in Moab increased by 9 feet in 2 hours. Additionally, areas near Moab reported 0.80 to 1.2 inches of rain.
Flash flooding occurred at the intersection of Pack Creek Road and La Sal Loop Road as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar. Water pummeled the bridge and flowed over the road.
Flash flooding occurred north-northwest of Moab as a result of heavy rain. Social media reports showed a prolific waterfall over slick rock with water flowing on the side of Utah Highway 128.
Flash flooding occurred on Kane Springs Road as a result of heavy rain. Social media reports showed a prolific waterfall over slick rock.
A swift water rescue was performed near mile post 40 on Alamo Road.
The intersection of 4th Ave and 22nd St around the Post Office in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
East County 14th Street in Yuma was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain over the Pipeline, Tunnel, and Schultz fire scars caused flash flooding in the area that closed Highway 89 in both directions.
Tyson wash was reported to hit 12 feet deep with debris. No damages or injuries were reported.
The river gauge on Agua Fria measured a 5 foot rise in 15 minutes (starting at 1215 PM MST).
SR-238 was closed entirely from Gila Bend to SR 347 due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding southeast of Three Points including Sierra Mountain Rd.
High flows were reported in the Clear Creek drainage in the southeastern portion of Zion National Park.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Main Street.

Heavy rain of 2-3 at the headwaters of Sabino Creek and Bear Canyon caused rapid rises in both streams. Flash flooding occurred at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area causing damage to trails and flooding of all recreation area bridges. Twenty five people became stranded in Bear Canyon and needed to be rescued as trails across the wash were flowing heavily and dangerously impassable. No injuries were reported.
Burro Creek Crossing Road was closed from Highway 93 to mile marker 14.
Sycamore Creek Road was closed from Burro Creek Crossing.
Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed, and one swift water rescue was performed.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Rock Canyon Creek where the water rose 3.5 feet.
Temple Bar Road was closed due to flooding.
Highway 95 was flooded near mile marker 71.

Videos showed washes overflowing in Fountain Hills, with water moving across Golden Eagle Park and then downstream over North El Pueblo Boulevard. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media pictures and video showed flooding along SR-87 near Shooting Range Road. Water appeared to be several inches deep, flowing over the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on SR-87 Northbound near N Fort McDowell Rd (MP 191). No damages or injuries were reported.
Jumbo Wash flooded Willow Beach, requiring evacuations.
Flooding was reported on the southbound lanes of SR-87 near Milepost 180. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Image from social media along Hackney Avenue in Globe showed a destroyed pickup truck lying along a box culvert, likely swept away by flood waters several feet deep along a wash running adjacent to the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

A rock slide was reported along Highway 68 between Taos and Embudo. This rock slide was likely caused by repeated rounds of rainfall and not just this one event. Exact time of the rock slide is unknown and is estimated from radar. Damages are estimated.
Flooding reported along Loop-101 near East Cactus Road in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Picture shows Russell Rd near Utility St impassable due to flash flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding on roadway near the intersection of North Via Linda and East Via de Ventura in Scottsdale. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video showed running flood waters, several inches in depth, in the intersection of North Tatum Road and East Doubletree Ranch Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported along the entrance ramp at Princess Drive onto the Loop 101 in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Video showed Cactus Park in Scottsdale flooded with multiple feet of standing water. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

A video on social media showed flooding outside of a hose near Hotevilla. Another video showed water up to the road on Route 2 just south of Kykotsmovi Village. Hopi Police reported that water covered Highway 264 for a distance of 100 yards near mile marker 369 at 725 PM MST.  Arizona Department of Transportation had to send crews out to removed mud from the flood.
Flooding reported along US-60 near milepost 75. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Numerous videos and photos from the media and the public showed street flooding in the West Jordan area. One basement was flooded. Time of this report is estimated.

Video showed Indian Bend Wash running multiple feet deep, resulting in a car nearly submerged by the running flood waters along McCormick Parkway in Scottsdale. The person inside the vehicle had to be rescued by the Fire Department. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard, located about 3 miles upstream of the incident showed peak flow of 2.92 feet (1875 cfs), which was above alarm stage, at 1640 MST. Additional flow of just over 1000 cfs was likely added to the wash from the Berneil Wash, located about 1 mile upstream of the incident. The gauge along the Indian Bend Wash at Shea Boulevard did not go below alarm stage until just after 2015 MST. No injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Jackrabbit Wash just downstream of North Vulture Mine Road indicated water levels rising above the alarm stage of 2.9 feet at 1800 MST. The flow peaked at 5.70 feet (6000 cfs) at around 1910 MST.  Impacted area included Wickenburg Road, located about 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages or injuries were reported.
Caltrans report of flash flooding with water and debris flowing over the road on Highway 78 and Borrego Springs Road.

Video showed a car submerged from the floodwaters of Indian Bend Wash along East Starlight Way and North Hayden Road. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge near the incident showed water levels above alarm stage at 1815 MST, peaking at 4 feet (3397 cfs) at 1924 MST, and dropping below alarm stage at around 2145 MST. No injuries were reported.

Video images from social media showed raging flood waters occurring near Salome Highway just east of US-60. Timing estimated from radar. In addition, the Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge located along Centennial Wash in Wenden showed water levels rising above alarm stage at around 1950 MST, peaking at 3.37 feet (1323 cfs) at around 2034 MST and not going below alarm stage until around 2330 MST. The impacted areas from Centennial Wash include Salome Road, which is located about 4.8 miles downstream of the gauge location in Wenden. No damages or injuries were reported.
Multiple road closures due to flooding were reported in Aguila from the Flood Control District of Maricopa County. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Hackberry Road was closed.

Broadcast video showed a lady stuck at a skate park located along the Indian Bend Wash near McDowell Road in Scottsdale. Rescuers unable to get to her for a couple of hours at least due to the flood waters of several feet along the wash. An aerial rescue was performed around 2215 MST. Just 2 miles upstream along the wash near Indian School Road, a Flood County District of Maricopa County gauge reported water levels going above alarm stage after 1830 MST, rising to a record stage of 5.76 feet (3929 cfs) at around 1907 MST. The water level did not go below flood stage until several hours after, at 230 MST on the 13th. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on Sate Route 98 near K'ai'bii'to.

Several vehicles were stuck in flooding on Highway 62 near mile marker 62.
SR-177, just north of Desert Center, was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

A flash flood was reported on Highway 89 about 8 miles northeast of Doney Park (mile post 430...north of Wupatki Trails and south of the Sunset Crater turnoff).  The highway was closed in both directions.  Flooding also overtopped the highway at Brandis Way.
Scenic Drive in Capitol Reef National Park was closed due to flooding in the Grand Wash.
Cottonwood Road was closed.
Highway 62 was flooded near Hillview Road.
Flash flooding produced a washout on Ophir Canyon Road. Time of the event is estimated based on reports.
Several roads in Golden Valley were closed.
Highway 78 near Milepost 53 was flooded, with multiple vehicles stuck in the floodwaters. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway 78 was flooded at Milpitas Wash with debris across the road. A vehicle was reported to have been damaged by the rocks on the road. No injuries were reported.
Two roads were flooded and impassable.
Six to eight inches of rapidly flowing water crossed roads in Grand Wash and Capitol Gorge in Capitol Reef National Park.

Spotter reported via Facebook, that water running over US Highway 50, about 2 miles SE of Ruth. The observer sent a photo and estimated the water was about 6 to 12 inches over the road. Some sand and silt were noted in the photo as well.
Ogilby Road closed near the intersection with Sidewinder Road due to flooding. Vehicles were stranded between two washes pushing sediment and debris onto roadways. No injuries were reported.
White Hills Road was closed.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour fell upstream to north of the Catalina Mountains in Pinal County. The Canada Del Oro Wash flowed over its banks south of Edwin Rd.
Needles Highway was flooded.
Flooding was reported on US-95 near Milepost 60. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on US-95 near Milepost 72. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in Oracle caused extensive street flooding throughout the town.
The stream gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek showed almost a one foot rise in 30 minutes.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms washed out a large portion of State Road 211 near the intersection of Utah Highway 191. Significant water flowed across the highway. Vehicles were stranded in the area as a result.
A spotter reported major flooding around Kirkland due to very heavy rain.  That wash flows south then west toward Bagdad.
Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed, and one swift water rescue was performed. A rain gauge measured 2.48 in one hour.
Flooding was reported on Highway 191 near Wide Ruin.
Hualapai Mountain Road was flooded near mile marker 5.

Heavy rain across the Rafael Fire (June 2021) caused a flash flood that entered the Verde River. The river gauge showed a 2.5 foot (600 CFS) increase in flow. The Verde River is a main stem river so flooding was not an issue once the flow reached that river.
Hackberry Road was closed.
Heavy rain (2.40 inches in a short time) caused flooding in Model Creek and water was flowing over the Peeples Valley Road near the Model Creek School.
The Antelope Creek river gauge at Wickenburg Ranch started rising at 430 PM (around 349 CFS) and peaked at 1359 CFS at 455 PM MST.
Mineral Park Road was closed from Highway 93 to the mine entrance.
Chicken Springs Road was closed.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Pictures on Social Media showed that the road from Polacca to Low Mountain was washed out and impassable. The wash likely flooded to Tolani Lake.

A video showed a flood wave traveling down Pinal Creek in Six Shooter Canyon before overtopping a bridge along Six Shooter Canyon Road. Flood waters could be seen traveling down the road making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
A flash flood was observed in the Pine Creek Slot Canyon due to earlier heavy rain upstream on Clear Creek.

The FCDMC streamflow gage along 4th of July Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along Agua Caliente Road. The gage peaked at a depth of 0.74 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.
Images showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to high flow over low water crossings. Timing and exact location estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Washes were reported to be running across SR 72 and McVay Road, causing impacts to the roadways. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding in Pima, AZ.  Highway 70 became flooded and impassable.
Several videos of major flooding north of Chinle were posted on social media.
Multiple instances of flooding were reported along SR 95 south of Quartzsite, impacting travel on the roadway. No injuries were reported.

ADOT reported that SR 95 was closed due to flooding near milepost 80. There were also reports of a couple of cars that attempted to cross the flooded road but were not able to make it across and had to be pulled out. No injuries were reported.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek near the Colorado River showed a 5 foot rise (to 1500 CFS) in less than 15 minutes.  This flooding was downstream from The Supai Village.
SR 95 north of Quartzsite was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Antares Road was closed.
Multiple roads were closed in and near Golden Valley, and one swift water rescue was performed.
Flooding was reported in farmland and along roads near the Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City. This wash flows west then south to the Little Colorado River.
Flash flooding was reported in Clear Creek within Zion National Park.
Heavy roadway flooding and minor basement flooding occurred in Colorado City.
A flash flood on Short Creek in Hildale flooded a home.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and Tunnel/Pipeline fire scar (2022) caused flash flooding.  North Copeland Lane was overtopped with muddy water and debris 8 inches deep and 10 to 15 feet wide. There was also minor flooding of Henry Drive near Campbell Avenue.
Lower Antelope Canyon was close due to flash flooding. Water remained in the popular tourist attraction (sandstone slot canyon) through much of August 16 due to residual flood waters (large puddles).

The Hot Na Na Wash in Marble Canyon (16.5 miles down the Colorado River from Less Ferry) experienced a major flash flood. A rafting party arrived at camp around 600 PM. The wash began to flow around 615 PM and ran well past midnight. The wash was raging at around 700 PM. The waterfall from the flood hit the rock layer below and splashed back up in the air more than 30 feet. Several bodies of farm large animals were in the flood.|Radar precipitation images indicated that heavier rain also fell in the Tanner Wash drainage to the east through south of Hot Na Na Wash.  However, no reports from this area were received.
Major flooding was reported north of Many Farms Lake.
Indian Route 15 from Burnside to Greasewood flooded in areas and there were puddles on the road. This is a paved road.

The river gauge on the Little Colorado River near Cameron showed a 3 foot rise between 715 PM and 1115 PM.  The majority of this flow was likely from the Moenkopi Wash that had a flash flood the day before.
The IMET on the Calf Canyon fire reported flash flooding along New Mexico 276 due to the Maestas Creek overfilling its banks. Damages are not known.
Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar caused Canoncito Creek to overfill its banks and flood Highway 518. Damages are not known.
Highway 62 was flooded, and Lucerne Vista Ave was flooded between Yucca Trail and Pueblo Trail.
Swiftly flowing water up to the windows of a car swept it off of Highway 95.
The south end of Joshua Tree National Park was closed due to flooding along Pinto Basin Road between Ocotillo Patch and the Cottonwood Visitor Center. No damage or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain on the Calf Canyon burn scar ran into the Rito San Jose, causing it to overfill its banks. This caused significant flooding near Rociada as high and fast-moving water ran up against a house near Highway 105 and County Road A4B. Water nearly swept away a large propane tank as well. Reports were also received of water near another building in Rociada and with water up to the bumpers of several parks vehicles. Damages are a rough estimate.
Flash flooding was reported in Clear Creek, Pine Creek, and Spry Canyon in Zion National Park.
Heavy rain near Church Rock forced the closure of Interstate 40 in both directions at mile marker 33.

The Colfax County emergency manager reported minor damage to State Route 21 as the nearby Moras Creek and Rayado Creek flowed over the roadway. Damage was mainly along the shoulder. Damages are estimated.
The North Fork Virgin - Springdale, Nr gauge rose from near 50 cfs. to 1160 cfs. A corresponding rise over 3 ft. was recorded on the gauge height.
Flash flooding was reported in the Tse Bonito Wash and across State Route 264 in Window Rock.

Video shared on the social media platform Tik Tok showed impressive and devastating flash flooding near Sheep Springs. A massive wave of water near U.S. Highway 491 swept horse trailers, farm equipment, and lawn furniture downstream. Water overtopped the hoods of parked vehicles and inundated a few structures and residences. Damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain near Tse Bonito caused water to flow over State Route 264 at mile marker 1. Reports were received of cars stalled on the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain near Yah-Ta-Hey caused water to flow over State Route 264 at mile markers 9 through 10. Any damages are not known.
Flash flooding reported along County Road 4990 at Armenta Wash near Bloomfield with water flowing over the roadway. This completely destroyed the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain fell over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) and caused flooding in Wupatki Trails and into Cinder Lakes and closed Highway 89 about a mile north of the neighborhood.
Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road, near Warrior Drive. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and the Tunnel/Pipeline Fire scar (2022) caused flooding over a driveway near Glodia Drive and Copland Lane.  A large debris flow was also seen at the intersection of Campbell Avenue and Henry Drive.
The steam gauge on Agua Fria River near Cordes Junction showed a 3.47 foot rise.
A stream gauge on Dry Beaver Creek showed a 1.55 foot rise.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Main Street.

A FCDMC stream gage along Sols Wash exceed alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing on Vulture Mine Road. At 1529MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 2.51 feet and a flow of 1,577 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.
Short Creek flooded all the road crossings in Colorado City.
Social media videos showed flash flooding over roads in and near Hildale.
A swift water rescue was performed.

The San Juan County emergency manager reported flash flooding at Chaco National Park. High water rises were reported along the Chaco River, and one unknown roadway within the park was completely destroyed. Time of this report is estimated based on radar, and damages are also estimated.
A stream gauge on the Wet Beaver Creek measured a 2.15 foot rise.
Boundary Cone Road was closed.
Heavy rain caused a 2.2 foot rise in Newman Canyon which flows into Upper Lake Mary.
Oatman Highway was closed.
ADOT reported flooding on SR 95 near milepost 111, impacting travel on the road. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
A wash was reported to be flowing six inches in depth across Cibola Road off of SR 95. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
Flash flooding was reported along Pine Creek near the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel.
Cane Beds Road was closed near East 3100, and Rosy Canyon Road was closed to the UT state line.
Highway 95 was flooded just south of the CA/NV state line.
Oatman Highway was closed.
Oatman Highway was closed.
Daisy Mountain Fire and Medical reported a swift water rescue on Country Road near New River Road after a person attempted to cross a flooded low water crossing. No injuries were reported.
Several roads flooded and one car was floated.
MCDOT reported Bartlett Dam Road at Cave Creek road was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Shinarump Drive was flooded.
Flooding blocked Highway 62 and Parker Dam Road, and there were rockslides along Parker Dam Road.
The Navajo Times reported a major flash flood in lower K'ai'bii'to Creek. Water flooded a portion of State Route 98. Heavy equipment was used to remove water, debris, mud, and rock from the road.
A video showed flooding on 14th Street south of Carefree Highway, impacting travel on the roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.
Interstate 40 was closed for a time on the eastern side of Joseph City.
CHP reported that U.S. 95 north of Blythe was closed due to flooding. There were also reports of vehicles washed off the roadway. No injuries were reported.
Flooding at 59th Avenue and Greenway Road caused the roadway to become impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
The stream gauge on Wet Beaver Creek showed a 4.5 foot rise in 60 minutes (6 ENE of Lake Montezuma).  A gauge down steam (2 SW McGuireville) showed a 6.5 foot rise in less than an hour.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in less than 2 hours caused flash flooding in Oro Valley and the closures of Overton and Hardy Roads and Linda Vista Blvd.

Flows increased on the North Fork of the Virgin River in Zion National Park. The trail became impassable near the mouth of The Narrows. Flood waters in The Narrows swept some hikers off their feet and isolated others on higher ground. Two people were swept downstream. One was swept a couple of hundred yards and found. The individual survived with minor injuries. The other was reported as missing to Zion National Park officials later that evening, and was found deceased the following Monday. The North Fork Virgin - Springdale river gauge, which is downstream from The Narrows, rose from approximately 75 cfs to 735 cfs, corresponding to a rise of slightly over 2 feet in height.
Flash flooding was reported in the vicinity of The Narrows in Zion National Park.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 caused flash flooding and road closures in southwest Tucson along Camino Verde as well as Old Ajo Hwy.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding and road closures in Picture Rocks.  A school bus became stuck in floodwaters at Ina and Sandario Rds.
Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar caused water and debris to flow over Devil's Canyon Road at an Eagle Creek low water crossing. Damagers were not known.
The Hildale Dispatch reported two road closures near waterways due to rises from flash flooding.
Short Creek flooded Hildale Street.
An image showed Ashbrook Wash running across a low water crossing along El Pueblo Boulevard north of Grande Boulevard, making the road impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Tonto Creek showed a 2.4 foot rise between 515 PM and 645 PM near Jakes Corner before the creek entered Roosevelt Lake.
A low water crossing on Pima Road south of Legend Trail Parkway became impassable due to a wash flowing approximately one foot in depth over the roadway. No damage or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Cave Creek exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings such as Canyon Creek Road. At 1809MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 6.89 feet and a flow of 3,670 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.
Several videos from a spotter as well as verbal confirmation of flash flooding near Highway 142.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding between mileposts 7-23. No damage or injuries were reported.

A video showed Flying E Wash flowing across a low water crossing along Vulture Mine Road, making the roadway impassable. An upstream FCDMC streamflow gage along the wash exceeded alarm stage, peaking at a depth of 1.77 feet and a flow of 269 CFS at 1858MST. No damage or injuries were reported.
Granite Creek rose 4.5 feet at the USGS gauge in Prescott.
MCDOT reported that Salome Road was closed between I-10 and milepost 22 due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
A video showed a wash flowing across a low water crossing south of Salome on Harquahala Road, making the roadway impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
MCDOT reported that Centennial Road between 517th Avenue and 555th Avenue was closed due to flooding in Centennial Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Delaney Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting a downstream low water crossing along 411th Avenue. At 2139MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 2.94 feet and a flow of 426 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Columbus Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings along Highline Road and 579th Avenue. At 0110MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 3.57 feet and a flow of 322 CFS. No damage or injuries were reported.

Two periods of heavy rain, each of 1 across much of the watershed, which was part of the Bighorn Fire burn scar, caused Sabino Creek to overtop bridges at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area. Some hiking trails, which were affected by high flows earlier in the month, sustained additional damage.

Recent heavy rain and an additional 1 to 3 inches of rain brought debris flow down from the Soldier Canyon burn scar.  The Emergency Manager reported Round Mountain Road was closed from 4 feet of mud and debris.

The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that hours of light, steady rainfall with totals of 1 to 2.5 inches caused burn scar flash flooding on the McBride burn scar near Ruidoso. All of Gavilan Canyon was flooded. Damages are estimated.
Upstream heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 2 hours caused Canada Del Oro Wash to flood part of N Lago Del Oro Parkway, resulting in its closure.
