Flooding was reported along Park Boulevard near Mount Minerva Hoyt, impacting travel on the road. No damage or injuries were reported.
ADOT reported that SR 238 was closed due to flooding. Timing and exact location estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in the vicinity of Davis-Monthan AFB caused flash flooding and the closure of nearby roads including Contractors Way.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding at Carlsbad Caverns. New Mexico State Road 7 was closed leading into Carlsbad Caverns. Carlsbad Caverns was closed and was being evacuated. Tourists were stranded at the caverns due to the road closure. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. State Highway 137 was closed at US Highway 285 due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. Dark Canyon Road at Hidalgo Rural Road was closed due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. Black River Village Road was closed at a low water crossing west of Malaga. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. A family in their vehicle was washed away at a low water crossing along Dark Canyon Road southwest of Carlsbad. They were rescued with no injuries. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. White Pine Road was closed due to flooding at the low water crossing west of Lakewood. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. The Diving Rock area southeast of Seven Rivers was closed due to flooding. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A video showed a wash flowing across a low water crossing along Silver King Road, making the road impassable. Other videos in the Queen Valley area also showed high flow in Queen Creek. Timing estimated from radar. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused major flash flooding of roads and homes in Spring Valley on Hackberry Creek. Flash flooding in Mayer caused threatened the town water supply infrastructure.
Grand Wash in Capitol Reef National Park was closed due to flash flooding.
Flash flooding occurred in Grand Wash in Capitol Reef National Park, with 1-2 feet of water flowing over the road.
A spotter reported torrential downpour with a lot of fast moving running water near their residence.  The flood waters damaged a few of their fences.
A video from social media showed significant flows on Alvey Wash, with at least several inches of water and debris flowing across Cedar Wash Road. Location is approximate.
A flash flood was observed in Sulphur Creek near Panorama Point in Capitol Reef National Park.

One inch of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding near State Route 83 in the Lyle and Brushy Canyon areas south of Canelo.  Two occupants of a pickup truck were rescued from three feet of flowing water.
A debris flow from the Trail Mountain Fire burn scar was observed on Huntington Creek near the Huntington Power Plant.
Flash flooding was reported along Pine Creek within Zion National Park.
White Rim Road in Canyonlands National Park was washed out at Upheaval Wash as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. A vehicle was hanging over the edge of the washed out road.
Several feet of water flowed through a neighborhood in Spanish Valley as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms.

Areas along Mill Creek experienced flash flooding as the creek overflowed due to heavy rain from thunderstorms. Water flowed over a park bridge, a dam had damage as an 18 inch diversion pipe cracked and filled with sand, and debris backed up on culverts which resulted in significant overland flooding.

Training thunderstorms produced upwards of 1 to 2 inches of rain within one to two hours in an around Moab. The Mill Creek Parkway - a recreational path that runs through the center of Moab, was reported to be ���completely decimated��� as a result of the flooding. Several areas had their water turned off after flood waters led to a broken water main.  Numerous homes and businesses had upwards of 12 inches of water and debris inside resulting in significant property damage.
Debris from Mill Creek flowed into the Colorado River as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms.
MCDOT reported that Patton Road between 195th Avenue and 203rd Avenue was closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain in Utah caused a two foot rise on the Paria River just before it joined the Colorado River at Lees Ferry.

Flow in Centennial Wash caused a low water crossing along Centennial Park Road to become impassable. An RV attempted to cross the flooded roadway but was swept off the road. Images also showed damage to the roadway from the flooding. No injuries were reported.
Rincon Road at Hassayampa River (normally dry) was close due to flooding.  The stream gauge on Martinez Wash at Whickenburg showed a 2 foot rise to 700 CFS rise on this normally dry wash.

A FCDMC streamflow gage along Sols Wash exceeded alarm stage, making a low water crossing along Vulture Mine Road impassable. At 0424MST, the gage peaked at a depth of 3.65 feet and a flow of 3,822 CFS. A social media video showed Sols Wash flowing across Vulture Mine Road and Wickenburg dispatch reported the road was closed as a result of the flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.
A spotter posted a photo of their property flooding with an estimated water depth of 6 inches at it's crest.
Tonto Rreek rose 2.25 feet between 730 AM and 800 AM about 10 miles south of Gisela.
Flash flooding was reported in Cannonville and Henrieville, with mud and debris on state Route 12 between the towns.
New Mexico Highway 11 was closed from mile marker 68 to 86 due to flooded low water crossings.
Agua Fria River rose 8 feet near Humboldt at 515 PM and then rose 4 feet near Cordes Junction rose 4 feet at 815 PM.
Cataract Creek/Havasu Creek rose 18 inches at the Supai Gauge.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding on Big Bug Creek.  The water rose to the level of the bridge in Spring Valley.  The water almost overtopped South Spring Lane at 635 PM. Photos on social media showed flooding in other areas of the community.
Water, mud, and rocks covered Temple Bar Road 8 miles west of Temple Bar.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Road.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Road.
Several roads in Golden Valley were closed.
Hualapai Mountain Road was closed from mile marker 4.5 to the ranger station.
Legend Ranch Road was closed.

Localized heavy rain near Taos clogged an arroyo, causing water to flood the Los Cordovas area. Blueberry Hill Road at Lower Las Colonias Road was closed due to flash flooding with water two feet in depth. Two nearby houses had about one foot of standing water inside. New Mexico Highway 240 near Cotton Road was also closed due to four feet of water over the roadway. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rain in the Cuba area caused flooding over U.S. Highway 550 which impeded traffic. No damages are known.
Heavy rain in eastern Albuquerque caused street flooding across portions of the metro area. No damages are known.
Horseman Park Drive from River Road to Little Valley Elementary was closed due to flash flooding.
A flash flood was reported on Big Chino Wash by Yavapai Country Flood Control District. A river gauge on the wash showed a 4.64 foot rise.
A breach in the berm along Rucker Creek near Bell and Thompson Roads resulted in flash flooding of roadways near the creek in eastern sections of Elfrida.

Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge along Apache Trail in Apache Junction broke Alarm Stage at around 1630 MST, with flow peaking at 1.15 feet (38 cfs). This likely caused the intersection of 4th Avenue and Royal Palm Avenue to become impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
The river gauge on Granite Creek in Prescott measured about a 3 foot rise in about 90 minutes (from 7.40 at 300 PM to 10.35 feet at 430 PM).
Heavy rain caused flooding at Fir Street and Monte Tesoro Drive.  The water covered the road one to two feet deep.
Torrential rain caused flash flooding of the pit mine near Bagdad. Some of the pit walls failed and collapsed. Workers were evacuated from the mine.
McVay Road, just south of SR-72, was impassable to cars due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding in southern Tucson. Swift water rescues from vehicles occurred near Bilby Rd. and Nogales Highway and Valencia Rd. and Park Ave.
West Quail Trail Street and West Tyson Street closed due to flooding, with the flooding most likely coming from Tyson Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain of 2-2.5 in less than 90 minutes northeast of town caused flash flooding in St. David, mainly southwest of State Route 80, although the highway was closed due to flooding for a period of time. A total of 53 homes sustained at least some flood damage. A homeowner with a basement reported flood water hit a depth of 6 feet, destroying a new furnace and damaging electrical wiring. Floodwaters also affected septic tanks and wells.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in Elfrida and upstream of a breached berm along Rucker Creek caused flash flooding of streets in Elfrida. Yards also became flooded to the bases of houses.

Flood Control District of Maricopa County stream gage along Jackrabbit Wash exceeded alarm stage at 2236 MST, making the Vulture Mine Road low water crossing impassable and mostly likely Wickenburg Road, located 5 miles downstream. Flow peaked at 3.35 feet and 1034 CFS at 2305 MST and dropped below alarm stage at 2340 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain on I-8 near the Crestwood Road on-ramp. Multiple vehicles parked on the right hand side due to the torrential rain, hail, and poor visibility.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) Fire scar caused flash flooding over Alice Drive.  The water, mud, and many basketball sized rocks made Alice Drive impassable.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2021) caused flash flooding in Schultz Creek. The creek rose 4.84 feet at Highway 180. The water flooded apartments, homes, and streets on the west side of Highway 180.
Interstate 15 was closed due to flooding between Bailey Road and Nipton Road. The highway, onramps, and offramps were also flooded at Yates Well Road.
Water flooded roads 5 miles east of K'ai'bii'to.
Granite Creek in Prescott rose about three feet.
Highway 160 was flooded in both directions at Tecopa Road.
S22(Borrego-Salton roadway) was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Caltrans closed SR-177 in both directions between I-10 and SR-62 due to flooding in multiple locations. Power lines were also down along SR-177. SR-177 was reopened around 0800PST, August 25th. Timing of flooding impacts based on radar. No injuries were reported.

Separate social media videos showed water from Fortuna Wash flowing over S Ave 14 1/2 E and E 48th Street, causing the streets to become impassable. Most of the rain, estimated around 1 to 2 inches fell over the headwaters of Fortuna Wash, 3 to 5 miles to the southeast of Fortuna Foothills. No damages or injuries were reported.
The intersection of Rodgers Lane and Meldora Ave was flooded.
US-95 near Milepost 69 was flooded. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Interstate-10, a major throughway between Phoenix, AZ and Southern California, had a section of the two eastbound (EB) lanes fully washed out due to flash flooding. Video during the washout appear to show the drainage pipes under the road were overcome and compromised by the magnitude of floodwaters. Radar rainfall estimates in this area were around 2-3 inches, with much of the rain falling in less than 2 hours. The washout occurred a few miles east of State Route 177/Desert Center. Caltrans closed I-10 EB due to the washout. I-10 westbound (WB) was also closed briefly due to an overturned semi-truck and SR-177 had already been closed, due to its own separate flooding impacts and downed power lines, by the time of the I-10 washout. This caused major traffic delays and detours through Eastern Riverside County. One EB detour lane was opened around 0700PST on August 25th after emergency construction and the second EB detour lane was not opened until 2300PST August 27th. Timing of flooding impacts based on radar. No injuries were reported from this event.
Hackberry Road was closed.

Clatrans closed SR-78 in both directions near the I-10 interchange due to flooding. SR-78 was reopened around 0800PST, August 25th. Timing of flooding impacts estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain of more than 1 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and closures of residential streets south of Orange Grove Road between La Cholla and La Canada. Additionally, a man was rescued after becoming trapped under a bridge by floodwaters near Blacklidge and Walnut.
A vehicle was stuck on Highway 62 in flash flooding, eventually leading to the closure of the highway.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in Saguaro National Park and damage to Bajada Loop Rd.
Highway 95 was flooded.
Report from La Paz County Emergency Management of water rushing into houses. Washes in the area were running full. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on SR-72, west of McVay Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway 95 was flooded, and at least one vehicle was stuck in the water.
Ten to 15 vehicles were stuck between two flooded areas on Highway 95 just north of Vidal Junction.
Flooding was reported about two miles west of Jeddito at the intersection of State Route 264 and BIA-9101.
Highway 190 was flooded in several areas west of Death Valley Junction. The water was about a foot deep and carried a significant amount of debris.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 160.
Highway 127 was flooded.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 on Tucson's southeast side caused localized flash flooding. Escalante Rd. was closed at the Atterbury Wash and a man was rescued from his vehicle in the Alamo Wash at Yale Dr.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 southeast of Valencia and Mission Rds. caused the West Branch of the Santa Cruz River to flood Drexel Road, causing its closure.
Highway 190 was flooded between Furnace Creek and Cow Creek.

Portions of the 9-mile scenic loop drive in Natural Bridges National Monument received flash flooding as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. The road was closed until debris was cleared the next day.
The Little Colorado River had a 3 foot rise above Lyman Lake.
Highway 95 was flooded.
Flash flooding was reported in Isaac Canyon near Court of the Patriarchs.

The stream gauge on the Big Bug Creek in Mayer showed a rise from 1.9 to 4.9 feet in about 40 minutes starting at noon.  The flood water over topped the Spring Lane bridge over Big Bug Creek in Spring Valley at 130 PM. A video on social media showed water flowing over a low water crossing on Thunderbird Trail in Cordes Junction at 155 PM.  A river gauge on the Agua Fria River just downstream from the confluence with the Big Bug Creek showed a rise from 3.7 feet to 7.9 feet between 200 PM to 300 PM.

A river gauge on Black Canyon Creek showed a rise from 1.8 feet to 3.4 feet between 205 PM and 321 PM. A video on social media at 342 PM showed water rapidly flowing over Maren Avenue at a low water crossing on Black Canyon Creek.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge of Jackrabbit Wash at Vulture Mine Road reported water levels rising rapidly above alarm stage at around 1713 MST, with a peak flow of 4.88 feet (3651 cfs) at 1803 MST, and going back down below alarm stage at around 1926 MST. This amount of water flow likely flooded Aguila Road upstream of the gauge and Wickenburg Road, where a water rescue was performed, located 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No injuries were reported. Based on the report from the Phoenix Dispatch, water got halfway up on an unoccupied vehicle stuck along the flood waters from Jackrabbit Wash located along Wickenburg Road.
Video of flash flooding on Peralta Road, east of Gold Canyon, which stranded motorists. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Carlsbad. There were several road closures throughout Carlsbad due to high water. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Carlsbad. There was water a couple feet deep along West Lea Street and South 6th Street in Carlsbad. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Eddy County. Several roads were closed along Black River near Malaga. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A webcam showed the Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Rd.

Wickenburg Police Department reported Vulture Mine Road at Sols Wash was closed due to flooding. The road was reported closed at 2005MST, but flooding impacts likely began around 1950MST based on radar and an upstream streamflow gage. The streamflow gage is roughly 2 miles upstream and measured 1.69 inches in 1 hour ending at 1900MST. Streamflow exceeded alarm stage at 1930MST. The gage peaked at 4.10 feet and 4815 cfs at 2010MST. Flow fell back below alarm stage at 2100MST.  No damages or injuries were reported.
Oatman Highway was closed from mile marker 40 to East Silver Creek Rd.
Flooding with water 3-4 feet deep was reported along US-95 about 14 miles south of Quartzsite. No damages or injuries were reported.
Rocks were washed onto Hwy 190 at Towne Pass.
Water, mud, debris, and rocks closed Hwy 190 between mile markers 110 and 115 with about 20 vehicles unable to get through. The entry road to The Inn was washed out.
Several roads in and near Golden Valley were closed.

Several incidents occurred between the Mountain Springs and Ocotillo area due to flash flooding. Large rocks were reported falling onto I-8. Significant water flow was reported along Meyer Creek wash, resulting in several roads which intersect the wash to become impassable. Highway 98 was closed between Imperial Highway and Drew Road due to the flooding. A mesonet station in Mountain Spring reported 2.67 inches with 1.02 inches falling in one hour. No injuries were reported.
Three to four pickup trucks were stuck in the wash on Dunaway Road near I-8, causing the closure of the road. A vehicle was washed off Evan Hawes Highway. No injuries were reported.
Water flowing across Old Highway 80 into Mexico, completely covering the roadway and making it impassable based on video. About 2 inches of widespread rain fell in the area.
Highway 78 east of Ocotillo Wells was closed due to flooding and debris on the road. No injuries were reported.
North Imperial Avenue between Adams Avenue and East Main Street in El Centro was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
About 6 inches approximately of flowing water was observed across Dolphin Drive in Salton City. No damages or injuries were reported.

Several roads that intersect Waterman Wash in the Rainbow Valley/Buckeye area were impassable/closed due to flooding. This included Riggs Road, Tuthill Road between between Pecos Road and Fairview Street, and Narramore Road between Dean Road and Airport Road. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge of Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road reported a peak flow of 6.12 feet (1151 cfs), which was 2.82 feet above alarm stage. No damages or injuries were reported.

SR-238 was closed in its entirety between Gila Bend and SR-347 due to significant flooding. The Maricopa Fire and Medical Crew as well as the Goodyear Fire Department in a collective effort had to rescue approximately 32 people in stranded vehicles. No injuries were reported.
Heavy rain over the Tunnel and Pipeline fire scar caused flash flooding across Highway 89. The highway closed in both directions at mile marker 430 from 108 PM until 440 PM.
Hwy 395 was partially flooded.
Flooding, debris, and road damage closed Hwy 190.
Hwy 317 was closed, and water flowed through stores in southeast Caliente off Elle Mtn.
Hwy 168 was flooded at The Narrows.

A nearly stationary thunderstorm over El Porvenir produced over two inches of rainfall on this area of the Calf Canyon burn scar. This caused flash flooding on Beaver Creek and Gallinas Creek with significant debris found on Highway 65. The IMET on duty found several locations along Highway 65 that were covered in tree debris, rocks, and mud. Some buildings along the roadway were inundated with a couple of feet of water. The IMET also noted that water had threatened homes in the area as well, but these homes seemed to have been protected with sandbagging. Damages are estimated.
Badwater Rd was closed due to flooding, debris, and road damage.
Hwy 136 was closed due to mud with a motorcycle stuck.
Hwy 190 was flooded and damaged at and just west of Towne Pass.
Pine Creek Rd was covered with water, boulders, and debris, stranding campers.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Rd.

The river gauge at the Village of Supai showed a 1.83 foot rise at 1045 AM. The stream gauge at the confluence with the Colorado River (about 10 miles down stream from the Village of Supai) had a 5.5 foot rise in about 45 minutes at 1145 AM. The crest was at 12.57 feet with a flow of 1735 CFS. Base flow is at about 7 feet with a flow of 70 CFS.
A river gauge on the Paria River near the Colorado River showed a 1.83 foot rise at 545 PM MST.
Flash flooding was reported about 10 miles north of Joseph City at the intersection of Blairs Spring Wash and North Porter Road. The dirt road was washed out by the flooding and a vehicle got stuck.
Flash flooding occurred due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm. Law enforcement reported Peavine Canyon road was washed out and impassable.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding with mud/debris flows across Lake Hughes Road, about 2 miles south of the Elizabeth Lake Road intersection. Several vehicles were stuck in mud and debris.
Portions of Wildcat Canyon Rd on the Barona Reservation under 3-10 inches of running water due to heavy rainfall. Visibility reduced to 1/4 mile during rain.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along State Route 33, about one mile north of the Lockwood Valley Road intersections. Several vehicles were stuck in mud and debris.

Heavy rain from residual moisture associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay occurred across northern portions of the Inland Empire, leading to multiple instances of flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported by a trained spotter on University Parkway and Kendall Drive near Devore, with one foot of water covering the roadway. Farther south toward Rialto, flooding occurred across all lanes on I-215 northbound. Flooding was also reported near San Bernardino across all lanes from University Parkway to Mount Vernon Ave.

Highway 18 between Waterman Canyon and Highway 138, heavy rain led to debris flows including boulders up to 1 foot in diameter across all lanes. Water several inches deep was also flowing across lanes.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Highway 166, west of New Cuyama. The flooding was the result of heavy rain from strong thunderstorms.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Mount Baldy Road, about 6 miles north-northeast of Claremont.
California Highway Patrol reported a significant mudslide across Highway 14 at the intersection of Avenue O.

California Highway Patrol reported significant flash flooding and mud/debris flows across Pine Canyon Road, west-northwest of Lake Hughes. Officers reported 24 vehicles stuck in mud and debris. Over 50 people had to be air lifted out of the area due to no emergency vehicle access.
Heavy rain of 3-4 in three hours caused flash flooding and road closures in Green Valley, including Camino Del Sol and Abrego Drive.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding and mud/debris flows about 3 miles south-southwest of Neenach. Several vehicles, including a fire truck, were stuck in mud. Several miles of Old Ridge Route Road were closed.
California Highway Patrol reported severe flooding along the Northbound Interstate 5 from Pyramid Lake to Smoky Bear Lane.

The City of Queen Creek posted on social media at 2140MST saying Rittenhouse Road near Ocotillo Road was closed due to flooding. Timing of impacts based around radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Signal Butte Road between East Germann Road and East Barnes Parkway as well as Germann Road at South Crismon Road were closed due flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along East Fork Cave Creek Wash near North 7th Avenue in Phoenix indicated water levels rising above alarm stage at 2232 MST, with the flow peaking 3.77 feet (1557 cfs) at 2259 MST, and not going below alarm stage until 2359 MST. This likely made North 7th Avenue impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
The Agua Fria River rose 4 feet near Cordes Junction. This is normally dry.
Zzyzx Rd was damaged, and Mojave Rd was impassable from Rasor Rd to Kelbaker Rd.

Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported that Eagle Eye Road was closed between Aguila Road and Mile Post 0 due to flooding. Timing and location of impacts was adjusted based on radar. There were no reports of damage.

Photos from the La Paz County Public Works showed parts of Alamo Road washed out due to extensive flooding from overflowing washes that intersect the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
SR-72 at Milepost 25 near Bouse was impassable due to wash flowing over the roadway. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported along Highway 96 near Bagdad.
Several roads were closed, and a swift water rescue was performed on Oatman Highway.
Burro Creek Crossing Rd was closed.
Seventeen Mile Road was closed.
Signal Rd was closed.

Localized heavy rainfall on Gavilan Ridge flowed downhill onto the McBride burn scar which caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road from Janet Drive northward to Airplane Canyon. Burn scar flash flooding resulted in rock and mud debris along the roadway. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in southern portions of the Inland Empire. The Department of Highways reported a swift water rescue of a person seeking refuge on top of a vehicle. Local emergency managers also reported the southbound lane of I-15 was flooded at Dos Lagos.||The following are measured rain reports in the region:||Mesonet Station CW7445 Temescal Valley, 10 SE Corona: 1.78 inch.||Mesonet Station ECSC1 El Cariso RAWS, 5 WSW Lake Elsinore: 1.28 inch.

Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in the San Bernardino County Mountains. Rain amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches occurred in the region. The Department of Highways reported a flash flood near Crestline, with multiple vehicles stuck in flood water on Lake Drive at Forest Shade Drive. The following are measured rain amounts from various Mesonet sites:||Mesonet Station FW1313, 1 WNW Running Springs: 3.58 inch.|Strawberry Peak, 3 WSW Lake Arrowhead: 2.88 inch.|Heaps Peak RAWS, 3 NW Running Springs: 2.68 inch.|Mesonet Station CRQC1, 1 SSW Lake Arrowhead: 1.74 inch.|Mesonet Station PPOC1 Panorama Point, 2 SSW Crestline: 1.66 inch.|Mesonet Station FW0025 Lake Arrowhead South, 1 SE Lake Arrowhead: 1.52 inch.
Oatman Hwy was closed.
Eight water rescues occurred, five to ten homes had water in them, and an observer measured 3.86 inches of rain in just under two hours.
Six to eight inches of water plus mud and debris covered the northbound lanes of Hwy 160.
CHP report of flooding on Highway 247, 3 vehicles possible submerged.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in southwest Tucson. Roads closed include Old Ajo Highway, Long Cast DR. and Iberia Ave.
A large amount of water and mud covered Main St at Hinkley Rd.
CHP report of a driver stuck in flash flooding with water coming into the vehicle.

A large flash flood and debris flow occurred on Prospect street off of Valley of the Falls in Forest Falls, CA. The debris flow originated on the 2020 El Dorado burn scar after 1.1 inches of rain in an hour on Yucaipa Ridge. More than 1 debris flow occurred but the largest crossed Prospect street moving and damaging vehicles as well as damage homes. At least 2 homes had major damage. One fatality occurred when an older female was buried in debris, 3 days later found by search and rescue dogs. Residents took photos of debris flows and flash flooding including video and Ring security cameras. WCM visited the damage and SAR activity on September 13 and spoke with residents who shared additional photos and descriptions. A 20 foot boulder was lodged just above their home and their Jeep was washed down the hill (caught on Ring camera).

A major flash flood debris flow occurred in Birch Creek through Potato Canyon. This area was affected by lesser debris flows October and December 2021 and August 2022 but this flood filled the entire channel in layers, overtopped and damage the Steakhouse restaurant in Oak Glen, took out power poles, pushed large boulder and layers of mud downstream onto Oak Glen Road and pushed up to windows on a couple homes. WCM Alex Tardy did a storm survey. Estimated 100,000 cubic yards of debris removed by San Bernardino Public Works. Video of the debris flow between 3 and 4 pm was recorded.

Morongo Indian reservation had extensive mud, rock and logs in a major debris flow off the 2020 Apple burn scar which traveled down the San Gorgonio River. This inundated the Banning Water Plant and pushed mud, rocks and logs onto roads.

A storm survey by WCM found several debris flows on Valley of the Falls road in Forest Falls. The largest produced mud and rocks as high as 10 feet, completely covering the Valley of the Falls road. Other flash floods and debris occurred further into the canyon (deeper) affecting the roads and residences property. Homeowners discussed and described the flooding and impact. Most severe since August 2014.
Numerous roads in and near Golden Valley were closed.
Fort Irwin Rd was flooded.
Heavy rainfalls lead to water over the road near US-395 and Spring Valley drive.
Heavy rainfall caused water to flood State Route-359 on the Nevada side.
Three feet of water over the road on Route 66 at Frontier Road. Side of the road is eroding.
The Seligman Fire Department reported 4 to 6 inches of water flowing over the streets in the center of town.
Banegas Crossing was closed.
Huffriter Rd was closed.
Pump Station Rd was closed.
Bogles Ranch Rd was closed.

Moderate to heavy rain fell across Zion National Park and surrounding areas, with 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of around 0.50 inches. As a result, the North Fork Virgin at Springdale river gauge recorded a rapid rise in stage from around 50 CFS to over 1200 CFS in under 2 hours. Additionally, park rangers at Zion National Park reported flooding in many slot canyons in the park, as well as several observed waterfalls.
One lane of Hwy 93 was flooded just south of Hwy 168.
Both sides of Hwy 395 were flooded near Olancha Ln. Later reports noted large boulders in the road, and stated that the road was flexing from the water.
Hwy 190 was closed.
Hwy 395 was flooded at Lone Willow Dip (in addition to the Olancha Ln flooding also documented in this episode), stranding 50 to 100 cars between the two flooded areas.
Hwy 190 was washed away by a 10 to 15 foot high wall of fast-moving water near Centennial Flats. One truck was swept away; the occupant was unharmed.
Hwy 136 was closed.
Hwy 93 was flooded at Lincoln Co mile markers 105 and 109.
Knee high mud was over Hwy 190, and a school bus was stuck in the mud.
There were multiple reports of flooding in Alamo.
Hwy 6 was flooded with water and mud.

Significant road flooding occurred in Moapa, Moapa Valley, Overton, and Valley of Fire State Park. The Overton co-op observer measured 1.89 inches of rain, including 0.80 inch in 20 minutes. Multiple vehicles were stuck in Valley of Fire.
Hwy 160 was flooded.
The intersection of Farm Rd and Grand Canyon Dr was flooded.

Moderate to heavy rainfall from earlier in the day resulted in a flood wave traversing downstream along the Virgin River. The Virgin at Virgin river gauge recorded a flow increase from 333 CFS at 12:15 am MST to a peak of 2020 CFS at 2:00 am MST.
Havasu Creek rose two feet in 15 minuets just above the Village of Supai.
Debris occurred over State Highway 376 from mile markers 68 to 72 along with water running over the roadway. NDOT closed the highway. Depth of debris appears to be several inches from photo.

Bureau of Land Management officials reported a flash flood wave moving down Phipps Wash toward the Escalante River. This is most likely associated with a brief thunderstorm which moved through the area between roughly 11:30 am MST to 12:30 pm MST and produced moderate to heavy rainfall. Event time is based upon report.

Park rangers relayed a report of flash flooding in Capitol Gorge, with floodwaters as much as 4 feet deep. This is associated with showers and thunderstorms which moved through the area between around 12:30 pm MST to 2:00 pm MST and produced around 0.50 inches of rainfall.
The Lincoln County emergency manager reported Gavilan Canyon Road near Janet Drive experienced flash flooding as heavy rain fell on the McBride burn scar. Damages are not known.
Salome Hwy between 331st Ave to 355th Ave was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Tonopah Salome Highway in Tonopah was closed between 315th Ave and 327th Dr due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Baseline Rd in the Palo Verde region was closed between Johnson Rd and 331st Ave due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Video from broadcast of media showed water and debris flowing over roadway off of Grand Ave & Jomax near Wittman. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Centennial Wash near the Railroad area reached action stage at 954 MST, with a peak flow of 10.12 feet (1341 cfs) at 1112 MST. Flash Flood impacts downstream where Centennial Wash crosses old U.S. 80 occurred 1.5 hours after action stage was reached, which is 6 miles downstream of the gauge. The flow returned below alarm stage at 1507 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

Moderate rain moved over portions of Wire Pass and Buckskin Gulch slot canyons, as well as nearby drainages, with 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates up to 0.75 inches. Flash Flooding was reported by the Paria Contact Station at 12:00 pm MST, with reports of several hikers in the area needing to form human chains in three separate locations to escape flood waters. No injuries were noted at the time of report.

A strong thunderstorm moved through portions of the Paria River drainage basin, with widespread 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches. This generated a flood wave that propagated downstream, with the Paria near Kanab river gauge rising from 100 CFS around 1:00 pm MST to 1180 CFS at 1:25 pm MST.
SR-238 closed between Milepost 4 and 24 due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.

Strong thunderstorms moved over the Oquirrh Mountains over the course of an hour or two, resulting in moderate to at times heavy rain over the Jacob City Fire burn scar. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour rainfall estimates were in the 0.50 to 0.75 inch range. This was enough to result in a flow along Soldier Creek, which resulted in the evacuation of one house by State Route 36 and a road closure.

Multiple thunderstorms with moderate to heavy rainfall moved over Bryce Canyon National Park during the late evening hours. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 3-hour rainfall estimates showed widespread amounts of 1 to 2 inches, and the Bryce Canyon Airport ASOS recorded nearly 1.5 inches of rain over the span of 3:30 pm MST to 4:30 pm MST. Many trails sustained damage, with some leading to extended trail closures. The Queen's Garden trail suffered a few debris flows with unstable footing and two retaining wall failures. The Peekaboo Loop suffered numerous debris flows and points of trail surface erosion. The Bryce Point Peekaboo Connecting Trail suffered numerous rockfalls and debris flows, two retaining wall failures, and deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Fairyland Loop trail suffered deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Navajo Loop trail had a tree downed on the Two Bridges side. The Wall Street side of the Navajo Loop Trail suffered further debris flows and complete trail erosion in some sections, resulting in an extended trail closure.

Video showed Arizona Department of Public Safety performed a swift water rescue by air around 2100MST. A family of 6 (2 parents and 4 kids) in an SUV were washed off of Val Vista Road near Warren Road at a low water crossing with Vekol Wash. Floodwaters were over the hood of the SUV after being pushed downstream. All 6 individuals were safely rescued from the roof of their vehicle and were unharmed. A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge on Vekol Wash near I-8, located approximately 14 miles southwest, showed the flow going above alarm stage at 1340 MST, peaking at 7.80 feet (2465 cfs) at 1540 MST, and returning below alarm stage at 1754 MST. A news article mentioned this was the second swift water rescue performed in a matter of a few hours. Details on the other rescue were not found.

Ralston Road at the Vekol Wash low water crossing in Ak-Chin Village was flooded and was impassable for several hours. Peak floodwater height was measured at nearly 7 feet at around 1951 MST by the Pinal County Flood Control gauge at the crossing. Timing estimated based off when the water level first reached 1 feet deep. No damages or injuries were reported.

Heavy rain from nearby thunderstorms resulted in 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor estimates of around 1 to 2 inches total. Garfield County Dispatch reported flooding in Tropic, Cannonville, and Henrieville. One basement was flooded. Time estimated by radar.
Heavy rain over far south-central Utah and far north-central Arizona resulted in a flash flood through Paria Canyon. The river gauge near the Colorado River showed almost a 4 foot rise.

Nearby thunderstorms with moderate rainfall resulted in 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor accumulation estimates of around 0.25 to 0.75 inches. The Pine Creek near Escalante stream gauge spiked to a peak flow of 228 CFS at 7:15 pm MST.

A thunderstorm moved through portions of the Escalante River drainage basin, producing moderate rainfall, with widespread 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of 0.50 to 1.00 inches in upstream tributary areas. This generated a flood wave that propagated downstream, resulting in the Escalante near Escalante river gauge spiking to  804 CFS at 9:50 pm MST.
Yarber Wash flooded Horsebreaker Road and other low water crossing about 5 miles east of  Dewey-Humboldt. A nearby rain gauge measured 3.50 inches of rain.
An unnamed road flooded approximately one-half mile east of Torreon Wash and one-mile west of Tinnian Road.
Tyson Street, West Quail Trail Street and East Kuhen Street were all closed due to overflowing water from Tyson Wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
US-60 near MP 58 in Salome was flooded due to the overflow from Centennial Wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Eagle Eye Road was closed between US-60 and Salome Highway due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
US-95 was impassable at around mile marker 69 due to overflowing water from the washes intersecting the highway. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water, rocks, and debris were reported across Hwy 95 north of Blythe. No injuries were reported.
A low-water crossing along Highway 72 just northwest of Bouse was impassible due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Park Blvd was closed just outside the west entrance to Joshua Tree National Park.
Three drivers were rescued after their cars stalled in water, and Nellis Blvd was closed due to the flooding.
A park employee with Joshua Tree National Park share video and report of roads washed out in the Indian Cove section of the park. No damages or injuries were reported. Timing based on radar.
Multiple roads were flooded, and one van was stuck in flowing water.

Law enforcement reported roadway flooding on I-10 along the Riverside/San Bernardino County line. County and Bryant Road intersection closed due to flooding, with several inches of water over the roadway. Social media reports of flood damage to inside of garages and backside of two homes in the area. CWOP site in Yucaipa reported 0.84 inch of rain in 25 minutes.
Heavy rain of an inch in one hour caused flash flooding near Agua Caliente Park and the closure of Soldier Trail Rd. near Roger Rd.
Officials from Capitol Reef National Park reported 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through a wash that feeds into the Grand Wash, as well as 1 to 2 feet of water flowing through Grand Wash itself.
Hwy 62 was flooded and partly washed away.

Zion National Park officials reported that normally dry washes near Canyon Junction were seeing flash flooding, that there were waterfalls on both sides of Zion Canyon, and that the campground had minor flooding. A thunderstorm which moved through produced an estimated 0.25 to 0.75 inches of rainfall per Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour analysis.

Along CA 177 near the border of Joshua Tree National Park, just north of Desert Center, two washes were completely flooded. The California Highway Patrol requested for Road Flooded signs to keep cars from driving into the flooded roadway. No damages or injuries were reported.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flows from Sheets Gulch into Sandy Creek.
Capitol Reef National Park officials relayed a public report of flows across Burr Trail Switchbacks, resulting in the road becoming impassable.

The river gauge on Havasu creek near the Colorado River rose 6.7 feet in 15 minutes between 1130 and 1145 PM MST. The river gauge is below/downstream from the Village of Supai. The flood damaged all six bridges in and around Supai Village, some of which were a total loss. The main foot and mule trail to the village was damaged and in need of repair. This 8 mile trail is the only way to the village from a road other than by helicopter.

More than 50 people were stranded overnight in Grand County, Utah after heavy rain from severe thunderstorms wiped out a portion of Mineral Bottom Road which led to a remote boat ramp. The rain completed demolished a section of switchbacks with large boulders accumulating.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek.
The Fort Pearce Wash gauge peaked at 789 cfs.

Numerous roads were closed in Spanish Valley due to flash flooding as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. This included Shumway Lane and Old City Park, Floy, Hastings, Sunny Acres, and Kerby Roads. Roads remained closed overnight. The Pack Creek gauge on Pack Creek Road reported a rise of 4 feet when about an inch of rain fell in 90 minutes.
The Escalante at Escalante river gauge peaked at 518 cfs with a flood wave around 7 p.m.
A webcam showed the Vock Wash flooded Stockton Hill Rd.
Four feet of water was flowing over Back O' Beyond Road in Sedona near Cathedral Rock.
The Clarkdale Police Department reported that the Old Jerome Highway/89A was closed due to flooding and debris.  Reta Street was also closed due to the flooding.
Bogels Ranch Rd was closed from Upper Trout Creek Rd to Back Rd.
Pump Station Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.
Huffriter Rd was closed from Hwy 93 to Back Rd.

Social media video showed good flow along a wash that runs through the Gold Canyon Golf Resort, making several of the cart paths that runs through the wash impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
State Route 238 was closed between mile posts 7 and 24, northeast of Gila, due to flash flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Video showed evidence of considerable flash flooding over Highway 95 at Castle Dome Mine Road, impeding and slowing traffic. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flash flooding along Ogilby Road near Indian Pass Road resulted in mud and gravel mult spots along the road. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
A vehicle stalled in floodwaters along Aberdeen Road near Highway 95 and was assisted by the Yuma Fire Department. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Chino Dr was closed from Morenci Rd to Aztec Rd.
Shinarump Dr was closed from Aztec Rd to Colorado Rd.

Department of Highways reported flooding at SR-74 E and Cranston Ranger Station at mile marker 49. Water covering the road, originating from the Fairview Fire burn scar. Mesonet station CNSC1 Cranston reported 1.03 inch of heavy rain within two hours.
Yucca Creek flooded Indio Ave.
Heavy flooding reported on the on and off ramp of South 4th street and I-8 in El Centro. No damages or injuries were reported.

Significant flooding was reported in the El Centro Regional Medical Center. There was 18 inches of flowing water in the parking lot, with the water entering the facility and affecting the emergency room as well as the radiology department. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported in the area of SR-387 and SR-187 in Sacaton. No damages or injuries were reported.
Social media video taken from Queen Creek showed a significant water current several inches deep flowing in the area just south of the San Tan Mountains. No damages or injuries were reported.
Plows from the California Highway Patrol removed flood debris from SR-111 near Milepost 65. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on I-17 near Bell Road in Phoenix. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding reported on US-95 near Milepost 104 in Quartzsite. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water flowed down Utah Trail.
Emergency management reported moderate flow of water down Utah Trail located in the northwestern portion of Joshua Tree National Park. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video from a storm chaser showed flash flooding washing away Mohave Road. The location of the flooding was about 6-7 miles north of I-10, just northeast of Blythe, CA. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
Water running along the eastbound lanes of I-10 resulted in closure of the highway near Ford Dry Lake Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Large rocks and boulders washed onto Amboy Rd.
All washes along SR-177 just north of Desert Center were flooded with Big Wash estimated to have received the most rainfall. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Car Stranded along Senator Wash Road about 5 miles south-southwest of Martinez Lake due to flooding. No injuries were reported.
Coyote Canyon in Anza-Borrego State Park was closed off due to flooding.
Social media report showed slow traffic on SR-238, between mile markers 23 to 40 due to flooding on roadway. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge located along Tiger Wash reported water levels along the wash going above alarm stage (5.9 feet) at 16:48 MST, with water levels peaking at 6.06 feet (587 cfs) at 16:57 MST. Flow went below alarm stage at 17:17 MST. Flooding from the wash would have occurred 3.5 miles downstream along Eagle Eye Road 65 minutes later, at around 18:00 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Winters Wash in Tonopah showed flow going above alarm stage (1.28 feet) between 18:06 and 18:08 MST, with the flow going above the bankfull stage (3.32 feet) at 18:38 MST and peaking at 4.27 feet (1400 cfs) at 19:18 MST. The flow went below bankfull at 22:49 MST and below alarm stage at 01:43 MST on the 16th. Roads intersecting the wash that were affected from the flow along Winters Wash included Indian School Road, located 1.1 miles downstream of the gauge, and along Salome Highway south of I-10 located 4.6 miles downstream of the gauge. Along Indian School Road, there were reports at around 19:37 MST from a trained spotter of many cars stranded and it is unknown whether or not any of the vehicles sustained damage. No injuries were reported.

Pictures were sent in from a trained spotter of water entering the Adelante Healthcare facility and some of the downtown stores in Buckeye. Water was estimated to be 6 to 8 inches deep. No injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Rainbow Wash reported flow rising to above alarm stage (1.4 feet) between 17:21 and 17:25 MST, exceeding the bankfull stage (4.1 feet) between 18:17 and 18:27 MST and peaking at 4.42 feet (2368 cfs) at around 18:55 MST. Any flooding impacts from the wash included Old US-80 and Patterson Road, located about 5.6 miles downstream. The wash went below bankfull stage at around 19:31 MST, before another rise above the bankfull stage occurred at around 23:02 MST. The flow did not go below action stage until around 00:47 MST on the 16th.
About two feet of water and debris flowed over Amboy Rd at Midway Rd. At least one vehicle was stuck.
Social media videos showed water entering homes from backyards being flooded in the area of roadway MC 85 and East Baseline Road. No injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Waterman Wash at Rainbow Valley Road showed flow going above alarm stage (3.3 feet) between 19:28 and 20:07 MST and continuing to rise for several hours more to reach a peak flow of 7.25 feet (1700 cfs) at 23:38 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along Tuthill Road, located 3.2 miles downstream and Narramore Road, located 6.4 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage at 07:03 MST on the 16th. A truck was swept off Narramore Road due to the strong current from the wash. There was no information received about the occupants that were inside the truck.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Cruff Wash showed flow going above alarm stage (2.5 feet) between 20:29 and 20:31 MST, reaching a peak flow of 3.25 feet (448 cfs) at 21:13 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred at Agua Caliente Road, located about 2 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage between 21:42 and 21:48 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Delaney Wash showed flow going above alarm stage (1.87 feet) between 22:51 and 22:53 MST, with a peak flow of 2.3 feet (255 cfs) at 23:07 MST. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along 411th Avenue, located 2.1 miles downstream and Salome Highway, located 3.7 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage between 5:05 and 5:51 MST on the 16th. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along Centennial Wash at the Union Pacific Railroad showed flow going above alarm stage (8.5 feet) between 21:53 and 21:56 MST and continuing to rise for several hours more to reach a peak flow of 13 feet (4315 cfs) at 02:06 MST on the 16th. Flooding along the wash likely occurred along the Old US Highway 80, located 6 miles downstream. Flow fell below alarm stage at 13:34 MST on the 16th. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Streamflow Gauge along East Fork Cave Creek near 7th Avenue showed the flow going above alarm stage (2 feet) at around 2:36 MST, peaking at 3.33 feet (1239 cfs) at 3:05 MST, and dropped below alarm stage between 4:01 and 4:36 MST. Flooding likely occurred at the low water crossing along 7th Avenue. No damages or injuries were reported.

A video showed flooding occurring from Bloody Tanks. Water was reaching the bottom of a bridge as well as going around it, briefly trapping the person recording the incident. The location of the incident was in the area of Schulze Ranch Road and U.S. 60. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video was taken at the intersection of Superstition Drive and Remington Road showing flash flooding occurring. Small hail was also falling in the area.

Ontario Fire department reported 6 person in the swiftwater channel in John Galvin park where the channel begins near I-10. Rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches per hour had occurred from 7 am to 9 am in Ontario and Rancho Cucamonga. 3 persons were rescued. 3 more person were later found drowned in a retaining pond which was filled 15 to 20 feet high with storm runoff water. The bodies were not found until several days later due the water being too deep and low visibility. Multiple agencies were involved in the week long recovery efforts. The channel runs south past Ontario airport to where it reached the storage collection ponds on East Philadelphia Street. Search and rescue in Cucamonga Channel reported by CalOES and Ontario Fire Department. As many as 10 people experiencing homelessness were swept away as a surge of water occurred following 2 hours of heavy rain. Five people were immediately rescued, one person immediately reported deceased, with two additional bodies recovered (one of November 14, the other on November 16).

Heavy rain fell in and around the Apple/ El Dorado burn scar on November 8, resulting in debris flow and flash flooding. Roadway flooding was reported on Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road, with the roadway washing out at 12099 Oak Glen Road.
Department of Highways reported washouts on Ice House Canyon Road and Mt Baldy Road, with vehicles stuck. Total rainfall of 3.7 inches at Mt Baldy.
Chollita Rd was flooded.
Sunnyslope Dr was flooded.

Swiftwater rescue along North Indain Canyon Drive in Whitewater Wash in Palm Springs around 12:30 PM. Multiple vehicles were trapped with three drivers and a dog rescued successfully. Multiple roads, including Gene Autry Trail, Indian Canyon Drive, Vista Chino Road and North Indian Canyon Drive remained closed through 6 AM the following day.
Oatman Hwy was closed from mile marker 36 to mile marker 40.
DW Ranch Rd was closed.

Swiftwater rescue of woman in Cucamonga Wash at Airport Drive. The Ontario Fire Department reported the woman received minor injuries. Rainfall rates of 0.5 to 0.7 inch from Fullerton to Rancho Cucamonga between 7-8 am. The main IVT frontal band moved through Southern California 7-10 AM.

Swiftwater rescue in the Santa Ana River at Garden Grove Blvd. The area received 0.5 to 1 inch of rain at the time of rescue. An adult male was successfully rescued but taken to the hospital. The main IVT frontal band moved through Southern California 7-10 AM.

Palm Springs Police Department closed North Indian Canyon Drive through the Whitewater wash due to water over the road, with the closure reported at 4:26 PM and December 11, remaining closed through 1 PM on December 12. The Riverside County Mountains reported 1-2 inches of rain prior to the closure, and Palm Springs reported 0.23 inch.

Orange County Fire Authority reported 2 vehicles stuck in water on the 4th Street off-ramp on SR-55 Northbound. Occupants were stuck inside and on top of their vehicles and required rescuing.  Rainfall totals generally between 1.10 and 1.75 inch occurred in this area on New Year's Eve.

Sacramento County OES confirmed the levee along the Cosumnes River breached in at least two locations overnight, causing flash flooding in the surrounding areas. Highway 99 between Dillard Rd and Grantline Rd was flooded with numerous vehicles stuck in flood waters, requiring water rescues. Highway 99 was closed around midnight due to flooding. Flooding continued into January 2023.

The Cosumnes River rose rapidly due to very heavy rains and already elevated levels from previous storms. Sacramento County OES confirmed the levee along the Cosumnes River breached in three locations overnight, causing flash flooding in the surrounding areas from Rancho Murieta to Wilton. SR 99 between Dillard Rd and Grantline Rd was flooded with numerous vehicles stuck in flood waters, requiring water rescues and was closed around midnight due to flooding. Flooding continued well into January. Sacramento County issued an evacuation warning overnight for the Wilton area, changed to a shelter-in-place warning a couple of hours later due to unsafe travel conditions with surrounding flooded areas. There were an estimated 3,200 to 3,500 people in the impacted area. There were three drownings attributed to the flooding, each entered as an individual event.

Flash flooding on College Avenue near SR76 reported by CalTrans. Full highway closure with disabled vehicles due to water up to 2.5 feet deep. Rainfall rates of 0.84 inch per hour occurred in the area, per observations from KCRQ ASOS.

The California Highway Patrol on January 4 reported a fatality associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood due to levee breaks. A female body was found outside a vehicle near Dillard Road east of CA-99. This is one of three confirmed fatalities from this event.

Sacramento County Sheriff confirmed a drowning on January 4 associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood event. A female body was found inside a vehicle. This was the third drowning associated with the event. This flooding was due to levee breaks on the Cosumnes River.
Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to heavy rain, park rangers at Zion National Park reported several canyons around the park were flooding.

There was a male fatality due to drowning in a submerged car, confirmed by Cosumnes Fire Department near SR 99 and Dillard Rd. A levee breech on the Cosumnes River caused the flash flood. This was one of three drowning deaths reported from the flash flood event. The Cosumnes Fire Department said they rescued dozens of people in the area over the past 24 hours. A helicopter from Metro Fire also rescued several people in the area. SR 99 remained closed due to flooding on the roadway. Several vehicles are still stuck in the flood waters. Wilton firefighters responded to 25 vehicles stranded in flood water and half a dozen fallen power lines. They also cleared many downed trees from the roadways as they navigated around Wilton.

Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to at times heavy rain, local law enforcement reported flash flooding in Snow Canyon State Park, including water moving over Snow Canyon Road which made the road impassable. The flooding also necessitated the closure of the south entrance to the park.

Rainfall rates of 0.5 to 0.8 inches per hour were observed in this area between 4 and 5 PM. Total rainfall of 1.30 inches occurred just west of Cranston Station near Valle Vista at Blackburn Road and State Highway 74. Flooding occurred at this location around 2:30 PM as well.

Floodwater out of Whitlow Canyon led to the closure of Silver King Rd. The employee from Queen Valley Fire Department said it was the highest flow he has ever seen. A Pinal County Flood Control streamflow gauge on Queen Creek at El Camino Viejo measured peak flow around 7 feet. No damages or injuries were reported.
A video on social media showed flash flooding on Wet Beaver Creek between Rim Rock and Lake Montezuma.

Swiftwater rescue of two vehicles stuck in wash on North Indian Canyon Drive near Sunrise Parkway. Whitewater and Morongo Canyon (Whitewater Trout Farm) and Lower Snow Creek received 0.5-1 inch from 6am-12pm. Video of vehicles in lower water crossing submerged in flowing water.
A woman and her 5 year old child were swept down a flooded roadway near San Marcos Creek. The woman survived, but her 5 year old child died.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Las Pilitas Road near Lake Santa Margarita. The bridge was impassable due to flooding.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Highway 1 near the Quintana Road.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding along Orcutt Garey Road near Dominion Road.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding along Highway 135 at the intersection of Batchelder Road.
A Fresno television station reported an evacuation order was issued by Madera County for flash flooding in the Bass Lake and North Fork areas, including the Bass Lake Mobile Home Park in North Fork.
A 60 year old woman was swept away in her SUV by raging flood waters along Avila Beach Road.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Highway 33 near Casitas Springs.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding which closed Highway 101 near Carpinteria.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding along Highway 46 near Painted Cave Road. The flash flooding resulted in a mudslide across the roadway.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Highway 101 near Bath Street. Several vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding near Creston Road. The flooded river severely damaged the bridge.

The Coalinga Fire Department performed a swift water rescue of a driver from a vehicle which was trapped in high flood waters at the intersection of SR 33 and Phelps Ave. near Los Gatos Creek in Coalinga. The rescue was also reported by local broadcast media.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding and mudslides on San Antonio Road near Highway 1.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding and mudslides on San Franciquito Canyon Road near Spunky Canyon Road.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Highway 246 between Sweeney Road and Mission Gate Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding, south of the city of San Luis Obispo. Law enforcement reported a vehicle stuck in the mud.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding which closed Highway 150 north of Santa Paula.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across Grimes Canyon Road. One vehicle was stuck in rising flood waters.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding and mudslides near the on and off ramps of Highway 33.
The Santa Clara River breached the bridge, flooding both directions and broke the center divide.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across Interstate 10 near Santa Monica.
Heavy rainfall produced a mudslide across the intersection of Huasna Road and Huasna Townsite Road.

Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across Halsey Canyon Road. Two to three feet of fast-moving water trapped passengers in an SUV. Los Angeles County Fire Department Swift Water Rescue Team has to save the occupants of the vehicle.
Significant flash flooding reported near Dolliver and Highway 1 intersection.
Harmony Grove Rd flooded at Wilgren Drive near Elfin Forest with four feet of water flowing in both directions into Elfin Park. Rain of 1.25-1.50 inch was reported that afternoon.
Orange County Fire Authority reported a swiftwater rescue of a young adult clinging to a tree in a creek, with rapidly moving water below. The person was airlifted out with no injuries reported.

A series of Pacific storm systems produced widespread heavy rainfall across the San Diego metro area, producing rainfall totals of 3-5 inches near Fashion Valley from January 14-17, with the heaviest occurring the morning of January 15- the morning of January 16. The San Diego River reached 12.4-12.7 feet at Fashion Valley.||Every cross street in Mission Valley along the San Diego River was flooded, including toward the San Diego Trolley. Three vehicles were abandoned and under 2-3 feet of flowing water on Camino Del Este, Qualcomm Way and Fashion Valley Road. The San Diego River overflowed, with over 1 foot of standing water into the nearby parking structure.||Numerous swiftwater rescues were conducted, including one rescue of a woman whose car was completely submerged into the flood waters at Camino De La Reina and Avenida del No; a helicopter search for two victims was conducted near 4700 Pacific Highway, with five victims having been rescued from the water.||Hotel guests at the Riverleaf Inn were evacuated and vehicles were submerged in flowing water.

Harmony Grove Road closed due to flooding, with 1-2 feet of flowing water from the Escondido Creek. Rainfall of 2 to 3 inches had been reported in the prior 24 hours, with 4 to 5.5 inches in the 72 hours leading up to the flooding.
Highway 62 was flooded with water and debris from Senilis Avenue to Park Avenue.
The Department of Highways reported water flowing across Cole Grade Road from the San Luis Rey River. Rainfall of 8 to 11 inches had been received in the 72 hours prior to the flood report.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Interstate 5 near Lankershim Boulevard near Burbank. A couple of vehicles were stuck in the flooded roadway.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding on Highway 150 at the intersection of Santa Ana Road near Lake Casitas. A couple of vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.
San Bernardino County Fire conducted a swift water rescue of one occupant from a truck. Report of rushing water enveloping the lower half of the truck.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding and significant mud and debris flows near the 19000 block of Placerita Canyon Road. Several vehicles were stuck in mud that was 25 feet deep.

Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding near the 1300 block on Highway 135, near Vandenberg Village. Swift water rescue team had to rescue two people who drove their vehicles around barricades and into the flooded roadway.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding on Ladera Canyon Road near the community of Ojai. Swift water rescue team had to rescue a couple people trapped in a vehicle, due to the flood waters.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding on Highway 101 near Campo de Cahuenga. All lanes of the 101 experienced significant flooding.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding on Highway 134 near Buena Vista Drive.
Heavy rainfall produced flooding as well as mud and debris flows on Interstate 405 near Rinaldi Drive in the San Fernando Valley.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding and significant mud and debris flows across Soledad Canyon Road near Aqua Dulce Road.
Report from CalTrans of Sig Alert, Closure due to flooding at transition of I-5 and Highway 55. About 0.8 inch of rain fell in the area at the time.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in Santa Barbara county. Highway 135 was closed from Bell Street to the Harris Grade, due to significant mud and water flowing across the roadway.
Fresno County Fire Department reported that three people were rescued from high water by boat near Bonanza Dr.
Fresno County Fire Department reported flooding into residences near the SR 180 and Dunlap Rd. near the Mill Creek Drainage.
Fresno County Fire Department reported water water over a bridge on Hopewell Rd.
California Highway Patrol reported Chimney Rock Road was completely washed out, due to heavy rain and flash flooding.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding near the community of Atascadero in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported mud and rocks across Highway 41.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in San Luis Obispo county. California Highway Patrol reported road closures between Avila Beach Drive and San Luis Bay drive, due to flooding.
California Highway Patrol reported significant flooding in the community of Cambria in San Luis Obispo county. At a gas station, water rose to a depth up to half of the gas pumps.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris completely blocking York Mountain Road and Shadow Canyon Road.
California Highway Patrol reported mud and debris blocking the offramp of Highway 154.

Flash flooding was reported in the downtown area of Sonora due to heavy rain from a severe thunderstorm. Tuolumne County OES reported a creek flowing out of banks, and water flowing over Washington Street, impacting approximately 25 to 30 homes, 10 public buildings and 30 businesses.
Calaveras County Sheriff Dispatch reported significant roadway flooding with two houses flooded in Copperopolis.
Tuolumne County Emergency Manager reported significant roadway flooding in the town of Tuolumne with creeks overflowing their banks.
Video submitted on social media showed Circle Mountain Road inundated by a fast-running wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Calaveras County Public Works reported the closure of Cooper Cove Drive between Black Creek Drive and Cheyenne Road in Copperopolis due to severe road damage by flooding.
A video was posted on Twitter showing flash flooding in Biola.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across the Inland Empire from the evening on March 14 through the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 2.00-3.50 fell, with local amounts up to 4 inches closer to the San Bernardino County Mountains. Flash flooding was reported early on the morning of March 15; firefighters responded to a vehicle in swift moving water, and the rescue was successful. Also, Grove Ave between Merrill Ave, Chino and Riverside Ave in Ontario saw 2 to 4 inches of running water covering the entire roadway. Kimball Ave in Chino between Quality Way and Euclid Ave were flooded with 2 to 4 inches of standing water.
Swiftwater rescue conducted by firefighters at Matthews Rd and Palomar Rd, with a vehicle submerged in one foot of water, with four occupants rescued.
Moderate rain in the higher elevations plus melting snow flooded Highway 159 in multiple places between Calico Basin Road and Blue Diamond Road.

Persistent moderate to at times heavy rain resulted in flash flooding throughout Beaver Dam Wash. For example, the Catclaw Canyon stream gage increased from a dry no-flow state of 0 CFS to a peak flow of approximately 2923 CFS. Cameras also showed water flowing in this typically dry wash.
Zion National Park reported multiple waterfalls and high flows at various locations throughout the park associated with ongoing rainfall.
Hilldale Dispatch reported multiple low-lying road closures due to high flows on Short Creek.
Caltrans reported 2 feet of water (photos included) on fast lane of state highway 60 at Jack Rabbit Trail, causing lane closures.  Between 400 and 418 pm local.
Amboy Road near Roy's was flooded.
Highway 95 was closed near 7th Street, and multiple swift water rescues were needed.
Water and debris flooded Bruce Woodbury Drive, Needles Highway, Casino Drive, and the Edgewater parking lot and garage. The floor of the Tropicana Casino also flooded.

Highway 95 flooded in several places between Airport Road and mile marker 50, with multiple vehicles stuck. The road eventually washed out completely at mile marker 50. The Five Mile Road onramp to Interstate 40 East also flooded.
Interstate 15 flooded.
Water and debris flooded Highway 127.
County Route 1 was closed.
Oatman Highway was damaged by flooding of the Warm Springs Wash.
Indian Head Drive was closed near the intersection of McCormick Boulevard due to flood damage.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge at Casandro Wash in Wickenburg registered flows going above alarm stage, which is 2.2 feet, at 20:03 MST. The flow reached a peak of 4.76 feet (343 cfs) at 20:30 MST and went below flood stage by 22:03 MST. This likely contributed to flooding along the inflow to Casandro Dam as well as small road crossings that intersect the wash. No damages or injuries were reported.
Portions of Jack Burden Rd in Wickenburg closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Portions of Vulture Mine Rd in Wickenburg closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
A trained spotter reported fast-moving water over Via Montezuma at Murrieta Creek, prompting a road closure.

Fairly persistent showers moved over Sulphur Creek during the morning hours, with thunderstorms moving over the Capitol Reef National Park area during the early afternoon. The storms resulted in quick bursts of heavy rain, with radar estimates showing around 0.4 to 0.6 inches of rainfall over the affected area. Subsequently, Capitol Reef National Park officials reported approximately 8 to 10 inches of water flowing through Sulphur Creek near the Capitol Reef National Park Visitor Center. A visitor report of knee- to thigh-deep water within Spring Canyon was also relayed from a Park Ranger.

Twitter report of flash flooding near Guadalupita within the Hermit's Peak Calf Canyon burn scar. Drainage below Silva Canyon on the burn scar flowed out of the banks and flooded nearby driveways and properties near SR-434 south of Guadalupita. Damages are unknown.
Heavy rain caused flooding along Highway 69 in Prescott Valley. Rose Creek flooded Hornet Drive.
Running washes lead to the closure of North Vulture Mine Road in Wickenburg. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Yavapai County Alert gauge on Black Canyon Creek showed about a two foot rise at 1040 PM.  A downstream gauge (Auga Fria--AFRA3) showed a rise at 200 AM on April 20. The river remained elevated through the evening of May 23.

Scattered thunderstorms moved across the area from late morning through the afternoon hours. Radar estimates indicated 1.25 inches to 2.5 inches of total rainfall near the affected area. A Park Ranger with the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument subsequently reported and sent pictures of Hole-in-the-Rock road near the 25 Mile Wash area, where floodwaters associated with the rain overtopped road culverts and resulted in a minor road washout.
Cima Road was closed at Interstate 15 due to flooding and erosion on both sides of the freeway. At least one vehicle was stuck with water up to the bottom of the doors.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding with several streets underwater. Photos were received of street flooding at Main Street and Orchard Avenue. High water marks were up to the front doors of businesses with some using sandbags. There were no reports of property damage or casualties.

Scattered thunderstorms developed across southern Utah on Saturday, moving across the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument towards the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. Locally heavy rainfall was associated with these thunderstorms, with radar estimated rainfall from around 0.75 inches to 1.5 inches noted across the Buckskin Gulch area. Two flood waves resulted, as noted on the Paria River at Lees Ferry gauge, downstream of the canyon. This gauge showed an initial gradual increase to around 50 cfs over the course of 2 hours, followed by a rapid increase to approximately 150 cfs over 15 minutes. The second bump would correlate to roughly a 1 foot rise at Lees Ferry, which would be much higher in the narrow slot canyon area of Buckskin Gulch. During the time of flood waves propagation through the slot canyon, at least 2 permitted hikers were hiking through the canyon. They were reported to be planning on hiking approximately 5 miles into Wire Pass and the Buckskin Gulch slot canyon areas. Kane County Sherriff's department received word of a deceased person within the trail, and subsequently recovered the bodies of two deceased individuals. It is believed that the men drowned in the initial flood wave, and were then washed 7 to 10 miles downstream.
Public report of traffic driving through several inches of moving water along Highway 395 at Desert Flower Road.
Flash flooding stranded multiple vehicles at and near Artist's Palette.
Highway 178 was closed east of Highway 127 due to flooding.
Highway 178 was closed at the junction of Highway 127 due to flooding.

NWS storm survey conducted by WFO San Diego. Several sections of Mountain View Road were covered in mud as much as two feet deep with damage on the side pavement. El Mirage Raws recorded 1.23 inches of rain during the afternoon on May 21. Radar total estimates of 2-4 inches occurred in surrounding areas. Standing water along El Mirage Road with one home surrounded by water. A nearby dry lake bed was partially water logged.
Flooding northwest of Twentynine Palms washed away multiple vehicles and caused at least one sinkhole in a road.
Highway 190 was flooded with water and debris and partially washed out. One vehicle was stuck.
Flooding and a mudslide affected the East Main Street off ramp of Interstate 15 South.
Heavy rains caused flash flooding in Clovis, Texico, and Cannon Air Force Base. There were multiple reports of roads becoming closed and impassable with vehicles being stranded.

Widespread 1 to 2 inches of radar estimated rain fell in Niland and areas just east into the Chocolate Mountains. A large area of considerable runoff flowed through Niland and the surrounding area, as evident in reports and before and after Sentinel2 satellite images, with upwards of 6 inches to 1 foot of flowing water in some areas, per photos and videos. Major flash flooding impacts were experienced. The East Highline Canal east of Niland, was overcome with flood waters and silt, mainly north of of Flowing Wells Rd. The overflowing canal was first reported a little after 1600PDT and only exacerbated the flooding. Several roads became impassable, unsafe, and subsequently closed due to flood water. At least a few cars became stuck in flood water leading to swift water rescues by land and air. The exact number of rescues is unknown. In Niland, several photos and videos showed flooded streets and yards, with water coming up to homes and businesses. There were a few reports of water entering homes, but it is unknown how many homes were impacted. Also impacted in the area was agriculture, as several fields had flood water moving through them. It is unknown the extent of any damages to the agricultural fields or the exact number. Sentinel2 satellite images showed evidence of all the disturbed earth, deposited mud and silt, through Niland, the agricultural fields and surrounding areas. In a statement by Imperial Irrigation District, the impacts to East Highline Canal resulted in a delay of 133 water deliveries. Also the O Lateral canal, which branches from East Highline canal, suffered structural damage. The main highway through the area, Hwy-111, was flooded in several locations, which hampered relief efforts. The small town of Slab City, to the northeast of Niland, was cut off from the rest of the Imperial Valley due to the flooded roads. As a result of the significant impacts, the County of Imperial issued an emergency proclamation for additional and better resources. Red Cross assisted in relief and a couple shelters for evacuees were established. There were no injuries reported from this event and specifics on property and crop damage is unknown and thus grossly estimated.

Street flooding reported in Clovis.
Water 8 to 9 inches deep was reported at the intersection of West Grande Avenue and North Hull Street. A car was stalled in deep water nearby at West Grande Avenue and West 1st Street.
Road closure from standing water over roadway along NM 267 from mile marker 10 to 13.
The emergency manager reports water standing on all roads near Tatum, including Highways 206 and 380.

Heavy rainfall caused sudden and strong runoff through diversion channels and arroyos across town. Swift water rescues were done at Rachel Road SE and Four Hills Road and Wyoming Blvd. and Indian School Road. Two people were rescued, while a third did not survive at the Rachel Road and Four Hills location.
