A debris flow was also reported within the Tijeras Arroyo that runs just south of the Albuquerque Sunport but water remained in its banks.
The county emergency manager relayed reports of street flooding along 21st Street at Thornton and Cameo Streets. The Hillcrest Park also flooded.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding within the Blue 2 burn scar upstream of Bonito Lake.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Eagle Creek and debris flow over State Highway 532.

Broadcast media shared a report from a semi-truck driver of flash flooding along NM Highway 42 just southeast of Willard, NM. Accumulating hail and an estimated 6 to 8 inches of heavy rain washed out and shutdown this stretch of highway. Snow plows were needed to be used to clear the way. There are no reports of injuries or casualties. Damage is an estimate.

Heavy rains over the new South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding along Cedar Creek that raged through the Innsbrook Village near NM Highway 48. An NWS Employee also recorded flash flooding along Cedar Creek down to Paradise Canyon Drive. Damage is unknown, and may be more related to the South Fork Wildfire.

Emergency management relayed reports of swift water rescues out of the Rio Ruidoso near Hollywood and at the River Ranch RV Park along U.S. Highway 70. Emergency management requested a flash flood emergency be issued along the Rio Ruidoso down to the Two Rivers Dam. There was an unknown number of people rescued.
NM State Emergency Operations Center relayed a report of flash flooding and mud slides along Gavilan Canyon Road within the McBride burn scar.
NM 542 just north of the intersection with NM 55 closed due to heavy rains and 8 to 10 inches of fast flowing water over the highway.
Underpass to I-25 Exit 361 flooded with rapidly rushing water and widespread flooding in the fields along the interstate. That road was covered with several inches of small hail.

Flash flooding and debris flow within the eastern edge of the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar resulted in a bridge being washed out along County Road A3. Exact location is unknown and damage is an estimate.

Flooding over U.S. Highway 85 at mile markers 200 and 204 requiring debris removal. Reports of home damage from arroyo flooding, and a water rescue of a couple trapped in a mobile home due to surrounding flood waters. Injuries are unknown. Flood damage reported in homes from the arroyo flooding. Damage costs are an estimate.

Heavy rains forced sharp rises along the Rio Chama between Medanales and Espanola. These rises were observed to peak at 7.95 feet at the Rio Chama near Chamita (CMTN5) gauge, resulting in flooding along U.S. Highway 84 between the junction of U.S. Highway 285 and Abiquiu that impacted 40 residences. This also resulted in heavy sand deposits near Medanales that resulted in the Rio Chama rerouting through adjacent agricultural fields two days later on June 22nd. Damage is an estimate given the lack of information and is an aggregate of the damage caused by the rerouting of the Rio Chama into the aforementioned agricultural fields as this was a direct result of the flash flooding that occurred on the night of the 20th into the morning of the 21st.

Several rounds of thunderstorms moved over the Pima area from 6 PM until after 10 PM in the evening. This caused extensive street flooding and flash flooding with water running curb to curb on numerous streets.
A flash flood due to heavy rain was reported at Blue Pool Wash.

There was a photo of water over the roadway and localized flooding near the intersection of 800 N and 1100 E at Meads Wash. The Carbon County Regional Airport/Buck Davis Field ASOS reported 0.44 inches of rain in less than 15 minutes, then 0.59 inches over the following 30 minutes.

Heavy rain on the McBride burn scar resulted in flash flooding with mud and ash off the hillsides roughly between NM 48 and Eagle Creek Road, and a second area along Gavilan Canyon road by Meander Drive was washed out with debris over the roadway. Both sections of Gavilan Canyon Road were closed. A water main break also occurred that exacerbated the situation. Damage is an estimate based on clearing the debris on the roadway.
Heavy rain overtopped and washed out several dirt roads in the area.
Diamond Fork Road near the Fifth Water Hot Springs trailhead was closed due to mudslides.

Multiple reports of flash flooding across Farmington including along the La Plata and San Juan Rivers, including vehicles driving across flooded low water crossings. A video from the emergency manager showed the La Plata River raging and partly out of its banks. These included along Southside River Road on the west side of Farmington. A vehicle was stuck in a ditch along the San Juan River, thankfully the driver made it out safely. There was an overflowing ditch and arroyo with fast moving water at Brookside Drive and Navajo Street. There was several inches of water moving across Crouch Mesa east of Farmington and south of Flora Vista. U.S. Highway 64 at Andrea Drive and between County Road 5500 and 5777 where the road was completely flooded with swift moving water and impassable. A normally dry wash also observed a one foot rise with debris including small pieces of furniture. Flooding lasted well after the heavy rains ended as evident on the San Juan River gauge (FRMN5) showing river levels did not recede until after 10:00 pm MDT. Damage is an estimate based on the very limited information provided.
Water was flowing over Hwy 191 at Milepost 491 (near Rock Point). There were stranded vehicles. Time of was event estimated. Report and photo from Social Media.

Flash flooding from heavy rains closed NM Highway 65 from mile markers 2 to 4 or one mile south of Montezuma where culverts were washed out. Flowing water 1 to 3 feet deep also reported over El Llano Road, Cinder Road, Palo Verde Road and at the intersection of 7th Street and Mills Avenue. Road closures were also reported along State Road 65 at Campus and El Camino, as well as along 8th Street north of Mills Avenue. Robertson Cardinal football field was completely covered in standing water. The Las Vegas Water Treatment Plant also flooded. A mandatory evacuation order was issued at 9:54pm MDT for this area due to the dangerous flooding across Las Vegas to Montezuma. Damage is an estimated given very limited information.
Widespread flooding reported along Tecolote Creek in Mineral Hill stretching over to NM Highway 283 from mile markers 3 to 13 that closed the highway. Any damage is unknown.
Flash flooding was reported in Little Wildhorse Canyon and Bell Canyon. Several camps were impacted by mud and debris washed downstream.

The Cibola County Emergency manager reported multiple vehicle rescues from flood waters. The Rio San Jose was out of its banks between Sargent and Davis Streets with several streets flooded in town. Swift moving water several inches deep was observed over First Street and Roosevelt Avenue. Damage is an estimate.

Significant flooding occurred due to heavy rains from a thunderstorm near Valley of the Gods and northeast of Mexican Hat. Fast moving waters covered Highway 163 near Valley of the Gods for a distance of 540 meters and 1 meter deep. Cottonwood Wash had major flood, surrounding house and filling flood plain. San Juan River spiked from 8.3 ft (2670 cfs) to 17.99 ft (20,700 cfs) near Mexican Hat. 28 people were trapped and stranded while on a river trip on the San Juan River where Lime Creek enters and eventually rescued. However, their boats and gear were swept away and lost in floodwaters.

Major flooding in Moab and Castle Valley from strong thunderstorm that produced very heavy rain across town, Mill Creek, North Mill Creek, Kane Creek and a drainage above Castle Valley. 1 inch of rain fell in 15 minutes for a rainrate of 4 inches per hour. 2 reported missing in Moab area with an abandoned vehicle discovered in Mill Creek drainage after flash flooding, 1 was found deceased and other assumed fatality but not found.

Thunderstorms brought heavy intense rainfall over the Tucson Metro area. Rainfall totals ranged from 1 to 2.5 inches from Pima County Alert Gauges. ||Tucson Fire Department responded to over 25 calls with 15 of those calls relating to stranded drivers or stuck in swift moving water. Two adults were found dead in a wash after a swift water rescue attempt.
The road from Rough Rock to Black Mesa was washed out with very large boulders blocking the road.

Raging waters on Cedar Creek overtopped its banks in spots, resulting in the closure of Paradise Canyon Road near Hull Road. Muskat Ball Drive at Cedar Creek was impassable due to flooding with medium to heavy debris. County Road 127A (Upper Eagle Creek Road) was impassible with medium to heavy debris along the road. Alto Lake also flooded over a short time.
Flash flooding was reported in Pleasant Creek.
A flash flood was reported in Phipps Wash.
Water was flowing at the intersection of Butler and Foxglenn in Flagstaff. There was a video on social media of a vehicle driving through the flood water and almost stalled.
Heavy rain, estimated at 2 to 3 inches caused flash flooding along Central Highway north of Highway 80.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge peaked at 487 cfs after starting off dry at 0 cfs earlier in the day.
The Nogales Wash at Nogales exceeded bankfull at about 8 feet causing flooding in the Morley Road region of Nogales.

Highway 9 was closed due to flooding between Mile Marker 11 and Mile 68 east of Columbus.  Most flooding occurred in Luna County with the large road closure due to not wanting traffic from either direction to enter the flooded area.

NMDOT reported the bridge along U.S. Highway 64 at the AZ border was severely damaged by flash flooding. The original bridge was in the process of being replaced and what was destroyed was a temporary bridge structure until a new bridge was constructed. Damage is an estimate.
Flash flooding was reported in Grand Wash and water was over the road on state Route 24 in Capitol Reef National Park. Time is estimated from RADAR.
Flooding was reported on Interstate 70 between mileposts 96 and 103.
Flash flooding was reported on Pleasant Creek.
Water flooding over NM 605 north of Milan prompted the closure of the highway.
A flash flood with water several feet deep was reported on House Rock Valley Road. Time and location are approximate.

Heavy rainfall from strong to severe thunderstorms moved over the Moab area, causing flash flooding through the downtown Moab streets as well as the Mill Creek drainage where water was running over a few of the roads. Rainfall estimates of 0.8 to 1.5 inches fell during this time. Hail also accompanied the heavy rain with some hail up to quarter size.
Flooding of dirt roads was reported in Hanksville.
Heavy rain brought 1 to 2 foot deep flash flood and debris through the very popular Antelope Canyon area.

Flash flooding in eastern Garfield County stranded 4 people on an elevated rock in Hog Canyon near state Route 95. Department of Public Safety helicopter and Swift Water Rescue crews were on standby. The individuals were able to move safely to dry ground. Time is estimated from radar.
The Huntington Power Plant reported flash flooding, and debris was reported across state Route 31. Location is approximate.
Water and debris completely covered Gavilan Canyon Road at the Gavilan Canyon Softball Field, making the road impassable.

Heavy rain measured to have ranged from 1 to 2 inches within one hour across the Albuquerque metro area caused major flash flooding. Underpasses and low lying intersections in downtown were inundated with deep floodwaters. An SUV and public transit bus were partially submerged under the water and had to be retrieved by a tow truck. There were reports of street flooding and vehicles being stranded elsewhere across town. The Albuquerque Fire Department reported they performed 7 swift water rescues in the arroyos around town and 18 overall responses to folks impacted by the floodwaters. Of these responses, 10 were to help people stranded. An unknown number of homes near downtown and south of downtown received flood damage. The Albuquerque Police Department, Convention Center and City Hall also experienced flooding, but the damage was mostly aesthetic according to media reports. Total damage is an estimate based on limited information and extent of damage.
NMDOT reported standing water on NM 542 and NM 55 prompting a road closure.

Heavy rains on the Hermit's Peak Calf Canyon burn scar resulted in flash flooding and water over the highway at multiple points of State Road 283 just west of Las Vegas, NM. There were no reports of damage.
Heavy rains overnight produced flash flooding along NM-65 just north and northwest of Las Vegas, NM. There were no reports of damage.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused a 2.3 foot rise on Oak Creek in Sedona.
Cannon AFB weather reported spotty flooding with 8 to 12 inches depth of water in spots, but no impassable streets.
Flash flooding occurred in Las Vegas on Mills Avenue near the state Behavior Health Institute Building.

Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms on the South Fork and Salt Fire burn scars resulted in flash flooding and debris flows across the Upper Canyon and Brady Canyon neighborhoods along the Rio Ruidoso. A bridge on Main Road at McDaniel Road was washed from the debris flow and runoff. Video on social media showed the roof of a house along with other household debris sliding down the Rio Ruidoso upper canyon among fast moving water. Additionally, a woman was trapped in a tree due to high rushing water. Runoff from the rainfall moved downstream through the Rio Ruidoso exceeding its banks and impacting the Fern Trail and Paradise Canyon near downtown Ruidoso. Several car and water rescues were conducted in this area. The Riverside RV Park in Hollywood along the banks of the Rio Ruidoso was completely flooded out. Another video on social media showed the Rio Ruidoso at Ruidoso Downs Racetrack and Casino out of its banks flooding the horse racetrack. Additionally, crews with excavators are seen digging up dirt along the banks of the Rio Ruidoso at the racetrack cleaning up prior flash flood damage. Thankfully, no injuries or fatalities were reported from the catastrophic flash flooding. Property damage cost is an estimate.

Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall from thunderstorms impacted the South Fork and Salt Fire burn scars for a second day in a row. This resulted in exacerbated flash flooding and debris flow in the same locations along the Rio Ruidoso. A house near downtown Ruidoso was reported to have been pushed 10 feet due to flash flooding. A busted water line and gas leak were also reported in the area. An SUV with 3 occupants inside floated down the Rio Ruidoso. Thankfully, all 3 occupants were rescued. The worst impacts from this episode of flash flooding and debris flow occurred on U.S. Highway 70 in Hollywood. The highway and its various intersections, including Mechem Drive and Sudderth Drive were shut down. Fast and heavy debris flow resulted in a road collapse near the Sudderth Dr. and U.S. Highway 70 intersection. The debris flowing down U.S. Highway 70 at one point included a large shipping container. Property damage cost is an estimate.

Highway 62 was closed between El Rey Ave and Encelia Ave, with at least two feet of water and debris over the road. Numerous cars were stuck, and swift water rescues were needed. Nearly three feet of water and mud flowed through a motel, destroying the first floor.
Calle de Los Campesinos road was partially washed out. 1 inch of rain and large hail occurred in about 60 minutes. This location is just west of State Route 74 in Palm Desert.
Flash flooding was reported at Highway 58 and Community Blvd.
Heavy rain ranging from about 1 to 2.5 inches resulted in about 5 swift water rescues across the region.

The USGS stream gauge along the Agua Fria River near Humboldt (AFHA3) reported a 7.86 foot rise starting at around 700 PM, peaking at around 9 PM, and retrning to near normal at around 1 AM. The Agua Fria River gauge near Mayer (AFMA03) began to rise at around 100 AM, rose 2.5 feet by 200 AM, and the dropped to near normal at 1200 PM on the 15th.||There was a Swift water rescue at 835 PM off of Bradshaw Mountain Road in the Quailwood Subdivision (Agua Fria River). Vehicle in the water with two occupants. Report from spotter on social media.
Extensive flooding in area washes occurred just southeast of Sierra Vista as rainfall amounts of at least 2 to 3 inches occurred. Monson Road closed due to flooding.

Water over Bartlett Dam Road at Camp Creek. Heavy rain fell on the Wildcat Fire Burn Scar with 1.65 inches of rain recorded in less than one hour at the Camp Creek at Bartlett Dam Road rain gage operated by Maricopa County Flood Control. The County Flood Control notified Maricopa County Department of Transportation to barricade road. No damages nor injuries were reported.
NMDOT reported difficulty driving on NM Highway 50 between mile markers 1 and 3 due to standing water and debris over the roadway.
A USGS stream gage on the Verde river showed a one foot rise upstream from Camp Verde.

The USGS stream gauge on the Verde Rive downstream of Camp Verde (VCVA3) recorded a 1.68 foot rise from 500 PM to 700 PM. The river returned to normal around 200 AM on the 18th.  The heavy rain likely fell over the West Clear Creek drainage.
The USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fira River near Dewey-Humboldt (AFHA3) reported a 2.75 foot rise bettween 700 PM and 745 PM. The river returnred to near normal at 200 AM on the 18th.
A radio report of flash flooding was received from heavy rain on the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar along NM Highway 94 just north and west of Sapello, NM.
KOB relayed a viewer report of flash flooding on NM Highway 50 near exit 299 near Glorieta, NM. There was a foot of water over the roadway.
Highway 127 was flooded near mile marker 15. One car was stranded due to water getting into the ignition.

USGS stream gauge on the Verde River near Camp Verde (VAVA3) reported a 1.26 foot rise from earlier thunderstorms upstream at 745 PM. Another gauge downstream (VCVA3) started to rise at 200 AM, peaked at 600 AM (just under a one foot rise), and then returned to near normal at 600 AM on July 19.

A late evening batch of moderate to heavy showers passed over the complex of burn scars in and around Ruidoso producing a half inch to one inch of rainfall in the area. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred, focusing through Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso after 11pm MDT. Flood waters overtopping bridges and roadways were reported in several areas including Mechem Dr. at Brady Canyon Dr., U.S. Highway 70 at Cedar Creek, and Paradise Canyon Road at Cedar Creek. Evacuations were ordered from the Upper Canyon area to areas along the Rio Ruidoso from west of town through to mobile home areas near Hollywood along U.S. Highway 70. Several swift water rescues were conducted, including for two vehicles trapped in water near Johnson Rd., an elderly resident who was unable to evacuate on Brady Canyon Dr., and one resident trapped on one side of a bridge at Paradise Rd. and Foothill Rd. that was overtopped by water. Cherokee Mobile Home Park sustained damage with water flowing beneath mobile homes. Home damage was reported along Brady Canyon Dr. from the elderly couple who needed assistance evacuating. A culvert on Cedar Creek above the ranger station was completely torn out and washed out onto the roadway. Rises on the Rio Ruidoso at the Hollywood gage spiked from 1.58 feet to 8.16 feet within 90 minutes before waters started to recede.
The Ruidoso Police Department reported fast moving water flowing along the sides of Highway 70.

Heavy thunderstorms on the South Fork burn scar resulted in another round of burn scar flash flooding, debris flow and severe property damage across the Upper Canyon and Brady Canyon neighborhoods along Mechem Drive west of downtown Ruidoso. Bridge 2 at Main Road and Fox Road became impassible due to flooding. Debris flows resulted in arching powerlines over the flood water at Brady Canyon. An SUV was trapped against a tree due to flood waters just north of Brady Canyon Road. There was a rescue of two juveniles from a house at Meander Drive and Paradise Canyon Drive. Runoff from the flash flooding resulted in the Rio Ruidoso to instantly rise to major flood stage and a new record level of 15.80 feet. This resulted in more flash flooding at the Ruidoso Downs Casino horse racetrack. Flash flooding caused damage to the racetrack, two bridges near the entrance of the facility, and in the barn area. After this latest instance of flash flooding, officials decided to shut down the horse racetrack for the remainder of the summer season and move upcoming scheduled races to Albuquerque. Thankfully, no injuries or fatalities were reported from this instance of burn scar flash flooding. Property damage is an estimate.
Significant water flow was reported along US 70 near the Casino Apache Travel Center.

Tijeras Arroyo overtopped Via Sedillo for the second time in a week. The large embankment created by road crews to protect the roadway from additional flood waters was blown out again. Mud, rocks, and debris covered a large section of the roadway.

Caltrans Kyburz Maintenance responded to a mudslide near the Caldor Fire Burn Scar on Eastbound Highway 50 near Strawberry on July 20th, as thunderstorms were producing locally heavy rain over the mountains on this day. The slide did not impact traffic. No observations were available in the area but radar estimated rain amounts of around an inch in under an hour.
Social media video showed water running over Dripping Springs Road.
Pine Creek was flowing around 3 feet deep through Pine. Pinewood Tavern at Highway 87 and Hardscrabble Mesa Road was closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding with a depth of 6 inches across parts of Portales. Locations included U.S. 70 and Kilgore Road in northeast Portales and 18th Street near downtown Portales. No reports of any damage from flooding.

A BLM Ranger reported a large flash flood of Dry Valley Creek where it meets Rock Springs Creek. The flash flood waters were reported to by up to 4-6 feet deep given a water mark left behind that was higher than the vehicle. Further south, a BLM Ranger reported flash flooding near the Old Town Paria site, with a couple feet of water reportedly flowing off the surrounding terrain and into the Paria River. Times estimated.
Yavapai County ALERT stream gage measured a 1.5 ft rise on Big Bug Creek in Mayer.

The Paria River near Kanab river gage showed a rapid rise from minimal flow to a peak flow of 409 CFS. Flooding was also confirmed by an observer along the Paria River with supporting pictures and documentation.

County official reported 4.0 mi WSW of Lockwood, NV, road closures between Hidden Highlands Drive and Sleepy Hollow Drive due to flash flooding in the area of Hidden Valley. About 100 homes were affected by the flooding.
The gage at Aqua Fria below Ash Creek (YAAA3) showed a quick, 3 foot rise. Flash           flooding would have occured upstream prior to the reported rise at YAAA3.

Numerous roads closed due to Flash Flooding in the Drexel Heights area. A Pima County Sheriff reported a motorist stuck in a vehicle on flooded roadway that was rescued by emergency services due to flooding of the Black Wash.
Sierra County dispatch reported flooding across Truth or Consequences, Elephant Butte and Williamsburg.

Rainfall amounts of around half an inch over the South Fork burn scar resulted in more flash flooding across the Upper Canyon and Brady Canyon neighborhoods west of downtown Ruidoso. Runoff on the burn scar resulted in flash flooding on the Rio Ruidoso resulting in road closures along and near the banks of the river, including White Mountain and Sunny Slope Drive, Brady Canyon Road and Mechem from Cedar Creek, and Gavilan Canyon Road. Property damage is an estimate.
NM DOT reported flooding on mile marker 7 along NM 434 which prompted a road closure and the deployment of a cleanup crew to clear rocks and debris.
Heavy rain triggered a landslide along Whitney Portal Road, blocking both lanes with large boulders.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Road.
Water and debris were all over Highway 127 at Dumont Dunes Rd.
Highway 62 was flooded in multiple places from Mesquite Springs Rd to Encelia Dr.
Three roads were closed due to flooding.
Roads along the Indian Cove Campground Site in Joshua Tree National Park closed due to flooding. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Kelbaker Rd was closed from I-40 to Kelso Depot due to flash flooding and debris flow. The road reopened on 7/25.
Emergency Manager reported a mudslide 2.0 mi SW of Wellington, NV, along Hoye Canyon Road due to heavy rainfall.
The intersection of Highway 62 and Godwin Rd was flooded.
Highway 168 was flooded with water, rocks, and debris near Deep Springs Ranch Rd. A plow had to clear the road.
A USGS stream gage on Tonto Creek (TNRA3) rose just over a foot between 600 PM and 1000 PM. The water returned to a stable level by noon on the 25th.

Flash flooding was reported along Sheep Creek Road near Kodachrome Basin. The road was reported to have experienced flash flooding in several areas over a 5 to 6 mile stretch requiring heavy equipment cleanup due to mud and debris. Report noted from Kodachrome State Park official as well as NWS employee.
A strong thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding in and around Kanarraville. One house received flood damage from water, mud, and debris per Iron County Emergency Management.
Road flooding on Sahuarita Road east of Comsoft Drive.
Reports of flash flooding northeast side of Tucson included the following:|1) Tanque Verde Loop Road south of Linden Street at the Tanque Verde Creek.|2) Redington Road near Canyon del Salto Wash.
Water over Agua Caliente Road at 4th of July Wash.  Maricopa County Flood Control stream gage located about one mile upstream of road exceeded Alarm Stage. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Numerous reports of flash flooding across the Tucson Metro. ||Reports included the following: |1) Water Rescue near Silverlake and Euclid Ave.|2) Swift water rescue on Bilby and Fontana with motorist stranded on roof of car.|3) Public reported flooding in the street near Grant and Dodge Road. Flooding above the sidewalk and public transit bus struggled to drive through the street.|4) Multiple swift water rescues in Central Tucson.
SR-238 closed due to flooding west of Mobile. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Old US-80 Highway closed due to flooding. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Flooding on SR-87 Northbound near N Hashan Kehk Rd in Sacaton. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Two to three inches of rain fell in the Hereford area resulting in Flash Flooding.

A USGS stream gage along the Little Colorado River near St. Johns (LCSA3) reported a 3.8 foot rise between 530 PM and 830 PM.  The flow returned to near normal around 800 AM on the 28th.  St. Johns police reported that multiple homes being flooded along Commercial Street and along 7th Street South near the Little Colorado River. Street flooding was also occurring in St Johns.
Emergency manager reported Brady Canyon Dr. and Ponderosa Dr. were closed due to water flowing over the roadway, caused by burn scar flash flooding.
Mesonet stream gauge along Gilson Wash recorded an approximate 2.38 ft jump, impacting downstream low water crossings. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Rainfall amounts of 0.50 to 1.50 inches fell on the South Fork burn scar west of downtown Ruidoso during the early afternoon hours. This rainfall resulted in more burn scar flash flooding and debris flows across neighborhoods in Alto and Ruidoso. The Cherokee Mobile Village along U.S. Highway 70 at the Lincoln and Otero County line was evacuated due to flash flooding. Mechem Dr. became impassible again due to Cedar Creek overflowing its banks and rushing over the roadway. Heavy flows along Cedar Creek caused Mechem Dr. to become impassable, washed out a part of Musket Ball Dr. and brought debris flow over Cree Meadows Drive. Flooding of the Rio Ruidoso resulted in the closure of Gavilan Canyon Road and the evacuation of the Gavilan Mobile Home Park. Debris flow on the Rio Ruidoso destroyed a culvert on the eastern end of the Ruidoso Downs racetrack. Water and debris flow reported west of Alto making NM 532 impassable. Fortunately, no reports of significant water rises were received downstream of the water breach at Ruidoso Downs. Culvert and trailer park damage cost is an estimate.

Numerous reports of flash flooding in the Bisbee area including mud and gravel over much of Brewery Ave making it impassable. Additionally, Green Bush Wash west of Bisbee flowed over roads and private properties. Public also reported approximately 1-3 inches of water flowing over Highway 92.
Numerous washes in the Tucson area flowed including Cienega Creek. There were numerous reports of road closures throughout Tucson due to flooding.

Heavy rain caused an incrase in the water flowing down the Little Colorado River near St Johns.  The flow started to incrase at 1500 and peaked at around 2 feet higher at 1700. The river dropped back to near normal at 2100.
Roads in Nogales including Industrial Park Drive closed due to flash flooding.
The local Fire Department reported flooding near the junction of Alpine Village Road and NM Highway 48 just south of Alto, NM.

Flash flooding and debris flows on the Rio Ruidoso in the Upper Canyon area along Main Road was relayed by Emergency Management and was seen on a USGS camera. Debris piled up and clogged some culverts along Main Road in Ruidoso. Another debris flow from this same heavy rain event resulted in the closure of Gavilan Canyon Bridge near Hollywood. Overall, the debris flows stayed within the banks of the Rio Ruidoso and did not overwhelm any of the main bridges in Ruidoso. Damage cost is an estimate based on cleanup costs of the clogged culverts.
Highway 322 was flooded and impassable.
Local law enforcement reported flash flooding just outside of the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar along NM 434 at mile marker 3 that closed the road.
Roadway flooding reported near Wentworth Rd and Interstate 10.

According to the Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located at Cruff Wash, water levels rose above the alarm level stage of 2.5 feet at around 1952MST and crested at 3.91 feet, which is above the bank full level stage of 3.88 feet, at around 2015MST. Water levels fell below alarm stage at around 2105MST. Based on the information of problem areas produced by the Maricopa County Flood Control District, flooding was likely along the low water crossing of Agua Caliente Road located above 2 miles downstream of the gauge. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Time is estimated from radar and reports. Heavy rain resulted in a debris flow off the Bear Fire burn scar. Mitigation efforts in Crandall and Bear Canyons minimized impacts. Flooding occurred in the median at the intersection of U.S. Highway 6 and U.S. Highway 191 because a drainage was clogged by debris. There was mud across U.S. Highway 191 at milepost 272. A few small rocks made it to U.S. Highway 6 near Crandall and Bear Canyons. Drainage ditches were filled with debris.
A USGS river gauge on Oak Creek in Sedana measured a two foot rise in 15 minutes from heavy rain near Munds Park.

Local Nevada BLM Officials surveyed flood damage caused by a slow moving thunderstorm at the Dolly Varden Mountain Range. The survey provided evidence of flooding from water runoffs onto a service road caused by a thunderstorm over the area that lasted 2.5 hours that created a deep trench and water overflow over the service road at the range. Estimated radar precipitation between 1.5 to 2 inches of rain. Pictures of the survey and coordinates are attached.
Heavy rain due to a thunderstorm caused a car to get stuck in a neighborhood wash drainage across intersection of E Calle Sonora and N Calle Guadalupe.
SR-238 closed between mile markers 25 and 35 due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Sevenmile Wash rose approximately 2 ft, making low water crossings across the wash impassable. Timing estimated from radar estimated precipitation. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Cienega Creek rose at least three feet.
Reports of flash flooding with running water over roadway at the intersection of Sopori Wash and W Arivaca Rd.
A river guage (YAAA3) on Aqua Fria River (below Ash Creek) showed a rapid 3.5 foot rise beginning at 7:00 PM MST. The river returned to near normal levels at midnight.

Reports of flash flooding on roadways and stranded vehicles near Washington Ave and Golf Course Road in Douglas. There was also a car stuck in flooded roadway at Primrose St and Washington Ave in Douglas.

Damage from flash flooding occurred along County Road A3A. Debris and rubble were scattered across roadways and driveways with some vehicles trapped in the debris. Another video in the same area showed vehicles trapped in flash flooding in Rincon Montoso southwest of Rociada. Property damage for cabins and vehicles is an estimate.

Thunderstorms with heavy rainfall went through the Tucson Metro on August 8th resulting in 0.5 to 1.0 inches of rain leading to flash flooding and running washes. In addition, the Pima County Medical Examiner found that drowning was the primary factor in the death of one individual. The individual was found in Aviation Wash on August 9th with debris and running water.
A driveway a few miles south of Edgewood became flooded and impassable.
An arroyo that flows underneath I-40 just east of Wagon Wheel flooded and exceeded its banks with an observed water rise of 7 feet.
Zion National Park dispatch reported widespread flash flooding within Zion Canyon, including in Behunin Canyon and along the North Fork of the Virgin River.
Camino de la Tierra closed just south of Tumbleweed Dr due to flash flooding.
A roughly 700 cfs flash flood was recorded by the Paria River near Kanab gauge at 12:40 a.m. MDT.
Social media video shows a road washed out at intersection near E. Frontage Road and Bar D 4 Road near Santa Cruz south of Espanola. Road repair cost is an estimate.

The Albuquerque Fire Department rescued an injured man and a dog in 7 feet of water in an arroyo channel. A second man was spotted lifeless moving down the North Diversion Channel near Menaul Blvd. and eventually Osuna Road. His body was recovered in the North Valley outfall of the channel. Rainfall of 0.50 to 1.40 was reported upstream of the arroyo channel.

NM State Police reported a road closure on State Highway 434 due to flooding and runoff from the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar flowing across the road. Road closure time estimated based on radar data.
The Emery County Emergency Manager reported around 2 feet of water was observed flowing through Bell Canyon. Time is estimated by archived radar and MRMS data. Exact location is estimated.

Heavy rains from a thunderstorm fell upstream of Indian Creek and Salt Creek Wash between 1630 and 1800. Water flowed through both Indian Creek and Salt Creek Wash where it intersects with Highway 211 in Canyonlands National Park Needles District causing flash flooding with water flowing rapidly through the washes with some small tree branches.
Flash flooding in the Pine Lake community left some rural roads impassable.

Flooding of several roads in the Cornville area, including Cornville Road near Cactus Road was seen on a social media video. Another video showed property and street flooding east of Page Springs Road and north of Cornville Road. There was also flooding along Harmony, Oak Run Lane, and Page Springs Road. Flooding of multiple homes along Alvey and Brooks Lanes. The fire department personnel reported at least 6 homes flooded in Cornville.
Videos and data showed a flash flood of Wahweap Creek.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a crest of 830 cfs at 9 a.m. MDT as the peak of the flood wave passed by the gauge.

Anza Borrego State Park reported, video taped and photographs flash flooding from Fish Creek and across Split Mountain Road. Runoff caused damage to paved road. NWS Kineros modeling predicted 4 to 5 feet water levels at the exit of Fish Creek canyons before Split mountain road on the San Diego County side.

San Diego department of Public Works reported mud flows and flash flooding on the Great Southern Overland Stage route S2 and Vallecito Wash crossings. 2.54 inches of rain was recorded. Public Works also provided photos of the flooding and NWS did a storm survey the next day.

Video showing flash flooding in multiple spots along Split Mountain Rd, with most significant flooding at the Fish Creek Wash crossing. The road was washed out at this point and floodwaters were reportedly as deep as 4-6 feet based on sediment flow and depth of the wash. No injuries were reported.
SR-98 closed between Imperial Highway and Brockman Road due to flooding with several vehicles hydroplaning on the road. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Very heavy rain in the mountains above Littlefield flowed down into the community, leaving the Farm/Fleet Rd underpass under I-15 flooded with approximately 10 feet of water. Other roads in the area were also flooded, including the northbound lanes of I-15 near mile marker 9.

Storms over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding in the Upper Canyon neighborhood including Johnson Road and Main Road requiring the closing of Main Road at Bridge 1. High flows in the Rio Ruidoso eventually flowed downstream resulting in water flowing across North Eagle Drive. Ruidoso Municipal Schools were put under a shelter in place notice while the flash flood warning was in effect.
The stream gauge on Chevelon Creek showed a rapid rise of around 4 feet between noon and 200 PM MST. The creek return to near normal levels at around 100 AM MST on August 13.

Time is estimated. Homes in Saratoga Springs sustained water damage due to intense bursts of rain, in particular on South Island Road. City parks were also impacted with floodwaters. Construction sites were also affected by rainfall.

Heavy rain fell over the Pipeline Fire scar in Weatherford Canyon. This sent a flash flood about 1.5 feet deep down Government Tank Wash.  The water covered Waterline Road and Switchback Trail. The water then flowed into the first retention basin just west of Landfill Road.
Park rangers reported that multiple canyons near the Observation Point area had flash flooding. Time is estimated.

Park rangers reported deep fast flowing water in Buckskin Gulch. The exact details regarding depth of water are not known. Three hour radar estimated precipitation across most of the warned area ranged from 1-2 inches.

Heavy rain over far northern Arizona and south-central Utah caused several spikes on the Paria River just before it joined the Colorado River upstream from The Grand Canyon. The water flow started to increase (from 4.98 feet) around 100 PM MST on August 13.  There were three crests in the flow: 6.24 feet at 500 PM, 704 feet at 800 PM MST on August 13, and 7.66 feet at 300 AM MST on August 14. The flow returned to near normal at around 1100 PM on August 14.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge recorded a peak flow of 1270 cfs when the flood wave passed through.
A park ranger reported water across Notom Road from Burrow Wash.
The Escalante River near Escalante gauge recorded a flow increase to 2300 cfs.

The Tooele County emergency manager reported a debris flow from the Jacob City Fire burn scar on county roads near Soldier Creek. Utah Department of Transportation officials also reported mud and rock across state Route 36 following the Flash Flood Warning.
Flash flooding was reported in the North Fork of the Virgin River. There were two injuries, with search and rescue going into the Narrows to recover those impacted.
Time is estimated. Hikers were stuck in Cottonwood Narrows off Cottonwood Road and were rescued.
Time is estimated. Hikers were stuck in Paria Canyon and had to be rescued due to elevated river flows.
Time is estimated. Hikers were reported stuck after flash flooding and required rescue in Bull Valley Gorge.

Time and location are estimated. A flood wave was observed at the Muddy Creek near Emery gauge, with a rise from around 34 cfs to around 700 cfs between 4:45 and 5 p.m. MDT. This flood wave would have then routed into the warned area between 5 and 6 p.m. MDT.
Time is estimated. A flash flood was reported at Catstair Canyon.
Time is estimated. A professor of atmospheric science at The University of Utah shared a video showing flash flooding on the East Fork of the Virgin River near Barracks Ranch River Crossing.
Time is estimated. St. George Police reported standing water on I-15 at Washington, milepost 10, that likely led to a rollover accident.
Highway 389 was flooded with water, mud, and debris.
The East Fork Virgin River near Glendale gauge showed two distinct flash flood waves. One at 8:45 p.m. MDT around 145 cfs and one at 10:45 p.m. MDT around 500 cfs.
The Paria River near Kanab gauge jumped from around 15 cfs to 2280 cfs in less than 30 minutes, corresponding to a rise of over 3 ft.
Pictures shared on social media show a flash flood moving through Ft Pearce Wash at Commerce Drive.
A park ranger reported flash flooding along Sulphur Creek just outside of Capitol Reef National Park.
Flooding of Nogales Wash in adjacent roadway.
Lots of water and dirt flooded Highway 95, with pockets of roadway washed out in the area.
The river guage on Carrizo Crreek showed a rapid 2 foot rise starting at 6 PM on August 22 and peaked at 1100 PM. The flow decreased and leveled out around 400 AM on Agust 23.
Water, mud, and debris covered Highway 95 near Goffs Road.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 66 to Main Street due to flooding.

Snow Canyon State Park reported flash flooding. Campers were displaced from the campsite, multiple waterfalls were observed, and employees had to wait on water to recede at a low water crossing as the flowing water was up to car door handles.

Zion National Park officials reported multiple waterfalls and high flows in multiple slot canyons in Zion Canyon. The North Fork Virgin River near Springdale gauge indicated a spike from 58 cfs to 251 cfs in five minutes, peaking at 264 cfs. Around this time, Zion National Park rangers reported elevated flows and waterfalls in canyons continued. The  East Fork Virgin near Glendale gauge peaked at 357 cfs, after starting at 47 cfs.

Heavy rain fell over the Catract Creek and Havasu Creek drainages.  Radar estimated  1-2 of rain fell early in the afternoon of August 22nd. Flash flooding occurred which resulted in many people being evacuated from the campgrounds on the creek, with helicopter evacuations for people stranded at the remote village of Supai.  At least 6 homes had flood damage in the Village of Supai. Over 100 campers were stranded in the campground. One person was washed away near the confluence with the Colorado River. Her body was recovered over 18 miles down the Colorado River three days later.
Flooding in Corona De Tucson area. Road closed at Sahuarita west of Wilmot due to flooding.  Road also closed at Davidson and Sahuarita due to flooding.
A trained spotter reported a large flash flood with water lapping the bottom of the U.S. Highway 89 bridge over the Paria River.
Considerable water running along low water crossing on N. Thornydale Rd. just south of W. Hardy Rd.

Heavy rain due to thunderstorms over the area resulted in 1.5 to 2 inch per hour rainfall rates with pea size hail mixed in. This resulted in flooding across downtown Moab with 2 feet of water flowing through downtown. Mill Creek saw a rise in water levels which runs through town with water cresting the roadway bridge. Water was also seen running over some driveways.
Considerable water running along low water crossing on N. Thornydale Rd. just south of W. Hardy Rd.
The Dirty Devil Above Poison Springs Near Hanksville gauge peaked at 1052 cfs, likely indicative of flash flooding through most of the slot canyons to the north.

Heavy runoff within the Baker Arroyo jumped out and flooded west and south, impacting U.S. Highway 64, Christ the King Catholic Church, the Central Consolidated School District and the Chat and Chew restaurant. At least two homes were destroyed or made uninhabitable. Damage cost is an estimate.

Heavy runoff within the Salt Creek Wash overtopped a bridge along Farm Road or B.I.A. 364 and nearby homes. Vegetation overgrowth exacerbated these flood waters. Yellow Arroyo also flooded out over property, homes and nearby roadways from the same round of thunderstorms. Damage cost is an estimate.

Locally heavy rainfall estimated to be near two inches per hour over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding along the Rio Ruidoso. Water over Bridge 2 on Main Road in Ruidoso was reported. Water over roadways was reported elsewhere in Ponderosa Heights, and near Alpine Village.

Locally heavy rainfall on the Salt burn scar resulted in flash flooding on secondary roads off U.S. Highway 70 and within the Cherokee Mobile Home Park. There were no reports of injuries, casualties or damage.
Brief heavy rainfall of 0.20 over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding and road closures over portions of Brady Canyon Road from South Oak Drive to Mechem Drive.

A fast moving storm developed over the South Fork burn scar, quickly moving east and producing 0.84 of rainfall over the McBride burn scar. Flash flooding was reported over roadways at University Dr. and Mechem Dr., Gavilan Canyon Rd. at several locations from Eagle Creek to east of Warrior Dr., and on Paradise Road. Debris was reported over the road at Prospect Rd. and Gavilan Canyon Road. While road closures were reported there were no reports of damage, injuries or casualties.
Intersection flooded and closed at East 3rd Street and Kilgore Avenue.
Eddy County Emergency Management reported three swift water rescues from the Dark Canyon Arroyo and multiple road closures. The cost of property damage is an estimation.

A video shared on social media showed a portion of Highway 2 south of Lake Arthur in southern Chaves County under six inches of water. Radar and gauge readings showed the likely period of flooding rains occurred in the morning from 8am to 9am MDT, while the reports were received later in the early afternoon when the heavier rain ended.

Rainfall amounts superseding 0.60 inches resulted in burn scar flash flooding off the South Fork and McBride burn scars. Water over the road at Paradise Canyon Dr. and Hull Road resulted in a closure of the roadway. Water and debris was also reported over Friedenbloom Drive.
Curb to curb street flooding in portions of Lovington.
Report shows Eagle Draw water crossings of roads are closed in Artesia.
A trained spotter reported flooding over the bridge crossing County Road A4A, just west of NM 94. Event time estimated based on radar reflectivity and time report occurred.

Law enforcement reported flooding on the north end of County Road A-1 in Sapello, NM. The Sapello Fire Department reported 2 foot deep water over the roadway. Event time estimated based on radar reflectivity and time report occurred.
Damage reported throughout Bandelier National Monument from significant flash flooding. All trails on the property were closed except for one within the official park boundaries.

Flash flooding with debris over Via Sedillo road in the town of Sedillo between NM Highway 333 and Camino Verde Road. Flow at Tijeras Arroyo in Sedillo was at least 6 inches deep based on high water mark. Time estimated based on radar reflectivity.
Highway 62 was flooded at White Feather Road.
Neighborhoods off Encelia Drive were flooded with roads impassable.
The rive guage on Granite Creek in Prescott measured over a 6.5 foot rise in one hour betweeb 400 PM and 500 PM. The creek slowly dropped to near normal levels by 500 AM early the next morning.
A big rig was stuck in mud on the Goffs Road offramp from Interstate 40.

Strong thunderstorms generated torrential rainfall across the Cuyama Valley, producing flash flooding across Highway 166 near Wasioja Road. Twenty three vehicles were stuck in the flood waters and debris on Highway 166.
Highway 127 was impassable due to being flooded with 1.5 feet of water plus rocks and debris. One car with four occupants was stuck and water was coming into the car.
Fast flowing from a nearby culvert washed out a dirt road a few miles south of Chacon, within the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. The location is estimated.

U.S. Highway 285 washed out at mile marker 137 and mile marker 151 due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms. Additionally, NMDOT closed U.S. Highway 285 from mile marker 135 to 138 due to flash flooding. Flash flooding resulted in vehicles being stuck in several inches of water and multiple areas of the highway becoming impassable. An accident also occurred on the highway about 14 miles north of Roswell due to hydroplaning.

Historically bad flash flooding across Roswell, reported by numerous emergency officials and the public. Thunderstorms training over Roswell dumped an all-time one-day rainfall record of 5.78 at the Roswell Airport with numerous other public weather stations across town ranging from 4 to 9 inches. Major flooding was reported across the city and nearby low-lying areas south and west of town. Numerous vehicles were submerged in over 4 feet of water while several more were swept away. The Roswell Daily Record reported that as many as 500 rescues were carried out over the weekend during and after the flooding. Estimates have as many as 400 homes and 200 businesses facing significant damage. The Roswell Convention Center was hosting a UFO festival when flood waters up to 5 feet entered the building. Attendees were being rescued from the rooftop. Roswell's Spring River Zoo also suffered extensive damage including the loss of one donkey. Flood damage was also sustained to Roswell's Landfill and Wastewater Treatment Plant. All roads entering the city were closed by State Police. The city lost 4 fire trucks and 7 police patrol cars with numerous city facilities damaged. There is one confirmed direct fatality from drowning and one indirect fatality from a heart attack reported and there may have been more as many vehicles were swept away along the Spring River drainage.
Two feet of water reported at the Burnt Well Guest Ranch where roadways near the ranch were flooded.

The NM Department of Transportation reported river flooding along the Rio Felix south of Roswell overtopping and damaging the U.S. Highway 285 bridge, and overtopping  the NM State Highway 2 bridge just north of Hagerman closing both bridges. Flooding from heavy rains and poor drainage also extended over much of Dexter just north of Hagerman. Damage is an estimate. A Flood Warning was issued and repeatedly extended until local reports of the water receding came from local Emergency Management.

Heavy rain resulted in multiple low water crossings along County Road A19A being flooded with several inches of water. Additionally, parts of San Pablo Creek and Tecolote Creek overflowed its banks in the Mineral Hill area.

U.S. Highway 285 and State Road 2 (Old Dexter Highway) in and around Dexter were impassible due to flood water moving across the respective roadways. Additionally, the neighborhood area near Ken Road west of U.S. Highway 285 was under 2 to 3 feet of water. Flooding also occurred in fields along U.S. Highway 285 at East Ottawa Road inundating the highway.
Water from Walnut Creek overflowed onto State Road 2, resulting in the closure of the roadway.

Video shows the water flowing over Bottomless Lakes Road north of Bottomless Lakes State Park. The road was closed due to being impassible from the floodwaters. Additionally, water was flowing across U.S. Highway 380 at mile marker 177 and at a rest stop next to the Mescalero Sands North Dune area.

A trained spotter reported bar ditches full of water from heavy rainfall, and State Highway 267 (Floyd Highway) had several places covered in 6 to 12 inches of water. However, the road still remained passable.
California Highway Patrol reported a bridge over the Merced River at Merced Falls was washed over.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and debris flows at the intersection of the Pacific Coast Highway and Kanan Dume Road. Numerous rocks and mud covered the intersection.

Heavy rain produced flash flood and mudflows across the westbound lanes of Highway 210 in the Santa Clarita Valley. Mud flowing across the highway resulted in numerous vehicles sliding across the highway.

Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain which generated flash flooding and debris flows across the intersection of Soledad Canyon Road and Aqua Dulce Canyon Road. Significant mud, rocks and debris were reported across the intersection.
Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 118 and Balboa Boulevard. Three lanes of the Highway 118 were flooded.
Heavy rain produced significant flash flooding and debris flows at the intersection of Lake Avenue and East Altadena Drive. Mud and debris flows resulted in the closure of all three northbound lanes.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 605 and Lower Azusa Road. The onramp was flooded with over two feet of water.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 10 and Caesar Chavez Boulevard. Multiple vehicles were disabled due to the flooding.

State route 330 is closed on February 14.  Just after 7 pm February 13, multiple vehicles were floating in a ravine full of water, mud and debris. A couple vehicles had occupants in them. Videos available. This is the line burn scar.
Three vehicles reported to have been stuck due to debris flow from flash flood.
State route 330 remains closed due to Thursday evening's flash flooding.
Four vehicles submerged in water up to the windows. Lifeguards rescued several. Rainfall rate as high as 1.1 inch in 1 hour.  La Jolla Village and Villa La Jolla Drive.
Strong thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the city of Los Angeles. At the intersection of Highway 101 and Campo de Cahuenga, significant road flooding was reported.

Delayed report. Swift water rescues. Vehicles in mud, debris and water. 6 persons  affected. Mud was half way up the side of one vehicle and drivers were trapped. 3  automated weather stations recorded 0.5 inches in 1 hour. Several mud slides reported.

Corrects time for previous flash flood report from 6 NNE of Mission Beach. 4 vehicles submerged in water up to the windows. Lifeguards rescued several. Rainfall rate as high as 1.1 inch in 1 hour. La Jolla Village and Villa La Jolla Drive.

Carroll Canyon Road and Pacific Heights Boulevard. 2 vehicles submerged in water, rescued by lifeguard boat. GW3482 weather station recorded 1.22 inches between 8 and 9 pm. Other stations recorded 1.07 and 1.16 inches. Miramar MCAS recorded 0.99 inches.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of Highway 118 and Interstate 405.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of Haskell Avenue and Chatsworth Street.
Flash flooding was reported along San Fernando Mission Boulevard in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles county.
State Highway 275 at mile marker 6 was closed due to flooding and standing water on the roadway.

U.S. Highway 84 was closed through Fort Sumner due to severe flooding over the highway. Numerous flooding impacts were reported in town including crop damage from flooded fields, residential road closures and damage due to water over roads, and irrigation ditches overflowing. The Fort Sumner high school football field was flooded due to the heavy rainfall.

At 2:53 AM MDT, a swift water rescue was conducted near a low-water crossing at Black River near Black River Road. A vehicle was reported to have been swept downstream. No injuries were reported. The time is radar estimated. Property damage is an estimation.

At 4:41 AM MDT, a swift water rescue was conducted at a low water crossing over the Black River along Higby Hole Road. No injuries were reported. The time is estimated using radar. The property damage is an estimation.
A social media post showed an oil field road closed due to flooding of a low-water crossing near the Pecos River in far southern Eddy County. The time was estimated from radar.
Heavy rainfall from severe thunderstorms resulted in 2.5 feet of water flowing over State Highway 20 from mile marker 37 to 41 leading to the closure of the highway.

The Cat Claw Canyon flood/river gauge reported a rapid rise from a no-flow 0 CFS state to a peak flow of 620 CFS. Flash flood area extrapolated downstream to account for likely continued propagation of flood wave.
Old Highway 91 was flooded just south of the AZ/UT state line.
Highway 62 was flooded at Iron Mountain Pump Plant Road.
A vehicle was submerged in flood waters.
State Route 238 near the intersection with South 99th Avenue in Mobile, AZ was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Intersection of State Route 85 and Maricopa Road in Gila Bend was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from the radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
There were multiple swift water rescues of people stuck in cars. One man was swept down a wash and drowned.
Highway 95 flooded just south of the CA/NV border.
Highway 95 was flooded just north of Highway 163.
The Willow Beach access road was closed due to flooding.
A web cam showed that the Antelope Wash flooded Mountain View Road and knocked down a fence.
Hancock Street was flooded.
Aztec Road was flooded, and one car was abandoned in the floodwaters.
The Archibald Wash flooded Pierce Ferry Road, stopping traffic as the road became impassable.
Stockton Hill Road was flooded and impassable.
Needles Highway was flooded with water and boulders just south of the CA/NV state line.
Highway 95 flooded at mile marker 70.
Camp Mohave Road was flooded.
Bullhead Parkway was flooded with water and large rocks.
There was flooding near the intersection of North Avenue and North Lane.
Boundary Cone Road was closed from Highway 95 to Mountain View Road.
County Route 1 and Oatman Highway were both closed due to flooding.
Roadway and street flooding in/around Tatum was reported by emergency management. The timing is approximated by radar. No damage was reported.

The San Miguel County Fire Chief shared delayed reports of flash flooding occurring in several locations of the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar from a thunderstorm. Water flowing over roadways was reported southwest of Sapello at County Roads A2 and A3 near Las Dispensas, County Roads A18 and A19 near Mineral Hill, and over Cunningham Rd. and El Llano Rd. crossing Gallinas Peak between Montezuma and Las Vegas.

Photos taken along Bartlett Dam Rd show evidence of flash flooding over the road in multiple spots, including at the Camp Creek crossing, with many small boulders, sediment, and other debris left over in the road. No injuries were reported.
City officials reported flash flooding near Lomas Blvd. and Central Ave. with several roadways in the area under high water.

Flash flooding in the Albuquerque arroyo channel system resulted in a fatality. The body was first spotted in the Hahn Arroyo near Pennsylvania Ave. in northeast Albuquerque before the deceased body was retrieved in the arroyo washout pond at the end of the North Diversion Channel near 4th Street and Edith Blvd. in the North Valley.
Numerous reports of water, debris, rocks, and mud over roadways, prompting closures.  Several portions of NM 170, La Plata Highway, and N 36, Upper Fruitland Highway, were impacted.
Water and debris covered Highway 93 between Lincoln County mile markers 2 and 4, closing the highway.
Water and debris covered Highway 93 between Clark County mile markers 80 and 81, closing the highway.
Valley of Fire Highway was flooded and closed near the I-15 exit.
Several roads were flooded, and at least five cars were stuck in the water.
The shoulder of Highway 62 was washed out.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in 1 foot of standing water around homes along U.S. 64 in Kirtland. Another home had water entering the garage. Up to 3 inches of water was observed running across U.S. 64 near the Coolidge Arroyo along with a large area of flood waters backs up from a nearby drainage along U.S. 64 just west of County Road 6500.

Tribal officials from the Havasupai Reservation reported that trails were flooded and impassable along Havasu Creek causing hikers to be stranded.  All hikers were later accounted for, no injuries or fatalities.  Some structures in the village of Supai were also impacted.
Antares Road was closed from mile marker 1 to Pierce Ferry Road due to flooding in numerous locations.
Goffs Road was flooded and closed.
Needles Highway was flooded at Budweiser Road and between Park Road and Aha Macav Parkway.
A USGS Stream Gage indicated a rise of over 6 feet in Kanab Creek due to heavy rain upstream.
Kelbaker Road was flooded with water, debris, and large rocks.
Approximately two feet of water flowed through the intersection of Highways 190 and 127, trapping the occupants of one vehicle.
Video showed Fish Creek Wash experienced flooding, making a low water crossing along Split Mountain Road impassable. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
The intersection of 4th Street and California Avenue in Parker was closed due to flooding. No damages nor injuries were reported.
The USGS Escalante River gauge (ESCU1) spiked to 2491 cfs as the flood wave moved through.
Flowing water with debris over State Highway 47. Peak depth at around half a foot to a foot. The flash flooding resulted in significant backup of traffic on the highway.
Media reported that four hikers were rescued on the Bighorn Canyon Trail after being stranded due to flash flooding along Harris Wash. Video also showed flash flooding of the normally dry wash.

Video shared on social media by local media showed severe flash flooding and flowing water filled with debris across a property at Calle De Baca and Highway 116 in southwest Belen. A large work trailer was swept away in the flood waters. The flash flooding plugged one culvert and wiped out a second culvert. Additionally, the heavy rainfall resulted in overflowing retention ponds resulting in localized flooding for other nearby residents.

Flash flooding was reported along Taylor Canyon on the afternoon of June 4h. This flooding eroded a six food embankment along White Rim Road in Canyonlands National Park, and carried sediment all the way to the Green River. Additionally, several washes along Taylor Canyon Road ran and washed out sections of Taylor Canyon Road. No other damages, and no injuries or fatalities, were received.
Minor flash flooding was observed in Spring Canyon at the confluence with the Fremont River. Time is estimated from radar.
Highway 93 was flooded between Clark County mile markers 70 and 80.

A Snow Canyon State Park employee reported damage to West Canyon Road due to flooding. A tent was also flooded, forcing a camper to sleep in their vehicle. Rainfall estimates in this vicinity indicated between .70 and .90 inches of rain had fallen in around 90 minutes. Time is estimated by radar.
Park rangers reported a flash flood in Sulphur Creek at Capitol Reef National Park.
A visitor to the Grand Staircase Escalante visitor center reported flash flooding in Big Horn Canyon.
Trained spotter reported 4 to 6 inches of rushing water over his driveway on his ranch property several miles north of U.S. 56/412 in far western Union County.
Large accumulations of hail and rainfall overflowed drainages and flooded parts of the interstate and the nearby service roads along I-40 at Bowlins Flying C Ranch.
Large accumulations of hail covering areas along I-40 combined with heavy rainfall resulted in rushing water over the roadways and drainages to overflow their banks.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the South Fork and Blue 2 burn scar resulted in flash flooding and debris flows of 6 to 8 inches on North Loop, Main Road, and Brady Canyon Road in the Upper Canyon area just west of downtown Ruidoso. Some flowing water and debris flow was also observed on Ski Run Road and Highway 48 near the Alto Reservoir.
Flash flooding was reported out of Carlsbad Caverns National Park. The park's staff evacuated the area. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar. No damages were reported.

Heavy rain on the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding and flowing water across Ebarb Dr. from Perk Canyon along with Brady Canyon Rd. and Ponderosa Dr. The flash flooding continued downstream with a dumpster floating down Rio St. and Grindstone Canyon Rd. and flowing water closing Johnson & Main Rd. Large debris was reported at the 300 block of Cedar Creek. Water was also observed reaching the bridge at Two Rivers. Finally, flooding was observed at the Riverside RV Park near Gavilan Canyon Rd. and Sudderth Dr.
Multiple cars and a fire truck stuck in deep water. Damage is unknown.

Flash flooding off the Salt burn scar coming out of Bear Canyon. Swift water rescues  conducted at the Cherokee Mobile Home Park, the Elevate Hotel, and for three vehicles at the Otero Federal Credit Union. Flash flooding reported at the Twin Spruce RV park, U.S. Highway 70 and Sudderth Dr. and U.S. Highway 70 and mile mark 261 closed due to burn scar flash flooding. Damage is an estimate based on vehicles rescues. No injuries or fatalities reported.
Flood waters reported over NM129 just north of I-40 at the Newkirk Gas Station.
Workers on the White Sands Missile Range reported Flash Flooding near the intersection of Range Road Route 7 and 10.
The Orogrande Gate on the White Sands Missile Range received 4.62 of rain and caused some portions of the road from Highway 54 to get flooded.
Flash flooding of the normally dry Fourmile Draw with 4 to 5 feet of water over North Lake Road. Duration is an estimation.
Highway 185 was reported to be impassable between mile markers 25 and 30.
Flooded crop fields and water over County Road 5.
Flash flooding off the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar along NM 518 has closed the highway between mile markers 37 and 38.
Debris and water washouts along I-25 which was shut down for a period of time at mile marker 190. This required a bulldozer to clear the debris the following day.
The public reported flooding off the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar along the Rio la Casa above Cleveland, NM.
Flood waters flowing over the roadway from nearby arroyo along Quail Trail near Maple  Road.
Another round of storms in the day brought flash flooding to areas of Highway 185 about 5 miles south-southeast of Rincon with several low water crossings impassable.
White Sands Missile Range personnel reported flooding around the intersection of Range Route 6 and 9 with roads impassable in places.

Burn scar flash flooding off the South Fork and Salt burn scars that ran along the Rio Ruidoso from the Upper Canyon down to Hollywood. High water was reported over multiple roadways along the Rio Ruidoso, notably along Ebarb Dr. and Johnson Rd., Mechem Dr., Main Bridge 2, N. Grindstone Canyon Rd., Country Club Dr., Gavilan Canyon Rd., Eagle Dr. Bridge, Sudderth Drive. The McDaniel Bridge in the Upper Canyon area, a small water crossing, was destroyed. Damage is an estimate based on washed out culverts and the destroyed McDaniel Bridge.
Emergency management reports the closure of the bridge at Main Rd. and Fox Drive over the Rio Ruidoso from burn scar flash flooding off the South Fork burn scar.
Water from heavy rainfall was flowing over Highway 154 west of Rincon.
A trained spotter sent video and photos of Yuma Wash flooding over N. Reed Road between W Road 4.5 N and W Road 5 N.
A flood wave (flash flooding) was reported in Sulphur Creek at the Capitol Reef National Park western Boundary. Approximately 0.25 to 0.50 inches of rain fell to create the flood wave.
Runoff out of Allie Canyon flowed across Highway 35 to a depth of 1.5 feet.
Burn scar flash flooding off the Salt burn scar produced high water flows and culvert issues diverting water into the Cherokee Mobile home park that ran right up to people's homes.
A county official reported a 5 foot rise in 45 minutes at the Rio de Flag Coconino County ALERT gauge located near the Flagstaff Mall.
Yavapai County Sheriff's Office reported a bridge in Spring Valley was impassable with water flowing over the road.  A car was also stranded on the bridge.
An estimated 3 ft of water moved across low water crossing on Forest Service 143 Rd.
A USGS stream gauge on the Little Colorado River near Woodruff reported a 6.3 foot rise  in one hour from near nearby thunderstorms  producing heavy rainfall.
Public reported, via social media, a video of flash flooding in Big Bug Creek across a low water crossing.
Public sent via social media a video of a flash flood along Big  Bug Creek. The person posting the video said it was the highest flow since 2021.
A Yavapai County river gauge on the Agua Fria River at Kelton Ranch reported a 6.3 foot  rise in 15 minutes. Peak flow was 9,515 cubic feet per second.
A USGS river gauge on the Agua Fria River at Cordes Lakes reported at 5.9 foot rise in 45  minutes from thunderstorms upstream along Big Bug Creek.
Video and photos show 2 to 4 feet of murky floodwater rapidly moving through Pinal Creek, with Beer Tree Crossing impassable. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Social media photo showed a flooded low water crossing along AZ-72, just northwest of McVay Road, with around 6-12 inches of flowing water over the road. Timing estimated from radar. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Over four inches of rain fell east of Highway 180 and flowed east, overtopping the highway between mileposts 150 and 152.  Flooding caused erosion of the eastern half of the highway.

Heavy rainfall over the Albuquerque metro area produced dangerous fast flows on the area arroyo system. Two swift water rescues were performed in the diversion channel along I-40 and the Snow Heights neighborhood. Additionally, a man was trapped and swept up among floodwaters in an arroyo near Carlisle and Menaul Boulevard. Crews searched the North Diversion Channel and nearby areas for at least an hour before deploying an airboat in a washout area at Roy Avenue and Fourth Street. The man was not found in the washout area. The individual is assumed to have been deceased.

Heavy rain exceeding 2 inches caused thick dirt and debris runoffs over roadways across western Rio Rancho which caused at least one road closure and debris removal efforts. During debris removal efforts around sunrise, road crews located a deceased male near the intersection of Northern Blvd. and Calor Rd. NW.
A video from a KOB viewer on social media showed large areas of water inundating farmland and nearby properties around El Cerro. Time and location are estimated.
Overnight flood waters inundated a residence in Las Nutrias along NM 304. Flood waters also closed NM 304 at Las Nutrias Road, washing dirt onto the highway requiring debris removal later that day.
A USGS stream gauge reported a rise of 5.01 feet on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt.

Heavy rainfall due to thunderstorm activity caused flash flooding on 1st street from River Rd to Grant Rd. Swift water was crossing roads at several junctions. A rainfall gauge in the area had 1.01 inches of rainfall in the span of 1 hour.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall causing South Old Nogales Highway to close from  Flato Wash to Lumber Road. A nearby rain gauge had 1.14 inches of rainfall in 1 hour.

Heavy rainfall due to a slow moving thunderstorm produced an estimated 0.5-1.0 inch of rainfall causing running washes and rivers. A swift water rescue took place at prince and  river park drive with no injuries to the 4 people and dog saved from a car.

Public reported a low water crossing at N. Contessa Way flooded and impassible with several feet of flowing water. Radar estimated 1.25-1.75  inches occurred in 30 minutes over the Dry  Beaver Creek Basin just north of McGuireville.

Slow moving thunderstorms formed over Benson, AZ that produced heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding. Over the 2 hours that rainfall fell, two rainfall gauges reported 1.10-1.25 inches of rainfall. Drivers had to turn around due to flooding over roadways that are impassible with multiple cars pulling over to side of road due to the heavy rainfall.

Slow moving thunderstorms formed over Benson, AZ that produced heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding. Over the 2 hours that rainfall fell, two rainfall gauges reported 1.10-1.25 inches of rainfall. A section of Pomerene Road had roadway flooding.

Heavy rain from slow moving storms on the South Fork and McBride burn scars resulted in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars. Several roads along and crossing the Rio Ruidoso were closed due to the resultant flash flooding and debris flow in the river. This included Mechem Drive, Ebarb Drive at Main Road and West Redwood Road, Fern Trail at Terrance and Grindstone, Eagle Bridge on Eagle Road, Gavilan Bridge on Gavilan Canyon Road in Hollywood, Cree Meadows at Country Club and Heath, Robin Road, Hull Road, and Paradise Canyon Road. The floodwaters and debris flow washed away a vehicle on Porr Drive. No information was known on if any occupants were in the vehicle at the time. Another vehicle was stuck in flood waters at Apache Hills Drive and Grant Drive. Finally, 2 to 3 inches of water entered a home on Ash Drive.

Heavy rain on the South Fork burn scar from slow moving thunderstorms during the early afternoon hours resulted in another round of flash flooding across roads and neighborhoods on and downstream of the burn scar. This resulted in Main Road at bridge 2 to become impassable, and the closure of Ebarb Drive and Porr Drive due to 3-6 inches of flowing water over the road. Additionally, the runoff and debris flow continued downstream on the Rio Ruidoso with the river overtopping the bridge at Gavilan Canyon Road just north of Sudderth Drive in Hollywood.

Another round of thunderstorms on the South Fork and McBride burn scars resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the burn during the evening hours. Water and debris were observed flowing near Flume Canyon Drive, Mecham and White Mountain Drive, Warren Tucker and White Mountain Drive, and on Gavilan Canyon Road at Eagle Creek Road and between Janet and Edwards Drive.
White Sands employees reported water running over Baylor Canyon Road south of Organ.  There was also deep water over NASA Rd about 4 miles north of Organ.

Heavy rain from slow moving severe thunderstorms resulted in severe flash flooding in the East Mountain communities of Cedar Crest, Tijeras and Sedillo. A 300 pound woodchipper was carried downstream on the normally dry Arroyo de San Antonio until becoming lodged in a tree. Video taken by a viewer in Tijeras and shared by a broadcast meteorologist shows Tijeras Arroyo flowing out of banks. A small tree was also moving downstream in the arroyo. Spotters also observed flood waters flowing down hillsides around Tijeras, Tablazon, and Zuzax with hail, rocks, mud, and debris covering parts of SR-333. Finally, low water crossings were completely flooded on secondary roads just east and south of the Zuzax exit at I-40.
Flash flooding was reported with 6 inches of water coming out of Soldier Canyon onto Highway 70 and into Mescalero.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the South Fork burn scar resulted in some minor water rises in the Rio Ruidoso with some water coming off the Upper Canyon and putting debris over Main Road by main bridge 2. Some debris on Cedar Creek Drive at Musket Ball Drive and near Mechem Drive resulted in a brief closure of the road to allow for crews to clean up the roadway.
Flash flooding was reported on Tularosa Creek above Bridal Falls.  Debris-laden flow flooded backyards.  Crosscreek Road low water crossing dangerously flooded.
A trained spotter reported flash flooding across roadway. With a nearby measured rainfall of 1.18 inches in 30 minutes.

Heavy rainfall caused flash flooding across Overton Rd due to water moving through the Canada del Oro Wash. Overton Rd remained closed from La Cholla Blvd to La Canada Drive into the following day with an unknown opening time.
ADOT reported State Route 87 closed due to flooding of an underpass at milepost 342 in Winslow.
A USGS stream gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek (TNRA3) reported a 2 foot rise after heavy rainfall upstream earlier in the morning.
Heavy rain over the South Fork burn scar resulted in floodwaters overtopping Main Road Bridge 2. A swiftwater rescue was also conducted at Sleepy Hollow Bridge.
Debris flow off of the Trout Fire was flowing down Pictograph Canyon across Highway 35. The road was impassable.  Radar indicated 1.5 to 2 inches of rainfall above the road.
The USGS stream gauge on Cataract Creek below Heather Wash measured a 2.8 foot rise in one hour due to upstream heavy rainfall.
Public reported 2 feet of water in Webber Creek with debris from the West Fire scar after heavy rain fell on the scar.
Public reported a minor debris flow in the gully crossing Control Road (FS 64) after heavy rain fell on the West Fire scar.
Flooding was reported via AZ511.com on the I-17 Southbound lanes near Stoneman Lake Rd.
Flash Flooding made Trigg Road impassable near the confluence of Conejo and Vallentine  Creeks with a concrete culvert becoming inundated and damaged. Location is  approximate.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars near Ruidoso produced flash flooding. Water and debris overflowed U.S. Highway 70 at Sudderth Dr. and Ruidoso Downs, White Mountain Dr., Gavilan Canyon Rd. from Alto Cafe to Meander, and Alpine Village Road. The Cherokee Mobile Home village was evacuated with swiftwater rescues performed there, and at Big-O Tires and on Friedenbloom Drive. Damage is an estimate.
Heavy rains over the Laguna burn scar produced water and debris over a dirt road making it impassable.
Zion NP rangers reported flash flooding of Keyhole slot canyon along with other waterfalls coming developing along other eastern park slot canyons. Time is estimated.

Emergency manager reported that a campground near Pine Valley Reservoir was flooding with clogged drains and water running down the road. At 4:00 pm MST, adjusted USGS Gauge on the Santa Clara near Pine Valley showed around a 235 cfs flood wave.
High water in Kanarra Falls required several hikers to be rescued. Time is estimated  based on radar.

The USGS Paria River Gauge near Kanab reported a double peak in streamflow to around 1200 CFS on the evening of July 17th. The initial rise in flow was likely associated with storms earlier in the day in the upper Paria River Basin.
Broadcast media report of a dry wash running across road approximately 4 miles north of Panguitch.
Flash flooding was observed on the ESCU1 gauge with a sharp rise from a zero-flow state to a peak of 110 CFS.
Public reported significant rises on La Verkin Creek. Time and location estimated.
Rocks and debris a few inches deep washed over Morning Star Mine Road.
