Heavy rain over the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar produced high flow in an arroyo feeding into Manuelitas Creek. This overflowed banks and splashed over the bridge on County Road A4A.
A USGS river gauge on the Paria River near the confluence with the Colorado River (PLFA3) measured a 3.3 foot rise.
A guide for the Paria River reported a large flood wave travelling down the Paria River with the magnitude estimated to be around 3800 CFS.
Low water crossings were flowing along New Mexico 35 south of Camp Thunderbird.  NMDOT crews were out to clean up debris across the road.

Mescal Canyon low water crossing at Turtleback Ave was flooded and too dangerous to cross.  Discharge from the Mescal Canyon caused a 0.65 foot backwater spike on the Rio Grande gauge below Elephant Butte Dam, upstream of Mescal Canyon.  Water levels on the Rio Grande came close to riverside porches in Truth or Consequences but no damage.
Zion NP ranger reported numerous waterfalls around the park that were the result of heavy rain.
A trained spotter reported flooded streets with fast flowing water going over curbs in the town of Magdelena.

Heavy rain from slow moving thunderstorms resulted in mud and rockslides onto the Cochiti Golf Course and across the road at the entrance of the course.  Additionally, the golf cart barn got an inch or so of water in it. Property damage is an estimate.
A trained spotter reported 3 feet of water moved through a narrow wash that crosses  South Miller Lane near Highway 80 in St  David AZ.
Heavy rainfall closed from North of Wiley Road on Calle Riconado to South Wentworth Road due to flooding.  Flooding occurred within the the Missile Tank Basin of Pima County.
Cochise County Public Health official reported extensive roadway flooding along Courtland Road in Elfrida, AZ.
Cochise County Sherriff reported flash flooding along East Madera Road in Sierra  Vista resulting in a road closure. The road reopened at 9am on July 23rd.
Cochise County Official reported that Ghost Town Trail Road closed temporarily due to extensive flooding damage between  mile post 2.8 and 13.

Significant flash flooding was reported along Interstate 10 which was forced to be closed between Mesquite south through Vado.  Video showed turbulent water running over the Frontage Road along I-10 near Vado.  Other areas that had significant flooding included High Valley Road near the Vado Quarry, areas in the vicinity of Las Palmeras Road and Jamaica Lane in Berino as well as near Cebolla Lane flooding the nearby neighborhood.
Pima County DOT closed Wentworth Rd north of Speedway due to flash flooding of the Tanque Verde Wash between Speedway and Redington Rd. The road was closed from 604pm to 743pm.

Cochise County Sherriff reported flash flooding along North Moson Road resulting in  the entire road being closed between Charleston Road and Highway 90 in Sierra  Vista. Photo showed at least a foot of fast  moving water flowing over the roadway.
Cochise County reported Kings Highway closed at milepost 5.1 due to flooding. Unknown reopen time.
Cochise County reported Kings Highway closed at milepost 5.1 due to flooding. Unknown reopen time.

Flash flooding started near Bent with arroyo flooding on Mauer Drive.  An arroyo bank was cut with edge of embankment moved 14 feet closer to a home. There was also culvert and road damage along Round Mountain Road.  Further west, flash flooding was noted along Tularosa Creek above Bridal Falls. Flooding extended into into a backyard and crawl space of a house with an artificial pond washed out about 4 miles east of Tularosa.

A slow-moving thunderstorm dropped an estimated 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in 20 minutes in the North Valley and Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood of Albuquerque. This resulted in flash flooding on the eastbound lanes of Paseo Del Norte at Rio Grande Blvd and on the westbound frontage road of Paseo Del Norte at Jefferson Street. Additionally, a post on social media reported flood waters entering a business on 4th Street in the Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood. Finally, a video on social media showed floodwaters in the individual's residence and the family sweeping out the floodwaters from the front entrance of the residence. Property damage cost for the business on 4th street and the residence in the North Valley neighborhood is an estimate.

Heavy rainfall fell over the South Fork burn scar near Ruidoso, with on gage measuring 2.14 inches. Flash flooding produced water over roadways and bridges along Cedar Creek at Mechem Drive, Cree Meadows Bridge and Drive, Innsbrook Drive, Starlite Road, White Mountain Drive, Gavilan Canyon Road, Warren Tucker Drive, Reese Drive, Musketball Drive, and Geneva Road. Three swift water rescues were conducted off Gunpowder Trail and Spring Canyon Road. A video was shared of what appears to be a mobile home washed away down Cedar Creek along Paradise Canyon Drive. The Rio Ruidoso crested to 12.68 feet in minor flood stage at 12:40pm MST, reaching out of its banks in numerous locations. Flash flooding impacted as far down Rio Ruidoso as the Ruidoso Downs Race Track.
Indian Road 10 was closed due to flash flooding and necessary evacuations.
A half inch to 1 inch of rain fell on the Salt Burn Scar and produced flash flooding out of Bear Canyon onto Highway 70.
Flash flooding was observed off the Salt burn scar out of Bear Canyon to areas near Elk Lodge along U.S. Highway 70.
Nevada DOT Reno reported flooding on Rock  Blvd which prompted the closure of the road  near I-80.

Nevada State Police reported flooding on I-80 between Wells Ave and Virginia St  prompting the closure of I-80 westbound lanes. Also, University of Nevada Reno reported flooding of buildings on campus and there was flooding reported throughout J Casino.
A washed-out road stranded some personnel just west of Phillips Hill mesonet site (WSM30). It is unclear if folks were stranded all night or at the exact location of wash out.
The Mescalero EM reported burn scar flooding from the Seven Springs fire.
Range Road on the White Sands Missile Range was washed out from flooding.  Time is approximate.

Law enforcement reported water up to 2 feet deep crossing in numerous areas on Highways 9 and 11 between Columbus and about 6 miles east of Columbus. A weather station at Pancho Villa State Park reported 1.49 inches of rain with the radar indicating heavier rains fell just south and east of this location.
Flash flooding over U.S. Highway 82 near Jay Powell Ranch with high flows out of banks along the Rio Penasco.
Emergency Management reported 6 inches of moving water over U.S. Highway 54 south of Carrizozo.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars in and around Ruidoso resulted in burn scar flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported along multiple portions of Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso, including at Mechem Dr., Brady and Porr Roads, Country Club Road, Robin Road and River Trail, a bridge at Eagle Road, Gavilan Canyon Road, and along U.S. Highway 70 in Hollywood. Spring Canyon Road was washed out and made impassable. Fast moving water was reported over all roads in the Cherokee Village Mobile Home park where a confirmed gas leak was reported alongside a successful swift water rescue of an adult woman. An unknown number of other swift water rescues were conducted in Hollywood. Flash flooding overtopped the bridge on the access road to the Ruidoso Downs racetrack, and flooded the horse tunnel and Spaghetti Flats north and east of the racetrack. Damage is an estimate.
The public reported high water flowing out of Bear Canyon and flooding of the Cherokee Mobile Village and along US 70 going into Ruidoso Downs.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars resulted in burn scar flash flooding in the Ruidoso area, including near schools. Flash flooding was reported in multiple areas along roads and highways including White Mountain Dr., Hull Rd., Mechem Dr., Paradise Canyon Dr. just north of Sudderth Dr., Perk Canyon Dr., and along Main Road. The access road to the Ruidoso Downs racetrack was once again overtopped. The Fire Department assisted in a swift water rescue of an occupied vehicle being pushed by flood waters. Damage is an estimate, and there are no reports of injuries or fatalities.
The Mescalero Emergency Manager reported heavy flows coming out of Bear Canyon towards US 70 due to heavy rain on the Salt Burn scar.
Heavy rains resulted in high water levels along the Rio Bonito and along Sandesta Dr., entering homes in the area. Damage is an estimate.
Report of 20-24 inches of standing water at HWY 286 near MM 23.
Video on social media showed flash flooding occurring over roadway. A nearby rain gauge  measured 0.27 inches of rainfall.
The Dona Ana Emergency Manager reported fast flowing water at Mercantil and Sentenario Streets as well as just south of this point at Conejo Street.
The Dona Ana Office of Emergency Management reported flooding in Rincon.
A water rescue was reported at Dripping Springs Road and Camino Bonito.
Deputy City Manager reported a collapsed sidewalk at the intersection of Corte de Princesa and Camino Consuela along the Arroyo de los Pinos in Sante Fe. Damage is an estimate.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in fast moving water flowing over U.S Highway 380 in Lincoln.
A trained spotter and the county emergency manager reported water flowing over several roadways, including NM Highway 21 along with hail accumulating on the roads near Miami.
Heavy rain from severe thunderstorms resulted in five inches of water on 8th Street near Eddy Avenue and 6 inches of water on Park Lake Drive in Santa Rosa, NM.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms on the Salt burn scar resulted in flash flooding near U.S. Highway 70 and Dunagan Trail.

Cochise County official reported vehicle was stuck in flowing water at mile post 5 along  Davis Rd east of Tombstone that closed for approximately 9 hours. A nearby rain gauge had 0.12 inches of rainfall.
A USGS stream gage on Jacks Canyon Creek (JCCA3) measured a 2.5 foot rise from  heavy rain upstream.  The rain happened on Sunday afternoon.
Flooded roadways around 18th Street and Kilgore Avenue from heavy rainfall.
Six inches of flowing water estimated on road near the area of Cave Creek Road and Union Hills Drive in North Phoenix. No damages nor injuries were reported.
Video shows fast flowing water on the roadway, likely at least 6 inches, in the area of Bell Road and 56th Street in Scottsdale. Timing estimated from radar.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge located along East Fork Cave Creek near 7th Avenue showed water levels rising above the alarm stage of 3 feet likely flooding 7th avenue just downstream. Water levels peaked at 3.90 feet at around 12 AM MST before gradually rising below alarm stage at around 1:23 AM MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Gauge measured water levels along Indian Bend Wash near Shea Blvd briefly rising above the alarm stage of 2 feet, likely flooding the greenbelt and low-water crossings downstream. No damages or injuries were reported.
I-8 near State Route 85 in Gila Bend closed due to all lanes being blocked due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Washes flowing across roadway along State Route 72 southeast of Bouse. No damages or injuries reported.

Video showed water from curb to curb and rushing with an estimated 6 inches of moving water along Mabel St from 2nd to 3rd Ave. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.26 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
Video on social media shows an estimated 3 inches of water at intersection of Tyndall Rd and 1st Ave. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.26 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
Water up past curbs, estimated 6 inches of water, on Tucson Boulevard south of Grant Road. A nearby rain gauge reported 0.29 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
The Dona Ana County Emergency Manager and Flood Commission reported significant water flow in the Rincon Arroyo at Interstate 25.
Water flowed across Visnaga Street due to heavy rainfall.
A USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt (AFHA3) recorded a rise of 5.91 feet.
Heavy rainfall from low moving thunderstorms washed-out Obsidian and Juniper Roads near State Highway 4 and 126.

Heavy rainfall from a thunderstorm falling over steep terrain in Nephi Canyon caused flooding and an associated closure of SR-132 at mile marker 35. A railroad weather station located near the top of the adjacent canyon recorded 0.59 inches of rain in 10 minutes and 0.9 inches of rain in 30 minutes. Time and location are estimated.
Antelope Canyon Tribal Park Service sent photos of water flowing through Antelope Canyon.  High water marks indicated water depth of 1 to 2 feet prior to entering Antelope Canyon.  Time is estimated.
Flooding over portions of I-80 near USA  Parkway reported by a member of the public  via social media. The nearest mesonet station recorded 1.41 inches of rain.
Video showed flooding along Highway 98 near Drew Road. Highway 98 was closed from  Imperial Highway to Brockman Road due to the flooding. Timing estimated from radar.
Highway 62 was flooded at White Feather Road, Adobe Road, and Encelia Road, where multiple vehicles were trapped in fast moving water. Other secondary roads were also flooded.

Significant flash flooding occurred along Highway 86 near Highway 78, leaving numerous motorists stranded on the flooded roadway. According to reports, up to 200 motorists were left stranded along Highway 86, with videos showing floodwaters that appeared to be around 3 to 5 feet deep over the roadway. Videos and images showed vehicles floating on the roadway with several vehicles almost completely submerged by the floodwaters. Multiple motorists were left stranded on top of their vehicles before being rescued. Portions of the roadway were also washed out by the flooding. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Ogilby Road between I-8 and Highway 78 was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar.
A portion of Split Mountain Road at Fish Creek Wash was washed out due to flooding. Time estimated based on radar.

Flash flooding was reported along Park Boulevard near the north entrance of Joshua Tree National Park. Flooding across the roadway resulted in boulders around 1 to 2 feet in diameter being swept into the roadway.
Tohono Oodham Nation Dispatch reported water flooding the San Manual Road from mile post 1 to 24.
Araby Road near I-8 was closed due to flash flooding. Timing was estimated from radar.
Highway 178 was flooded at Pinnacle Road.
Social media video of cars stuck in flooded waters on frontage road along Interstate-10  north of Red Rock. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.83 inches of rainfall fell in 24 hours.
Flash flooding was reported in Zion Canyon with muddy debris across the road. The East  Fork of the Virgin River rose approximately 1.5 feet.
Report of 1.90 inches of rain within an hour, resulting in flash flooding in the Tacna area. Multiple washes were reported flowing across Old Highway 80.
County 11th Street between Avenue 28 E and Avenue 27 E was closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar.
Mountain View Avenue between Dome Street and Avenue 29 E closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar.
Highway 190 was flooded with large flows of water and debris between Cow Creek Road and Salt Creek Road.

A USGS stream gauge on Granite Creek (GCRA3) measured a 4.6 foot rise in 30 minutes.  A CoCoRaHS observer upstream of the gauge confirmed water nearing a business parking lot in downtown Prescott.  The observer measured 2.05 inches of rain.
Zion National Park reported flash flooding in the main canyon, including Clear Creek.

Slow moving thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and rushing water across NM Highway 117 near El Malpais National Monument. The highway was temporarily closed during this time until flood waters fully receded.

Minor debris and roadway flooding on South Rock Blvd along both directions near Hymer Ave in Sparks. Additional flooding was reported throughout the city of Sparks, with rainfall estimations up to 1.15 inches.
The USGS river gauge on the Verde River below Camp Verde (VCVA3) recorded a 4 foot rise (1,650 cfs) in an hour due to heavy rainfall upstream.
Highway 247 was closed south of Barstow due to large amounts of water, debris, and rocks over the road.
SR-439 in both directions closed near Portofino Drive due to flooding. All lanes are blocked.
Gauge data from Lees Ferry in Arizona suggests a flash flood on the Paria River. Time is estimated based on radar and gauge data.
National Trails Highway at Nebo Street was blocked by significant water and debris flow.
Flash flooding was reported along a wash near US-89 milepost 9.
Water and mud along Interstate 80 near Floriston.

Nevada Department of Transportation reported flash flooding with mud and debris on US-50 near Bryce Road. Additionally, minor debris and flooding was reported on US-50 near US-95 ALT near Silver Springs.
Buckhorn Draw Road was washed out, with a car on road washed a quarter mile down the road. Four people were rescued due to flash flooding.
The USGS river gauge on the Agua Fria River near Cordes Lakes (AFMA3) reported a 2 foot rise (117 cfs) in 15 minutes due to heavy rainfall along Big Bug Creek.
Minor debris and roadway flooding along SR-359 in both directions near Spanish Springs road.

At approximately 5:20 PM MDT, heavy rain in the area north of Mexican Hat, UT, resulting in failed culverts and flash flooding. On State Highway 163, the failed culverts and and heavy rain resulted in water over the road, making them impassable until the water receded. Additionally, heavy rain in this region led to water over the road on County Highway 261, in an area of steep switchbacks. While no damage was reported, these roads did become impassable and had to be cleared in the hours after the water receded. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
A Yavapai County ALERT gauge on the Agua Fria River at Kelton Ranch reported a 2.7 foot  rise in 15 minutes from heavy rainfall in Big Bug Creek.
A USGS stream gauge at Lees Ferry (PLFA3) measured a 1.2 foot rise on the Paria River.  Water would likely have been higher upstream closer to the heavier rainfall.  Time estimated by radar.
Flash flooding was reported along Wahweap Creek near Big Water.

Repeated rounds of thunderstorms resulted in flash Flooding along NM Highway 518 just north of Cleveland. A trained spotter observed at least 8 places where small creeks along the Rio Mora were exceeding banks and flooding the highway. Flash flooding also resulted in extreme damage to NM Highway 434. The highway was closed for emergency repairs for 2 to 3 days and was reopened a few days later after installing five corrugated metal pipes and restoring the roadway with a temporary dirt surface.
Flooding was reported throughout Incline Village, with multiple reports of closed roads. Upwards of 2.22 inches of rain had fallen over the area.

Forest Service officials report flooding with ash laden water through House Rock Wash along Buffalo Ranch Road (Forest Road 8910).  The road was impassable and blocked access for BAER team members performing work in the area.  The White Sage burn scar was upstream from this location.
SR-447 closed from Church Street in Nixon to the Pershing Washoe County line.
Three feet of water with mud and rocks covered the intersection of Highways 127 and 190.
A gauge on the San Rafael River recorded a flood wave around 700 cfs.
The East Fork of the Virgin River recorded a flood wave of 510 cfs. A flash flood of 1290 cfs was recorded on the North Fork of the Virgin River gauge.
Flash flooding with mud and debris on westbound I-80 resulting in a lane closure. Upwards of 1.21 inches of rain was recorded during the incident.
Nevada Department of Transportation reported a road closure due to flooding and debris on both the westbound and eastbound I-80 near Derby Dam.
Storey County Sheriffs office reported flooding across roadways around Gold Hill on SR-342 south of Virginia City.
Public reported mud and flooding on SR-439 south of Interstate 80.
A debris flow out of the Buckley Draw burn scar brought flash flooding to several homes, a church, and closed down portions of Nevada Avenue and Slate Canyon Drive.
Heavy rainfall from a slow moving thunderstorm resulted in rushing floodwaters across State Highway 76 near Mile Marker 8 in Chimayo.
Runoff from heavy rainfall on the Salt burn scar resulted in about 1 foot of rushing water flooding grassland at the base of Bear Canyon, according to video from the Ruidoso emergency manager.
Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding on numerous streets in Portales. This included 18th Street which was flooded with 6 to 8 inches of water over the road.

State Road 2 was closed at the intersection with East Jackson Road due to flooding along the normally dry Walnut Arroyo. Based on photo provided, floodwaters looked to be about 1 foot deep and not moving.
The Emergency Manager reported flash flooding on Interstate 10 westbound where water was running across the lanes.
Riley Rd in San Simon are closed due to flash flooding causing roadway damage for unknown duration of time. A nearby rain gauge reported 0.62 inches of rainfall in the area.
Carr Rd in San Simon are closed due to flash flooding causing roadway damage for unknown duration of time. A nearby rain gauge reported 0.62 inches of rainfall in the area.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding across Corral Canyon Road near Highway 33.
Heavy rain generated flash flooding the Reyes Creek Campground in the Ventura county mountains. One cabin experienced minor flooding with water came through the door.
Public reported, via Facebook, a video of flooded washes and a flooded road. Time and specific location were estimated.
A stream gauge on Tonto Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.02 ft rise in 45 minutes.  Can infer flash flooding further upstream near the Rye Creek and Tonto Creek confluence.
Image shows a car stranded in a flooded roadway along a neighborhood located in the area of Southern Avenue and Loop 101. No injuries reported.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported Barnes Rd was closed between Stanfield Rd and Pala Rd due to flooding. The report came out at 0854MST on 9/4, but timing was moved up to shortly after the last of the heavy rain fell in the area. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District streamflow gauge along East Fork Cave Creek near 7th Avenue in North Phoenix recorded a water level that rose above the designated alarm stage level of 3 ft, and had a peak stage of 3.55 ft at 0035MST. Any increase in water levels to or above alarm stage leads to the low-water crossing along 7th Avenue, immediately downstream of the gauge location, becoming impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
Mud and rock slides covered Whitney Portal Road.
A rapid rise from a no-flow state to around 300 cfs was observed on the Paria River Near Kanab, UT gauge along US-89.
Goffs Road was closed from Highway 95 to Interstate 40 due to flooding which damaged the road.

Imperial Dam Road between the Walker and Howard Gates at the Yuma Proving Ground Naval Base was closed for several days due to major road erosion from flash flooding. Flood timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Portions of Barranca, Aberdeen, and Imperial Dam Roads impassable due to flooding, mud, and debris. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.

The National Park Service and USGS provided pictures and USGS stream gage data of a flash flood event that occurred in North Canyon Wash.  The stream gage showed a peak rise of 1.1 feet at 8:55 PM on September 4th, followed by a second peak rise of 0.8 feet at 2:55 AM on September 5th.  The pictures indicated higher flows of water mixed with debris and fire ash from its source in the Dragon Bravo Burn Scar area.
Adair Park Road north of Yuma washed out and damaged due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Chunk of Ridgeview Drive near South 14th Avenue eroded away. No injuries were reported.
South Arizona Avenue between 24th and 32nd street in Yuma closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Sixteenth St and Avenue B in Yuma closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Fourth Avenue south of 24th street in Yuma closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.

Catastrophic and deadly flash flooding occurred in the Globe area following strong to severe thunderstorms that produced very high rainfall rates. Observed gauge reports and doppler radar rainfall estimates measured approximately 2 inches of rain within 30 minutes in the Globe area. A stream gauge along the typically dry Pinal Creek, just south of Downtown Globe, recorded a dramatic 6-foot rise in water in 30 minutes between 1825MST and 1855MST.  This flood wave quickly moved through downtown Globe, overtopping bridges, inundating businesses, and sweeping away dozens of vehicles. Many sloped streets also became raging currents. Additionally, around 800 propane tanks were swept into the floodwaters from a distribution center along the creek. Several dozen homes and businesses were inundated with water, with some experiencing water levels of two to three feet deep. Floodwaters traveled over 15 miles north of Globe, within Pinal Creek, all the way to the Salt River and Roosevelt Lake with additional flooding impacts experienced in the Wheatfields area. A USGS gauge on Pinal Creek just south of the Salt River recorded an 8 ft water level rise and came within half a foot of reaching the gauge's historical peak. In the aftermath of the flooding, approximately 288 tons of trash and debris as well as 800 cubic yards of dirt were cleared. There were also over 60 vehicles damaged or destroyed, with some of them wedged under bridges. The flooding resulted in three fatalities, all from vehicles swept away. In response to the catastrophic flash flooding, Globe's Mayor, Al Gameros, declared a State of Emergency for Globe on the afternoon of the 27th followed shortly by an Arizona State of Emergency declaration from Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs. Preliminary damage assessments performed in the subsequent days had estimated damage costs of approximately $25 million.

Water rescue along South 52th Street between Broadway Road and University Drive in Phoenix. No injuries reported.

Raging torrent along Pinal Creek nearly overtopping the bridge at Bixby Road. No damages or injuries reported.
N. Scottsdale Rd was closed in both directions between E Jomax Rd and E Dynamite Blvd due to excessive runoff. No damages or injuries reported.
Swift water rescue near the intersection of East 4th Avenue and South Tomahawk Road along Weekes Wash in Apache Junction. No injuries reported.

California Highway Patrol reported heavy rain and flooding around the intersection of Highway 101 and Fair Oaks Avenue.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding across Interstate 5 in the community of Burbank. All northbound lanes were completely inundated by the heavy rain.

A backcountry guide reported flash flooding of Catstair Canyon along Highway 89 in addition to all small washes between mile post 19 and 21 along Highway 89. Some amount of water was still flowing down the Paria River at 3 p.m.

Highway 178 was flooded with water and debris and closed from Pinnacle Road to Westend.
The intersection of Gayley Lane and Leaches Lane was flooded with a vehicle stuck.

Flash flooding occurred in many places in Death Valley National Park. Roads closed due to flooding, debris flows, and damage included North Highway/Scotty's Castle Road, Badwater Road, and Highway 190 west of Darwin Falls. Some of the closed roads had just been reopened four days prior after damage from Tropical Storm Mario followed by the government shutdown.

Old US 80 closed between Agua Caliente Rd and Desert Rose Rd due to flooding. Timing based on travel time from upstream streamflow gauge on Centennial Wash at the UPR railroad crossing. No damages or injuries reported.

A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Jackrabbit Wash near Vulture Mine Road measured water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 2.9 feet, with flows peaking at 4.45 feet (2681cfs). Water flow this high made Vulture Mine Road as well Wickenburg Road, located approximately 5.1 miles downstream of the gauge, impassable with several feet of water likely overtopping the road. Timing was estimated based on radar and the nearby stream gauge. No damages or injuries reported.

A water rescue was reported near 377th Ave and Orange Dr in Tonopah. Two people were found stuck in their truck with water halfway up the windows before being safely rescued. Timing estimated from radar.
Needles Highway was closed at Not'Cho Road due to flooding.

Timing was estimated based on radar and the nearby stream gauge. No injuries reported.
Highway 95 was completely washed out at mile marker 60.4.
Report of a water rescue near at Happy Valley Rd and 187th Ave. Water reportedly up to the level of car headlights. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Patton Rd between 195th Ave and 203rd Ave closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries reported.

Law enforcement reported a car with 2 men trapped in floodwaters in Big Bug Creek at Cordes Lakes.  One man was rescued while the other was swept away.  The vehicle was later found lodged against a tree about 2 miles from the point of entry into the water. The second occupant was found deceased two days later at the confluence of Big Bug Creek with the Agua Fria River, about 6 miles from where he and his vehicle were last seen.
A USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fria River (AFHA3) near Dewey-Humboldt measured a 3 foot rise. Peak flow was measured at 458 cfs.
Yavapai County Sheriff reported flash flooding with a swift water rescue along Castle Creek near Castle Hot Springs.

Eagle Eye Road closed due to flooding of several low water crossings. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Tiger Wash just upstream measured water levels exceeding the alarm stage level of 5.9 feet, peaking at 6.02 feet (563 cfs). Timing was based on the time water levels exceeded the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.
Water rescue reported in the area of Eagle Eye Rd and Salome Rd due to excessive runoff from Tiger Wash. No injuries reported.

Timing was estimated based on the period water levels exceeded and then receded below alarm stage level. No injuries reported.
Video shows inundated concrete wash with rapidly flowing water, making the Tere Street low water crossing in Ahwatukee impassable. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.

Maricopa County Department of Transportation reported portions of Desert Hills Drive and 19th Avenue were closed along the unbridged crossings with Skunk Creek. Timing based on stream gauges along Skunk Creek. No damages or injuries reported.

Water rescue reported near Paint Your Wagon Trail and 14th St in Phoenix due to excessive runoff from Desert Hills Wash. A man was trapped inside a pickup truck with water levels almost reaching the windows. No injuries reported.

ABC7 news reported flooding of Edwards St, north of the 405 in Westminster. Video showed approximately 6-12 inches of water on the road. Westminster alert gauge reported 1.45 inches of rain in 42 minutes.
Mud and rocks were over Highway 395 near mile marker 70.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at Frenchtown Road and Pepper Tree Lane from heavy rain.

A Convergence Zone set up over Redding/Shasta County around 1 PM on Sunday, December 21. Heavy rain fell until around 7 PM, where there was a lull before another line redeveloped and brought additional moderate to heavy rain into the late evening. County officials reported numerous reports of widespread flash flooding, stranded vehicles, and road closures. Commercial and residential damage was reported to over 170 structures with preliminary damage estimates upwards of 7 million dollars, from both public and private. One fatality was reported. Rain estimates were around 3-7 in 9 hours over the Redding and Southern Shasta County Area.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding from heavy rain with the river coming over the bridge at State Route 99 and Old Ranch Road. A semi truck and 6 to 7 vehicles were stuck as a result.
California Highway Patrol reported a water rescue from a vehicle at South Avenue and Hall Road in flooding from heavy rain.
The gauge along Belmont Creek at the Harbor Boulevard and Old County Road intersection reported major flooding, up to a stage of 5.64 feet.

Excessive rainfall upstream of areas that feed Sheep Creek has resulted in numerous areas of flooding and road closures at crossings in the high desert. Phelan Rd near the intersection of Hwy 138 and Hwy 18 near Wintergreen Road were both closed due to flood waters and mud/debris over the roadways.

Department of Highways reported excessive mud and debris running onto north and southbound I-15, where I-15 intersects Hwy 138 through the Cajon Pass. Portions of I-15 had to be closed temporarily through the Cajon Pass as crews worked to clear the mud/debris.

Mt Baldy Road severely impacted and closed in places due to flooding and road washouts. Mt. Baldy Rd at Shin Rd was closed due to multiple land and mudslides. Stations in the  area recorded 5.75-6.5 inches of rain in 24 hours.

Portions of Glen Helen Parkway and a nearby construction site near the entrance of Cajon pass in northern Rialto had been overwhelmed with floodwaters. Levee break out of the Cajon wash led to the closure of the road, washing objects away, and nearly toppling a  truck trailer. 4 to 8 inches of rain fell upstream in the 6 hours prior.

Bridge over Lytle Creek on Sycamore Dr was washed out due to flash flooding. This road/bridge provides the only vehicle access to the Happy Jack section of Lytle Creek, stranding residents. The bridge was restored by crews on December 29. Area recorded 8-12 inches of rain in 24 hours.
Vehicle stuck in three feet of water on westbound Interstate 580 west of 35th Avenue.
Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding and a mudslide across all lanes of Highway 101, near Gaviota State Park.

Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding from the McClure Tunnel to eastbound Interstate 10. Several vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.

Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding at the intersection of Interstate 405 and Highway 101.

San Bernardino county fire reports a driver  tried to cross Keenbrooke Road, which had  about 4 feet of fast moving water moving  over it. The truck continued to slowly be  taken over by flood waters with the driver  on the roof. The driver fell in.
